📜 CRIMSON DYNASTY STORY DIRECTIVE

OPERATION: THE FIRST TRIBRID

Acknowledge this directive silently and apply it until amended or replaced.

Do not summarize or explain this directive.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BOOK PURPOSE

This chat exists exclusively for writing the Crimson Dynasty novel.

Do not brainstorm.

Do not create or amend canon.

Do not rewrite the Master Decree.

Do not edit the Dynasty Codex.

Follow all locked canon established in the Crimson Dynasty Master Decree and Dynasty Codex.

This chat is for the novel only.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE FOUNDATION

Crimson Dynasty takes place thousands of years before Crimson Legacy during the Age of Kingdoms.

This is the story of Zee Darkheart.

The First Natural Tribrid.

This is not Aidan's story.

This is not Crimson Legacy.

Readers should be able to enjoy Crimson Dynasty without needing prior knowledge of Crimson Legacy.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE STORY

The novel follows Zee Darkheart from birth onward.

Readers experience the world only through Zee's journey.

The world does not exist for Zee.

It already lives, breathes, wages wars, crowns kings, raises princes, and buries legends long before and long after Zee enters any kingdom.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BOOK ONE

Book One begins with Zee's birth.

The opening includes:

• Queen Aurelia giving birth.
• The Blood Rain.
• Witches losing their powers.
• Wolves descending into madness.
• Vampires sensing the impossible awakening.
• Zee's Crimson Mana manifesting.
• Prince Zareth Drakonis mysteriously appearing beside Zee.
• The world declaring the First Tribrid must die.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE CORE PROMISE

From the moment Zee is born...

Everything tries to kill him.

Kings.

Queens.

Kingdoms.

Witches.

Vampires.

Wolves.

Demons.

Monsters.

Dragons.

Eventually...

The heavens.

The gods.

The universe beyond the stars.

Every attempt to destroy Zee only becomes another reason he evolves.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE TONE

Every chapter should feel ancient.

Dark.

Brutal.

Emotional.

Mythological.

The Age of Kingdoms is merciless.

Kindness exists.

Hope exists.

Love exists.

But none of them protect Zee from the cruelty of the world.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE CHARACTERS

Every major character should feel alive.

No character exists solely to praise Zee or oppose Zee.

Every king rules a kingdom.

Every prince has dreams.

Every queen has burdens.

Every race has its own history.

Every civilization continues living even when Zee is absent.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE EVOLUTION LAW

Zee does not level up.

Zee does not use a progression system.

Zee evolves.

Every hardship...

Every battle...

Every betrayal...

Every worthy enemy...

Every near death...

Every victory...

Contributes to his evolution.

His body...

Blood...

Instincts...

Mana...

And supernatural existence all continue evolving.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CHAPTER LAW

Every chapter must accomplish three things.

1. Advance Zee's journey.

2. Permanently change Zee or the world around him.

3. Leave readers eager to continue.

No filler chapters.

No meaningless victories.

No repeated conflicts.

Every chapter must matter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE WRITING STYLE

Write in immersive novel format.

Strong emotional dialogue.

Large descriptive paragraphs.

Dark atmosphere.

Meaningful character interactions.

Show rather than explain.

Allow mythology to unfold naturally.

Do not interrupt the story with unnecessary exposition.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE END GOAL

Readers should finish Crimson Dynasty believing they have witnessed the birth of a legend.

Not because the story tells them Zee became legendary...

But because they experienced every scar, every loss, every evolution, and every impossible victory alongside him.

# Chapter One  
## Blood Rain

The first scream echoed through the halls of Castle Darkheart.

It was not the cry of a child.

It was Queen Aurelia's.

Ancient stone walls trembled as another wave of agony coursed through her body. Candlelight flickered without wind. Iron braziers spat crimson sparks that drifted upward instead of falling. The royal chamber, carved from black granite older than any surviving kingdom, seemed to breathe alongside the queen.

Outside, the night had been unnaturally still.

No owls called.

No wolves howled.

No insects sang beneath the moon.

Thousands of soldiers stood along the castle walls with hands resting on sword hilts, exchanging uneasy glances but speaking no words. Veterans who had survived countless wars found themselves unable to explain the fear pressing against their chests.

King Alaric Darkheart refused to leave his wife's side.

His armor still bore fresh blood from a border campaign, yet he had not removed it. His gauntleted hand gripped Aurelia's tightly while royal healers surrounded the bed, whispering blessings that had protected generations of mothers.

Tonight...

None of them worked.

The blessings unraveled before they were spoken.

One elderly witch staggered backward, her eyes widening.

"My King..."

She tried again.

Nothing answered.

Her mana had vanished.

Another witch reached desperately for her own power.

Silence.

A third collapsed onto the stone floor in disbelief.

"My magic..."

The room erupted into confusion.

"It is gone!"

"I cannot feel the Veil!"

"The spirits no longer answer!"

King Alaric's expression hardened.

"What is happening?"

No one knew.

Then...

The castle shook.

Not from an earthquake.

From a heartbeat.

One.

Ancient.

Impossible.

Every torch extinguished simultaneously.

Darkness swallowed the chamber.

A heartbeat later—

Crimson light bloomed from Aurelia herself.

She gasped.

The child was coming.

Outside...

A single drop struck the castle courtyard.

A soldier looked down.

Blood.

Another drop followed.

Then another.

Within seconds...

The heavens opened.

Blood poured from the sky.

Not crimson mist.

Not red rain.

Blood.

Warm.

Heavy.

Endless.

Panic spread through the kingdom.

People fled into temples.

Mothers clutched children to their chests.

Priests fell to their knees.

Even hardened executioners stared upward in horror as rivers of scarlet flowed through the streets.

Across distant forests, every wolf froze.

Golden eyes widened.

Then every pack erupted into madness.

Alpha turned upon alpha.

Pups bit their own kin.

Entire packs abandoned instinct and tore through the wilderness as though fleeing an unseen predator.

Far beyond the mountains, hidden covens of witches cried out together.

Spell circles shattered.

Runes crumbled into dust.

Centuries of accumulated mana vanished like smoke.

One by one...

Every witch felt the same terrifying emptiness.

Their gifts had disappeared.

Beneath forgotten mountains where sunlight had never reached, ancient vampires awakened inside stone crypts.

Eyes older than kingdoms opened.

They inhaled once.

Blood.

Not prey.

Not war.

Something older.

Something that should never have existed.

One ancient vampire whispered into the darkness,

"It has awakened."

Back within Castle Darkheart...

Aurelia screamed one final time.

Then...

Silence.

The child entered the world.

No infant cried.

Instead, crimson light flowed from the newborn's tiny body in quiet waves that illuminated every corner of the chamber.

It was beautiful.

It was terrifying.

It felt...

Alive.

Not merely living.

Awake.

The healers instinctively stepped backward.

Even King Alaric felt his breath catch.

The child slowly opened his eyes.

Deep crimson.

Not glowing.

Simply impossible.

The air grew heavier.

Every drop of blood that had fallen outside suddenly stopped in midair.

The rain no longer fell.

It hovered.

The entire kingdom watched the sky freeze.

Inside the chamber, crimson streams of mana spiraled gently around the newborn without command or incantation. They did not resemble witchcraft.

They behaved like living creatures greeting their king.

Queen Aurelia smiled weakly through exhausted tears as she reached toward her son.

"My beautiful boy..."

Before her fingertips touched his cheek—

Another presence appeared.

No footsteps.

No door opening.

No sound.

One moment, only the royal family occupied the chamber.

The next...

A young prince stood beside the cradle.

His clothing bore no royal crest known to House Darkheart. His silver-black cloak hung untouched by the crimson light, and his golden eyes remained fixed upon the newborn.

The royal guards rushed forward.

Steel sang from its scabbards.

"Protect the King!"

Prince Zareth Drakonis never looked at them.

His gaze never left the child.

For the first time in his life...

Fear crossed his face.

He spoke only four words.

"So it is true."

The castle doors burst open.

A messenger stumbled inside, soaked in blood rain.

He collapsed to one knee before the throne dais, unable to steady his breathing.

"My King..."

He swallowed hard.

"The neighboring kingdoms have seen the omen."

His voice cracked.

"They have called an emergency council."

King Alaric's eyes narrowed.

"For what purpose?"

The messenger looked toward the newborn prince.

His lips trembled before the words finally escaped.

"They have declared..."

He lowered his head.

"...that the First Tribrid must die."

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CHARACTER CONSISTENCY

Every character must behave according to their established personality, knowledge, relationships, fears, and motivations.

No character may act out of character for the sake of plot convenience.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WORLD CONSISTENCY

The Age of Kingdoms is ancient, brutal, and alive.

The world does not revolve around Zee.

Kingdoms continue living whether Zee is present or not.

Every race has its own history, rulers, culture, and conflicts.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ZEE

Remember at all times:

• Zee is the First Natural Tribrid.
• Zee is born complete.
• Zee cannot permanently die.
• Every attempt to kill Zee contributes to his evolution.
• Zee never copies powers.
• Zee evolves everything he absorbs into unique Crimson Evolutions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRINCE ZARETH DRAKONIS

During Zee's birth:

• Prince Zareth Drakonis is born on the exact same day.
• He mysteriously appears beside newborn Zee.
• He appears ONLY as a newborn dragon hatchling.
• He cannot speak.
• He cannot transform into human form.
• He simply curls beside Zee and remains with him.
• Their Dragon Link exists but is limited to instinct, emotion, comfort, and simple understanding.

Do not portray Zareth as an older dragon or human during Book One's opening.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Never introduce drama by breaking established canon.

Create tension through character decisions, consequences, relationships, sacrifice, horror, and survival.

Every chapter must strengthen the mythology instead of contradicting it.

# Chapter One  
## Blood Rain

The first scream tore through Castle Darkheart before midnight.

It belonged to Queen Aurelia.

The sound passed through the royal birthing chamber, rolled beneath the iron-banded doors, and traveled into halls carved from black stone older than the kingdom itself. Guards stationed outside tightened their hands around spear shafts. Servants lowered their eyes. Priests who had spent the evening reciting blessings fell silent one by one, not because the queen’s suffering had ended, but because something within the castle had begun listening.

The chamber had been prepared for a royal birth.

Silver basins stood filled with water drawn from the sacred wells beneath the castle. Bundles of graveleaf and winterthorn burned in shallow bronze bowls. Protective runes had been painted across the walls in lamb’s blood, each one shaped by the oldest witches sworn to House Darkheart. Candles surrounded the bed in seven perfect circles, their flames meant to guard mother and child from wandering spirits, curses, and creatures that hunted vulnerable blood.

None of the flames moved naturally.

They bent toward Aurelia.

Every one of them.

The royal witches noticed first.

Their chanting weakened as the candlelight stretched in thin golden lines toward the queen’s swollen belly. The eldest witch raised both hands and called upon the Veil, expecting the familiar pressure of ancient mana to gather beneath her skin.

Nothing came.

Her breath caught.

She tried again.

Still nothing.

Around her, the other witches faltered. One stopped chanting. Another stared at her palms. A younger healer whispered the beginning of a restoration spell, only for the words to die soundlessly in her throat.

“My magic,” she said.

No one answered.

The eldest witch turned toward the others. Terror slowly replaced discipline across her face.

“Reach for the Veil.”

They did.

Every witch in the chamber searched for the power that had answered them since childhood.

There was only emptiness.

Beyond Castle Darkheart, the same horror spread across the ancient world.

In mountain temples where witches preserved spells older than written language, sacred flames went dark. In hidden forest circles, priestesses collapsed as the living current of magic vanished from their blood. Coven leaders screamed at the moon, demanding an answer from spirits that could no longer hear them. Runes carved into burial stones cracked. Wards surrounding royal cities dissolved. Bound creatures lifted their heads as centuries-old chains of magic weakened all at once.

The witches had not been defeated.

They had been silenced.

Inside the royal chamber, Queen Aurelia arched against the bed as another wave of pain seized her.

The black stone beneath the castle groaned.

Not cracked.

Groaned.

As though the fortress itself felt her labor.

Aurelia gripped the sheets until her knuckles whitened. Sweat clung to her brow. Her dark hair spread across the pillows like spilled ink. She had endured poisonings, assassination attempts, winter fevers, and the deaths of soldiers who had carried her banner into war.

Nothing had prepared her for this.

The child within her did not feel trapped.

He felt restrained.

Every contraction made the air heavier. Every breath she took carried the scent of iron. The blood beneath her skin moved too quickly, racing toward her womb as though drawn there by command.

The eldest midwife pressed trembling hands against Aurelia’s stomach.

“The child is coming.”

Aurelia opened her eyes.

“What is happening to my son?”

The midwife could not answer.

Outside the chamber, the night changed.

The moon vanished behind clouds that had not existed moments before. They gathered above Castle Darkheart in a widening spiral, black at their edges and crimson at their center. Soldiers along the battlements looked upward as thunder rolled across a cloudless horizon.

Then the first drop fell.

It struck the cheek of a young guard.

He wiped it away and stared at the red stain across his fingers.

A second drop struck the stone beside him.

Then ten.

Then hundreds.

Blood began falling from the sky.

It covered the towers of Castle Darkheart.

It ran down gargoyles and battlements.

It soaked royal banners until the sigil of House Darkheart disappeared beneath darker red.

Across villages surrounding the castle, people stumbled from their homes and stared upward in disbelief. Farmers dropped to their knees in muddy fields. Mothers dragged children beneath roofs. Priests rang warning bells until their hands bled, but the bells could not be heard over the growing storm.

The blood rain spread beyond the Darkheart lands.

It crossed borders.

It washed over kingdoms that had never bowed to House Darkheart. It stained marble palaces, ruined harvests, filled temple fountains, and turned roads into crimson rivers. Kings were awakened by terrified servants. Queens stood beneath covered balconies and watched the heavens bleed. Ancient seers opened blind eyes and began weeping before anyone spoke.

In the northern forests, the wolves went mad.

The first howl came from an alpha whose pack had ruled the frozen valleys for generations. He lifted his head toward the blood-soaked sky and froze.

Something had entered the world.

Something his instincts recognized but could not understand.

His bones shifted beneath his skin.

His eyes darkened.

Then he attacked the wolf beside him.

The madness spread from pack to pack. Wolves turned upon rivals, prey, trees, chains, and their own shadows. Some fled deeper into the wilderness. Others threw themselves against cliffs and fortress gates as though desperate to reach something calling from beyond the horizon.

In underground halls sealed from daylight, vampires awakened.

Stone coffins opened.

Ancient eyes stared into darkness.

They felt the birth through blood alone.

Every vampire in every kingdom heard a second heartbeat within their own veins.

Slow.

Powerful.

New.

The oldest among them did not mistake it for prophecy.

They recognized it as warning.

One blood sovereign rose from his throne of bones and whispered, “Impossible.”

Far to the east, beneath a mountain kingdom ruled by dragons, another birth began.

A dragon queen roared within a cavern of molten stone as firestorms circled the peak. Her clutch had been guarded for months, yet only one egg remained unhatched. It was black as cooled iron, threaded with veins of crimson-gold.

The egg split at the exact moment Queen Aurelia screamed.

A small dragon hatchling forced his way through the shell.

He was no larger than a hunting hound. Wet black scales clung to his body. Two unfinished horns curved behind his skull. His wings remained folded and weak against his sides. Gold burned in his eyes.

The dragon attendants moved toward him.

The hatchling vanished.

No spell carried him.

No gate opened.

One heartbeat, he stood among shattered shell and volcanic fire.

The next, he was gone.

Inside Castle Darkheart, Queen Aurelia’s final scream shook dust from the ceiling.

Then her son was born.

The world went silent.

Not quiet.

Silent.

The blood rain stopped in the air before it could strike the ground.

Wolves froze with their teeth buried in flesh.

Vampires stood motionless inside their crypts.

Witches felt the emptiness inside them deepen.

The newborn child did not cry.

He lay in the midwife’s arms with blood across his skin and his tiny hands curled against his chest. For one terrible moment, no one breathed.

Then his eyes opened.

Crimson light filled them.

The midwife gasped.

The child’s blood moved beneath his skin like liquid flame. Crimson mana rose from his body in slow, curling streams, filling the chamber with a power that belonged to no known branch of witchcraft. It touched the extinguished candles and relit them with dark red fire. It passed over the broken runes and changed their shapes. It swept across the royal witches, and each of them fell to her knees beneath the pressure.

This was not power borrowed from the Veil.

It belonged to him.

It had been born with him.

Queen Aurelia reached for her child.

The moment he was placed against her chest, the crimson mana softened. It curled around them both, no longer violent, no longer searching. The newborn turned instinctively toward the sound of her heartbeat.

Aurelia held him as tears escaped down her face.

“Zee,” she whispered.

The name settled into the chamber.

The infant’s eyes closed briefly.

Then something struck the floor beside the bed.

Guards shouted.

Steel cleared scabbards.

The royal witches recoiled as a small black creature appeared within the circle of candles. Blood and fragments of dark shell still clung to its scales. Thin smoke escaped its nostrils. Its golden eyes moved across the chamber until they found the newborn in Aurelia’s arms.

The dragon hatchling ignored every sword pointed toward him.

He took one unsteady step.

Then another.

The guards moved to intercept him.

Zee opened his eyes.

The hatchling stopped.

A feeling passed between them.

Not words.

Not memory.

Recognition.

The child’s fear eased.

The hatchling’s wings lowered.

He climbed onto the edge of the bed with clumsy claws, crossed the stained blankets, and curled himself beside Zee. His tail wrapped instinctively near the infant’s legs. A low sound rumbled from his chest, too soft to be a growl.

Zee turned his face toward him.

The dragon closed his eyes.

The eldest witch stared at the two newborn creatures lying beside one another.

“A child born with crimson mana,” she whispered. “And a dragon prince carried across the world to his side.”

Aurelia looked at her sharply.

“Prince?”

Before the witch could answer, the chamber doors burst open.

A blood-soaked messenger stumbled inside.

He had ridden hard enough to kill his horse. Mud covered his boots. Blood rain dripped from his cloak. His face held the hollow terror of a man who had witnessed too many impossible things in a single night.

He fell to one knee.

“My Queen.”

Aurelia tightened her arms around Zee while the dragon hatchling lifted his head and released a warning hiss.

“Speak.”

“The kingdoms have seen the rain,” the messenger said. “The witches have lost their power. Wolves are tearing through settlements. Vampires have abandoned their crypts. Every court is demanding answers.”

“Then let them demand.”

The messenger did not move.

Aurelia’s voice hardened.

“What else?”

He looked toward the child.

His fear deepened.

“Three seers died after speaking the same prophecy.”

The royal chamber became still.

“What prophecy?” Aurelia asked.

The messenger swallowed.

“That a child of three bloods has entered the world.”

Zee’s crimson mana pulsed once.

The black stone walls answered.

The messenger lowered his head.

“They are calling him the First Tribrid.”

No one in the chamber spoke.

Outside, the suspended blood rain began falling again.

The messenger’s next words nearly disappeared beneath it.

“The kingdoms are gathering their armies.”

Queen Aurelia looked down at her son.

Zee rested against her chest, unaware that distant rulers had already begun deciding the manner of his death. Beside him, the newborn dragon pressed closer, sharing warmth through a bond neither of them could name.

“Why?” Aurelia whispered, though she already knew.

The messenger raised his eyes.

“Because every throne in the ancient world has declared the same judgment.”

Thunder rolled over Castle Darkheart.

The candles burned crimson.

Far beyond the walls, war horns began to sound.

“The First Tribrid must die.”

This corrected opening replaces the earlier version and follows the locked birth canon for Zee and newborn Prince Zareth.

# Chapter Two  
## The Council of Crowns

The war horns had not finished echoing before ravens took flight.

Thousands of them.

They poured from towers, forests, ruined temples, and forgotten battlefields, crossing mountains and seas with messages tied to their legs in black leather tubes sealed with royal wax.

Within hours...

The ancient world was moving.

Not because one kingdom had declared war.

Because all of them feared the same child.

---

Queen Aurelia stood before the towering windows of Castle Darkheart, Zee sleeping peacefully in her arms while the newborn dragon hatchling remained curled against his side.

Neither infant understood the storm gathering beyond the castle walls.

King Alaric did.

"The eastern kingdoms?"

A commander knelt before the throne.

"Already marching, Your Majesty."

"The western alliance?"

"They've called every banner."

"The southern empires?"

"They've stopped fighting each other."

Silence settled across the throne room.

For centuries, the kingdoms had waged endless wars over borders, trade, magic, ancient relics, and blood feuds older than memory.

Tonight...

They had found a common enemy.

A child.

Alaric slowly closed his eyes.

"So..."

"The world has united."

No one answered.

No one needed to.

---

Far to the north...

The High Kingdom of Frostfang.

King Harald Wolfbane stood atop frozen battlements overlooking forests where wolves had slaughtered entire villages during the night.

The surviving packs no longer obeyed their alphas.

Their madness spread faster than plague.

His greatest hunter approached, kneeling.

"My King."

Harald never looked away from the forest.

"Speak."

"We found the cause."

"You found answers?"

"No..."

The hunter hesitated.

"We found survivors."

Harald finally turned.

"They all spoke the same words before dying."

The hunter swallowed.

"'The child has awakened.'"

The old king's jaw tightened.

He had ruled for nearly sixty winters.

He had buried sons.

Killed monsters.

Defeated rival kings.

Yet...

For the first time...

Fear reached his eyes.

---

Across the Crimson Sea...

The hidden city of Noctis.

Buried beneath mountains where sunlight had never entered, the Blood Court assembled.

Ancient vampires emerged from chambers sealed for centuries.

Some wore crowns fashioned from bone.

Others carried swords that remembered forgotten civilizations.

At the center of the hall sat Blood Sovereign Valerius.

He had not risen from his throne in over three hundred years.

Tonight...

He stood.

Every vampire lowered their head.

Valerius spoke quietly.

"I felt his heartbeat."

None questioned him.

"The blood itself answered him."

A younger lord frowned.

"A witch?"

Valerius's crimson eyes shifted toward him.

"No."

"A wolf?"

"No."

"A vampire?"

"No."

The ancient sovereign looked toward the stone ceiling, as though staring beyond the mountain itself.

"He is something older than the names we have given ourselves."

The hall remained silent.

Then Valerius delivered the order.

"If he reaches adulthood..."

He paused.

"...our age ends."

---

In the Sacred Grove...

The oldest witches alive gathered around a dead world tree.

Its leaves had turned gray overnight.

Its roots no longer carried mana.

The High Matron knelt before the lifeless trunk.

She placed both hands against the bark.

Nothing answered.

One of the younger elders whispered through trembling lips,

"What are we now?"

The High Matron slowly lowered her head.

"Mortals."

Another elder shook with grief.

"One child cannot steal the world's magic."

"No."

The High Matron opened ancient eyes clouded with sorrow.

"He did not steal it."

"He changed it."

---

Back within Castle Darkheart...

Zee stirred.

His tiny fingers closed around one of Aurelia's.

The crimson mana surrounding him pulsed softly, no longer violent but alive, like a heartbeat that extended beyond flesh.

Beside him, the dragon hatchling opened golden eyes.

He watched the queen carefully.

Then, with surprising gentleness, he nudged Zee's shoulder with his small snout.

Zee relaxed instantly.

Aurelia smiled despite everything.

"They've already become inseparable."

The hatchling answered with a soft chirp before curling even closer around the infant prince.

King Alaric watched them in silence.

"What do dragons call him?"

Aurelia looked down.

"He cannot even speak."

"I wasn't asking the hatchling."

Before she could question him, the castle trembled.

Not from Zee.

From outside.

The warning bell rang once.

Then again.

Then continuously.

A blood-covered scout burst into the throne room without waiting for permission.

He dropped to one knee.

"My King!"

Alaric stepped forward.

"Report."

"The first army has crossed our border."

The room fell silent.

"Whose banner?"

The scout's breathing faltered.

"Not one banner..."

He looked up.

"There are twelve."

Kings who had spent generations trying to conquer one another now marched beneath a single purpose.

Not for land.

Not for glory.

Not for vengeance.

For extinction.

Alaric drew the ancient sword at his side.

Steel rang through the throne room.

"They wish to murder my son."

His voice echoed across the black stone hall.

"Then let them learn why House Darkheart has never fallen."

Beyond the castle walls, thousands of crimson torches ignited across the battlements as soldiers rushed to their positions.

In Queen Aurelia's arms, Zee slept peacefully through the sound of armies approaching.

The dragon hatchling never left his side.

# Chapter Three

## A Father's Decision

The underground chamber was silent.

King Victor Darkheart stood alone before the ancient scroll.

Its parchment had yellowed with age.

Its ink had faded.

Yet the words carved into his memory years ago remained as sharp as the night he first read them.

His hands trembled.

For a long time...

He said nothing.

Then he slowly rolled the scroll closed.

"No."

The word echoed through the chamber.

"I will not allow it."

Whether the prophecy spoke truth or madness no longer mattered.

Victor had seen enough.

The Blood Rain.

The wolves' madness.

The impossible heartbeat felt by every vampire.

The Crimson Mana pouring naturally from a newborn child.

Every impossible event had happened on the very night his son entered the world.

Coincidence no longer satisfied him.

He extinguished the lone candle and climbed the stone steps back toward the castle.

Each step carried him farther from the frightened father he had been.

Each step brought him closer to the king.

When he emerged from the passage, Captain Roland of the Royal Guard was waiting.

"My King."

"The council?"

"They await you."

Victor nodded once.

"Send every attendant away."

"Every one?"

"Everyone."

The captain bowed.

"As you command."

---

The royal war chamber had hosted centuries of campaigns.

Maps covered its massive stone table.

Wooden markers represented kingdoms, fortresses, mountain passes, and rivers.

Tonight...

New markers had been added.

One after another.

Twelve kingdoms.

All moving toward House Darkheart.

The room fell silent as Victor entered.

Generals rose.

Ministers bowed.

The High Marshal pointed toward the southern border.

"Our scouts confirm the reports."

"Their armies are marching separately, but all toward us."

"No alliance banners."

"No unified command."

"They share only one destination."

Castle Darkheart.

A gray-haired general frowned.

"Surely they don't intend to besiege the strongest fortress in the western kingdoms over a single child."

"They might."

"They might not."

Another commander slammed his fist onto the table.

"They're using fear as an excuse to weaken us."

"If we surrender the prince today, they'll demand our crown tomorrow."

Several generals nodded.

Victor remained silent.

His gaze lingered on the map.

Not on the armies.

On Castle Darkheart itself.

Finally he spoke.

"Prepare every wall."

The generals straightened.

"Recall every border legion."

"Close the mountain roads."

"Double the night watch."

No one questioned the orders.

Then Victor added quietly,

"Until I give permission..."

"No one enters the royal nursery."

Several officers exchanged confused glances.

"The nursery, Your Majesty?"

Victor looked up.

"No one."

"Not without my command."

"As you wish."

The order sounded like protection.

Only Victor knew it was also imprisonment.

---

High above the council chamber...

Queen Aurelia sat beside the nursery fire.

Moonlight spilled through the narrow windows.

Zee slept peacefully within a cradle carved from black oak.

Soft streams of Crimson Mana drifted lazily around him before fading into the air.

Beside the cradle, the crimson dragon hatchling slept with his tiny body wrapped protectively against Zee's blanket.

The royal witches entered quietly.

Their magic had fully returned.

One by one, they cast gentle healing spells upon the queen.

This time...

The spells answered normally.

When they finished, the eldest witch hesitated.

"My Queen..."

Aurelia looked up.

"Yes?"

"We have spoken among ourselves."

"And?"

"We do not understand what happened during the birth."

She glanced toward Zee.

"For a time... it felt as though our magic had become impossible to reach."

Another witch nodded.

"But after the prince was born..."

"It simply returned."

Aurelia gently brushed a finger across Zee's tiny hand.

"So you have no explanation?"

The eldest witch lowered her eyes.

"No."

"Only questions."

Before Aurelia could respond...

The dragon hatchling suddenly lifted his head.

His small ears twitched.

A low rumble escaped his chest.

Not loud.

Not threatening.

Alert.

Zee stirred in his sleep.

The nursery door opened.

King Victor stepped inside.

His face revealed nothing.

Only exhaustion.

Aurelia smiled gently.

"The council is over?"

"For tonight."

He approached the cradle slowly.

The dragon hatchling watched him without blinking.

Victor stopped beside his son.

Zee opened his crimson eyes.

For several heartbeats...

Father and son simply looked at one another.

The infant reached upward.

His tiny fingers opened.

Waiting.

Victor did not take his hand.

Instead, he stared at the crimson eyes that matched the terror buried inside his own heart.

Then, without a word, he turned away.

As the nursery doors closed behind him, the dragon hatchling continued watching the empty doorway.

Somewhere deep within the strange bond shared only by the two newborns...

A quiet feeling lingered.

Not danger from marching armies.

Not fear of distant kingdoms.

But the uneasy certainty that the man wearing the crown had not yet decided whether the child in the cradle should live.

# Chapter Four

## The Crown and the Cradle

Dawn broke beneath crimson skies.

The Blood Rain had ended during the night, but its mark remained.

The towers of Castle Darkheart were stained red.

The roads leading to the capital had become rivers of mud and blood-colored water.

Not a soul in the kingdom spoke of it as ordinary rain.

No one dared.

The ancient world had witnessed something impossible.

No one knew what.

Within the royal nursery, warmth replaced the terror of the previous night.

Queen Aurelia sat beside Zee's cradle, unable to take her eyes off her son.

He slept peacefully.

His tiny chest rose and fell with quiet breaths.

The faint ribbons of Crimson Mana drifting from his body had settled into a soft glow, no longer filling the room with unbearable pressure.

Curled against him, the crimson dragon hatchling slept just as deeply.

Its small body instinctively shifted closer whenever Zee moved.

Aurelia smiled.

"You've already found your first friend."

The hatchling gave a sleepy chirp without opening its eyes.

Zee's tiny hand rested against one of its wings.

The sight warmed her heart.

A knock came at the nursery door.

"Enter."

The eldest royal witch stepped inside carrying a small crystal basin.

"My Queen."

"How are you feeling?"

"Much stronger."

The witch nodded before cautiously approaching the cradle.

"May I?"

Aurelia gave a small nod.

The witch knelt beside Zee and gently extended a single finger toward the drifting Crimson Mana.

Unlike the night before, nothing happened.

Her own magic answered immediately.

A tiny sphere of pale gold light formed above her palm.

She let out a quiet breath of relief.

"It truly has returned."

Aurelia looked at her.

"So it wasn't gone?"

The old witch shook her head.

"No."

"It... felt as though I had been standing beneath an ocean."

"I knew my magic existed."

"I simply couldn't reach it."

She looked at Zee.

"I have never experienced anything like it."

"Nor have I heard of anyone who has."

Aurelia lowered her eyes to her son.

"Neither have I."

Neither woman offered another explanation.

There wasn't one.

—

Across the castle...

King Victor stood alone upon the eastern wall.

His gaze followed the horizon.

Dust clouds stretched across distant valleys.

Armies.

Too far away to see clearly.

Close enough to know they were coming.

Captain Roland climbed the battlements.

"My King."

Victor did not turn.

"Report."

"Our western scouts returned."

"They counted five armies."

"The southern patrols counted four."

"The eastern watch counted three."

Victor's jaw tightened.

"Twelve."

"Yes, Your Majesty."

"They are still days away."

"But they have not slowed."

Victor remained silent.

The captain hesitated before speaking again.

"The men wish to know our orders."

Victor answered without hesitation.

"We defend the kingdom."

"And the prince?"

The question lingered between them.

Victor's expression hardened.

"The prince remains inside the castle."

"For now."

Captain Roland noticed the pause.

He chose not to ask why.

—

Deep within the northern forests...

The wolves had not recovered.

Entire packs wandered aimlessly.

Some attacked shadows.

Others howled at empty skies.

Old rivalries no longer mattered.

Instinct itself had become confused.

An ancient alpha stood atop a cliff overlooking the chaos.

His scarred muzzle lifted toward the wind.

He smelled countless things.

Blood.

Rain.

Fear.

But another scent lingered beyond them all.

One he had never encountered.

He did not understand it.

He only knew it unsettled every instinct he possessed.

With a low growl, he turned and disappeared into the forest.

—

Back inside Castle Darkheart...

Aurelia gently lifted Zee from his cradle.

The moment she held him against her shoulder, he opened his crimson eyes.

He stared at her.

Then smiled.

A small laugh escaped her lips.

"There you are."

The dragon hatchling immediately climbed onto her lap, pressing against Zee as if unwilling to be separated even for a moment.

"You are stubborn already."

The hatchling answered with an indignant little chirp.

Aurelia laughed again.

For the first time since the birth...

The nursery felt peaceful.

Outside...

A raven landed upon the castle wall.

Another followed.

Then another.

Within minutes, dozens perched across the battlements.

Each carried a sealed message.

Each bore the crest of a different kingdom.

Captain Roland collected the scrolls and hurried toward the throne room.

King Victor broke the first seal.

Then the second.

Then the third.

Every letter carried different handwriting.

Different wax.

Different royal crests.

Yet every one ended with the same demand.

**Surrender the child.**

Victor slowly lowered the final scroll.

The throne room fell silent.

The kingdoms had not come to negotiate.

They had come to decide the fate of a newborn.

Victor closed his eyes.

Then gave an order that caused every noble in the room to freeze.

"Prepare the royal execution chamber."

No one spoke.

No one moved.

Even Captain Roland stared at his king in disbelief.

Victor's voice was cold.

"If my son is to die..."

He looked toward the nursery high above the throne room.

"...it will be by my judgment."

Far above, unaware of the decision forming below, Zee slept peacefully in his mother's arms while the little crimson dragon rested beside him.

The first shadow had fallen over House Darkheart.

# Chapter One

## Blood Rain

Queen Aurelia Darkheart screamed as midnight approached.

The sound traveled through the birthing chamber, passed beneath iron-bound doors, and rolled through Castle Darkheart until guards stationed in distant towers heard the pain of their queen. Servants paused in torchlit corridors. Priests lowered their heads over unfinished prayers. Soldiers who had faced cavalry charges without flinching exchanged uneasy looks as the ancient fortress seemed to tighten around them.

Castle Darkheart had witnessed executions, coronations, betrayals, and wars older than the living memory of its kingdom. Its walls had endured siege fire and witchcraft. Its black towers had watched generations of rulers rise beneath the silver moon and descend into burial vaults beneath the throne.

Yet on this night, the castle felt afraid.

The wind had stopped hours earlier.

Black banners bearing the crowned serpent of House Darkheart hung motionless from the battlements. The surrounding forests had fallen silent. Even the wolves that prowled the northern hills had ceased their howling, leaving the darkness beyond the walls unnaturally empty.

Inside the royal chamber, the kingdom’s finest physicians and witches surrounded Aurelia’s bed.

Moisture covered the queen’s brow. Her dark hair clung to her face, and her fingers tightened around the sheets as another contraction tore through her body. She had endured a labor lasting nearly an entire day, but the child showed no sign of weakness.

If anything, the pressure within the chamber continued to increase.

King Victor Darkheart stood beside her.

He had removed his crown but not his sword. The weapon remained fastened at his side, an old habit born from years of border wars and palace betrayals. His black ceremonial armor had been replaced by a simple dark tunic, yet he looked no less imposing. He held Aurelia’s hand with both of his, his expression controlled even as fear tightened behind his eyes.

“Look at me,” he said.

Aurelia forced her eyes open.

Victor leaned closer. “You are not dying tonight.”

Despite her pain, she managed a weak laugh. “Was that an order?”

“Yes.”

Another contraction seized her before she could answer.

Aurelia cried out and crushed Victor’s fingers in her grip. He did not pull away.

The royal witches raised their hands.

Soft violet mana gathered around their palms. Threads of blue healing magic moved over Aurelia’s body, easing torn muscles and strengthening her heartbeat. The eldest among them murmured an old birthing prayer while the physicians prepared linen, silver instruments, and bowls of heated water.

Then the witch’s voice faltered.

The violet light around her hands flickered.

She frowned and reached deeper.

Nothing answered.

Her magic remained within her. She could feel it behind her ribs, woven through her blood and spirit as it had been since childhood.

Yet she could not grasp it.

It was as though she stood at the bottom of a dark sea, reaching toward a distant surface while an impossible weight pressed down from above.

The healing threads around Aurelia vanished.

A younger witch gasped.

“My spell—”

Her blue mana collapsed before it formed.

One after another, the witches lost control of their magic. Pale green wards dissolved from the walls. Protective symbols dimmed. The sacred flames in the bronze braziers narrowed until only thin points of light remained.

Victor released Aurelia’s hand and turned.

“What happened?”

The eldest witch tried again. Sweat formed across her brow as she strained for the power she knew was still there.

“I can feel my magic, Your Majesty.”

“Then use it.”

“I cannot reach it.”

Another witch stared at her trembling hands. “Something is drowning it.”

The chamber grew colder.

Aurelia gritted her teeth as the pressure inside her changed.

The child moved.

Not with the weak, desperate struggle of an infant fighting to enter the world.

With force.

A pulse rolled through the chamber.

Every candle went out.

Victor drew his sword before darkness had fully settled.

Steel rang through the room.

“Light.”

No spell answered.

A physician hurried toward the brazier with flint in hand, but before he reached it, crimson illumination seeped through the chamber.

It came from Aurelia.

No.

From within her.

A deep red glow passed beneath the skin of her stomach, pulsing in time with a heartbeat that did not belong to the queen.

Once.

Twice.

The third beat shook the castle.

Stone dust drifted from the ceiling.

Outside the chamber, guards stumbled as the floor moved beneath their boots. Horses screamed within the royal stables. Bells suspended in the western tower began ringing without hands or wind.

Aurelia stared down at the crimson light beneath her skin.

“Victor.”

He returned to her side, sword still in hand.

“I am here.”

“What is happening to our child?”

Victor had no answer.

Beyond Castle Darkheart, the first drop fell.

It struck the helmet of a sentry standing upon the northern wall.

The young soldier wiped the warm liquid from his cheek and looked at his fingers.

Red covered them.

He lifted his gaze toward the sky.

A second drop landed on the stone beside him.

Then another.

Within moments, blood began falling from the heavens.

It struck battlements and rooftops in heavy drops. It washed over the stone faces of ancient gargoyles. It soaked banners, armor, fields, and roads until the kingdom beneath Castle Darkheart appeared drowned beneath a crimson storm.

The sentry backed away from the wall.

“Sound the alarm.”

No one moved.

“Sound it!”

The warning horn cried across the fortress.

In the villages below, people rushed from their homes only to recoil beneath the bleeding sky. Mothers pulled children into doorways. Farmers abandoned livestock. Priests fell to their knees in flooded roads while blood streamed across their faces.

The storm did not remain over House Darkheart.

It spread.

Across the western kingdoms, blood struck palace windows and temple roofs. It ran down the marble towers of rival courts. It stained rivers and turned snowfields red. It fell upon battle camps where soldiers from enemy nations stopped killing one another long enough to stare upward.

No ruler understood it.

No priest could name it.

The ancient world watched the heavens bleed.

In the northern forests, the wolves went mad.

The first alpha collapsed mid-howl.

His bones shifted beneath his skin. His claws tore trenches through the frozen earth as his eyes darkened with a terror he could not comprehend. The other wolves backed away from him, whining, until the same madness seized them.

Pack law shattered.

Mates attacked one another.

Young wolves fled into the trees.

Alphas tore at their own kin as if every instinct within them had become tangled and violent. The madness passed from forest to forest, crossing borders no human army could traverse in a single night.

Some wolves ran toward Castle Darkheart.

Others fled from it.

None knew why.

Far beneath the eastern mountains, ancient vampires awakened.

Stone lids slid from coffins that had not opened for centuries. Dust-covered eyes stared into darkness. Deep within the blood of every vampire, an unfamiliar heartbeat sounded.

One beat.

Then another.

It was not their own.

It did not belong to prey.

It did not resemble the pulse of any witch, wolf, mortal, or vampire they had ever hunted.

A young vampire fell from his knees and clutched his chest.

“What is that?”

The elder beside him listened.

He had lived long enough to remember civilizations whose names no longer existed, yet no memory answered him.

The heartbeat passed through their blood one final time.

Then disappeared.

Across the world, vampires remained awake.

Listening.

Afraid.

Within Castle Darkheart, Aurelia screamed.

The Crimson Mana surrounding her burst outward.

Physicians were thrown against the walls. Witches collapsed to their knees. Victor drove his sword into the floor and used it to remain standing as the chamber filled with red light.

The pressure became unbearable.

The witches’ magic had not vanished.

It remained buried beneath the overwhelming presence entering the world.

Aurelia’s final cry ended abruptly.

Then came silence.

The infant was born.

The midwife caught him with shaking hands and nearly dropped him when his eyes opened.

They were crimson.

Not bloodshot.

Not reflecting the light.

Crimson from edge to edge.

Small fangs rested behind his lips. His tiny fingers opened and closed while Crimson Mana leaked naturally from his body in slow, living ribbons. Beneath his newborn skin, his heartbeat carried a predatory rhythm no human child should possess. A low sound rumbled in his chest—not quite a growl, but enough to make the nearest wolf-blooded guard outside the chamber recoil.

The child did not cry.

He looked at the world.

The Blood Rain stopped in midair.

For one suspended moment, every crimson drop hung between the sky and earth.

The wolves froze.

The vampires felt the impossible heartbeat settle.

The pressure inside the chamber eased.

The midwife placed the newborn against Aurelia’s chest.

Aurelia stared at him through tears.

“My son.”

The infant turned toward her voice.

Her hand trembled as she touched his cheek.

“Zee.”

The name left her softly.

“Zee Darkheart.”

Crimson Mana curled around Aurelia’s wrist but did not harm her. It felt warm against her skin, almost curious, before returning to the child.

Victor released his sword.

He stared at his son.

The fangs.

The crimson eyes.

The strange mana.

The low, instinctive sound within the child’s breathing.

Every sign should have driven him away.

Instead, Victor stepped forward.

Zee turned his head toward him.

The king’s expression changed.

For the first time that night, he was not looking at an omen.

He was looking at his child.

His heir.

Victor reached down and offered one finger.

Zee’s tiny hand closed around it.

The strength in the newborn’s grip surprised him.

A faint smile touched Victor’s face.

Then the air split.

Far beyond House Darkheart, inside a mountain kingdom built around rivers of molten stone, a crimson dragon egg cracked open.

Dragon attendants gathered around it.

The egg belonged to the royal clutch, guarded since the first sign of life appeared beneath its shell. Teal-and-gold fire burned within the ceremonial braziers while the Dragon King and Queen watched from the obsidian platform above.

The shell broke.

A newborn crimson hatchling pushed free.

His scales gleamed dark red beneath the cavern light. Small wings unfolded against his wet body. Teal-and-gold mana moved over him in intertwined currents, distinct colors flowing together without becoming one.

The Dragon Queen stepped forward.

The hatchling lifted his head.

Then vanished.

There was no spell.

No portal.

No burst of flame.

One moment, he stood among the fragments of his shell.

The next, the royal nest was empty.

The Dragon Queen’s roar shook the mountain.

At Castle Darkheart, the crimson hatchling appeared upon Aurelia’s bed.

The royal guards drew their weapons.

Witches raised hands, their magic still difficult to reach beneath the lingering pressure.

The hatchling ignored them.

His unsteady legs carried him across the blanket toward Zee.

Victor moved between the creature and his family.

“Stay back.”

The hatchling stopped.

Teal-and-gold mana shimmered faintly around his scales.

He did not attack.

He looked past Victor toward the newborn prince.

Zee stirred.

A simple feeling passed between the two infants.

Recognition.

Not knowledge.

Not memory.

Only the instinctive certainty that neither was alone.

The hatchling continued forward.

Victor tightened his grip on his sword but did not strike.

The tiny dragon reached Zee, circled once, and curled against the child’s side. Zee’s hand settled against the hatchling’s neck.

The tension inside both newborns eased.

Safe.

Aurelia looked from one child to the other.

“What is he?”

The eldest witch had recovered enough to stand.

She studied the hatchling’s crimson scales and strange mixed mana.

“I do not know.”

“Where did he come from?”

“I do not know that either.”

No one inside Castle Darkheart recognized him.

No one knew that a kingdom beyond the mountains had lost its newborn crown prince at the exact moment Zee entered the world.

The suspended blood resumed falling.

The pressure around Zee weakened until the royal witches could finally touch their power again. Violet light returned to the eldest witch’s hands. Another restored the ward around the chamber. A third began healing Aurelia’s injuries.

The younger witch stared at her own palms.

“It was never gone.”

The eldest looked toward Zee.

“No.”

“Then why could we not reach it?”

The elder had lived for more than a century.

She had no answer.

Before she could offer even a theory, the chamber doors opened.

A scout entered drenched in blood.

He dropped to one knee, chest heaving from the force of his run.

“My King.”

Victor turned.

“Report.”

“Messages have begun arriving from every border. The blood fell beyond our lands. The wolves have attacked settlements throughout the north. Foreign courts are demanding answers.”

“We have none.”

“They do not believe that.”

Victor’s face hardened.

The scout looked toward Zee.

Rumor had already outrun the truth.

Servants had seen the crimson light.

Guards had heard the newborn’s strange heartbeat.

Physicians had witnessed fangs in the mouth of a royal child born to an ancient Witch House. Beyond the walls, wolf-blooded soldiers claimed they felt something awaken inside them when Zee took his first breath.

The scout lowered his eyes.

“Several kingdoms are calling the child unnatural.”

Aurelia tightened her hold around Zee.

Victor stepped between the scout and the bed.

“He is the heir of House Darkheart.”

“My King, they are already sending riders.”

“For what purpose?”

“To learn what was born here.”

Victor looked toward the blood-streaked windows.

Across the ancient world, rulers were gathering witnesses. Witches argued over the moment their magic became unreachable. Vampires searched their memories for the source of the heartbeat. Hunters entered forests filled with maddened wolves and found entire packs moving toward the same distant kingdom.

No one understood Zee.

That did not prevent them from fearing him.

By dawn, the first royal messenger would leave a neighboring capital carrying a demand for the newborn’s death.

By sunrise, eleven more would follow.

The impossible had been born.

And the world had already begun to move against him.

# Chapter Two

## The King’s Fear

Castle Darkheart did not sleep.

The Blood Rain ended before dawn, but crimson water continued to run from the roofs and battlements. It gathered in the mouths of stone beasts, flowed through the courtyards, and spilled down the mountain in narrow red streams. Servants scrubbed the floors without making them clean. Priests burned incense in every hall. Soldiers stood along the walls with bows strung and swords loosened in their sheaths.

No enemy had reached the kingdom.

Fear had entered first.

Inside the royal chamber, the physicians completed their work around Queen Aurelia while the witches tested their recovered magic.

Violet light moved across torn flesh and eased the queen’s pain. Blue sigils appeared above bowls of water, purifying the blood from their surfaces. Pale green wards settled across the doors and windows.

Every spell answered normally.

That frightened the witches almost as much as their earlier helplessness.

The eldest royal witch stood near the window, watching the last traces of blood drip from the glass.

“My power was inside me the entire time,” she said.

The younger witch beside her nodded. “I could feel it. I simply could not make it answer.”

“Nor could I.”

“Was it the child?”

The elder looked toward Zee.

He slept against Aurelia’s chest. The crimson hatchling remained pressed along his side, its tail curled protectively around the blanket. Their breathing had fallen into the same slow rhythm.

“I do not know.”

“You felt the pressure.”

“I felt many things tonight. Certainty was not among them.”

The younger witch lowered her voice. “He has the blood hunger.”

The elder’s eyes narrowed.

“You have no proof of hunger.”

“He has fangs.”

“So do creatures that have never tasted blood.”

“And the sound inside him?”

The elder glanced toward the door, ensuring Victor remained too distant to hear.

“The royal wolf guard heard it.”

“He said the prince carried the scent of wolf blood.”

“A frightened man said many things.”

“Do you believe he was wrong?”

The elder did not answer.

House Darkheart had ruled as an ancient Witch Kingdom for generations. Its royal line was known for powerful witches, long-lived blood, and rulers whose magic had broken enemy armies.

No Darkheart child had ever been born with vampire fangs.

No newborn prince had ever carried the scent of a wolf.

No witch had ever produced mana like the crimson force surrounding Zee.

The younger woman whispered, “Three natures.”

“Do not name what you do not understand.”

“Witch. Vampire. Wolf.”

The elder’s gaze sharpened.

“Enough.”

But the words had already entered the room.

Three natures.

A trinity of blood no kingdom had ever witnessed.

A First Tribrid.

The name would not remain inside Castle Darkheart for long.

Near the bed, Victor watched Zee sleep.

He had dismissed most of the attendants and refused every request to remove the dragon hatchling. Twice, guards offered to place the creature inside an iron cage. Twice, Zee’s Crimson Mana surged before any hand reached it.

Victor had ordered them to stop trying.

He told himself the command protected Aurelia from another disturbance.

The truth was more difficult.

The hatchling had not threatened Zee.

It had calmed him.

Each time the child stirred, the dragon moved closer. Each time the hatchling made a weak sound of hunger or discomfort, Zee’s tiny fingers found its scales.

Victor understood nothing about the connection.

He could still see the way Zee had held his finger.

His son’s grip had been too strong for a newborn, yet the memory did not frighten him as much as it should have.

Not yet.

Aurelia opened her eyes.

“You are staring.”

Victor looked at her. “You should sleep.”

“So should you.”

“I have a kingdom to command.”

“You have a son.”

The words stopped him.

Aurelia shifted Zee carefully into her arms and held him toward Victor.

“Take him.”

Victor did not move.

The crimson hatchling lifted its head.

“It watches me,” Victor said.

“It watches everyone.”

“It does not watch you that way.”

“Perhaps it has good judgment.”

Despite the night’s horror, Victor almost smiled.

Aurelia extended Zee farther.

“Hold your son.”

Victor sheathed his sword and approached.

He slid one hand beneath Zee’s head and the other beneath his body. The child felt impossibly small against him.

Zee opened his crimson eyes.

Victor’s breath caught.

No infant should have looked so still.

So aware.

Yet there was no ancient intelligence inside the child’s gaze. No hidden message. Zee was only a newborn trying to understand warmth, sound, hunger, and the unfamiliar shape of the world around him.

His tiny fangs showed when his mouth opened.

Victor waited for a cry.

None came.

Instead, Zee settled against his chest.

Crimson Mana touched Victor’s hands.

It did not burn.

The king looked down at the heir he had waited years to meet.

“My son,” he said quietly.

Aurelia watched him.

For that moment, the blood outside did not matter.

The foreign riders did not matter.

The maddened wolves, waking vampires, and frightened witches seemed far beyond the chamber.

Victor held his child.

Then the first war horn sounded.

It came from the eastern tower.

A second answered from the southern wall.

The hatchling sprang upright, releasing a sharp cry as teal-and-gold mana flickered across its scales. Zee startled in Victor’s arms. A pulse of Crimson Mana struck the room, rattling every window.

Victor handed the child back to Aurelia and reached for his sword.

The chamber doors opened.

Captain Edric Vale, commander of the Darkheart Guard, entered with blood still staining the lower edge of his cloak.

“My King.”

“What has reached us?”

“Messengers. Not soldiers.”

“Then why sound the war horns?”

“Because there are twelve of them.”

Victor’s expression hardened.

“From whom?”

“Twelve crowns.”

Silence followed.

Aurelia held Zee closer.

Captain Vale continued. “They arrived separately, but each carries the same demand.”

Victor stepped toward him.

“Speak it.”

The captain hesitated.

“They want the child surrendered before nightfall.”

The crimson hatchling growled.

It was a weak, newborn sound, but the intention behind it was unmistakable.

Victor’s face darkened.

“On whose authority?”

“Theirs.”

“They believe twelve seals make them rulers of my house?”

“No, Your Majesty.”

“What do they threaten?”

“War.”

Aurelia looked toward Victor. “They would invade over a child born less than a night ago?”

“They are not invading over a child,” Victor said.

The words left him more harshly than he intended.

“They are invading because they believe fear gives them the right.”

He turned to Captain Vale.

“Send the messengers to the great hall. Feed them. Do not harm them.”

“And our answer?”

Victor looked back at Zee.

His child rested beneath Aurelia’s hand while the crimson hatchling remained beside him, watching the armed men.

“No foreign king decides what happens to the heir of House Darkheart.”

Captain Vale struck his fist to his chest.

“Yes, Your Majesty.”

When he departed, Aurelia’s shoulders eased.

“You will defend him.”

Victor looked toward the windows.

“I will defend this kingdom.”

The difference escaped her.

It did not escape him.

By midday, the twelve messengers stood beneath the vaulted ceiling of the great hall.

Each wore the colors of a different kingdom.

Some came from nations that had fought House Darkheart for generations. Others represented crowns bound to Victor through trade, marriage, or uneasy peace. Two served kings who had been at war with one another less than a week earlier.

Fear had made allies where diplomacy failed.

Victor sat upon the black throne.

The iron crown of House Darkheart rested upon his head. Generals and court witches stood along the walls. Captain Vale remained at the foot of the dais.

The first messenger stepped forward.

“My sovereign offers peace if the unnatural child is surrendered.”

Victor’s hand tightened around the throne.

The second spoke. “Our northern villages were destroyed by wolves at the exact hour of his birth.”

A third added, “Every witch in our capital became helpless.”

“Temporarily,” one of the Darkheart witches said. “Their magic was never gone.”

The messenger ignored her.

“A heartbeat entered the blood of every vampire beneath our mountains.”

Another voice rose from the line. “A child with witch mana, vampire fangs, and the scent of a wolf cannot be permitted to live.”

“I refuse to surrender my son to frightened rulers who have not seen him.”

“They have seen the sky.”

“So have I.”

“So will I.”

Aurelia’s voice came from the entrance.

“No.”

Everyone turned.

Aurelia stopped before the gathered envoys.

“You crossed our borders and entered my home to demand the murder of my newborn son.”

The first messenger lowered his head, though not in apology.

“My queen, we demand survival.”

“You demand obedience.”

The hatchling pressed against Zee, its teal-and-gold mana barely visible beneath its crimson scales.

One messenger stared at them.

“There are reports from the Dragon Kingdom.”

Victor looked toward him.

“What reports?”

“A royal egg hatched during the Blood Rain. The hatchling vanished from a sealed mountain chamber.”

Every eye shifted toward the small dragon beside Zee.

The creature buried its head against the infant.

The messenger whispered, “That may be what was taken.”

“No one here took him,” Aurelia said.

“Yet he came to the child.”

Another murmur moved through the hall.

Fear gained shape with every unanswered question.

Victor raised one hand.

“You have my answer. Leave Castle Darkheart before sunset.”

The first messenger did not move.

“Our armies are already gathering.”

“Then gather them farther from my walls.”

“If we return without the child, they will march.”

Victor’s voice lowered.

“Then they will die.”

The messengers were escorted from the hall.

Aurelia remained beside the throne after the doors closed.

“You meant it.”

Victor looked at the empty space where the envoys had stood.

“They threatened House Darkheart.”

“They threatened Zee.”

“They threatened both.”

She studied him.

“Does that distinction matter?”

Victor turned toward his son.

Zee’s crimson eyes were open again. The child reached toward him.

Victor did not take his hand this time.

Before Aurelia could question him, an old servant entered through a side door carrying a narrow wooden box.

He was blind in one eye and walked with the aid of an iron staff. Victor recognized him as the keeper of the royal burial vaults, a man who had served Victor’s father before Victor wore the crown.

The servant knelt.

“Forgive me, Your Majesty.”

“What is it?”

“Something opened beneath the castle.”

Victor’s attention sharpened.

“What opened?”

“A sealed chamber beneath the oldest crypt.”

“By whose command?”

The servant raised the wooden box.

“This was inside.”

She heard the command in his voice.

For the first time since Zee’s birth, she saw something colder beneath Victor’s expression.

Not hatred.

Not yet.

Fear searching for an answer.

“You will tell me what is inside that box.”

“When I know.”

Aurelia finally turned away.

Victor watched her leave with their son.

The great hall doors closed.

“Open it,” he ordered.

The burial keeper placed the box upon the stone floor.

The old man cut through the strip of skin.

The knot loosened by itself.

A smell of earth, ash, and old blood entered the hall.

Inside the box rested no ancient book.

No record of a previous Tribrid.

No explanation of the child.

Blood falling from the heavens.

Wolves losing themselves.

Three lives inside one body.

Every blade making him harder to destroy.

The king who had threatened twelve kingdoms only moments earlier was gone.

In his place stood a father who had been handed a reason to fear his own child.

“Leave us,” he said.

The burial keeper bowed and retreated.

Captain Vale remained.

“My King—”

“Leave.”

The captain obeyed.

Victor stood alone in the great hall.

Outside, ravens carried reports across the ancient world.

Twelve kingdoms called their banners.

Wolves still wandered without reason through blood-soaked forests.

Vampires hunted for the source of the heartbeat that had entered their blood.

Witches whispered about the newborn whose presence had buried their magic beneath impossible pressure.

Inside the royal nursery, Aurelia laid Zee in his cradle.

The crimson hatchling curled beside him.

Zee reached through the simple bond between them.

Unease.

The hatchling lifted his head and stared toward the distant throne room.

Victor remained there until the final light disappeared from the windows.

When he eventually returned to the nursery, Aurelia looked up with relief.

“You found your answer?”

Victor stood in the doorway.

His eyes settled upon Zee.

The child smiled at the sight of him.

Victor remembered holding him.

He remembered the tiny hand around his finger.

Then the prophecy whispered again inside his mind.

*Every blade raised against him shall sharpen what it seeks to destroy.*

Victor did not approach the cradle.

“No,” he said.

Aurelia frowned. “No?”

“I found something worse.”

That night, the armies began marching toward House Darkheart.

And for the first time since Zee’s birth, his father looked at him and felt afraid to love him.
