The scent led beneath the palace.

Ner’s mother had handled the silver tray for hours.

Her smell remained distinct beneath bread, soap, cooking oil, and the hundreds of palace scents clinging to the corridor.

Zee followed it to an unused storage chamber.

Then stopped beside the rear wall.

Vale watched him.

“There?”

Zee nodded.

Caldrin pressed against the stone.

Nothing.

Lucien summoned dark blue mana.

The wall revealed old inscriptions beneath the plaster.

“A sealed doorway.”

The royal witch frowned.

“This has not been opened in decades.”

Zee sniffed again.

“Today.”

Vale looked toward Lucien.

The king’s expression hardened.

“Open it.”

Magic struck the seal.

Stone shifted.

Cold air escaped.

A staircase descended beneath Vesper.

Lucien immediately turned.

“Zee stays.”

Zee opened his mouth.

“No.”

“But—”

“No.”

Zee looked toward Aurelia.

She pointed toward the corridor.

“Upstairs.”

He scowled.

Zareth growled.

“You too.”

Zareth looked offended.

Lucien almost smiled.

Then Ner spoke from behind them.

“I am going.”

Everyone turned.

His Golden Mana shimmered around his hands.

Aurelia approached.

“No.”

“That is my mother.”

“I know.”

“You said Zee could help because he can smell.”

“Yes.”

“I can feel her.”

Silence.

The royal witch stared.

“What?”

Ner looked toward the stairs.

“My magic.”

Pure gold gathered around his fingers.

A thin thread stretched toward the darkness.

Not physically.

More like light responding to something unseen.

“I feel her.”

Aurelia looked toward Ner.

Then Zee.

Then Lucien.

Lucien spoke first.

“He comes with us.”

Aurelia stared.

“You just told Zee no.”

“Because Zee does not possess whatever this is.”

Ner’s expression tightened.

“I am not staying.”

Aurelia hated the decision.

That did not make it wrong.

She looked toward Zee.

“You remain with Rez.”

Zee looked furious.

Rez stepped forward.

“I am coming too.”

Lucien pointed toward the ceiling.

“No.”

Rez blinked.

“You are taking Ner.”

“Ner can locate the prisoner.”

“I can protect Ner.”

“I can protect Ner.”

Rez’s Blue-White Mana flared.

“Can you protect him and fight whoever took everyone?”

Lucien went silent.

Rez had learned too much from watching adults use logic against one another.

Caldrin rubbed his forehead.

“The children are unionizing.”

Vale almost laughed.

Aurelia did not.

In the end, the group descended with Ner and Rez.

Zee stayed behind.

For seven minutes.

Then Zareth opened an old ventilation passage.

Zee smiled.

“You knew?”

The dragon sent an image.

Found before.

Of course he had.

Zee climbed inside.

Zareth followed.

---

Below Vesper, the architecture changed.

The stone became darker.

Older.

No Vesper sigils.

No palace wards.

The tunnel predated the kingdom above it.

Ner led through Golden Mana.

The light responded more strongly the deeper they traveled.

His face grew pale.

Rez remained beside him.

“You can stop.”

“No.”

“You look sick.”

“I am fine.”

“You are lying.”

“So?”

Rez looked surprised.

Ner continued walking.

Vale saw something ahead.

“Bodies.”

Everyone stopped.

Not dead.

Four missing citizens lay unconscious against the wall.

The baker’s apprentice.

Stable boy.

Laundress.

Another man.

Lucien crouched beside them.

“Alive.”

The royal witch examined one.

“Drained.”

“Blood?”

“No.”

“Mana?”

She hesitated.

“Something like it.”

Ner’s Golden Mana brightened.

“Mother.”

He ran.

Aurelia grabbed for him and missed.

“Ner!”

Rez followed.

The tunnel opened into an underground chamber.

Ner’s mother hung suspended inside a circle of black stones.

Alive.

Her eyes opened.

“Nereus?”

Ner stopped.

“Mother!”

A figure stepped between them.

Not a witch.

Not a vampire.

Not human.

Tall.

Thin.

Skin the color of old ash.

Two curved horns emerged behind its temples.

Caldrin drew his blades.

“Demon.”

The creature smiled.

“Eventually someone recognizes quality.”

Lucien’s mana gathered.

“Release her.”

The demon looked toward Ner.

Then his Golden Mana.

“No.”

Its smile widened.

“I waited for that.”

Aurelia’s eyes narrowed.

“You took random people to lure him.”

“Not random.”

The demon gestured toward the unconscious captives.

“Different magical signatures.”

“I was searching.”

“For what?”

The creature looked directly at Ner.

“Gold.”

Ner froze.

The demon continued.

“Pure.”

“Unmixed.”

“Bright enough to reach places ordinary witchcraft cannot.”

Aurelia stepped forward.

“How did you know it existed?”

“I did not.”

The answer surprised everyone.

“I heard rumors.”

“Golden hands beside the Tribrid.”

“Most rumors are worthless.”

“This one was not.”

Good.

Another independent enemy.

Another motive.

The demon did not care about Zee.

Not directly.

It wanted Ner.

That made the danger worse.

“Let my mother go,” Ner said.

The demon looked at him.

“Come closer.”

Rez immediately stepped in front of Ner.

“No.”

The demon smiled.

“Prince Vesper.”

Rez raised both hands.

Blue-White Mana gathered.

“Move.”

The demon laughed.

“Children with titles.”

“Always so brave when adults stand nearby.”

Rez cast.

Blue-White force struck the demon.

The creature disappeared.

Not moved.

Disappeared.

Then reappeared behind Ner.

Aurelia turned.

Too slow.

The demon grabbed him.

Golden Mana erupted.

The creature screamed.

Ner fell.

Rez attacked again.

The royal witch cast violet bindings.

Lucien sealed the exits.

Caldrin and Vale moved from opposite sides.

The demon became smoke.

Every attack passed through.

Then it reformed above them.

“Gold indeed.”

Ner’s mother screamed.

“RUN!”

The black stones around her ignited.

Ner looked toward her.

His fear became rage.

Golden Mana flooded the chamber.

Pure light filled every crack in the ancient stone.

The demon stopped smiling.

Ner raised both hands.

“I said let her go.”

The gold struck the prison circle.

The black stones cracked.

His mother fell.

Aurelia caught her.

The demon stared.

Not at Zee.

Not at prophecy.

At Ner.

Hungry.

“You could open things.”

Ner’s face hardened.

“I opened that.”

He pointed toward the broken circle.

Rez grinned.

“That was actually good.”

The demon lunged.

Something red struck from the ceiling.

Zareth crashed into it.

The creature slammed against the wall.

Everyone stared.

Aurelia’s expression became murderous.

“No.”

Zee dropped from the ventilation shaft.

He landed badly.

Rolled.

Stood.

And smiled.

“Found you.”

Aurelia looked ready to personally invent mortality.

“ZEE DARKHEART.”

He stopped smiling.

The demon looked toward him.

Recognition entered its face.

“So.”

Zee’s expression changed.

“You took Ner’s mother.”

“Yes.”

Wrong answer.

Crimson Mana thickened.

The demon’s eyes widened slightly.

Not because it knew Zee’s limits.

Because instincts worked both ways.

Predator recognized predator.

The demon became smoke.

Zee heard no heartbeat.

Smelled no blood.

Could not track it like a vampire or wolf.

New danger.

Different rules.

The smoke moved toward Ner.

Zee reacted with witch instinct.

His hand lifted.

Crimson Mana spread through the room.

Not binding the demon.

Binding the space.

The smoke slowed.

Lucien saw it.

“Now!”

Blue-White Mana from Rez struck first.

Golden Mana from Ner followed.

Lucien’s dark blue spell closed from behind.

The royal witch sealed the floor.

The demon was forced back into physical form.

Vale struck its leg.

Caldrin cut across its shoulder.

Black blood hit stone.

Zee smelled it.

His vampire instincts surged.

The demon saw that hunger.

Its smile returned despite the wound.

“There you are.”

Zee stared.

The demon rushed him.

Aurelia shouted.

Zee did not move.

The creature struck.

Claws tore across Zee’s chest.

Pain exploded.

His body hit the floor.

But death did not come.

Could not.

The wound began healing before the demon could pull its hand away.

Its expression changed.

Not understanding.

Shock.

Zee grabbed the demon’s wrist.

Crimson Mana entered the wound between them.

The demon screamed.

Its black blood moved.

Zee’s fangs extended.

Aurelia realized what was happening.

“Zee!”

Too late.

He bit.

Demon blood entered him.

The effect was violent.

His body arched.

Crimson Mana darkened around the edges.

Heat flooded his veins.

The demon ripped free and staggered backward.

Zee released it.

He did not copy the creature.

Something inside him rejected most of what entered.

The corruption.

The smoke.

The foreign hunger.

But one property remained.

The ability to sense presence where blood and heartbeat failed.

Not smell.

Not hearing.

Something beneath both.

The demon turned to smoke again.

Zee looked directly at it.

For the first time.

He could feel where it was.

The smoke stopped.

Zee pointed.

“There.”

Rez attacked.

Ner attacked.

Lucien sealed.

The demon was forced back into flesh.

Vale’s sword met it.

Caldrin’s followed.

The creature collapsed.

Still alive.

Barely.

Lucien stood over it.

“Who sent you?”

The demon laughed weakly.

“No one.”

Aurelia looked toward it.

“Why come?”

“Gold.”

Its eyes found Ner.

“Power like his opens old things.”

“What things?”

The demon smiled.

“Ask him when he is older.”

Lucien’s expression hardened.

The demon closed its eyes.

Not dead.

Unconscious.

Vale bound it.

Aurelia immediately crossed the room.

Zee knew that walk.

He backed away.

“Mother—”

“Do not.”

“I helped.”

“You disobeyed.”

“I helped first.”

“Zee.”

Zareth retreated.

Coward.

Zee glared at him.

The Dragon Link carried amusement.

Aurelia grabbed Zee and checked the wound across his chest.

Already closing.

Her anger broke slightly.

Pain remained.

He had still been hurt.

She held him tightly.

Then pulled back.

“You never do that again.”

Zee frowned.

“What?”

“Follow us into an unknown underground chamber.”

“What if someone takes Ner again?”

Ner looked toward him.

Aurelia closed her eyes.

There it was.

The problem no rule could solve.

Zee was becoming protective.

Not because anyone taught him.

Because the world had.

Every time it threatened someone he loved, it carved that instinct deeper.

Aurelia touched his cheek.

“We find another way.”

Zee looked toward Ner’s mother.

Alive.

Ner held onto her.

Rez stood beside them.

Zareth pressed against Zee.

Another way.

Maybe.

But Zee had already learned his own lesson.

When the world took someone he loved...

He followed.

---

By sunrise, the missing citizens were safe.

The demon remained imprisoned beneath layers of Vesper wards.

Ner’s mother survived.

The underground tunnels were sealed.

The palace celebrated quietly.

No feast.

Too many questions remained.

But Ner sat beside his mother’s bed holding her hand.

Zee sat on the floor nearby.

Rez leaned against the wall.

Zareth blocked the doorway.

Ner looked toward Zee.

“You came.”

Zee shrugged.

“I said I would.”

“You were told not to.”

“Yes.”

Rez nodded approvingly.

Ner smiled.

Then his Golden Mana appeared faintly around their joined hands.

Zee watched.

“Does it hurt?”

“No.”

“Do you know what it does?”

“No.”

Zee nodded.

“Me neither.”

Rez looked between them.

“That may be the wisest thing either of you has said.”

Zee threw a pillow.

Rez caught it.

Ner laughed.

His mother opened tired eyes.

“Quiet.”

All three boys froze.

Zareth did not.

He climbed onto the end of the bed.

She stared at the dragon.

“Not you too.”

Zareth curled up.

No one had the strength to move him.

Outside, Vesper woke.

And beneath the kingdom, something important had changed.

The demon had not come because of Zee.

It had come because of Ner.

For the first time, Zee confronted an enemy whose story did not begin with the First Tribrid.

The world was larger than his hunt.

His friends would have enemies of their own.

Their powers would create dangers of their own.

Their lives would not exist merely as extensions of his.

Zee did not understand that yet.

But he would.

And when he did, he would face one of the hardest truths of his childhood:

Loving people did not only give his enemies weapons.

Sometimes the people Zee loved carried wars that belonged entirely to them.

# Chapter Twenty-Four

## The Hunted Prince

Seven Years Later

Zee Darkheart was halfway up the eastern tower of House Vesper when someone tried to shoot him out of the sky.

He heard the bowstring before the arrow left it.

The sound reached him through wind, rain, bells, soldiers shouting from the courtyard below, and the violent beating of wings directly above his head.

Zee twisted.

The arrow passed close enough to cut several strands of black hair from beside one developing horn.

“Rude.”

A second arrow came.

This one never reached him.

Zareth dropped from the clouds like a crimson blade.

His enormous wing swept between Zee and the distant rooftop, knocking the projectile aside before it struck. Teal-and-gold Dragon Mana flashed across crimson scales as the ten-year-old Crown Prince of Drakonis released an angry roar that shook windows throughout the upper palace.

Zee winced.

“I heard it too.”

Zareth’s response entered the Dragon Link immediately.

**Arrow. You. Again.**

The meaning arrived without true words—anger wrapped around an image of Zee falling from the tower.

Zee rolled his crimson eyes.

“I was not going to fall.”

The Link answered with another image.

Zee.

Falling.

Headfirst.

Three summers earlier.

Into King Lucien’s ornamental pond.

Zee’s expression darkened.

“That was different.”

Zareth sent amusement.

Zee jumped from the tower.

Someone screamed below.

Zareth screamed louder.

For several heartbeats Zee dropped freely through open air, black coat snapping behind him. The small crimson-black horns growing from his temples cut through his windblown hair, and patches of permanent crimson scales along the sides of his neck caught the gray morning light.

He had no wings.

Not yet.

That did not stop him from doing stupid things involving heights.

Crimson Mana gathered beneath his boots.

The air compressed.

Zee hit the roof below, rolled once, and came upright in a crouch.

The assassin was already running.

“Got you.”

The figure glanced over one shoulder.

Black hood.

Leather armor.

Human heartbeat.

No spellwork Zee could sense.

Not every person hunting him was supernatural.

Sometimes ordinary people were simply greedy.

Zee ran.

At ten years old, his body remained small compared with the soldiers training throughout Vesper’s courtyards, but nothing about the way he moved resembled an ordinary child. His vampire nature sharpened the world around him. His wolf instincts read every shift in the assassin’s balance. Crimson Mana moved beneath his skin without waiting for conscious command.

And something hotter lived underneath all three.

Something newer.

Dragon.

Zee felt it whenever Zareth came close.

Whenever anger rose.

Whenever the strange scales along his shoulders expanded farther toward his arms.

He did not understand it.

He hated not understanding things about himself.

The assassin vaulted a stone railing.

Zee followed.

Below them, merchants crossing the lower palace square scattered as both figures landed among overturned baskets and startled horses.

“Move!” the assassin shouted.

A fruit seller threw an apple at him.

Zee almost laughed.

The assassin reached the alley.

Zee accelerated.

Too fast.

His shoulder struck the man’s back.

Both crashed through stacked wooden crates.

The assassin rolled first and drew a short blade.

Zee stood.

Blood ran from a shallow cut across his cheek.

The wound had already begun closing.

The man saw it.

Fear entered his heartbeat.

Zee heard that too.

“You should have stayed on the roof.”

The assassin backed away.

“You really are the monster they say.”

Zee’s smile vanished.

That word still worked.

Monster.

Abomination.

Curse.

Different kingdoms preferred different names.

None bothered him as much as *monster.*

Because Victor used that one.

Zee’s crimson eyes narrowed.

“Who paid you?”

The man attacked.

Zee moved before the blade reached him.

One hand caught the assassin’s wrist.

Too strong.

The man gasped.

Zee twisted.

Steel hit stone.

The assassin threw a fist.

Zee ducked and drove his shoulder into the man’s stomach.

The impact sent him backward.

Crimson scales spread farther across Zee’s forearm.

The assassin stared.

“What in the hell are you?”

Zee looked down.

More scales.

They always appeared when he became angry.

He hated that too.

“I asked first.”

The assassin reached for something beneath his coat.

Zee smelled metal.

Poison.

He reacted.

Crimson Mana struck the man’s chest and pinned him against the wall.

Not enough to crush.

Enough to stop movement.

The assassin strained.

Zee walked closer.

His juvenile horns glimmered dark crimson near their bases, fading almost black toward their tips.

“Who paid you?”

The man laughed nervously.

“You think there is only one bounty anymore?”

Zee’s face hardened.

Wrong answer.

Zareth landed behind him.

The alley shook.

The assassin looked up.

Then farther up.

Zareth had become terrifying over seven years.

Still young by Dragon standards, but already massive beside human children. Crimson scales covered his body from horn to tail, and teal-and-gold Dragon Mana moved beneath them like living fire.

The Dragon Link carried one simple intention.

**Bite?**

Zee almost smiled.

“No.”

Disappointment.

The assassin stared between them.

“You speak to it?”

Zee’s expression changed instantly.

“Him.”

The man swallowed.

Zareth lowered his head.

The assassin went pale.

Zee leaned closer.

“That is Crown Prince Zareth Drakonis.”

The man’s heartbeat accelerated.

“And if you call him *it* again, I might let him bite you.”

Zareth sent delight through the Link.

Zee ignored him.

The assassin looked toward the alley entrance.

Soldiers were coming.

Too late.

He smiled.

“Doesn’t matter.”

Zee frowned.

“What?”

“The arrow was not for you.”

The world stopped.

Zee’s eyes sharpened.

“Who?”

The assassin grinned.

Then bit down.

Zee heard the capsule crack between his teeth.

“No!”

He grabbed the man’s jaw.

Too late.

The assassin collapsed.

Not dead.

His breathing continued.

Sleeping poison.

Zee stared.

A distraction.

The arrows.

The chase.

The whole attack.

Zareth felt Zee’s realization through the Link.

**Ner.**

Zee turned.

They ran.

---

Nereus Azrion hated royal ceremonies.

He hated court robes.

He hated formal introductions.

He especially hated being called Nereus by people who had known him since he was three.

“Stand straight,” the palace steward whispered.

Ner remained exactly as he was.

The steward closed his eyes.

“Nereus.”

“Only my mother gets that tone.”

“You are addressing foreign delegates.”

“They know my name.”

“That is not the point.”

Ner looked across the Vesper receiving hall.

Delegates from three southern witch kingdoms stood beneath banners embroidered with old magical symbols. They had not traveled to see Zee.

For once.

They had come for him.

Pure Golden Mana had become harder to hide as Ner matured. At ten, he could summon it deliberately now, shape barriers with it, and open magical seals ordinary witchcraft could barely touch.

That had created opportunities.

And enemies.

Mostly enemies.

Rez stood beside him wearing Vesper blue and silver.

At seventeen, the prince had become tall enough that Ner hated looking up at him during arguments.

Blue-White Mana moved faintly along Rez’s wrist.

“You look miserable.”

Ner whispered, “I am.”

“Good.”

“Why?”

“Character building.”

Ner glared.

Rez smiled.

Seven years had turned him into exactly what Zee once accused him of becoming.

An older brother.

Annoying.

Protective.

Always present when trouble appeared.

And frequently responsible for the trouble.

A southern witch stepped forward.

Her hair had been braided with small copper charms.

“Nereus Azrion.”

Ner sighed internally.

“Yes?”

“We appreciate House Vesper permitting this meeting.”

Rez answered before Ner could.

“House Vesper permitted nothing.”

The witch looked toward him.

Rez smiled pleasantly.

“Nereus agreed to meet you.”

The distinction mattered.

Ner glanced toward him.

Rez gave the smallest nod.

Your choice.

Ner relaxed.

The witch noticed.

Good.

She changed approach.

“We have studied rare mana expressions throughout our kingdom for generations.”

Ner’s golden eyes narrowed slightly.

“I do not want to be studied.”

“We mean no harm.”

“That sentence usually comes before harm.”

Rez coughed.

The witch frowned.

Ner continued.

“What do you want?”

“To teach you.”

That surprised him.

“My Golden Mana?”

“Yes.”

“You have Golden Mana?”

“No.”

“Then how?”

The woman hesitated.

Ner smiled.

“That is what I thought.”

A second witch stepped forward.

“We know structures that may help you understand your gift.”

“That is different.”

“Yes.”

Ner considered.

He was interested.

That was dangerous.

His mother had taught him curiosity was not the same as trust.

He had learned the lesson beneath Vesper years earlier when a demon had hunted him for exactly what lived inside his hands.

“What would you want in return?”

The witches exchanged looks.

There.

Rez saw it too.

The first woman spoke carefully.

“Access.”

“To what?”

“Your mana.”

Ner’s face hardened.

“No.”

“For observation only.”

“No.”

“Nereus—”

“Ner.”

The room changed.

Only one person regularly called him that.

The southern witch did not understand.

Rez did.

He smiled faintly.

“Nereus is his name.”

The witch frowned.

Ner looked toward her.

“But Ner belongs to Zee.”

The woman clearly did not understand that either.

She would eventually.

A servant entered.

Fast.

Too fast.

Rez noticed.

His hand moved toward his sword.

The servant bowed.

“My Prince.”

“What happened?”

“There has been an attack near the eastern tower.”

Ner stood.

“Zee?”

“Alive.”

Neither boy relaxed.

“Zareth?”

“Alive.”

Rez’s jaw tightened.

“Then why are you running?”

The servant looked toward Ner.

“The palace wards around the southern wing just failed.”

Golden Mana erupted around Ner’s hands.

The foreign witches stepped backward.

Rez drew his sword.

Then every door slammed shut.

The copper charms woven into the visiting witch’s hair ignited.

She looked horrified.

“That is not ours.”

Rez turned.

“Everyone down!”

The floor exploded.

---

Zee felt Ner’s fear through no supernatural link.

He did not need one.

He knew his friend.

Seven years gave people a different kind of connection.

Zee and Zareth burst into the receiving hall through the upper balcony just as golden light flooded the chamber.

“Ner!”

Ner stood inside a sphere of Pure Golden Mana.

Rez was beside him.

Three foreign witches were trapped against the far wall beneath collapsing stone.

Something moved beneath the shattered floor.

Not human.

A hand reached upward.

Then another.

Stone-colored creatures climbed from beneath Vesper.

Constructs.

No heartbeats.

No scent.

No blood.

Exactly the kind of enemy Zee’s usual senses hated.

Rez saw him.

“About time!”

Zee jumped.

“You said I was banned from diplomatic meetings!”

“This is no longer diplomatic!”

“That happens around you a lot!”

Rez blasted a construct apart with Blue-White Mana.

Ner shouted, “Can you argue later?”

“No!” both answered.

Ner rolled his eyes.

The nearest construct attacked.

Zee blocked.

Its fist struck his forearms.

Pain traveled through bone.

His scales spread immediately.

Crimson-black plating covered more of his skin.

The impact still hurt.

But less than it should have.

Dragon durability.

Incomplete.

Growing.

Zee shoved the creature back.

Crimson Dragon energy mixed into his Mana for a heartbeat.

The effect shocked him.

Heat.

Dense.

Ancient.

The construct’s stone chest cracked where Zee touched it.

He stared at his own hand.

The scales had spread almost to his elbow.

Zareth saw.

The Dragon Link filled with recognition.

**Like me. Not me.**

Zee looked at him.

That was the closest Zareth had ever come to describing what was happening.

Not Zareth.

Dragon.

But Zee’s.

“Later.”

Zareth roared.

Together they attacked.

The constructs had been sent for Ner.

That became obvious quickly.

Every one ignored Zee whenever Ner moved.

The southern witches realized it too.

“We did not do this!” one shouted.

Rez looked toward them.

“I believe you!”

The witch blinked.

“You do?”

“If you wanted Ner kidnapped, burying yourselves under a ceiling would be extremely committed!”

Fair.

One construct reached through Ner’s golden barrier.

Its stone hand began absorbing light.

Ner’s expression changed.

“It is eating my magic.”

Zee saw the golden glow draining into carved symbols along the construct’s arm.

Not ordinary stone.

A magical vessel.

Someone had built it specifically for Ner.

Zee’s anger rose.

The crimson scales reached his temple.

His horns burned.

Not with fire.

With pressure.

Zareth felt it.

Warning.

Zee ignored him.

He grabbed the construct.

The thing immediately tried absorbing Crimson Mana instead.

Bad decision.

Its runes flared.

Then cracked.

Zee’s Mana did not behave like Ner’s.

Something crimson and draconic moved through the contact.

The construct’s entire arm shattered.

Zee ripped it away.

Rez stared.

“You have been practicing that?”

“No.”

“That is worse!”

Another construct struck Zee from behind.

He crashed across the floor.

Pain exploded through his ribs.

He heard something crack.

Then begin repairing.

He pushed himself up.

No death.

Never death.

Pain remained.

He hated pain.

Ner’s Golden Mana surged.

“Zee!”

“I am fine!”

“You are bleeding!”

“That happens!”

Ner looked furious.

His sphere expanded.

Golden light struck every construct simultaneously.

Not destroying them.

Revealing something.

Threads.

Thin magical lines stretched from the constructs down through the broken floor.

Control lines.

Ner saw them.

“So that is how.”

He closed his fist.

Pure Golden Mana traveled backward along every thread.

Far beneath the palace, someone screamed.

Every construct stopped.

Rez looked toward Ner.

“What did you do?”

Ner stared at the glowing threads.

“I found who was holding them.”

Zee smiled.

“That was good.”

Ner smiled back.

“Thank you.”

Rez looked offended.

“I have been complimenting you for years.”

“No, you have been insulting me educationally.”

“That is affection.”

Zareth smashed the final construct.

The floor shook.

The three boys looked toward him.

Zareth lifted his head proudly.

Zee laughed.

Then Aurelia entered.

The laughter died immediately.

She saw Zee.

Blood.

Broken ribs healing.

Scales spread across his neck and arms.

Horns glowing faintly crimson-black.

She stopped.

Something old moved behind her eyes.

Recognition.

Fear.

Zee noticed.

“Mother?”

Aurelia crossed the chamber.

She touched one horn.

Very gently.

Zee stiffened.

“You know what this is.”

Her hand stopped.

Rez and Ner looked toward her.

Zareth became completely still.

Aurelia withdrew.

“I know more than I have told you.”

Zee’s expression changed.

“How much?”

“Not here.”

That answer would have worked seven years ago.

Not now.

Zee stepped backward.

“Why?”

Aurelia looked around the destroyed hall.

Foreign witches.

Vesper soldiers.

Lucien entering through the western doors.

Too many ears.

“Because some truths become dangerous once spoken.”

Zee’s crimson eyes hardened.

“So you do know.”

“Zee.”

“My horns started growing when I was five.”

Aurelia said nothing.

“The scales started before that.”

Still nothing.

“Zareth makes them worse.”

The Dragon Link flashed annoyance.

Zee corrected himself.

“Stronger.”

Zareth settled.

Ner stared at him.

“You have been keeping track?”

“Of course.”

Rez looked toward Aurelia.

“He deserves an answer.”

She turned.

“He deserves to survive the answer.”

The room went quiet.

Zee’s anger weakened.

Not disappeared.

Changed.

“Is it about me?”

Aurelia looked directly at him.

“No.”

That surprised everyone.

Then:

“It begins with me.”

Zee stared.

Something in the shape of Aurelia’s face suddenly seemed different.

Not physically.

In memory.

Her unusual resilience.

Her sensitivity to Zareth.

The way Dragon Queen Drakonis had once studied her without understanding why.

Aurelia stepped closer.

“When we are alone.”

Zee wanted to demand more.

He was ten.

So instead he crossed his arms and said the cruelest thing he could think of.

“I am not going to forget.”

Aurelia almost smiled.

“I know.”

Lucien approached.

“The people controlling the constructs escaped.”

Ner turned.

“No.”

Everyone looked at him.

His Golden Mana remained connected to one final thread.

Faint.

Moving.

Ner smiled.

“I can still feel them.”

Rez’s face lit up.

Zee immediately understood.

Aurelia did too.

“No.”

All three boys looked toward her.

Rez tried first.

“My Queen—”

“No.”

Ner tried.

“They attacked me.”

“No.”

Zee tried.

“They are getting away.”

“No.”

Zareth lowered his head.

Aurelia pointed at him.

“Especially no.”

The Dragon Link carried deep offense.

Caldrin Marr appeared in the shattered doorway.

He examined the room.

Then the glowing magical thread running into the underground passages.

Then the children.

Then Aurelia.

“No what?”

Zee smiled.

Aurelia closed her eyes.

Caldrin looked toward the glowing trail.

“Oh.”

His own smile appeared.

“No.”

Zee’s face fell.

Caldrin continued.

“Not without me.”

Aurelia stared at him.

And somewhere beneath House Vesper, the surviving controllers of the stone constructs believed their attack had failed and their escape remained secret.

They had made one mistake.

They attacked children who had spent their entire lives being hunted.

Now Zee Darkheart was ten.

Ner had a trail.

Rez had a sword.

Zareth had wings.

And for the first time, the hunted prince was old enough to decide that he was tired of waiting for the next enemy to find him.

This time...

Zee intended to find them first.

# Crimson Dynasty — Chapters Twenty-Five & Twenty-Six

# Chapter Twenty-Five

## The Trail of Gold

Aurelia did not allow Zee to go.

Zee went anyway.

The difference was that, at ten years old, he had finally become clever enough not to announce it first.

The receiving hall remained filled with broken stone, shattered constructs, frightened diplomats, Vesper soldiers, and three southern witches loudly insisting that the attack had nothing to do with them.

Ner stood beside the hole in the floor.

The final thread of Pure Golden Mana remained wrapped around two of his fingers.

It descended into darkness.

Moving.

Fading.

But present.

“They are getting farther away.”

Aurelia looked toward Lucien.

“Send soldiers.”

Lucien was already issuing orders.

“Vale takes the first unit. Caldrin takes the second. Seal every known exit beneath the southern quarter.”

Rez folded his arms.

“And us?”

“No.”

Zee looked at him.

“That sounded familiar.”

Rez ignored him.

“I am seventeen.”

Lucien stared at his son.

“You say that as though seventeen is an ancient and respected age.”

“It is compared to them.”

Zee and Ner both glared.

Rez pointed between them.

“See?”

Aurelia crouched in front of Zee.

“You are staying here.”

“They attacked Ner.”

“Yes.”

“They are escaping.”

“Yes.”

“Ner can track them.”

“Yes.”

“So—”

“No.”

Zee frowned.

Aurelia continued before he could argue.

“You have broken ribs that are still healing.”

“They are almost done.”

“That sentence does not help you.”

Zee touched his side.

The worst of the pain had already faded.

His Natural Tribrid body repaired damage rapidly now, but healing did not make injury pleasant. Every breath still pulled against tender bone.

Aurelia touched one of the crimson-black scales along his neck.

“And whatever happened to these during the fight is not something I am willing to ignore.”

Zee’s expression sharpened.

“You said you would tell me.”

“I will.”

“When?”

“When there are not attackers beneath the palace.”

“That is always when people say later.”

Aurelia’s face softened.

“I know.”

Zee hated when she answered calmly.

It made rebellion less satisfying.

Behind him, Zareth sent a thought-fragment through the Dragon Link.

**Other way.**

Zee’s eyes shifted toward the dragon.

An image followed.

Old service shaft.

Western wall.

Down.

Zareth had found it years earlier.

Of course he had.

The dragon spent his childhood exploring every place adults told him not to enter.

Zee looked toward Ner.

Ner noticed.

Rez noticed Ner noticing.

Then Rez noticed Zee trying not to look guilty.

“Oh, no.”

Aurelia turned.

“What?”

Rez smiled immediately.

“Nothing.”

Zee stared at him.

Traitor.

Rez’s expression answered clearly.

*You owe me.*

Lucien called from across the chamber.

“Rez.”

“Yes?”

“You remain with them.”

Rez’s face collapsed.

“What?”

“You wanted responsibility.”

“I wanted to go.”

“You now have responsibility.”

“That is not the same thing.”

Lucien walked away.

Caldrin passed Rez on his way toward the underground passage.

“Character building.”

Rez looked murderous.

Caldrin smiled.

Then vanished below.

Aurelia kissed Zee’s forehead.

“Stay.”

Zee nodded.

He waited until she left.

Then turned toward Rez.

“No.”

Zee blinked.

“I did not say anything.”

“You have the face.”

“What face?”

“The one you used when you were six and decided stealing a vampire hunter’s horse was ‘reconnaissance.’”

“That worked.”

“You rode into a swamp.”

“The horse chose badly.”

Ner looked between them.

“We are wasting time.”

Rez pointed at him.

“You are supposed to be the sensible one.”

“I never agreed to that.”

The golden thread around Ner’s fingers dimmed.

His face changed.

“They are going to break the connection.”

Zee looked toward Zareth.

The Dragon Link flashed.

**Now.**

Zee ran.

Ner followed.

Zareth crashed through the side passage.

Rez stared after them.

For one long second, he considered doing the responsible thing.

Then cursed and followed.

---

The hidden shaft dropped steeply beneath the southern palace.

Zareth went first.

His wings scraped stone as he descended, teal-and-gold mana illuminating the passage in brief flashes.

Zee followed using handholds carved into the wall.

Ner climbed below him.

Rez came last.

“This is idiotic.”

Zee looked up.

“You followed.”

“So you would not die.”

“I cannot.”

Rez stopped.

The words carried more weight now that Zee was old enough to understand them.

Absolute immortality was not something Zee announced often.

Even among the people closest to him, it sat strangely.

Rez looked down.

“You know what I mean.”

Zee did.

He continued climbing.

The shaft opened into an ancient aqueduct beneath Vesper.

Water moved through narrow channels cut into black stone.

Ner landed beside Zee.

The golden thread brightened.

“This way.”

They ran.

The architecture became older the deeper they traveled.

Vesper stonework disappeared behind rough foundations belonging to whatever civilization had occupied the valley before House Vesper ever claimed it.

Zee’s vampire hearing stretched ahead.

Water.

Rats.

Three heartbeats.

Then five.

Then—

Nothing.

He stopped.

Rez nearly hit him.

“What?”

Zee listened again.

“The people ahead disappeared.”

Ner frowned.

“Teleportation?”

“No.”

Zee smelled the air.

Dust.

Water.

Metal.

Magic.

And something else.

Clay.

He remembered the constructs.

“More stone bodies.”

Zareth growled.

The Dragon Link carried warning.

**Walls.**

Zee looked around.

The tunnel walls were covered in carved human faces.

He had thought they were decoration.

One opened its eyes.

“Move!”

The wall exploded.

Stone hands reached from both sides.

Rez shoved Ner forward as a construct tore free behind them.

Blue-White Mana erupted from his palm.

The blast froze half the creature’s body.

Zee struck the frozen section.

Crimson scales spread across his knuckles.

Stone shattered.

Another construct emerged from the floor.

Then four more.

Ner raised both hands.

Pure Golden Mana expanded in a ring.

The constructs stopped.

Not immobilized.

Revealed.

Golden lines appeared beneath their stone shells.

“Threads again.”

Rez looked around.

“Can you follow them?”

Ner gritted his teeth.

“They split.”

Zee ducked beneath a stone fist.

“Then find the real one!”

“That would be easier if you stopped shouting!”

“I am helping!”

“You are loud!”

Zareth slammed into two constructs and sent both through the wall.

Rez pointed.

“He is helping.”

Zee glared.

Then one construct caught him.

A stone hand closed around Zee’s throat and lifted him.

Pain.

Pressure.

His feet left the ground.

His body did not die.

Could not.

But the grip crushed against muscle and bone hard enough to make his vision blur.

Crimson Mana erupted.

The construct absorbed it.

Its runes brightened.

Zee remembered what happened upstairs.

The harder he fed the construct, the more it stored.

So he stopped pushing.

Changed.

His wolf instinct took over.

Movement.

Balance.

Weakness.

The construct’s left knee shifted before every turn.

Zee kicked it.

Nothing.

Again.

A crack.

The construct tightened its grip.

Zee’s dragon nature responded.

Crimson-black scales spread across his throat beneath the stone fingers.

Protection.

Not full armor.

Enough.

Zee inhaled.

Then drove both heels into the damaged knee.

It shattered.

The construct fell.

Zee rolled free.

His neck already healed beneath the scales.

Rez struck the broken construct with Blue-White Mana.

It exploded.

“Still think this was a good idea?”

Zee coughed.

“Yes.”

Rez laughed despite himself.

“That is what I was afraid of.”

Ner suddenly shouted.

“There!”

Golden Mana raced along the floor.

One control line brightened more than the others.

It ran east.

Zareth tore through the remaining constructs.

They followed.

---

The tunnel ended at a bronze door.

No Vesper crest.

No known witch sigil.

Only a circular depression in the center.

Ner stopped.

His Golden Mana pulled toward it.

Rez looked at the door.

“They wanted you to open this.”

Ner’s face tightened.

“That is why they attacked the hall.”

Zee touched the bronze.

“Then why run here?”

Rez understood first.

“They did not fail.”

Silence.

Ner looked at him.

“They wanted me to follow.”

A slow clap came from the darkness behind them.

Everyone turned.

A man stepped from an alcove.

Middle-aged.

Gray robes.

No mask.

No royal colors.

Seven others appeared around him.

Witches.

Humans.

One vampire.

Different backgrounds.

Different weapons.

Mercenaries working under one contract.

The gray-robed man smiled.

“Prince Rez.”

Rez raised his sword.

“Nereus Azrion.”

Golden Mana gathered.

“Crown Prince Zareth.”

The dragon bared his teeth.

Then the man looked at Zee.

“Darkheart.”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“You built the stone things.”

“I designed them.”

Ner stepped forward.

“For me.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

The man looked toward the bronze door.

“Because I cannot open that.”

“What is inside?”

“I do not know.”

Zee blinked.

The man laughed.

“You expected something grander?”

“No.”

Zee looked at Ner.

“He sounds like Caldrin.”

Rez snorted.

The man’s smile disappeared.

“This chamber predates Vesper. Every magical lock responds to structure. Every structure can be solved.”

He looked toward Ner’s hands.

“Except this one.”

Ner said nothing.

“It rejects ordinary witchcraft.”

“Dragon Mana.”

“Blood magic.”

“Vampire compulsion.”

“Demonic contracts.”

“Everything.”

Rez looked at the bronze door.

“So you decided to use a child.”

“I decided to use the correct key.”

Ner’s Golden Mana flared.

“I am not a key.”

The man smiled.

“That depends on the lock.”

Zee’s expression changed.

Zareth felt it.

Anger.

The Dragon Link warned him.

**Scales.**

Zee looked down.

Crimson-black scales had begun spreading along his forearms again.

The gray-robed man noticed.

His eyes sharpened.

“So the reports were accurate.”

Zee looked at him.

“What reports?”

No answer.

The man raised one hand.

The mercenaries attacked.

Rez met the vampire first.

Blue-White Mana flashed against supernatural speed.

Zareth took the left side, wings filling the tunnel as teal-and-gold Dragon Mana blasted two witches backward.

Ner raised a Golden barrier.

Three spells struck.

The barrier held.

Zee went for the gray-robed man.

The man had prepared.

A black sigil struck Zee’s chest.

His Crimson Mana vanished.

Not gone.

Suppressed.

His scales dimmed.

Zee stumbled.

The man smiled.

“Ten years of reports.”

“Enough observations.”

“Enough failures.”

“We finally built something that interferes with you.”

Zee tried summoning Crimson Mana.

Nothing answered.

Pain shot through his chest.

The suppression seal tightened.

The man stepped closer.

“You see?”

“You are not incomprehensible.”

“Only complicated.”

Zee looked frightened.

The man mistook that for victory.

Zareth did not.

Through the Dragon Link came Zee’s actual feeling.

**Wait.**

Zareth understood.

He kept fighting.

The man crouched in front of Zee.

“Victor failed because he tried to destroy what he feared.”

Zee’s crimson eyes hardened.

The man continued.

“I prefer measurement.”

Zee punched him.

No Mana.

No spell.

Just a ten-year-old fist backed by vampire strength and wolf muscle.

The man flew backward.

Zee stood.

“You measured wrong.”

Rez laughed from across the chamber.

“That was good!”

The gray-robed man rose with blood running from his mouth.

“You—”

Zee attacked.

The suppression stopped his Mana.

It did not stop his blood.

It did not stop his vampire speed.

His wolf reflexes.

His Dragon-toughened bones.

He had spent his entire life being attacked by enemies who wanted one part of him neutralized.

The mistake was thinking Zee had only one part.

He ducked a spell.

Closed distance.

Hit the man again.

The artificer tried retreating.

Zee smelled fear.

Zareth cut off the exit.

Ner trapped the mercenaries behind a Golden barrier.

Rez disarmed the vampire and kicked his weapon away.

The fight ended.

The gray-robed man sat against the bronze door breathing hard.

Zee stood before him.

“Who paid you?”

The man smiled through blood.

“No king.”

“Who?”

“A collector.”

“Name.”

“I never received one.”

Rez searched his coat.

“Broker tokens.”

He held up three silver discs.

Different markings.

“Multiple clients.”

Zee looked toward the door.

“You attacked Ner because of this.”

“Yes.”

Ner approached.

“What happens if I open it?”

The man’s expression changed.

“I do not know.”

Ner stared at him.

“You were willing to attack an entire palace because you were curious?”

The man smiled faintly.

“Curiosity built kingdoms.”

Ner’s Golden Mana brightened.

“And ruins.”

He closed his fist.

The remaining control threads vanished.

All surviving constructs went still.

Permanently.

The gray-robed man watched him.

Something close to fear entered his face.

Ner looked toward Lucien’s approaching soldiers echoing through the tunnels.

“You wanted to know what I can open.”

He stepped away from the bronze door.

“Now you can spend the rest of your life wondering.”

That hurt the man more than defeat.

Zee smiled.

“I like that.”

Ner smiled back.

Then Aurelia entered the chamber.

Zee stopped smiling.

She looked at him.

Then Ner.

Then Rez.

Then Zareth.

Then the unconscious mercenaries.

Then the bronze door.

Her voice was terrifyingly calm.

“Seven minutes.”

Rez looked confused.

“What?”

“I left you alone for seven minutes.”

Zee pointed toward the prisoners.

“We caught them.”

Aurelia looked at him.

“You disobeyed me.”

“Yes.”

“You entered an unknown underground structure.”

“Yes.”

“You fought mercenaries.”

“Yes.”

“You were magically suppressed.”

Zee hesitated.

“Yes.”

Aurelia closed her eyes.

Ner whispered, “Should we run?”

Rez shook his head.

“Too late.”

Zareth began backing away.

Zee stared at him.

Traitor.

The Dragon Link carried one emotion.

**Survive.**

---

The bronze door remained closed.

Lucien ordered three guard stations built around it before sunrise.

No one would touch the lock without his permission.

Especially Ner.

The gray-robed artificer was imprisoned.

His broker tokens proved exactly what Aurelia had feared.

The attack had not belonged to the black-robed organization.

Nor the Twelve Crowns.

Nor Victor.

Several private collectors had funded it independently.

One wanted information about Golden Mana.

Another wanted whatever lay behind the bronze door.

A third had paid merely for observations of Zee’s developing scales.

Different enemies.

Different interests.

Same children caught between them.

But the hunt had changed in one important way.

This time, Zee had gone toward it.

Aurelia understood that.

And that frightened her more than she wanted to admit.

Because the infant she once carried between kingdoms was gone.

Zee was ten.

Curious.

Angry.

Loyal.

And increasingly unwilling to let adults fight every battle for him.

That night, Aurelia stood outside his room.

Zee sat on the floor beside Zareth.

He knew why she had come.

“You said you would tell me.”

Aurelia entered.

She closed the door.

“Yes.”

Zee looked toward the crimson-black scales along his arm.

“About this?”

Aurelia nodded.

Zareth lifted his head.

The Dragon Link became intensely attentive.

Aurelia sat opposite her son.

For several heartbeats, she simply looked at him.

Then she said:

“Your Dragon blood did not come from Zareth.”

Zee went completely still.

And somewhere inside him, something ancient stirred.

---

# Chapter Twenty-Six

## The Blood His Mother Hid

Zee did not speak immediately.

That was unusual.

Aurelia had prepared herself for questions.

Anger.

Accusations.

Perhaps the dramatic declaration that everyone lied to him.

Instead, Zee stared at his mother as though rearranging ten years of memories inside his head.

Zareth lay beside him.

The Dragon Link carried confusion from both directions.

Finally Zee looked toward the dragon.

“Then why does he make it stronger?”

“I do not know completely.”

Zee looked back at Aurelia.

“But you know where it came from.”

“Yes.”

“Who?”

Aurelia held his gaze.

“Me.”

Silence.

Zee laughed.

Not because it was funny.

Because he thought she had misunderstood him.

“You are a witch.”

“Yes.”

He waited.

Aurelia did not continue.

Zee’s smile disappeared.

“Mother.”

Aurelia lifted one hand.

For the first time in Zee’s life, she stopped hiding.

Magic moved through her.

Not the witchcraft Zee had known since childhood.

Something older answered beneath it.

Her pupils narrowed.

Heat entered the room.

Then scales appeared.

They began along Aurelia’s wrist.

Dark.

Deep red-brown beneath the candlelight.

Not Zareth’s crimson.

Not Zee’s Crimson scales.

Different.

A lineage entirely its own.

The scales moved halfway along her forearm before stopping.

Zee stared.

Zareth rose instantly.

Teal-and-gold Mana ignited along his spine.

Not aggression.

Shock.

The Dragon Link exploded with one overwhelming concept.

**Dragon.**

Zee stood.

“You are…”

Aurelia finished it.

“Dragon and Witch.”

Zee looked at her scales.

Then his own.

Then back again.

“No.”

Aurelia’s expression tightened.

“No?”

“You would have told me.”

The words hurt.

Zee was ten.

There was no elegant accusation.

Only a child realizing his mother had hidden part of herself every day of his life.

Aurelia lowered her hand.

The scales remained.

“I wanted to.”

“When?”

“When you were older.”

“I am older.”

“You are ten.”

“You let me think Zareth was doing this to me.”

“I never told you that.”

“You did not tell me anything!”

Crimson Mana flashed through the room.

His developing Dragon energy moved with it.

The scales along Zee’s neck spread toward his jaw.

Aurelia did not flinch.

Zareth moved closer.

The Dragon Link carried a warning.

**Angry.**

Zee glared at him.

“I know.”

Zareth sent another feeling.

**Mother. Hurt.**

Zee’s anger faltered.

Only slightly.

Aurelia saw.

“You have every right to be angry.”

“I hate when adults say that.”

“Why?”

“Because then they keep doing the thing anyway.”

Aurelia almost smiled.

This was not the moment.

“You are right.”

That surprised him.

Zee crossed his arms.

“Tell me everything.”

“No.”

His eyes widened.

Aurelia continued before he exploded.

“I will tell you what belongs to you.”

“What does that mean?”

“It means some of my history is mine to decide when to share.”

Zee stared.

“That is unfair.”

“Yes.”

He clearly had not expected agreement again.

Aurelia continued.

“But your blood belongs to you.”

She touched the scales on his forearm.

“You inherited this from me.”

“Was it there when I was born?”

“Yes.”

“Then why did no one see it?”

“Because it was dormant.”

Zee frowned.

“My Witch, Vampire, and Wolf were not.”

“No.”

“You knew those?”

“Very quickly.”

Zee touched one horn.

“And this?”

“Your horn buds appeared years later.”

“You were not surprised.”

Aurelia looked away.

Zee caught it.

“You knew.”

“I suspected.”

“How?”

“Because I had them once.”

Zee stared at her head.

“You have horns?”

“Not in this form.”

“Can you turn into a dragon?”

Aurelia went silent.

Zee leaned forward.

“Mother.”

“Yes.”

His mouth opened.

Closed.

Opened again.

Zareth’s Dragon Link filled with absolute fascination.

Zee looked toward him.

“You did not know either?”

Zareth answered with a violent burst of offended confusion.

No.

Zee nodded.

“Good.”

Aurelia raised an eyebrow.

“Good?”

“At least everyone was lied to.”

“I did not lie.”

“You hid an entire dragon.”

Aurelia almost laughed despite herself.

“It is difficult to hide an entire dragon.”

“You did.”

Fair.

Zee sat again.

“When did Zareth start waking it?”

Aurelia became more careful.

“I do not know that he did.”

“You said—”

“I said your Dragon blood came from me.”

She looked toward Zareth.

“But from the moment he appeared beside you, your dormant blood reacted to him.”

Zareth’s teal-and-gold Mana shimmered.

Zee’s Crimson Mana answered.

Two different powers.

Never becoming the same.

Aurelia watched.

“His presence may be a catalyst.”

Zee frowned.

“What is that?”

“Something that helps a change begin without being the thing that created it.”

Zee thought.

“So he did not give it to me.”

“No.”

“He just… wakes it up.”

“Perhaps.”

“Perhaps?”

“I promised you truth.”

Aurelia’s voice softened.

“Not guesses disguised as truth.”

Zee remembered all the times she had forced witches, kings, and scholars to say *I do not know.*

That mattered more now.

“Does the Dragon Queen know?”

“No.”

“Lucien?”

“No.”

“Rez?”

“No.”

“Ner?”

“No.”

“Vale?”

Aurelia hesitated.

Zee pointed.

“He knows.”

“He suspects.”

“That means yes.”

“It does not.”

“Caldrin?”

“Caldrin suspects everything.”

Zee nodded.

“That is true.”

The tension loosened.

Only slightly.

Zee touched the juvenile horn above his temple.

“Am I becoming a dragon?”

Aurelia looked at him.

“You already carry Dragon nature.”

“That was not my question.”

“No.”

Her answer came carefully.

“You are not becoming *only* anything.”

Zee frowned.

“You were born Witch, Vampire, and Wolf completely active.”

“That is why you are the First Natural Tribrid.”

“Dragon was inherited but asleep.”

“And now?”

“Awakening.”

“How far?”

“I do not know.”

“Will I grow wings?”

“Possibly.”

“Fire?”

“Possibly.”

“Can I fly?”

“Not today.”

Zee looked deeply offended.

Zareth sent laughter through the Link.

Zee shoved his snout.

“Shut up.”

Zareth shoved back.

Aurelia smiled.

Then Zee became serious again.

“Why did you hide being a Dragon?”

The question changed the room.

Aurelia’s smile disappeared.

Her scales slowly receded beneath her skin.

“Because there are things from before you were born that still know my blood.”

Zee watched her.

“Enemies?”

“Yes.”

“Dragon enemies?”

“Some.”

“Witches?”

“Some.”

“Victor?”

Aurelia went still.

Zee saw it.

“Father knows.”

Aurelia did not answer quickly enough.

Zee stood.

“He knows?”

“He knows part.”

“How much?”

“Enough that it became another thing between us.”

Zee’s expression hardened.

“Did he hate you too?”

Aurelia looked toward the candle.

“No.”

That answer carried more pain than yes would have.

“Victor once loved what he did not understand about me.”

“Then fear changed him.”

Zee thought of the father he barely remembered.

A face in fragments.

A hand he once trusted.

A voice that sometimes appeared in nightmares without words.

“Like me.”

Aurelia looked at him.

“Yes.”

Zee turned away.

For several moments he watched rain strike the dark window.

Then:

“I do not want to be like him.”

Aurelia’s expression softened.

“Then keep choosing differently.”

The same answer she had given him years ago.

People become what they keep choosing.

Zee remembered.

His anger quieted.

Not gone.

But his.

Controlled.

He turned back.

“Show me.”

Aurelia frowned.

“What?”

“Your dragon.”

“No.”

Zee’s face collapsed.

“Why?”

“Because this room is too small.”

His eyes widened.

Zareth rose immediately.

Excitement flooded the Link.

Zee grinned.

“When?”

“Not tonight.”

“Tomorrow?”

“No.”

“Next week?”

“Zee.”

“You said I deserve truth.”

“You deserve sleep.”

“That is not truth.”

“It is unfortunately true.”

Zee groaned.

Aurelia stood.

She kissed his forehead beside one horn.

“I love you.”

He remained annoyed.

“I know.”

She reached the door.

“Mother?”

Aurelia stopped.

Zee looked down at his scales.

“Are mine ugly?”

Aurelia’s face changed instantly.

“No.”

“They are darker than Zareth’s.”

“They should be.”

“Why?”

“Because they are yours.”

Zee looked toward Zareth.

The dragon sent a clear thought-fragment.

**Good scales. Bad horns.**

Zee stared.

“My horns are better than yours.”

Zareth growled.

Aurelia left before the argument became physical.

For the first time in years, she closed the door smiling.

---

The next morning began with training.

Rez attacked Zee before he finished complaining about breakfast.

A Blue-White blade of Mana swept toward his legs.

Zee jumped.

“You cheated!”

Rez followed with another strike.

“You were warned.”

“You said training!”

“This is training.”

“You attacked me while I was eating!”

“A battlefield does not respect breakfast.”

Ner sat on the wall eating an apple.

“That is the stupidest thing you have ever said.”

Rez pointed at him without looking.

“I am trying to teach.”

“You sound like Lucien.”

Rez missed a step.

Zee immediately hit him with a training staff.

Rez stared.

Zee smiled.

“Battlefield.”

Ner nearly fell from the wall laughing.

Zareth lay nearby, entirely unhelpful.

The Dragon Link carried approval.

Rez recovered.

“Again.”

This time Zee took position properly.

His body had learned seven years of survival.

Feet light.

Shoulders loose.

Wolf instincts reading movement.

Vampire senses tracking heartbeat.

Witch nature ready beneath his Crimson Mana.

Dragon energy new and restless underneath.

Rez attacked.

Zee blocked.

Blue-White Mana struck Crimson.

The impact pushed Zee backward.

He dug in.

Scales spread along his forearms.

Rez saw.

He changed angle.

Zee anticipated.

Their practice blades hit.

Again.

Again.

Rez was older.

Better trained.

More disciplined.

Zee was faster than he had any right to be.

Unpredictable.

And increasingly difficult to surprise.

Ner watched carefully.

Then Pure Golden Mana suddenly flickered around his hand.

He looked toward the palace.

Zee noticed.

“What?”

Ner jumped from the wall.

“The bronze door.”

Rez stopped.

“What about it?”

Ner’s face tightened.

“It opened.”

Everyone went silent.

Lucien had forbidden anyone from touching it.

Ner looked at his hand.

“I did not do anything.”

A bell rang beneath the palace.

Once.

Deep.

Ancient.

Then again.

Zareth stood.

The Dragon Link carried immediate warning.

**Below.**

A third bell rang.

The courtyard stones trembled.

Rez lowered his practice weapon.

“That cannot be good.”

Caldrin appeared on the upper balcony.

“No.”

He looked down at them.

“It cannot.”

Zee looked toward the palace entrance.

Aurelia emerged seconds later.

She met his eyes.

For once, she did not tell him to stay behind.

“Get your weapons.”

Zee blinked.

“Really?”

Aurelia pointed.

“Before I change my mind.”

Zee ran.

Ner followed.

Rez smiled.

Zareth spread his wings.

The bronze door beneath Vesper had remained sealed through kingdoms, wars, witches, demons, and generations of rulers.

Ner had refused to open it.

Yet something on the other side had apparently decided it no longer needed permission.

And when Zee Darkheart descended beneath House Vesper again, he would do so differently than before.

Not sneaking behind adults.

Not being carried away from danger.

Not merely surviving whatever found him.

This time, his mother knew he was going.

His brother stood beside him.

His best friend carried Golden Mana.

His dragon moved overhead.

And beneath Zee’s skin, a fourth inheritance had finally been named.

The hunted prince was still a child.

But for the first time in his life, the adults around him were beginning to understand something the world had learned much earlier.

Keeping Zee away from danger was becoming impossible.

Teaching him how to walk into it might be the only protection they had left.

# Crimson Dynasty — Chapters Twenty-Seven & Twenty-Eight

# Chapter Twenty-Seven

## The Door Beneath Vesper

The bronze door opened inward.

No hand touched it.

No spell forced it.

No Golden Mana reached toward the lock.

It simply moved.

Ancient metal dragged across stone with a sound that rolled through the foundations of House Vesper like something waking beneath the kingdom.

Zee stood at the bottom of the descending stairway with Rez to his right and Ner to his left.

Zareth occupied nearly the entire passage behind them.

At ten years old, the Dragon Crown Prince had long since outgrown tunnels built for humans, and his irritation moved clearly through the Dragon Link.

**Small. Bad. Break wall.**

Zee looked over his shoulder.

“No.”

Zareth sent him an image of the wall collapsing.

Then an image of himself walking comfortably through the new opening.

“That is still no.”

Rez glanced between them.

“What is he complaining about?”

“The tunnel.”

“He is a dragon.”

“That is his argument.”

Rez nodded.

“Strong argument.”

Aurelia stepped past them.

Her expression had changed since revealing the truth of her Dragon blood.

Not softer.

More exposed.

Zee noticed things now that he would not have noticed before.

The way her eyes lingered on old carvings.

How certain scents made her shoulders tighten.

How she always positioned herself where she could see both Zee and the nearest exit.

Some habits had nothing to do with being Queen.

Some were older.

Vale descended behind Aurelia with six Vesper guards.

Lucien followed.

Caldrin came last, carrying far more knives than anyone had asked him to bring.

The royal witch raised violet light above her palm.

It illuminated the open door.

Beyond it lay darkness.

Ner stopped several feet from the threshold.

His Golden Mana had become restless again.

Zee looked at him.

“You feel something?”

“Yes.”

“What?”

Ner frowned.

“I do not know.”

Rez sighed.

“You two say that constantly.”

Ner looked toward him.

“Would you rather I invent something?”

“No.”

“Then be quiet.”

Zee smiled.

Rez pointed.

“See what you created?”

“I did not create Ner.”

“You made him mean.”

Ner looked deeply pleased.

Aurelia turned.

“Enough.”

All three stopped.

Zareth did not.

He sent Zee a feeling of amusement.

Traitor.

The bronze door waited.

Lucien approached it carefully.

“No one crosses until we know whether the threshold is trapped.”

Caldrin stepped beside him.

“I volunteer Rez.”

Rez looked offended.

“You cannot volunteer someone else.”

“I just did.”

Lucien ignored them and looked toward the royal witch.

She extended one hand.

Violet Mana crossed the threshold.

Nothing happened.

A second spell followed.

Still nothing.

Then Ner’s Golden Mana flickered.

The open doorway answered.

A line of gold appeared along the floor.

Ner stepped backward.

The light stopped.

Everyone looked at him.

“I did not do that.”

Zee believed him.

So did Aurelia.

The door was responding to Ner.

That had always been the fear.

Lucien’s expression hardened.

“Nereus stays here.”

Ner stared.

“No.”

“Nereus.”

“You brought me because this reacts to my Mana.”

“I brought you because whatever opened that door may have been coming for you.”

“Then leaving me outside makes no sense.”

Rez whispered to Zee.

“He has a point.”

Lucien heard him.

“I am surrounded by insubordination.”

Aurelia looked at Zee.

“I understand.”

Zee frowned.

“I did not say anything.”

“You were about to.”

That was unfairly accurate.

Ner stepped toward the threshold.

Golden light brightened beneath his feet.

Nothing attacked.

Nothing moved.

He looked back.

“If it wanted to hurt me, it already knows where I am.”

Aurelia exchanged a look with Lucien.

Then nodded once.

“Stay between Rez and me.”

Ner smiled faintly.

“Yes, Your Majesty.”

They entered.

---

The chamber beyond the bronze door was not a room.

It was a road.

A stone avenue stretched downward at an angle too gentle to feel like a staircase and too steep to belong inside any ordinary foundation.

Columns lined both sides.

Each had been carved with hundreds of overlapping symbols.

Witch marks.

Wolf carvings.

Vampiric blood glyphs.

Dragon script.

Others none of them recognized.

Zee slowed.

“These were made by different people.”

The royal witch looked toward him.

“What makes you think that?”

“They do not feel the same.”

Aurelia looked more closely.

Zee was right.

Different tools.

Different ages.

Different magical traditions.

This place had not belonged to one civilization.

People had found it.

Used it.

Added to it.

Then left.

Caldrin ran one finger near a damaged carving without touching.

“Or died.”

Vale looked at him.

“You enjoy that possibility too much.”

“I appreciate preparedness.”

A sound traveled from farther below.

Metal.

Then silence.

Zareth pushed forward.

The Link carried warning.

**Something moved.**

Zee felt it too.

Not through blood.

Not heartbeat.

Through the strange demonic sense he had developed beneath Vesper years earlier.

Presence where no ordinary body could be tracked.

Something was ahead.

“Stop.”

Everyone did.

Zee pointed toward the left row of columns.

“There.”

Nothing stood there.

Many.

Records.

Fragments.

People walking this same path centuries earlier.

A vampire king.

A witch queen.

A wolf chieftain.

All arriving at different times.

Each approaching the same deeper chamber.

Mostly.

Silence.

Zee’s crimson eyes narrowed.

“Because you carry too many doors.”

Everyone saw.

Vale’s face changed.

House Vesper did not automatically know.

Aurelia’s expression became deadly.

The construct did not care.

“Dragon-Witch.”

No apology.

No explanation.

Not here.

“You said Lucien did not know.”

“I can confirm that.”

Caldrin smiled faintly.

“I suspected.”

“Proceed.”

“Why?”

“No.”

“You did not even ask.”

“So do I.”

Rez smiled.

Together.

Nothing else.

No treasure.

No bodies.

No monster.

Four circular platforms stood around a central pool of black water.

Each bore a symbol.

Gold.

Blue-white.

Crimson.

Teal-and-gold.

Rez stopped.

“No.”

Ner looked toward him.

“That is your Mana.”

Zee stared at the crimson pedestal.

Zareth growled at the fourth.

Too exact.

Too current.

Too personal.

“This was prepared recently.”

“No.”

Aurelia looked at her.

“These pigments are old.”

“I cannot tell.”

Caldrin crouched.

“Hundreds of years at least.”

“No.”

He pointed.

Crimson Mana flickered from his hand.

The pedestal responded.

The color changed.

Not crimson now.

His pedestal brightened.

Rez tested his.

Blue-white responded.

Zareth’s teal-and-gold surged.

The fourth pedestal awakened.

Not prophecy.

Not preparation.

Resonance.

The room was reading whoever entered.

Zee relaxed slightly.

Caldrin nodded.

“Good.”

Vale looked toward him.

“Why good?”

“Because I disliked the idea of an ancient room knowing our children’s colors before they were born.”

Aurelia’s expression remained hard.

“Do not relax.”

The central water moved.

An image rose.

Not a person.

A map.

The known kingdoms appeared across the surface.

Then points of light.

Hundreds.

Some in witch territory.

Some vampire.

Some wolf.

Some beneath mountains.

Some at sea.

One beyond the eastern deserts.

One impossibly far north.

Ner stared.

Lucien turned.

Rez stared at the map.

“So there are more doors.”

“No.”

“I said nothing.”

Zareth sent intense agreement.

Traitor.

The water rippled.

Another followed.

Light.

Aurelia grabbed Zee.

“From where?”

A single black line appeared beneath Vesper.

Moving toward them.

Fast.

Caldrin drew both blades.

The wall.

Its body resembled smoke trapped beneath bone armor. Six arms ended in thin hooked claws. No heartbeat. No blood. No scent.

Then three more followed.

Rez stared.

“You have a name for them?”

Caldrin smiled.

“I like this machine.”

Zee moved first.

Because he was closest.

Pain burned.

Crimson scales expanded instantly.

Adaptation.

Zee grinned despite himself.

The creature hissed.

Zee hit it with Crimson Mana.

Nothing.

The energy passed through smoke.

He switched.

Demonic sense.

Presence.

He grabbed where the body actually existed beneath the illusion.

His hand closed.

The predator screamed.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana struck the exposed form.

Ner sealed its retreat with Golden light.

Zareth unleashed teal-and-gold fire.

Not dead.

Still moving.

Aurelia attacked.

Her witchcraft struck first.

A flash of dark red Dragon energy crossed the spell.

The predator disintegrated.

Everyone stopped.

Ner controlled space.

Zareth tore through anything that became physical.

Aurelia combined witchcraft with carefully restrained Dragon power.

“Fair.”

“I am not a child.”

“Fair.”

“Tonight.”

About her blood.

Her hidden lineage.

Why she had spent a lifetime concealing half of herself.

# Chapter Twenty-Eight

## The Blood Before Darkheart

Aurelia took Zee beyond Vesper’s walls.

Not far.

Only to the old northern cliffs where the city disappeared behind pine forests and the mountains opened beneath a clear night sky.

Zareth came.

Of course he did.

Aurelia had expected that.

Rez and Ner did not.

Zee had protested.

Aurelia refused.

Some stories belonged to blood before they belonged to friendship.

Zee sat beside the cliff edge wrapped in a dark coat, knees pulled toward his chest.

Zareth lay behind him.

The Dragon Link remained quiet.

Listening.

Aurelia stood several feet away.

For a long time, she watched the moon.

Then she spoke.

“House Darkheart is not where my story begins.”

Zee looked up.

“I thought you were born there.”

“I was.”

“Then how?”

Aurelia smiled faintly.

“Birthplace and beginning are not always the same.”

Zee waited.

He was trying very hard not to interrupt.

Aurelia noticed.

“You may ask questions.”

“Good.”

He immediately raised one finger.

“What was your Dragon family called?”

Aurelia laughed.

“That quickly?”

“You said questions.”

“I did.”

Her smile faded.

“My Dragon blood comes from a lineage called the Vaelorian.”

Zareth lifted his head.

The name meant nothing to him.

No Drakonis memory answered.

That mattered.

Separate lineage.

Aurelia continued.

“They were never part of Drakonis.”

“Enemies?”

“Sometimes.”

“Friends?”

“Sometimes.”

Zee frowned.

“That is useless.”

“It is politics.”

“That is also useless.”

Aurelia almost smiled.

“The Vaelorians were older than several human kingdoms and younger than some Dragon Houses.”

“What color?”

“Many.”

“Your dragon?”

Aurelia looked toward him.

“Dark red.”

“Like your scales?”

“Yes.”

“Big?”

She raised an eyebrow.

“Yes.”

“Bigger than Zareth?”

Zareth growled.

Zee grinned.

Aurelia wisely declined to answer.

“Why hide it?”

That was the real question.

Aurelia’s expression changed.

“Because the Vaelorian line was hunted.”

Zee became still.

Not surprised.

Hunting was the language his childhood understood best.

“By who?”

“Several groups.”

“Dragons?”

“Yes.”

“Witches?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

Aurelia looked toward the valley below.

“Because Vaelorian Dragons could bond more easily with witchcraft than most Dragon bloodlines.”

Zee frowned.

“Like you.”

“Yes.”

“Dragon-Witch.”

“Yes.”

“Were there others?”

“Once.”

The word carried grief.

Zee heard it.

“How many now?”

Aurelia did not answer.

That was answer enough.

Zee looked down.

“Only you?”

“I do not know.”

The honesty mattered.

“Some may have survived.”

“Hidden?”

“Yes.”

“Like you.”

“Yes.”

Zee thought.

“And Victor knew?”

“Eventually.”

Aurelia sat beside him.

“Not when we first met.”

Zee stared.

“You hid it from Father too?”

“I hid it from everyone.”

“Why marry him?”

The question came childishly direct.

Aurelia smiled sadly.

“Because I loved him.”

Zee’s face tightened.

“But he hurt you.”

“Yes.”

“You still loved him?”

“For a long time.”

“That is stupid.”

Aurelia laughed quietly.

“Sometimes.”

Zee looked embarrassed.

“I did not mean—”

“I know.”

She touched his hair, careful around the juvenile horns.

“People can love badly.”

“That does not make the love false.”

“It makes it dangerous.”

Zee thought about that.

Then:

“When did Father find out?”

“Years before you were born.”

“How?”

“I told him.”

“Why?”

“Because I trusted him.”

Zee looked toward the horizon.

“And then?”

“Nothing happened immediately.”

That surprised him.

“Victor kept my secret.”

“For years.”

“He protected it.”

“He never used it against me.”

“Until?”

Aurelia’s eyes darkened.

“Until fear changed the meaning of everything.”

Zee did not ask which fear.

He knew.

His birth.

The prophecy.

The Blood Rain.

The world.

Him.

“Did he think my Dragon blood made me worse?”

Aurelia’s face hardened.

“Eventually, yes.”

Zee looked at his hands.

The permanent Crimson scales along his arms reflected moonlight.

“Do you?”

Aurelia turned sharply.

“No.”

He stared.

She touched his face.

“Never ask me that as though there is any answer but no.”

Zee swallowed.

“I just…”

He looked toward Zareth.

“He is Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“You are Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“I am…”

He stopped.

Aurelia waited.

“Too many things.”

There it was.

Not monster.

Not abomination.

Something quieter.

The fear beneath all the names adults had thrown at him.

Too much.

Too strange.

Too many pieces.

Aurelia moved closer.

“You are not pieces.”

Zee looked at her.

“You are Zee.”

“That sounds like something mothers say.”

“It is.”

“Is it true?”

“Yes.”

He frowned.

“How do you know?”

“Because I met you before anyone taught you what you were supposed to be.”

The words settled.

Zareth pressed closer behind him.

The Link carried warmth.

**Zee.**

Nothing else.

No titles.

No species.

No prophecy.

Zee.

His shoulders eased.

Aurelia continued.

“Your Witch blood does not erase your Vampire nature.”

“Your Vampire nature does not erase your Wolf.”

“Your Wolf does not erase what is waking from my blood.”

“And Dragon will not erase the three things you were born as.”

“You remain the First Natural Tribrid because that is what you were at birth.”

Zee touched one horn.

“And this is something else.”

“Yes.”

“Mine too.”

“Yes.”

He smiled faintly.

“Good.”

Aurelia raised an eyebrow.

“Good?”

“Zareth said my horns were bad.”

Zareth growled.

Zee pointed.

“He did.”

Aurelia laughed.

For several moments, the night became easy.

Then Zee asked the question she feared.

“Can you show me?”

Aurelia stopped laughing.

“Your dragon.”

She looked toward Vesper in the distance.

“No one is close enough.”

Zee’s eyes widened.

“That means yes.”

“It means stay where you are.”

He immediately stood.

“Sit.”

He sat.

Zareth rose.

His excitement flooded the Link.

Aurelia walked away from them.

Far enough.

Then stopped.

For the first time in decades, Queen Aurelia Darkheart allowed the form she had hidden beneath witchcraft and discipline to emerge completely.

Heat rolled across the cliff.

Her body changed.

Not violently.

Naturally.

Dark red scales spread across skin.

Her spine lengthened.

Wings unfolded from her back.

Bone reshaped.

Claws struck stone.

The transformation continued until the woman Zee had known all his life was gone.

A Dragon stood beneath the moon.

She was enormous.

Not as large as the Dragon Queen of Drakonis.

But large enough that Zee forgot how to breathe for several seconds.

Dark crimson-red scales covered her body, shaded almost black beneath the wings and along the spine. Witch sigils glowed faintly between some of the scales, not painted or carved, but naturally woven through her Dragon form.

Her eyes remained Aurelia’s.

That was how Zee knew.

“Mother?”

The Dragon lowered her head.

Zee laughed.

Pure childhood joy.

He ran.

Aurelia barely had time to react before Zee collided with her snout and wrapped both arms around it.

Zareth stared.

The Crown Prince of Drakonis looked personally betrayed that this enormous secret Dragon had existed beside him for years.

He approached.

Sniffed Aurelia.

Stepped back.

Sniffed again.

The Link flooded Zee.

**Mother. Dragon. Mother. Dragon.**

“Yes.”

Zareth looked at him.

**Why hidden?**

“I do not know everything.”

Aurelia released a low rumble.

Zee looked up.

“Can you understand me like this?”

She nodded.

“Can you talk?”

She gave him a look.

Zee grinned.

“Right. Dragon mouth.”

Zareth looked deeply smug.

Aurelia nudged him hard enough to roll him across the grass.

Zee collapsed laughing.

Zareth sprang upright, offended beyond measure.

Then the Dragon Link changed.

He challenged Aurelia.

Not seriously.

Young Dragon pride.

He spread his wings.

Teal-and-gold Mana ignited.

Aurelia’s witch-infused Dragon energy answered instinctively.

Zee felt both.

Something inside him surged.

His horns burned.

Crimson scales spread across his temples, neck, shoulders, ribs, and arms.

Crimson Dragon energy erupted through his Mana.

Aurelia turned immediately.

Zee gasped.

Pain struck his back.

Not injury.

Pressure.

Something pushing beneath bone.

He fell to one knee.

Zareth rushed toward him.

The Link flooded with alarm.

Aurelia shifted back to human form mid-run and caught Zee.

“Breathe.”

“What is happening?”

“I do not know.”

“Mother!”

“I know what I said.”

Pain intensified between his shoulder blades.

Zee gritted his teeth.

His body tried to change.

Not fully.

Not enough.

Two ridges formed beneath the skin of his upper back.

Then stopped.

No wings.

Not yet.

The Crimson Dragon energy collapsed inward.

Zee sagged against Aurelia.

Zareth pressed close.

The Link became frantic.

**Pain. Zee. Stay.**

“I am fine.”

Zee’s voice shook.

Aurelia examined his back.

No wound.

No permanent new structure.

Only two faint lines beneath the skin.

The beginning of possibility.

She looked terrified.

Zee noticed.

“What?”

“Nothing.”

“Do not do that.”

Aurelia closed her eyes.

Right.

No hiding behind nothing.

“Your Dragon nature reacted to both of us.”

“Both?”

“Me in full Dragon form.”

“Zareth’s Mana.”

“And the Link?”

“Possibly.”

Zee breathed slowly.

“Am I getting wings?”

“Not tonight.”

He looked disappointed despite the pain.

Aurelia stared.

“You are impossible.”

“I know.”

That word.

Impossible.

Once used like accusation.

Tonight it sounded almost affectionate.

Zee smiled.

Then something moved in the forest below.

Zareth turned first.

Aurelia turned second.

Zee smelled it third.

Dragon.

But not Drakonis.

Not Aurelia.

Different.

The three stared toward the trees.

A figure stepped into moonlight.

Human form.

Tall.

Silver hair.

Eyes glowing dark red.

Aurelia went completely still.

Zee looked at her.

“Mother?”

The stranger smiled.

“Aurelia Vaelorian.”

The name hit her like a blade.

Zareth growled.

Zee’s Crimson Mana rose.

Aurelia stepped in front of both children.

Her voice changed.

Not Queen.

Not mother.

Something older.

“You should be dead.”

The stranger’s smile widened.

“So should our bloodline.”

Silence consumed the cliff.

Then he looked past Aurelia.

At Zee.

His expression changed.

Recognition.

Not of the First Tribrid.

Of the scales.

The horns.

The blood beneath them.

“Well.”

Aurelia’s hands began glowing.

The stranger’s eyes returned to her.

“You really did have a son.”

Zee stared.

This enemy had not come because of the Blood Rain.

Not because of Victor.

Not because of the Twelve Crowns.

Not because of the bounty.

Not because of the black-robed organization.

He had come for Aurelia.

For the blood she had hidden long before Zee was born.

And for the first time, Zee Darkheart stood face-to-face with an enemy from his mother’s past.
