# Crimson Dynasty — Reconstructed Chapters Twenty-Seven & Twenty-Eight

# Chapter Twenty-Seven

## The Door Beneath Vesper

The bronze door opened inward.

No hand touched it.

No spell forced it.

No Golden Mana reached toward the lock.

It simply moved.

Ancient metal dragged across stone with a sound that rolled through the foundations of House Vesper like something waking beneath the kingdom.

Zee stood at the bottom of the descending stairway with Rez to his right and Ner to his left.

Zareth occupied nearly the entire passage behind them.

At ten years old, the Crown Prince of Drakonis had long since outgrown tunnels built for humans, and his irritation moved clearly through the Dragon Link.

**Small. Bad. Break wall.**

Zee looked over his shoulder.

“No.”

Zareth sent him an image of the wall collapsing.

Then an image of himself walking comfortably through the new opening.

“That is still no.”

Rez glanced between them.

“What is he complaining about?”

“The tunnel.”

“He is a dragon.”

“That is his argument.”

Rez nodded.

“Strong argument.”

Aurelia Darkheart stepped past them.

Her expression had changed since admitting the truth of Zee’s Dragon blood the previous night.

Not softer.

More exposed.

Now that Zee knew to look, he noticed things he would have missed before.

The way Aurelia’s eyes lingered on old carvings.

How certain scents made her shoulders tighten.

How she automatically positioned herself where she could see both Zee and the nearest exit.

Some habits had nothing to do with being Queen of House Darkheart.

Some were older.

Vale descended behind Aurelia with six Vesper guards.

King Lucien followed.

Caldrin came last, carrying far more knives than anyone had asked him to bring.

The royal witch raised one hand.

Violet Mana formed above her palm.

It illuminated the open doorway.

Beyond it lay darkness.

Ner stopped several feet from the threshold.

His Pure Golden Mana flickered faintly around his fingers.

Zee looked at him.

“You feel something?”

“Yes.”

“What?”

Ner frowned.

“I do not know.”

Rez sighed.

“You two say that constantly.”

Ner looked toward him.

“Would you rather I invent something?”

“No.”

“Then be quiet.”

Zee smiled.

Rez pointed at him.

“See what you created?”

“I did not create Ner.”

“You made him mean.”

Ner looked deeply pleased by the accusation.

Aurelia turned.

“Enough.”

All three stopped.

Zareth did not.

Amusement moved through the Link.

Traitor.

The bronze door waited.

Lucien approached carefully.

“No one crosses until we know whether the threshold is trapped.”

Caldrin stepped beside him.

“I volunteer Rez.”

Rez looked offended.

“You cannot volunteer someone else.”

“I just did.”

Lucien ignored them.

The royal witch extended her hand.

Violet Mana crossed the threshold.

Nothing happened.

A second spell followed.

Still nothing.

Then Ner’s Golden Mana flickered.

The doorway answered.

A thin line of gold appeared along the floor.

Ner stepped backward.

The light faded.

Everyone looked at him.

“I did not do that.”

Zee believed him.

So did Aurelia.

The door was responding to Ner.

Lucien’s expression hardened.

“Nereus stays here.”

Ner stared at him.

“No.”

“Nereus.”

“You brought me because this place reacts to my Mana.”

“I brought you because whatever opened that door may have been coming for you.”

“Then leaving me outside makes no sense.”

Rez whispered to Zee, “He has a point.”

Lucien heard him.

“I am surrounded by insubordination.”

Aurelia looked at Zee.

“I understand.”

Zee frowned.

“I did not say anything.”

“You were about to.”

That was unfairly accurate.

Ner stepped toward the threshold.

Golden light brightened beneath his feet.

Nothing attacked.

Nothing moved.

He looked back.

“If it wanted to hurt me, it already knows where I am.”

Aurelia exchanged a look with Lucien.

Then nodded once.

“Stay between Rez and me.”

Ner smiled faintly.

“Yes, Your Majesty.”

They entered.

---

The chamber beyond the bronze door was not a room.

It was a road.

A stone avenue stretched downward at an angle too gentle to feel like a staircase and too steep to belong inside any ordinary foundation.

Columns lined both sides.

Each had been carved with hundreds of overlapping symbols.

Witch marks.

Wolf carvings.

Vampiric blood glyphs.

Dragon script.

Others none of them recognized.

Zee slowed.

“These were made by different people.”

The royal witch looked toward him.

“What makes you think that?”

“They do not feel the same.”

Aurelia examined them more carefully.

Zee was right.

Different tools.

Different ages.

Different magical traditions.

Whatever lay beneath Vesper had not belonged to one people.

Others had found it.

Used it.

Changed it.

Left pieces of themselves behind.

Caldrin moved one finger near a damaged carving without touching it.

“Or died.”

Vale looked at him.

“You enjoy that possibility too much.”

“I appreciate preparedness.”

A metallic sound traveled from farther below.

Then silence.

Zareth pushed forward.

The Dragon Link tightened.

**Something moved.**

Zee felt it too.

Not through blood.

Not through heartbeat.

Not through scent.

Through the strange perception that had developed after the demon beneath Vesper years ago—the ability to sense presence where ordinary predatory senses found nothing.

Something was ahead.

“Stop.”

Everyone did.

Zee pointed toward the left row of columns.

“There.”

Nothing stood there.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana gathered.

Ner raised Golden light.

The empty air distorted.

A figure appeared.

Not demon.

Not human.

Stone and metal covered its body in overlapping plates, but beneath the armor something translucent existed, like spirit trapped inside glass.

It did not attack.

It looked at Ner.

Then Zee.

Then Aurelia.

Its head tilted.

A voice emerged from nowhere Zee could identify.

“Four.”

Everyone froze.

Aurelia’s eyes sharpened.

“Four what?”

The construct ignored her.

Its gaze remained fixed on Zee.

“Three awake.”

Zee’s fingers moved instinctively toward the crimson-black scales along his neck.

Four.

Three awake.

He looked toward Aurelia.

She had gone very still.

Before Zee could ask, she stepped in front of him.

“Enough.”

The construct turned toward her.

Silence held.

Then:

“Two awake.”

Aurelia’s face changed.

Zareth felt it.

The Link tightened.

**Mother knows.**

The construct moved closer.

Vale raised his sword.

Lucien lifted one hand.

“Do not attack unless it does.”

The figure stopped at the edge of the light.

Its attention returned to Ner.

“Key.”

Ner’s Golden Mana flared.

“I am not a key.”

The construct tilted its head.

“Not object.”

“Then stop calling me that.”

“Function.”

Ner looked offended.

Rez leaned toward Zee.

“I think it insulted him mathematically.”

Ner glared.

The construct extended one hand.

The entire avenue awakened.

Thousands of carvings ignited at once.

Not in one color.

Many.

The stone beneath their feet vibrated.

Then images appeared between the columns.

Not visions of the future.

Records.

Fragments of people who had walked the same avenue centuries earlier.

A vampire king approached alone beneath a torn banner.

The image shifted.

A witch queen appeared with six attendants.

Then a wolf chieftain covered in scars.

Then a Dragon walking in human form.

Different eras.

Different visitors.

Different reasons.

None were Zee.

None were Ner.

None resembled the strange group standing there now.

Zee stared.

“What is this place?”

The construct answered.

“Convergence Vault.”

Aurelia’s expression tightened.

Lucien noticed.

“You know that name?”

“No.”

Too quick.

Zee heard it.

“Mother.”

“I said no.”

“You sounded like yes.”

Aurelia glared.

He stopped.

Mostly.

The construct continued.

“Built by none.”

Caldrin raised an eyebrow.

“Unhelpful.”

“Found by many.”

“Better.”

“Opened by rare resonance.”

Ner looked at his hands.

“Me.”

“Part.”

Ner frowned.

“Part?”

The construct turned toward Zee.

“Other part.”

Silence.

Zee’s crimson eyes narrowed.

“I did not open the door.”

“No.”

“Then why me?”

The translucent core inside the construct brightened.

“Because you carry too many doors.”

Aurelia stepped forward.

“That is enough.”

The construct looked at her.

“Hidden door.”

Aurelia’s scales flashed beneath her skin.

Not illusion.

Not reflected light.

Real scales.

Deep red-brown surfaced briefly along her wrist and neck.

Lucien went completely still.

Vale’s face changed.

The royal witch inhaled sharply.

Zareth surged upright.

The construct spoke.

“Dragon-Witch.”

Lucien looked at Aurelia.

For perhaps the first time in years, King Lucien Vesper had no immediate response.

“You are…”

Aurelia met his eyes.

“Yes.”

“You never told me.”

“No.”

Caldrin folded his arms.

“I suspected.”

Vale turned toward him.

“Of course you did.”

“I suspect everyone.”

“That does not count.”

“It counts when I am right.”

Aurelia ignored them.

Zee stared at his mother.

He had known since the previous night that the Dragon blood came from her.

But hearing something ancient recognize both parts of her made the truth heavier.

Real.

The construct turned away.

“Proceed.”

The avenue illuminated farther down.

Lucien’s expression hardened.

“Why?”

“No compulsion.”

“That was not my question.”

“Choice required.”

That answer mattered.

Nothing was forcing them forward.

They could leave.

Aurelia looked at Zee.

He was already staring down the illuminated path.

“No.”

Zee sighed.

“You did not even ask.”

“I know your face.”

Ner looked toward the deeper passage.

“So do I.”

Rez folded his arms.

“Well, I am seventeen.”

Lucien stared at him.

Rez lifted his chin.

“That argument has to work eventually.”

It did not.

They argued for nearly fifteen minutes.

Then continued anyway.

Together.

---

The avenue ended inside a circular chamber.

Four stone pedestals surrounded a central pool of perfectly black water.

Nothing rested on them.

No weapons.

No crowns.

No books.

No carved names.

Only smooth stone.

Zee stopped at the entrance.

“That is disappointing.”

Rez looked toward him.

“You wanted treasure?”

“I wanted something.”

Caldrin nodded.

“Reasonable.”

Ner stepped farther inside.

One pedestal illuminated.

Pure gold spread across its surface.

Everyone stopped.

Ner immediately stepped backward.

The gold disappeared.

He stepped forward again.

It returned.

Rez frowned.

“That one is reading you.”

Ner looked toward him.

“Very observant.”

Rez moved toward another pedestal.

Blue-White light awakened beneath his hand.

He withdrew.

The color vanished.

Zareth approached the third.

Teal-and-Gold Dragon Mana rippled across his scales.

The pedestal answered with the same mixed resonance.

Zee looked at the final stone.

Nothing.

Then he let a little Crimson Mana rise from his palm.

The pedestal ignited.

Crimson.

Not only the color of his witchcraft.

Something hotter stirred beneath it.

Crimson Dragon energy moved through the light for a heartbeat.

Zee stared.

Four pedestals.

Four current visitors.

Four present resonances.

Caldrin crouched beside Rez’s pedestal.

He examined the stone.

“No pigment.”

The royal witch nodded.

“No stored color either.”

Ner stepped away again.

His pedestal returned to gray.

Rez did the same.

Gray.

Zareth lowered his Mana.

Gray.

Zee released his.

Gray.

Aurelia exhaled.

“They were not waiting for you.”

Zee looked toward her.

“The room is reading us.”

“Yes.”

Ner’s expression eased.

“Resonance.”

Lucien nodded.

“Not prediction.”

Not destiny.

Not prophecy.

Whatever the chamber was, it had not known their colors before they were born.

It simply knew what stood inside it now.

Zee liked that answer better.

The black water in the center of the chamber moved.

A map rose from it.

No hands touched the surface.

Continents formed in light.

Kingdoms.

Mountain ranges.

Coasts.

Seas.

Some Zee recognized.

Much of it he did not.

Then points appeared.

Dozens.

Then hundreds.

Ner moved closer.

“What are those?”

The construct had followed them.

“Thresholds.”

Lucien looked toward it.

“Like the bronze door?”

“Related.”

Some points existed in witch territory.

Others beneath vampire kingdoms.

Several lay within wolf lands.

A cluster appeared beneath distant mountains.

Others glowed far out at sea.

Several existed beyond the borders of every kingdom shown on modern Vesper maps.

One sat beyond an eastern desert Zee had only heard about.

Another appeared so far north that Caldrin frowned.

“There is nothing there.”

The construct answered.

“Unknown.”

Caldrin smiled faintly.

“I like it less now.”

Zee stared at the distant lights.

The world suddenly felt much larger.

Not built around him.

Not waiting for him.

Full of places that existed whether Zee Darkheart ever found them or not.

Then one threshold turned black.

The point vanished.

Another followed.

Then another.

Ner’s smile disappeared.

“What happened?”

The construct stared at the map.

“Closed.”

“Destroyed?”

“Unknown.”

“Who closed them?”

“Unknown.”

“Why?”

“Unknown.”

Rez looked toward Ner.

“You must love this thing.”

Ner glared.

The water rippled violently.

Every threshold disappeared.

A black line cut across the map.

Moving.

Toward Vesper.

The construct’s translucent core flared.

“Unauthorized breach.”

Aurelia immediately pulled Zee backward.

Lucien turned toward the avenue.

“From where?”

No answer.

The black line moved faster.

Zareth spread his wings as far as the chamber allowed.

Teal-and-Gold Mana ignited.

Vale drew his sword.

Caldrin drew both of his.

Rez moved in front of Ner.

Ner shoved him sideways.

“I can stand by myself.”

“I know.”

“Then stop standing in front of me.”

“I am older.”

“That is becoming your entire personality.”

The wall behind the central pool rippled.

Not cracked.

Rippled.

Like stone becoming water.

Something came through.

Six hooked limbs first.

Then bone armor.

Then smoke.

The creature dragged itself into the chamber without disturbing a single loose stone.

No heartbeat.

No ordinary blood.

No scent.

Zee felt it only through the deeper perception beneath his other senses.

“There.”

The first Vault Predator turned toward him.

Three more emerged behind it.

Then five.

The construct spoke.

“Vault Predators.”

Rez stared.

“You have a name for them?”

“Designation.”

“Can they be killed?”

A pause.

“Eventually.”

Caldrin smiled.

“I have changed my mind. I like it again.”

The predators attacked.

Rez moved first.

Blue-White Mana spread across the floor in a wide arc and struck two predators from the side, changing their direction rather than trying to overpower them.

“Left!”

Vale and Caldrin were already there.

Vale caught one bone limb against his sword.

Caldrin drove a blade between two armored plates.

The knife passed through smoke.

He cursed.

“Less physical than advertised.”

Zee felt where the creature truly existed beneath the haze.

“Lower!”

Caldrin changed angle.

This time steel struck something.

The predator screamed.

Ner raised both hands.

Pure Golden Mana spread between the columns and sealed the space behind three creatures.

They tried slipping into smoke.

The gold compressed around them.

Not destroying.

Limiting.

“Now!”

Zareth launched.

True Dragon strength carried him across the chamber.

His claws struck one predator hard enough to tear bone armor free.

Teal-and-Gold Dragonfire followed.

The creature shrieked.

Aurelia cast from the opposite side.

Witchcraft first.

A sharp violet binding snapped around two limbs.

Then something deeper moved beneath her spell.

Dark crimson-red Dragon energy flashed through it.

Lucien saw.

So did Zee.

The binding strengthened violently.

The creature crashed into the floor.

Lucien raised a Vesper barrier behind the children just as another predator came through the side wall.

Its claws struck the barrier.

The shield bowed.

Lucien gritted his teeth.

“Move!”

Rez redirected it.

Ner closed the opening.

Vale cut low.

Caldrin cut high.

The predator recoiled.

Zee attacked.

Crimson Mana struck it.

The blast passed through its smoke.

Wrong.

He shifted immediately.

Demonic perception.

Presence.

He found the thing underneath its visible body.

Zee lunged where his eyes told him nothing existed.

His hands closed around something solid.

The predator screamed.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana struck the exposed core.

Zareth hit it from the side.

The creature broke apart.

One down.

The others learned.

A predator came for Zee from above.

He sensed it too late.

Hooked claws tore across his shoulder.

Pain burned through him.

He hit the floor.

Crimson scales spread immediately around the wound.

Permanent patches along his shoulder thickened.

New scales raced toward his upper arm.

The predator struck again.

Its claw scraped scales instead of flesh.

Still painful.

Less damage.

Zee rolled.

Another creature caught him around the ribs.

Six limbs wrapped around his torso.

Pressure increased.

His breath vanished.

Bone cracked.

Not death.

Never death.

Pain.

Crushing.

His body fought to survive while the predator tightened.

Zee’s Crimson Mana surged uselessly through part of its smoke.

He stopped wasting it.

Found the true presence.

Then struck.

Once.

Twice.

The predator squeezed harder.

Another rib cracked.

Zee screamed.

Zareth’s roar shook the Vault.

The Dragon Link flooded with rage.

**Zee. Pain. Break.**

Teal-and-Gold Mana exploded.

“Zareth, wait!”

Too late.

The dragon slammed into the predator.

Its grip loosened.

Zee tore free and rolled across stone.

His ribs had already begun knitting.

Slow enough to hurt.

Fast enough to keep him moving.

No resurrection.

Nothing returned because nothing had ended.

He stood.

Blood ran down his side.

The predator attacked his head.

One hooked limb closed around Zee’s developing horn.

Agony exploded through his skull.

Something answered.

Not Witch.

Not Vampire.

Not Wolf.

Crimson Dragon energy erupted from the horn.

The predator’s limb began burning from the point of contact.

Not Zareth’s fire.

Not Aurelia’s.

Crimson.

Zee’s.

The creature recoiled.

Zee fell to one knee and grabbed his head.

“Do that again,” Rez shouted, “but preferably without letting it grab your horn first!”

Zee glared.

“Helpful!”

Ner trapped another predator inside a shrinking Golden boundary.

“It is more useful than what you are doing!”

“I am bleeding!”

“You do that all the time!”

Rez laughed.

A predator nearly took his head off while he was distracted.

Lucien’s barrier caught it.

“Perhaps fewer jokes!”

“Yes, Father!”

“No promises!” Zee shouted.

Aurelia looked toward him.

“Zee!”

“Sorry!”

Caldrin laughed while stabbing something.

The creatures kept coming.

Not endlessly.

But enough.

Aurelia stopped holding back entirely.

Witch Mana surrounded her hands.

Dark red Dragon energy moved beneath it in thin flashes.

She did not transform.

She did not need to.

Both natures were present.

Both awake.

The construct’s words returned to Zee.

**Two awake.**

He understood that much.

Aurelia was complete in both parts.

Zee was not.

Four.

Three awake.

His scales did not change that.

Neither did his horns.

Neither did the Dragon energy moving through his blood.

Something inside him was still sleeping by whatever standard the Vault understood.

A predator rushed Ner.

Rez blasted it sideways.

Ner sealed the wall before it could escape.

Zareth attacked.

The creature dissolved into smoke.

Zee felt where it moved.

“Behind Rez!”

Rez ducked.

Vale’s sword passed over him.

Caldrin followed.

The predator became physical for half a heartbeat.

Aurelia bound it.

Lucien reinforced the binding.

Ner closed the space around it.

Zareth tore away the bone armor.

Zee grabbed the exposed core.

Crimson Mana entered through his hands.

The predator convulsed.

Not absorption.

Not blood evolution.

Just pressure focused exactly where its real body existed.

“Now!”

Rez struck.

Blue-White Mana detonated through the core.

The final Vault Predator collapsed.

Silence hit the chamber.

Zee dropped to one knee.

His ribs hurt.

His shoulder burned.

His horn throbbed.

Aurelia was beside him immediately.

“Look at me.”

“I am fine.”

“You are never allowed to say that while bleeding.”

“That seems unfair.”

She touched his ribs carefully.

He winced.

“Cracked.”

“Less cracked now.”

“That is not a medical term.”

Caldrin sheathed one sword.

“It should be.”

The construct flickered.

“Breach ended.”

Lucien stared at it.

“You could have warned us those creatures existed.”

“They did not.”

Caldrin raised an eyebrow.

“Until?”

“Door opened.”

Everyone looked toward Ner.

His eyes widened.

“That is not my fault.”

Zee looked toward him.

“No.”

Ner relaxed.

Zee grinned.

“It is ours.”

Ner shoved him.

Zee winced.

“My ribs!”

“You deserved that.”

Rez pointed between them.

“This is why neither of you gets sole credit.”

Zareth sent through the Link:

**Mine.**

Zee stared.

“You did not open anything.”

Zareth showed him an image of himself breaking the wall.

Rez laughed.

“He still thinks that would have worked.”

Aurelia closed her eyes.

“We are leaving.”

No one argued.

This time.

---

The bronze door remained open behind them.

Lucien did not order it destroyed.

He did not know whether it could be.

Instead, he ordered the entire lower approach sealed behind multiple guarded checkpoints.

No one entered alone.

No one touched the Vault without permission.

No one experimented with the thresholds.

Especially not the children.

Rez objected to that description.

Lucien ignored him.

As they reached the upper palace, Lucien stopped beside Aurelia.

“You are Dragon-Witch.”

Aurelia looked at him.

“Yes.”

“You planned to tell me?”

“No.”

Lucien absorbed that.

Caldrin passed behind them.

“I suspected.”

Lucien looked toward him.

“You have mentioned that.”

“I wanted to make sure history records it.”

Vale shoved him forward.

Lucien returned his attention to Aurelia.

“You trusted my kingdom with your son.”

“Yes.”

“But not with this.”

Aurelia’s gaze did not waver.

“They are different secrets.”

Lucien was silent.

Then nodded once.

“I may not like that answer.”

“You do not have to.”

“No.”

He looked exhausted.

“But I have an ancient Vault under my kingdom, disappearing thresholds across the world, creatures walking through stone, and a son who believes seventeen makes him invincible.”

Rez frowned.

“I have never said invincible.”

Lucien looked at him.

“You followed three ten-year-olds into a forbidden underground Vault.”

Rez considered.

“Fair.”

Ner looked toward Zee.

“You called it ours.”

Zee shrugged.

“We both opened it.”

“I did most of it.”

“You were the key.”

Ner stopped walking.

Zee smiled.

Ner punched him in the arm.

Rez laughed.

Zareth sent approval through the Link.

For the first time since entering the Vault, Zee felt light.

Then Aurelia touched his shoulder.

“Tonight.”

He looked up.

“What?”

“We talk.”

His smile disappeared.

Aurelia held his gaze.

“About my blood.”

Zee looked toward the faint scales still visible along her wrist.

House Vesper knew something now.

Lucien knew.

Vale knew.

The royal witch knew.

Caldrin had apparently decided suspicion counted as knowledge.

But Zee understood there was more.

A name.

A history.

A reason his mother had spent decades hiding half of herself.

Zee nodded.

For once, he did not argue.

Because the question waiting for him tonight was not about Victor.

Not about the prophecy.

Not about the Blood Rain.

Not about why the world feared him.

For once, part of the answer to who Zee Darkheart was might begin with his mother.

# Chapter Twenty-Eight

## The Blood Before Darkheart

Aurelia took Zee beyond Vesper’s walls after nightfall.

Not far.

Only north, past the final patrol road and into the high cliffs where pine forest gave way to open stone.

Zareth came with them.

Of course he did.

Rez tried.

Aurelia refused.

Ner asked once, heard the answer, then told Zee he expected every detail that did not belong to Aurelia alone.

Zee promised nothing.

Ner told him he was a terrible friend.

Rez told Ner that Zee had always been terrible.

Zareth stole Rez’s glove while they were arguing.

That ended the conversation.

Now only Aurelia, Zee, and Zareth stood beneath a clear night sky.

Vesper glowed faintly in the valley behind them.

Zee sat near the cliff edge with his knees pulled toward his chest.

His ribs had finished repairing.

The torn shoulder had closed.

Only dried blood remained on the shirt Aurelia had ordered him to change twice.

He had ignored her twice.

Zareth lay behind him, enormous crimson body curved around both Zee and the cold wind.

The Dragon Link remained quiet.

Listening.

Aurelia stood several feet away.

For a long moment, she watched the moon.

Then she spoke.

“House Darkheart is not where my story begins.”

Zee looked up.

“I thought you were born there.”

“I was.”

“Then how can it not begin there?”

Aurelia smiled faintly.

“Birthplace and beginning are not always the same.”

Zee thought about that.

Then raised one finger.

“You said I could ask questions.”

“I have not said that yet.”

“You were going to.”

Aurelia stared.

Zareth sent amusement.

Zee smiled.

Aurelia sighed.

“You may ask questions.”

“Good.”

His hand shot up again.

“What is your Dragon family called?”

“That quickly?”

“You said questions.”

“I did.”

Aurelia sat across from him.

Her expression became quieter.

“House Veyrath.”

The name settled between them.

Zareth lifted his head.

The Dragon Link offered nothing.

No recognition.

No remembered Drakonis history close enough for him to understand.

Zee noticed.

“Zareth does not know it.”

“I would not expect him to.”

“Why?”

“Because House Veyrath was never part of House Drakonis.”

Zee frowned.

“Enemies?”

“Sometimes.”

“Friends?”

“Sometimes.”

“Which one?”

Aurelia almost smiled.

“Both, depending on the century.”

“That is stupid.”

“That is politics.”

“That is what I said.”

Aurelia laughed.

Zareth’s head lowered again.

Zee continued.

“So we are not related to Zareth?”

“Not through my immediate bloodline.”

“Good.”

Zareth opened one eye.

Zee looked toward him.

“You are annoying enough already.”

The Dragon Link returned an image of Zee falling into Lucien’s ornamental pond.

“That happened once.”

Zareth added a second memory.

Another pond.

Zee frowned.

“Twice.”

Aurelia smiled despite herself.

Then Zee became serious.

“What made Veyrath different?”

Aurelia looked toward her hands.

“Compatibility.”

“With what?”

“Dragon nature and witchcraft.”

Zee leaned forward.

“Like you.”

“Yes.”

“House Veyrath had Dragon-Witches?”

“Eventually.”

“How?”

Aurelia paused.

“Not one single way.”

Zee waited.

She had promised truth, not everything.

“Veyrath Dragons possessed an unusual ability to coexist with certain forms of witch blood without one nature destroying or suppressing the other.”

“And you were born with both?”

“Yes.”

“A real Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“A real witch.”

“Yes.”

“Not half of each.”

Aurelia looked directly at him.

“No.”

“Both.”

“Both.”

Zee smiled faintly.

He understood that word.

Better than most.

“What happened to them?”

The smile vanished from Aurelia’s face.

“House Veyrath was hunted.”

Zee became still.

Hunted.

That language belonged to him.

“By dragons?”

“Some.”

“Witches?”

“Some.”

“Why?”

“Fear.”

“That is not enough.”

“No.”

Aurelia looked toward the distant mountains.

“Some wanted Veyrath destroyed because Dragon-Witch blood challenged rules they believed should never be crossed.”

“Some wanted our knowledge.”

“Some wanted our blood.”

“Some had older political reasons that had nothing to do with what we were.”

Zee thought of his own enemies.

Kings.

Hunters.

Researchers.

Vampires.

Demons.

People who wanted money.

People who wanted answers.

Not one reason.

Never one reason.

“How many Veyrath are left?”

Aurelia’s face tightened.

“I do not know.”

Zee looked at her.

“Are you the last?”

“I do not know.”

“You really do not?”

“No.”

That answer mattered.

She was not making certainty where none existed.

“I know some died.”

“I know some disappeared.”

“I know some learned to hide.”

Aurelia looked toward him.

“I was one of them.”

Zee touched one of his horns.

“So you hid the Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“For how long?”

“Most of my life.”

“Even from Father?”

“At first.”

Zee’s expression changed.

“Victor did not know?”

“No.”

“When you met?”

“No.”

“When you married him?”

Aurelia hesitated.

“Not immediately.”

Zee looked almost offended on Victor’s behalf before remembering who they were discussing.

“When did you tell him?”

“When I trusted him enough.”

“Why?”

“Because I loved him.”

Zee frowned.

“That seems dangerous.”

“It was.”

“Was it stupid?”

Aurelia laughed quietly.

“Sometimes love is.”

Zee watched her.

“What did he do?”

“When I told him?”

“Yes.”

“Nothing terrible.”

Zee blinked.

That was clearly not the answer he expected.

“He kept my secret.”

“For how long?”

“Years.”

“He did not tell House Darkheart?”

“No.”

“Did he hate that you were Dragon?”

“No.”

“Fear you?”

“Not then.”

Aurelia looked toward Vesper’s distant lights.

“Victor was not always the man you know through other people’s pain.”

Zee became quiet.

He had grown up hearing fragments of his father.

King.

Husband.

Enemy.

The first person who ever killed him.

The only one who ever would.

It was easier when Victor existed as one thing.

Monster.

But Aurelia would not let him become simple.

“When did it change?”

“Gradually.”

“Because of me?”

Aurelia looked sharply at him.

“Not because you did anything.”

“But after I was born.”

“Yes.”

Zee nodded.

He had stopped confusing sequence with blame years ago.

Mostly.

“The Blood Rain.”

“Yes.”

“The prophecy.”

“Yes.”

“The kingdoms.”

“Yes.”

“My three natures.”

“Yes.”

“And then he remembered you were Dragon too.”

Aurelia’s expression tightened.

“Fear changes the meaning of things.”

Zee looked toward her.

“You said people become what they keep choosing.”

“I did.”

“Father kept choosing fear.”

“Yes.”

“Even when he loved us.”

Aurelia was quiet.

“Yes.”

Zee looked away.

“That is stupid.”

Aurelia touched his hair.

“Sometimes.”

They sat quietly.

Then Zee asked, “Did he think your Dragon blood made me worse?”

Aurelia did not answer quickly.

Eventually:

“He wondered whether there were things inside you none of us could see.”

Zee touched the crimson-black scales at his neck.

“He was right.”

“That does not make what he chose right.”

Zee looked at her.

Aurelia continued.

“Fear can accidentally notice a truth and still build a lie around it.”

Zee thought about that longer than she expected.

Then his expression became uncertain.

“Mother?”

“Yes?”

“Am I four things?”

Aurelia looked at him.

The Vault’s words lingered.

Four.

Three awake.

“Yes.”

Zee stared.

“But I am the First Natural Tribrid.”

“Yes.”

“That makes no sense.”

“It does.”

“How?”

Aurelia moved closer.

“You were born carrying four natural blood natures.”

She touched the center of his chest.

“Witch.”

“Vampire.”

“Wolf.”

“Dragon.”

Zee looked down.

“At birth?”

“All four were yours.”

“But only three—”

“Woke with you.”

He looked back up.

“Witch, Vampire, Wolf.”

“Yes.”

“Dragon slept.”

“Yes.”

“Then the Vault…”

“Four.”

Aurelia held his gaze.

“Three awake.”

Zee looked toward Zareth.

The Dragon Crown Prince lifted his head.

Zee’s Crimson Mana stirred.

Teal-and-Gold Mana answered faintly beneath Zareth’s scales.

Aurelia continued.

“The world saw what was active.”

“Witch.”

“Vampire.”

“Wolf.”

“The impossible child born complete in all three.”

“That is why you became known as the First Natural Tribrid.”

Zee touched one horn.

“And Dragon was already there.”

“Yes.”

“Mine.”

“Yes.”

“Not Zareth’s.”

“No.”

Zareth sent offense through the Link.

Zee grinned.

“I did not say yours was bad.”

Zareth answered with the clear concept:

**Mine better.**

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“Your horns are ugly.”

Zareth growled.

Aurelia ignored them.

“Zareth did not give you Dragon blood.”

Zee looked back at her.

“He wakes it.”

“We think his presence helps stimulate what was already inside you.”

“The Link.”

“Possibly.”

“His Mana.”

“Possibly.”

“Being born the same day.”

“Possibly.”

Zee frowned.

“That is a lot of possibly.”

“It is the truth.”

He sighed.

“Fine.”

Aurelia touched one crimson scale.

“Your Dragon nature belongs to you.”

“It does not replace anything.”

“You are still Witch.”

“Still Vampire.”

“Still Wolf.”

“And Dragon.”

“Yes.”

Zee sat with that.

Then something quieter entered his face.

Aurelia noticed immediately.

“What?”

“Sometimes…”

He stopped.

“What?”

Zee stared at his hands.

“I feel like too many things.”

No grand declaration.

No tears.

Just a ten-year-old boy admitting something he did not know how to explain.

“Everyone has one thing they are supposed to be.”

“Ner is a witch.”

“Rez is a witch.”

“Zareth is a Dragon.”

“You are two things.”

Zee looked at her.

“I keep getting more.”

Aurelia moved beside him.

“You are not a pile of pieces.”

“That sounds like a mother answer.”

“It is.”

“Is it true?”

“Yes.”

“How do you know?”

“Because I knew you before anyone taught you names for yourself.”

Zee looked at her.

“You were Zee before anyone called you Tribrid.”

“Before anyone called you monster.”

“Before anyone called you prince.”

“Before you had horns.”

“Before the world decided what your existence meant.”

She touched his cheek.

“You are still Zee.”

Zareth pressed his snout into Zee’s shoulder.

The Link carried the same simple certainty.

**Zee.**

Nothing else.

Zee smiled faintly.

“That was also a Dragon answer.”

Aurelia smiled.

“Apparently he agrees with me.”

“Rare.”

Zareth shoved him.

Zee shoved back.

For a moment, the weight disappeared.

Then Zee looked at Aurelia.

“Show me.”

Her smile faded.

“My Dragon.”

“No.”

Zee’s face fell.

“Why?”

Aurelia looked around the empty cliffs.

Then back toward distant Vesper.

Zee saw the hesitation.

His eyes widened.

“You are going to.”

“I did not say that.”

“You looked around.”

“That proves nothing.”

“You sound like Caldrin.”

Aurelia closed her eyes.

“Stay here.”

Zee scrambled upright.

“You are!”

“Sit.”

He sat immediately.

Zareth rose.

Excitement flooded the Link.

Aurelia walked farther onto the open stone.

She stopped beneath the moon.

Then, for the first time in Zee’s life, Queen Aurelia Darkheart allowed the part of herself hidden beneath decades of discipline to emerge completely.

Heat rolled across the cliff.

Scales appeared first.

Dark red.

Deep crimson-red under moonlight.

Near-black shading spread beneath her arms and across her back.

Her body expanded.

Bone changed.

Wings unfolded.

Claws struck stone.

Her neck lengthened.

Her face reshaped.

The transformation continued until the woman Zee knew was gone from human sight.

A true Dragon stood beneath the stars.

Large.

Powerful.

Distinct from every Drakonis Dragon Zee had seen.

Dark red scales covered her body while near-black shading marked the undersides of her wings and parts of her spine.

And woven naturally between the scales were patterns that looked almost like witch sigils.

Not painted.

Not carved.

Born into her.

Magic moved through them.

Dragon and Witch.

Both.

Zee forgot every serious question he had ever asked.

His mouth fell open.

“Mother?”

The Dragon lowered her head.

Same eyes.

Same presence.

Aurelia.

Zee laughed.

Not nervously.

Not politely.

Pure childhood joy exploded out of him.

He ran.

Aurelia barely had time to lower her head before Zee wrapped both arms around her snout.

“You are huge!”

Aurelia released a deep rumble.

“Can you understand me?”

She nodded.

“Can you talk?”

Aurelia gave him a look.

Zee grinned.

“Right.”

Zareth had not moved.

For perhaps the first time in his ten years of life, Crown Prince Zareth Drakonis appeared completely stunned.

He stared at Aurelia.

Then at Zee.

Then back at Aurelia.

The Dragon Link erupted.

**Mother. Dragon.**

“Yes.”

**Hidden.**

“Yes.”

**Years.**

“Yes.”

Zareth looked personally betrayed.

Zee started laughing again.

“You lived with her for ten years and did not know.”

Zareth growled.

“You are a terrible Dragon.”

Zareth lunged.

Zee ran around Aurelia’s foreleg.

Aurelia shifted her head and blocked Zareth.

The young Dragon stopped.

Looked at her.

Then stepped closer.

He sniffed Aurelia.

Once.

Again.

Teal-and-Gold Mana shimmered along his spine.

Not hostile.

Instinct.

Recognition of another Dragon whose blood was completely separate from his own.

Aurelia’s Dragon energy answered.

Dark crimson-red power moved beneath her scales alongside faint witch patterns.

Zee felt both.

The Dragon Link tightened.

Zareth’s Mana.

Aurelia’s full Dragon presence.

Something inside Zee responded.

His smile vanished.

Heat struck his horns.

Zee grabbed them.

“Ow.”

Aurelia turned.

Crimson-black light moved through the developing horns.

His permanent scales brightened.

Then spread.

Across his temples.

Down his neck.

Over both shoulders.

Along his ribs.

Across his forearms.

More than combat usually triggered.

“Mother.”

Aurelia immediately shifted her attention fully toward him.

Zareth moved closer.

The Link flooded with concern.

**Hot. Zee.**

“I know.”

Crimson Dragon energy surged inside Zee’s Crimson Mana.

Not Aurelia’s energy.

Not Zareth’s.

His.

It rolled through him with enough force to make his knees buckle.

Zee fell.

Aurelia changed.

Her massive Dragon body folded rapidly back toward human form.

She reached him before he hit the stone.

“I have you.”

Pain developed beneath Zee’s shoulder blades.

Not a wound.

Pressure.

Internal.

Something pushing against bone and muscle.

He gasped.

“My back.”

Aurelia moved behind him.

Two ridges formed beneath the skin.

One on each side.

Zareth whined.

The Link became frantic.

**Pain. Wrong. Stop.**

“I cannot stop it!”

Aurelia placed both hands against Zee’s shoulders.

“Breathe.”

“Is it wings?”

“I do not know.”

“Mother!”

“I will not lie to you because you are frightened.”

The pressure intensified.

Zee gritted his teeth.

His body wanted to move toward a transformation it could not yet complete.

The fourth nature stirred.

Reached.

Then stopped.

No wings broke free.

No completed Dragon form emerged.

The ridges remained beneath the skin for several painful heartbeats.

Then slowly receded.

Crimson Dragon energy collapsed back into his Mana.

The scales along Zee’s face withdrew.

The permanent ones remained.

His horns cooled.

Zee sagged against Aurelia.

Zareth pushed his snout beneath Zee’s hand.

The Link carried one desperate feeling.

**Stay.**

Zee touched him.

“I am here.”

Aurelia examined his back.

No wound.

Two faint raised lines remained near the shoulder blades.

Not wings.

Possibility.

She stared at them.

Zee noticed her expression.

“What?”

Aurelia looked at him.

“I think both of us affected it.”

“Both?”

“My full Dragon form.”

She looked toward Zareth.

“His Dragon Mana.”

“The Link?”

“Perhaps.”

Zee groaned.

“More possibly.”

“Yes.”

He lay back against her.

“Am I getting wings?”

“Not tonight.”

He looked disappointed.

Aurelia stared at him.

“You were just in pain.”

“Yes.”

“And you are disappointed.”

“I want wings.”

Zareth sent smug approval.

Aurelia shook her head.

“You are both impossible.”

Zee smiled.

Then Zareth went still.

The Dragon Link changed instantly.

No humor.

No pain.

Warning.

**Dragon.**

Aurelia sensed it a heartbeat later.

Her head turned toward the forest below.

Zee inhaled.

He smelled it too.

Dragon.

But not Zareth.

Not Drakonis.

Not Aurelia.

Different.

Aurelia rose slowly.

Something changed in her face.

Not fear exactly.

Recognition approaching before sight.

A branch moved beneath the trees.

Footsteps followed.

A man emerged into moonlight.

Tall.

Silver hair fell past his shoulders.

His eyes carried a dark red Dragon glow.

He wore no Drakonis colors.

No Vesper crest.

No Darkheart sigil.

Aurelia went completely still.

Zee looked toward his mother.

“Mother?”

The stranger did not look at Zee.

Not first.

His attention belonged entirely to Aurelia.

For a long moment, neither moved.

Then the man spoke.

“Aurelia Veyrath.”

The name struck harder than any spell.

Aurelia stepped in front of Zee and Zareth.

Her hands began glowing with Witch Mana.

Dragon energy moved beneath it.

Her voice dropped.

“You should be dead.”

The stranger smiled.

“So should our bloodline.”

Silence consumed the cliff.

Only then did his attention shift.

Past Aurelia.

Toward Zee.

His eyes moved over the ten-year-old boy.

Crimson eyes.

Developing crimson-black horns.

Permanent Crimson scales.

The faint residual Dragon energy still moving beneath them.

Recognition entered the stranger’s face.

Not recognition of Zee’s full nature.

Not understanding of the First Natural Tribrid.

Recognition of something older.

Blood.

Veyrath.

His gaze returned briefly to Aurelia.

Then back to Zee.

“Well.”

Aurelia’s body tightened.

The stranger’s smile changed.

“You really did have a son.”

Zareth stepped beside Zee.

Teal-and-Gold Mana rolled over his scales.

The stranger noticed the Drakonis prince too, but offered no explanation.

No prophecy.

No answer for the Dragon Link.

No secret knowledge of Zee’s birth.

Whatever had brought this man to the cliffs had begun long before Zee Darkheart opened his crimson eyes beneath Blood Rain.

This was not one of Zee’s hunters.

Not yet.

He had not come because of Victor.

He had not come because of the Twelve Crowns.

He had not come because of a bounty, an experiment, or the prophecy.

He had come for Aurelia Veyrath.

For House Veyrath.

For a past Zee had only begun to discover.

And for the first time in Zee Darkheart’s life, the danger standing before him belonged to his mother before it belonged to him.

# Chapter Twenty-Nine

## The Ghost of Veyrath

Zee’s Dragon nature had not awakened all at once.

It had begun around his second year.

Before then, the fourth blood nature inside him had remained quiet—present from birth, inherited naturally from Aurelia, but buried beneath the three supernatural natures that had opened their eyes with him.

Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Zareth had been beside him from the beginning.

The Dragon Link, the constant presence of Teal-and-Gold Dragon Mana, their shared emotions, their fights, their closeness—all of it had quietly pressed against something already sleeping inside Zee.

At two, his body had begun answering.

First came abnormal heat.

Then temporary Crimson scales.

Durability that exceeded even what his other three natures should have given him.

Later, some scales stopped disappearing.

Horn buds followed.

Then Crimson Dragon energy.

Zee’s body had always adapted too quickly.

What might have taken decades in another bloodline had spent eight years growing inside a Natural Tribrid whose existence refused to remain still.

Yet the Convergence Vault had made one truth painfully clear.

**Four.**

**Three awake.**

Whatever Dragon was becoming inside Zee...

it had not finished waking.

Now, beneath the moonlit cliffs outside House Vesper, one of the dead had apparently come looking for it.

Not Zee’s dead.

Aurelia’s.

---

“You should be dead.”

Aurelia’s voice did not shake.

That frightened Zee more than if it had.

The silver-haired stranger remained several yards away beneath the trees, dark red eyes fixed upon her.

“So should our bloodline.”

Zareth moved beside Zee.

Teal-and-Gold Dragon Mana threaded between his scales.

The Dragon Link carried a sharp command.

**Behind.**

Zee frowned.

“No.”

Zareth turned his head.

**Danger. Behind.**

“I heard you.”

He stayed exactly where he was.

Zareth sent an image of biting him.

Zee would normally have argued.

Not tonight.

The stranger finally looked toward the Crown Prince of Drakonis.

Recognition touched his face.

“Drakonis.”

Zareth growled.

The man looked back at Aurelia.

“You keep unusual company.”

Aurelia’s Witch Mana gathered around both hands.

“And you still speak too much.”

The stranger smiled.

That smile carried familiarity.

Not affection.

History.

Zee saw it immediately.

“You know him.”

Aurelia did not look away.

“Yes.”

“Who is he?”

The stranger answered for himself.

“Someone your mother once trusted.”

Aurelia’s magic intensified.

“Do not speak to him.”

Zee looked between them.

That answered more than either realized.

The man noticed the scales along Zee’s temples again.

His gaze lingered on the crimson-black horns.

Curiosity.

Then confusion.

Not understanding.

Good.

He did not know what Zee was.

Not completely.

“Those are Veyrath traits,” he said.

Aurelia moved one step sideways, blocking more of Zee from view.

“They are his.”

The stranger’s expression shifted.

“Protective distinction.”

“Necessary distinction.”

Zee looked up at his mother.

He understood what she meant.

Not Veyrath scales copied onto him.

Not Zareth’s Dragon nature given to him.

His.

Everything inside Zee became Zee eventually.

The stranger looked toward the remnants of Crimson Dragon energy flickering around Zee’s horns.

“That is not how ours looked.”

Aurelia’s eyes narrowed.

“Ours?”

For the first time, the man’s confidence weakened.

Aurelia noticed.

“You have been gone too long to call anything ours.”

The stranger’s jaw tightened.

Zee watched carefully.

“You really thought he was dead.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because I saw enough to believe it.”

The stranger laughed quietly.

“You saw what they wanted survivors to see.”

Aurelia went still.

Zee hated that sentence.

“Who are *they*?”

Neither answered him.

Zee crossed his arms.

“I am standing right here.”

Aurelia glanced down.

“Zee.”

“You promised truth.”

“I promised truth about your blood.”

“This seems related.”

The stranger smiled.

“He has your persistence.”

“He has nothing from you.”

The smile vanished.

Zee caught that too.

Interesting.

“Mother.”

Aurelia exhaled slowly.

Then spoke without lowering her magic.

“His name is Sevran Veyrath.”

Zee looked at him.

Sevran.

The name stirred nothing.

No inherited Dragon memory.

No sudden recognition.

No magical revelation.

Just a man from a family Zee had only learned existed hours ago.

“How are you related?”

Aurelia answered.

“Cousin.”

Sevran’s expression hardened.

“Was.”

Zee frowned.

“You stop being cousins?”

Caldrin would have enjoyed the question.

Aurelia almost did.

“Blood does not stop.”

Sevran replied coldly.

“Families do.”

Zareth shifted.

The Dragon Link carried a memory-fragment from minutes earlier.

Aurelia in true Dragon form.

Then Sevran.

Then the smell shared between them.

Similar.

Not same.

Veyrath.

Zee understood.

“You are a Dragon too.”

Sevran looked at him.

“Yes.”

“A witch?”

A pause.

“No.”

That interested Zee.

“So not everyone in House Veyrath was Dragon-Witch.”

“No.”

Aurelia’s voice remained guarded.

“Compatibility did not mean every Veyrath carried both natures.”

Sevran looked at her sharply.

“You told him.”

“Tonight.”

“How much?”

“What belongs to him.”

“Then he knows very little.”

Zee immediately disliked him.

“I know enough to know Mother does not want you here.”

Sevran’s dark red eyes returned to him.

“You speak boldly for a child.”

Zee frowned.

“I am a child.”

Sevran blinked.

Apparently that answer had not occurred to him.

Zee continued.

“People keep saying that like I am supposed to be embarrassed.”

Zareth sent amusement.

Aurelia’s mouth almost moved.

Almost.

Sevran studied Zee longer.

Not as a legendary Tribrid.

Not yet.

As Aurelia’s son.

That somehow felt more invasive.

“What did Victor father?”

The cliff changed.

Aurelia’s magic erupted.

Zee barely saw her move.

One moment she stood beside him.

The next her hand was around Sevran’s throat.

She drove him into a tree hard enough to split the trunk.

Dark red Dragon energy flashed beneath her skin.

Sevran’s eyes widened.

Zareth surged forward.

Zee did too.

Aurelia snarled.

“Speak about my son like that again.”

Sevran grabbed her wrist.

His own Dragon strength surfaced.

The ground cracked beneath his boots.

“I did not come to insult him.”

“You came uninvited.”

“Because every other Veyrath path is watched.”

“By whom?”

Sevran looked toward Zee.

Aurelia tightened her grip.

“Eyes on me.”

He obeyed.

“Release me.”

“Answer.”

“Aurelia.”

“Answer.”

Something in Sevran’s face broke.

Not physically.

Emotionally.

“You still think the hunt ended.”

Aurelia froze.

Zee saw it.

“The Veyrath hunt?”

Sevran looked toward him despite Aurelia’s warning.

“Yes.”

Aurelia released him.

Sevran dropped to one knee, coughing.

She stepped back.

Zee came immediately beside her.

Aurelia placed one arm across his chest without looking.

Not pushing him away.

Keeping him close.

“Explain,” she said.

Sevran stood slowly.

“No.”

Zee stared.

Aurelia’s expression became dangerous.

Sevran continued.

“Not here.”

“You came here.”

“I followed your Dragon signature after it appeared tonight.”

Aurelia’s face changed.

Her transformation.

Zee understood immediately.

“You felt Mother become a Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“How far away?”

Sevran looked toward the eastern mountains.

“Far enough.”

Aurelia cursed quietly.

For decades she had hidden her true form.

Tonight she revealed it for Zee.

And someone had felt it.

Zee’s excitement from earlier curdled into guilt.

“If I had not asked—”

“No.”

Aurelia turned toward him immediately.

“This is not yours.”

“But—”

“No.”

Her voice softened.

“I chose to show you.”

Sevran watched them.

Something unreadable crossed his expression.

Then he looked toward Zareth.

“And his Mana helped amplify it.”

Zareth growled.

Sevran raised one hand.

“I am not blaming him.”

“Good,” Zee said.

Sevran looked at him.

“Protective.”

Zee shrugged.

“He is mine.”

Zareth’s head snapped toward him.

Zee corrected himself quickly.

“My friend.”

The Link carried deep offense.

**Prince.**

“My very annoying prince friend.”

Zareth settled.

Sevran stared at them.

“The Link is real.”

Aurelia’s expression hardened again.

“You know nothing about it.”

“No.”

That answer surprised her.

Sevran looked between the two ten-year-olds.

“I felt something when I approached.”

“What?”

“I do not know.”

Zee almost smiled.

Finally.

Someone else willing to say it.

Sevran continued.

“But your son’s Dragon nature reacts to the Drakonis prince.”

Aurelia stepped closer.

“We already know.”

“You know it reacts.”

Sevran’s gaze dropped to Zee’s horns.

“You do not know what happens when it finishes.”

Neither did he.

Zee heard that immediately.

“You do not either.”

Sevran looked at him.

“No.”

Aurelia’s shoulders eased by the smallest amount.

Sevran was not here with answers.

Only danger.

Those were different problems.

“Why did you come?” she asked.

Sevran looked toward the forest.

“To warn you.”

“About House Veyrath?”

“About what remains of it.”

Aurelia’s face tightened.

Zee listened.

Sevran continued.

“The survivors did not stay together.”

“Some hid.”

“Some were captured.”

“Some joined the people who hunted us.”

Aurelia’s eyes went cold.

“Names.”

“Not here.”

“You keep saying that.”

“Because we have been standing in the open for too long.”

Zareth suddenly turned.

The Dragon Link flashed.

**Movement.**

Zee heard it next.

Heartbeats.

Several.

Far below.

Not Vesper patrol rhythm.

Different.

Aurelia saw Zee’s face.

“How many?”

He listened.

“Seven.”

Then another.

“Nine.”

Sevran cursed.

“They followed me.”

Aurelia’s hand closed around his coat and yanked him forward.

“You brought them to my son?”

“I did not know they were still on me.”

“Who?”

Sevran looked toward the forest.

“I do not know which group.”

Zee frowned.

“That is not helpful.”

“No.”

Aurelia’s Witch Mana spread.

Dark violet lines disappeared through the earth.

Searching.

Zee felt Zareth’s Mana rising beside him.

Sevran began shifting.

Scales appeared along his jaw.

Dark red.

Different from Aurelia’s.

Different from Zee’s.

Aurelia grabbed his shoulder.

“No full transformation.”

Sevran looked at her.

“If they found me—”

“If you become a Dragon here, everyone within miles sees you.”

He stopped.

Aurelia looked toward Zee.

“Back to Vesper.”

“No.”

“Zee.”

“They followed him here.”

“Yes.”

“So they will follow us there.”

Aurelia paused.

He was right.

Zee continued.

“If we run straight home, we show them where.”

“Vesper is not hidden.”

“No, but why help them?”

Sevran stared at him.

“He thinks tactically.”

“He has had practice,” Aurelia said.

That sentence carried no pride.

Only grief.

Zee heard it.

Then one of the approaching heartbeats stopped.

Not death.

Stillness.

Hidden.

Another stopped.

Then another.

“They know I can hear them.”

Aurelia’s expression sharpened.

That meant preparation.

Whoever followed Sevran had information.

Maybe about Veyrath.

Maybe Zee.

Maybe neither.

Zee reached for the presence sense beneath his ordinary hearing.

There.

Nine figures spreading through the forest.

One was strange.

No normal heartbeat.

Not demon either.

Zee frowned.

“One is different.”

Sevran looked at him.

“How?”

“I do not know.”

“What do you sense?”

“Something alive.”

“That narrows it down terribly.”

Zee glared.

Aurelia almost smiled despite everything.

Then the first bolt came from the trees.

Not at Zee.

At Sevran.

He moved.

The projectile struck stone.

A black chain exploded from it.

Sevran’s face changed.

“Down!”

More bolts followed.

Zareth spread one wing in front of Zee.

Aurelia threw up a violet barrier.

The black chains hit it.

They did not break through.

They wrapped around the spell.

Then began tightening.

Aurelia’s face hardened.

“They adapted.”

Sevran looked at her.

“To Veyrath magic.”

Not Zee.

Not Vesper.

Not Ner.

Not Rez.

This hunt had its own history.

The barrier cracked.

Aurelia dropped it deliberately before the chains could collapse around them.

“Move!”

They scattered.

Figures entered the moonlight.

Seven wore gray armor without crests.

Two wore dark robes.

None carried the symbols of Zee’s known enemies.

The nearest raised a curved weapon.

“Sevran Veyrath.”

Sevran’s jaw tightened.

“You found me.”

“We never lost you.”

Aurelia glanced toward him.

He looked away.

That answer would require discussion later.

The hunter’s attention moved toward Aurelia.

He stopped.

For the first time, genuine surprise appeared.

“Aurelia.”

Not Darkheart.

Not Queen.

Just Aurelia.

The others shifted.

Recognition spread.

One whispered:

“She lives.”

Zee felt his mother become very still beside him.

The hunter smiled.

“This night improves.”

Then he noticed Zee.

The smile weakened.

Not because he knew what Zee was.

Because he saw the horns.

The scales.

A child standing beside Aurelia Veyrath.

“What is that?”

Zee’s expression changed.

Zareth snarled.

Aurelia stepped forward.

“My son.”

The hunter stared.

Understanding came only that far.

Aurelia.

Son.

Veyrath blood.

Nothing more.

Then greed entered his face.

“Take all three.”

Zee counted.

Three.

Aurelia.

Sevran.

Him.

Not Zareth.

The Dragon Prince was collateral.

Zee almost laughed.

Someone had finally arrived underestimating the wrong Dragon.

Zareth felt it.

The Link carried delighted violence.

**Now bite?**

Zee’s fangs showed.

“Now.”

Zareth attacked.

Teal-and-Gold Dragonfire tore across the cliff.

The hunters scattered.

Aurelia cast simultaneously.

Her Witch Mana struck the black chains and pulled them apart before they could reform.

Sevran slammed into the nearest armored man with enough force to drive him through a boulder.

Zee ran straight toward the second.

The hunter saw a ten-year-old boy.

That mistake lasted less than a second.

Zee ducked under the curved blade.

Wolf instinct read the man’s balance.

Vampire speed closed distance.

His fist struck armor.

Crimson Mana followed.

The chest plate dented inward.

The hunter flew backward.

Zee looked at his hand.

His scales had expanded.

The Dragon nature stirred.

Not fully awake.

Still useful.

Another hunter came from behind.

Aurelia shouted.

Zee turned too late.

The black chain wrapped around his torso.

It tightened.

Mana suppression followed.

Crimson light dimmed around him.

Pain crushed into his ribs.

But Zee remained standing.

The hunter pulled.

“Got you.”

Zee looked down at the chain.

Then at him.

“No.”

The man pulled harder.

Zee’s ribs compressed.

Pain sharpened.

His body adapted beneath it.

Crimson scales spread under the chain.

The suppression disrupted his Mana.

So Zee stopped relying on Mana.

He grabbed the chain with both hands.

Vampire strength.

Wolf muscle.

Dragon durability beginning beneath both.

He pulled back.

The hunter stumbled.

Zee yanked again.

The man flew toward him.

Zee headbutted him.

His juvenile horn struck the helmet.

Metal cracked.

Zee immediately grabbed his forehead.

“Ow!”

Zareth sent laughter through the Link while fighting two hunters.

“Shut up!”

Aurelia heard him.

“Focus!”

“I am!”

The strange heartbeat-less attacker moved.

Zee sensed it near his mother.

“Behind you!”

Aurelia turned.

Too late.

A gray blade cut across her side.

Blood hit stone.

Zee stopped.

Everything inside him changed.

“Mother.”

Aurelia staggered.

Not dying.

Wounded.

But blood was enough.

The hunter raised the blade again.

Zee moved.

Not with careful thought.

Not training.

Rage.

Crimson Mana exploded from him.

His horns burned.

Scales raced across his shoulders and neck.

The faint ridges beneath his shoulder blades tightened painfully.

His Dragon energy surged beside the three natures that had protected him since birth.

The black chain around him shattered.

Zee hit the attacker hard enough to carry them both across the cliff.

They crashed.

The hunter’s weapon skidded away.

Zee landed on top.

His fist rose.

Then Aurelia’s voice reached him.

“Zee.”

His hand stopped.

The hunter beneath him breathed rapidly.

Fear.

Zee wanted to hit him again.

Aurelia’s blood was still in the air.

“Zee.”

He looked back.

She stood.

One hand pressed to her side.

Alive.

Watching him.

Not afraid of him.

Never afraid of him.

“Come here.”

Zee’s fist remained raised.

Zareth’s Link pressed against his mind.

**Mother. Alive. Zee. Stop.**

Slowly, Zee lowered his hand.

He stood.

The hunter tried reaching for a hidden blade.

Zee kicked it away.

“Do not make me regret listening to my mother.”

Caldrin would have been proud.

The battle ended moments later.

Two hunters escaped into the forest.

Three lay unconscious.

Four were wounded badly enough that Aurelia’s bindings held them.

None carried identifying crests.

Sevran stared after the escapees.

His face had gone pale.

Aurelia noticed.

“You know them.”

“Yes.”

“Who?”

Sevran looked toward the prisoners.

“Not here.”

Zee groaned.

“I hate him.”

Aurelia almost laughed despite the blood on her side.

Sevran looked offended.

“I just helped save you.”

“You brought them.”

“Fair.”

Zareth moved beside Zee.

The Dragon Link carried immediate concern toward Aurelia.

Zee ran to his mother.

Her wound was already being wrapped with cloth from Sevran’s cloak.

Zee touched her arm.

“Are you okay?”

“Yes.”

“Truth.”

Aurelia looked at him.

“It hurts.”

“Bad?”

“Enough.”

Zee’s face tightened.

He hated that answer.

Because it was honest.

He looked down at the blood on her clothes.

The world could not kill him.

But it could still do this.

The lesson was old.

Tonight it felt new again.

Aurelia touched one of his horns.

“You stopped.”

Zee looked away.

“Because you told me.”

“No.”

He looked back.

“Because you chose to.”

Zee did not answer.

Sevran watched them.

Then something in his expression changed.

Not warmth.

Recognition.

Perhaps grief.

“They would have wanted to know you.”

Aurelia’s face hardened.

“Do not.”

Sevran stopped.

Zee looked between them.

“Who?”

Neither answered.

Zee sighed loudly.

“Everyone in this family is annoying.”

Aurelia laughed.

Actually laughed.

Even Sevran smiled.

For three breaths, they were not fugitives or survivors or hidden blood.

Then distant horns sounded from Vesper.

Lucien’s patrols.

The fight had been heard.

Sevran’s expression turned serious again.

“I cannot go inside those walls.”

Aurelia looked at him.

“You are going exactly inside those walls.”

“No.”

“Yes.”

“You have no idea what follows me.”

Aurelia stepped closer.

“You have no idea what follows my son.”

Sevran looked toward Zee.

Zee smiled sweetly.

Zareth bared his teeth.

Sevran considered.

“Fair.”

Aurelia looked toward the captured hunters.

“You came to warn me.”

“Yes.”

“Then you will explain everything you actually know.”

Sevran’s face tightened.

“Not everything belongs to—”

Aurelia’s Witch Mana flashed.

“Try that sentence.”

He stopped.

Zee grinned.

“That is what she does to me.”

“I understand why.”

Aurelia began walking toward Vesper.

Zee stayed beside her.

Zareth followed.

Sevran remained behind for one moment, staring toward the dark forest.

At the people who had found him.

At the bloodline he thought scattered.

At the cousin he thought gone.

Then at the ten-year-old boy carrying Veyrath Dragon blood alongside three other natural supernatural natures Sevran had not even begun to understand.

He followed.

Zee looked back once.

This was not his hunt.

Not originally.

That realization mattered.

For ten years, enemies had crossed kingdoms because of Zee Darkheart.

Tonight, Zee was walking into a war that had started before he existed.

Aurelia’s war.

House Veyrath’s war.

A history buried beneath the name Darkheart.

And for the first time, the hunted prince was not asking how to escape it.

He was wondering who had hurt his mother badly enough to make her hide half of herself from the world.

# Crimson Dynasty — Chapters Thirty & Thirty-One

# Chapter Thirty

## The Blood That Would Not Stay Still

Sevran Veyrath entered House Vesper under guard.

He complained about that before they reached the first gate.

“I came willingly.”

Captain Vale did not look at him.

“You were brought willingly.”

“There is a difference?”

“Yes.”

“What?”

Vale finally glanced over.

“You are surrounded by twenty armed soldiers.”

Caldrin walked on Sevran’s other side.

“And me.”

Sevran looked at the knives strapped across him.

“You count separately?”

“I like to.”

Zee walked ahead with Aurelia.

Zareth remained close enough that one crimson wing occasionally brushed Zee’s shoulder. The Dragon Link had been restless since the fight on the cliffs.

Not because of Sevran.

Because of Aurelia’s blood.

Zee could smell it.

She had already closed the wound in her side with witchcraft and wrapped it tightly beneath her clothes, but knowing she had been cut would not leave his head.

Every few minutes he looked up at her.

Every time, Aurelia noticed.

“I am still here.”

“I know.”

“Then stop checking.”

“I am not checking.”

“You looked at me six times since the gate.”

“Maybe I like looking at you.”

Aurelia raised an eyebrow.

Zee looked away.

Zareth sent amusement through the Link.

Zee glared at him.

“You are supposed to help.”

**Bad lie.**

Zee frowned.

The thought had been clearer than usual.

Not a word exactly.

But close.

The Link kept changing.

So did everything else.

His horns burned again.

Zee grabbed one.

Aurelia stopped.

“What?”

“Nothing.”

“Zee.”

“They are hot.”

“How hot?”

“Hot.”

“That is not useful.”

“They are attached to my head. I do not have a measuring spell.”

Sevran looked sharply toward him from behind.

“When did that start?”

Aurelia turned.

“Do not.”

Sevran ignored her.

“During surges?”

Zee looked at him.

“Sometimes.”

“After Dragon Mana?”

“Sometimes.”

“When angry?”

“Sometimes.”

Sevran frowned.

“You really do not know.”

Zee crossed his arms.

“That seems to disappoint everyone.”

“No.”

Sevran studied the crimson-black horns.

“It worries me.”

Aurelia stepped between them.

“Then worry quietly.”

They continued.

Zee’s horns cooled.

But his heartbeat did not.

Something inside him felt wrong.

Not sick.

Crowded.

As though every supernatural instinct he possessed had decided to speak at once.

He could hear Vesper soldiers behind the walls.

Smell the blood drying beneath Aurelia’s clothes.

Feel Zareth’s agitation.

Sense Sevran’s strange Veyrath Dragon presence.

Taste magic in the air from the castle wards.

And beneath all of that came something he could not identify.

A pressure.

Not around him.

Inside him.

Waiting.

---

Rez met them in the inner courtyard.

At seventeen, he had finally grown into the kind of prince strangers noticed before they noticed his attitude.

Tall.

Fast.

Sword belted properly.

Vesper blue and silver across his coat.

Blue-White Mana controlled cleanly beneath his skin.

Then he opened his mouth.

“You look terrible.”

Zee smiled immediately.

“I missed you too.”

Rez looked at the dried blood across Zee’s clothes.

Then at Aurelia.

Then Sevran.

Then the captured hunters.

His expression lost its humor.

“What happened?”

Ner arrived seconds later.

He was still carrying a book.

Pure Golden Mana shimmered faintly around its cover where he had apparently been practicing seals.

His eyes immediately found Zee.

Then Aurelia.

“You were gone for one conversation.”

Zee shrugged.

“It became complicated.”

Ner looked at Sevran.

“Who is that?”

Sevran answered.

“Sevran Veyrath.”

Ner looked toward Aurelia.

“Family?”

Zee nodded.

“Cousin.”

Sevran looked at him.

“Formerly.”

Ner frowned.

“That is not how blood works.”

Zee pointed at him.

“I said the same thing.”

Rez looked between Sevran and Aurelia.

“Veyrath.”

His eyes sharpened.

“As in her?”

Aurelia sighed.

“Yes.”

Rez looked at Sevran again.

“You are a Dragon?”

“Yes.”

“Dragon-Witch?”

“No.”

“Disappointing.”

Sevran stared.

Rez smiled.

“Welcome to Vesper.”

Lucien’s voice came from the palace steps.

“Nothing about this is a welcome.”

Rez looked over.

“I was being polite.”

“No one believed you.”

King Lucien descended.

His gaze moved across the prisoners first.

Then Sevran.

Then Aurelia’s wrapped side.

He stopped.

“You are injured.”

“I noticed.”

“Who?”

She indicated the prisoners.

Lucien’s face became cold.

His attention turned to Sevran.

“And you brought them.”

Sevran stiffened.

“I was followed.”

“Into territory sheltering my son, the heir of Drakonis, Nereus Azrion, and Zee Darkheart.”

“When you say it like that—”

“There is no better way to say it.”

Caldrin smiled.

“I like him angry.”

Lucien ignored him.

“Council chamber.”

He looked at the captured hunters.

“Cells first.”

Then Sevran.

“You come with us.”

Sevran exhaled.

“I expected hospitality.”

Aurelia walked past him.

“You survived meeting us.”

“That was the hospitality.”

---

The council chamber doors closed.

No servants remained.

Lucien sat at the head of the table.

Aurelia sat to his right.

Sevran sat opposite her under the watch of Vale.

Caldrin occupied a chair he had not been invited to use.

Rez stood beside the map table.

Ner sat on its edge.

Zee was supposed to be resting.

He had ignored that instruction.

Zareth could not comfortably fit inside, so he lay outside the open balcony doors with his head inside the room.

Lucien looked toward Zee.

“You should be in bed.”

“I am sitting.”

“That is not bed.”

“It is rest.”

Rez smiled.

Lucien looked at him.

“Do not encourage him.”

“I said nothing.”

“You have the face.”

Zee immediately looked toward Aurelia.

She almost laughed.

Lucien returned his attention to Sevran.

“Start talking.”

Sevran folded his arms.

“About?”

Vale moved closer.

Sevran unfolded them.

“House Veyrath.”

Aurelia’s expression hardened.

“What remains of it.”

Sevran looked at her.

“More than you think.”

“How many?”

“I do not know.”

“Where?”

“Scattered.”

“That tells me nothing.”

“It tells you the truth.”

Aurelia went silent.

Zee noticed.

She respected that answer even while hating it.

Sevran continued.

“When the old hunts broke House Veyrath apart, survivors chose differently.”

“Some disappeared completely.”

“Some hid inside human kingdoms.”

“Some entered witch territories under other names.”

“Some Dragons joined distant Houses.”

“Some were captured.”

His expression darkened.

“And some decided surviving mattered more than blood.”

Aurelia understood.

“They joined the hunters.”

“Yes.”

Ner frowned.

“The people on the cliff?”

“Not Veyrath.”

“Then who?”

Sevran looked toward him.

“One faction that has hunted Veyrath blood for years.”

“Name?”

Sevran hesitated.

Aurelia’s eyes narrowed.

“Do not make me ask twice.”

“They are called the Ashen Talons.”

Caldrin leaned forward.

“I know the name.”

Vale looked toward him.

“Of course you do.”

“They hunt Dragons.”

Sevran shook his head.

“Not only Dragons.”

“Then what?”

“Bloodlines they consider unstable.”

Aurelia’s jaw tightened.

“Veyrath.”

“Yes.”

“Dragon-Witch blood.”

“Especially.”

Zee touched one of his scales.

Sevran saw.

“They will want you now.”

Aurelia’s Mana flared.

Sevran raised both hands.

“I am not threatening him.”

“You are speaking too comfortably about people wanting my child.”

“I am warning you.”

Lucien intervened.

“Why did they keep hunting after House Veyrath broke?”

Sevran looked toward the table.

“Because a broken bloodline is easier to harvest than a united one.”

Silence.

Ner’s face changed.

He understood that kind of enemy too well.

“Blood.”

“Yes.”

“Experiments?”

“Sometimes.”

“Sale?”

“Yes.”

“Execution?”

“Yes.”

“Depends on the buyer?”

Sevran looked at Ner differently.

“You have dealt with people like them.”

Ner’s Golden Mana flickered.

“People like them dealt with me.”

Zee looked toward Ner.

An old memory surfaced.

Underground Vesper.

His mother chained in a circle.

The demon wanting Gold.

Zee’s horns suddenly burned.

He grabbed the table.

Rez noticed.

“You okay?”

“Yes.”

His voice came too quickly.

Rez frowned.

Zee’s scales spread across his wrist.

No anger.

No attack.

No obvious reason.

Aurelia saw.

“Zee.”

“I said I am fine.”

Crimson Mana escaped between his fingers.

The wooden table groaned.

Zee released it immediately.

A shallow handprint remained burned into the surface.

Everyone stared.

Zee stared hardest.

“I did not do that.”

Aurelia stood.

“Enough for tonight.”

“No.”

“Zee.”

“We finally have answers.”

“You are losing control.”

“I am not.”

A candle across the room went out.

Then relit.

The flame leaned toward Zee.

Not from wind.

The room became unnaturally quiet for one heartbeat.

Dust suspended in the light.

Then everything returned.

No one spoke.

Zee’s face went pale.

“What was that?”

Sevran rose.

“I have never seen—”

Aurelia rounded on him.

“Sit down.”

He sat.

Rez walked toward Zee.

“Hey.”

“I am fine.”

“You keep saying that.”

“Because I am.”

Rez crouched enough to look directly at him.

Zee hated that.

Rez had been doing it since Zee was small enough to be carried everywhere.

Older-brother eyes.

The ones that saw too much.

“When did you sleep?”

“Last night.”

“How long?”

Zee looked away.

Rez sighed.

“When?”

“I do not know.”

“You do.”

“Maybe an hour.”

Aurelia’s expression changed.

“Zee.”

“I could not.”

“Why?”

He looked toward Zareth.

The Dragon Link had been loud all night.

Not Zareth intentionally.

Just present.

Zee had heard the dragon dreaming.

Seen flashes of flight.

Felt Aurelia’s old fear.

He had heard heartbeats through stone.

Smelled blood from rooms away.

Every nature inside him had refused to settle.

“I could hear everything.”

Aurelia moved closer.

“Everything what?”

“Everything.”

Zee pressed both hands against his head.

“People.”

“Blood.”

“Magic.”

“Zareth.”

“Your wound.”

“Ner downstairs.”

“Rez walking around at three in the morning because he thinks no one knows.”

Rez blinked.

“How did you know that?”

“I heard you.”

“From the western wing?”

“Yes!”

The word came out too loud.

Crimson Mana burst.

Every window rattled.

Zareth rose outside.

The Dragon Link surged.

**Zee. Wrong. Pain.**

“I know!”

Everyone froze.

Aurelia spoke softly.

“Who are you talking to?”

“Zareth.”

“You shouted before he sent anything.”

Zee stared.

He had.

The boundaries felt wrong.

Thought.

Mana.

Instinct.

Emotion.

He could not tell where one ended.

Aurelia reached for him.

Zee flinched away.

Her face broke.

He saw it immediately.

“I am sorry.”

“You did nothing wrong.”

“I moved.”

“You are overwhelmed.”

“I do not want to hurt you.”

“You will not.”

“You do not know that.”

Aurelia stopped.

Truth.

She did not.

Zee backed toward the balcony.

Zareth moved closer.

The Dragon Link flooded him with concern.

Too much.

Zee recoiled.

“Stop!”

Zareth froze.

Hurt came through the Link.

Zee’s face crumpled.

“No. Not you. I mean—”

The room pulsed.

Blue-White Mana flashed around Rez defensively.

Golden Mana rose around Ner.

Aurelia’s Witch magic gathered.

Zee felt all of it.

Every source.

Every heartbeat.

Every emotion.

The pressure inside him answered.

His horns ignited crimson-black.

Scales rushed across his neck.

The faint ridges beneath his shoulders pushed painfully against skin.

The air tightened.

Lucien stood.

“Everyone out.”

Zee looked toward him.

“No.”

“That is not punishment.”

“I do not want to be alone.”

The words silenced the room.

Aurelia moved first.

“I am staying.”

Zee shook his head.

“You are hurt.”

“I am your mother.”

“That does not make you unhurt.”

Zee looked at Ner.

Golden Mana.

Bright.

Too bright.

His senses recoiled.

“Ner…”

Ner understood.

He lowered his power immediately.

“I am going.”

Zee looked guilty.

Ner stopped beside him.

“This is not me leaving you.”

“I know.”

“You better.”

Then Ner looked at Rez.

“Do something useful.”

Rez frowned.

“I am always useful.”

Ner left.

Lucien gestured for Vale, Caldrin, Sevran, and the royal witch to follow.

Aurelia remained.

Zee looked at her.

“Please.”

That hurt worse than any command.

“Zee—”

“Mother.”

His eyes filled.

“I can feel your blood.”

Aurelia went still.

The wound.

Her presence was feeding his panic.

Rez looked toward her.

“I will stay.”

Aurelia immediately said, “No.”

Rez looked at her.

“He asked you to go.”

“He did not ask you to remain.”

Zee spoke.

“Rez stays.”

Aurelia closed her eyes.

The room shuddered again.

Rez moved slowly toward Zee.

“I have him.”

Aurelia stared at the seventeen-year-old prince she had watched grow beside her son.

Not a servant.

Not a guard.

Family.

She nodded once.

“Do not challenge the surge.”

Rez gave her a look.

“I was not planning to wrestle his magic.”

Zee almost laughed.

Almost.

Aurelia approached her son one final time.

She did not touch him.

“I am right outside.”

Zee nodded.

“Promise?”

“Yes.”

“Do not leave.”

“I will not.”

She went.

Lucien paused at the doorway.

His eyes met Rez’s.

Father and son.

No words.

Rez nodded.

Lucien closed the doors.

Only Zee, Rez, and Zareth remained.

The dragon stayed on the balcony.

Close.

Quiet.

Rez looked at Zee.

Zee looked terrible.

Sweat against his forehead.

Crimson scales spreading without rhythm.

Horns glowing.

Hands shaking.

Mana moving around him like something alive and frightened.

Rez took off his sword belt.

Set it aside.

Then removed the dagger at his ankle.

Zee frowned.

“What are you doing?”

“Making sure you do not accidentally throw me through a wall while I am carrying something sharp.”

“I would not.”

Rez looked at the burned table.

Zee sighed.

“Fair.”

Rez stepped closer.

“What does it feel like?”

Zee swallowed.

“Like I am standing inside everyone.”

Rez stopped.

“That sounds awful.”

“It is.”

“Can you hear me?”

“Yes.”

“My heartbeat?”

“Yes.”

“Mana?”

“Yes.”

“Anything else?”

Zee looked at him.

For one moment his expression became frightened.

“I do not know.”

The candle flames bent backward.

Dust lifted from the floor.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana moved toward Zee without being summoned.

Rez looked down.

“That is new.”

Zee’s eyes widened.

“I am not doing that.”

“I know.”

“Rez.”

“I know.”

The air became still.

Not peaceful.

Waiting.

Rez stepped forward anyway.

He placed one hand on Zee’s shoulder.

Zee flinched.

Then held on.

Rez tightened his grip.

“I am here.”

The words did not fix anything.

But Zee believed them.

For a moment.

Then his horns burned brighter.

The entire room went silent.

Not quiet.

Silent.

As though sound itself had forgotten how to move.

Rez felt Zee’s fingers close around his wrist.

Too tight.

Desperate.

And somewhere beneath blood, Mana, Dragon heat, predatory instinct, fear, memory, and the impossible pressure gathering inside Zee Darkheart...

something new opened its eyes.
