Dren poured tea.

Zee did not touch it.

“Poison?” Dren asked.

“Yes.”

Dren laughed.

“Very good.”

“Common paralytic under the lavender.”

“Less common suppression agent beneath it.”

Dren’s smile widened.

“And?”

Zee inhaled.

“Dragonbane.”

The smile vanished.

There.

“You really can smell that?”

“Yes.”

Dren set the cup down.

“You are magnificent.”

Zee’s face cooled.

“Do not.”

“Do not what?”

“Talk about me like a specimen.”

Dren studied him.

“But that is exactly what you are.”

Wrong.

Zee almost killed him there.

Did not.

Information first.

“What do you want with my blood?”

“To understand transformation.”

“Ner.”

“Yes.”

“God blood.”

“Yes.”

“Your Dragon evolution.”

“Yes.”

Dren leaned forward.

“You drank things that should have destroyed you.”

“And?”

“You became more yourself.”

That sentence made Zee pause.

Dren noticed.

“Demon blood.”

“Dragon blood.”

“Divine blood.”

“Different poisons.”

“Different supernatural species.”

“You do not accumulate foreign powers.”

“You rewrite pressure.”

Zee said nothing.

Dren smiled.

“I understand you better than most.”

“No.”

“Why?”

“Because you think understanding my blood means understanding me.”

The smile thinned.

Zee leaned back.

“What were you planning?”

Dren’s eyes sharpened.

“To capture you.”

“Alive.”

“Yes.”

“How?”

“Would you like to know?”

Zee smiled.

“Yes.”

Dren lifted one finger.

The garden exploded.

---

Silver-black cables launched from beneath the stone.

Not magic.

Mechanisms.

Fast.

Zee moved.

One wrapped his ankle.

Another caught his wrist.

A third hit his chest.

The cables activated.

Suppression.

Dragonbane.

Vampire restraints.

Wolf irritants.

Witch-breaking sigils.

Everything at once.

Zee hit the ground.

Dren stood.

“Like that.”

Zee looked down.

Interesting.

His Vampire strength failed first.

Witchcraft became heavy.

Wolf senses flooded with artificial scent.

Dragon blood burned.

Good design.

Dren approached.

“You have been attacked by specialists.”

“I hired engineers.”

Zee flexed one hand.

The cable tightened.

Pain.

His Crimson adaptations reacted.

Not instantly.

Not enough.

Good.

Dren crouched.

“You see?”

Zee looked at him.

Human pupils now.

Calm.

“You made one mistake.”

Dren smiled.

“Which?”

“You built restraints for everything you know I am.”

Zee’s hand closed.

Nothing happened.

Dren laughed.

Then Zee smiled.

“Separately.”

His Wolf nature found balance first.

He stopped fighting the restraint and rolled with its tension.

The Vampire suppression expected direct resistance.

None came.

His Witch nature used one tiny gesture.

Two fingers.

Barely moving.

A sigil on the nearest cable rotated half an inch.

Wrong alignment.

The Dragonbane load shifted.

Crimson Demonic Dragon heat surged into the exposed weakness.

One cable snapped.

Dren stopped laughing.

Zee moved.

Vampire speed returned only partially.

Enough.

He caught Dren by the throat.

The other cables dragged behind him.

Dren gasped.

Zee headbutted him.

Horn edge opened his scalp.

Blood.

Mixed blood.

Artificial.

Zee smelled every layer.

Ner’s Golden barrier erupted around the garden.

Twenty-five seconds.

Exactly.

“Show-off,” Zee said.

Ner entered.

“You are tied to a statue.”

“Temporarily.”

Dren shouted:

“NOW!”

The hidden fighters moved.

Chaos.

The underground Witch cast first.

Ner’s Gold pierced the floor and broke the spell structure before it rose.

One archer fired.

Zee flicked two fingers.

The arrow bent.

Hit the second archer’s bow.

Wolf attackers came from the wall.

Zee tore one remaining cable free through brute force.

Not Vampire alone.

Dragon durability let the restraint cut deep without stopping him.

He caught the first Wolf by the throat.

Threw him.

Second attacked Ner.

Wrong.

Ner spoke one low Bloodsong note.

The Wolf’s circulation stumbled.

His body dropped to one knee.

Ner sealed him in Gold.

“Alive,” Ner said.

Zee looked toward Dren.

“For now.”

Dren ran.

Zee let him.

Ner looked over.

“You are letting him go.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

Zee’s pupils shifted into slits.

“Wolf.”

Understanding hit Ner.

“Oh.”

Zee transformed.

---

Dren reached the coastal forest.

He believed the trees would help.

They did.

Zee wanted the hunt.

Near-black Wolf form moved through wet brush without sound.

No horns.

No scales.

No magic.

Just Wolf.

Dren used scent blockers.

Zee tracked broken fern.

Dren crossed rock.

Zee tracked displaced insects.

Dren entered seawater.

Zee circled ahead.

Waited on the beach.

Dren emerged twenty minutes later.

Saw Zee.

Stopped.

The fear was exquisite.

Zee walked toward him slowly.

Dren backed into the surf.

“You need me.”

Wolf Zee showed teeth.

Dren pulled a blood-filled injector from his coat.

“Do you know what this is?”

Zee shifted back.

Human form returned.

He looked at the vial.

Dragon.

Demon.

Vampire.

Mixed.

Badly.

“You made a cocktail.”

Dren laughed.

“A weapon.”

“No.”

Zee stepped closer.

“A mistake.”

Dren injected himself.

His body reacted immediately.

Veins blackened.

Eyes turned red.

Bones shifted beneath skin.

Strength surged.

Then his heartbeat lost rhythm.

Zee watched.

Dren screamed.

Supernatural bloods fought inside him.

No Crimson biology to rewrite them.

No stable inheritance.

Just incompatibility.

Dren lunged anyway.

Zee caught the first punch.

Barely.

Strong.

Then another.

Dren became faster.

More unstable.

Zee’s assassin instincts stopped trying to match force.

Weakness.

The blood mixture kept pulling Dren’s left shoulder too high.

His right leg compensated.

Heart skipping every fourth beat.

Zee waited.

One.

Two.

Three.

Skip.

He struck the sternum exactly then.

Dren collapsed.

Zee caught him.

“Interesting.”

Dren coughed blood.

“You see?”

“Yes.”

“Then save me.”

Zee stared.

“Why?”

“I can give you everything.”

“Already have your ledgers.”

“You need my research.”

“No.”

“You could become—”

Zee’s face went cold.

“I decide what I become.”

He bit.

Dren screamed.

Zee drank.

Not because Dren’s blood offered some miraculous new power.

Because Zee wanted to know what artificial supernatural blood tasted like inside a failed vessel.

The answer was chaos.

His body separated everything immediately.

Foreign Vampire enhancement.

Wolf residue.

Witch infusion.

Dragon blood.

Demon corruption.

Nothing stable enough to keep.

Crimson biology rejected most of it.

That was useful too.

Not every supernatural blood source deserved adaptation.

Sometimes the correct evolution was refusal.

Zee drained Dren completely.

Then dropped the body into the surf.

Dead.

Second Covenant name finished.

---

Ner found Zee on the beach.

Blood at his mouth.

Waves around his boots.

“You killed him.”

“Yes.”

“Learn anything?”

Zee looked toward the corpse.

“My blood is smarter than his research.”

Ner laughed.

“That sounded arrogant.”

“It is also true.”

“What now?”

Zee pulled the Covenant list from his coat.

Three names remained.

Keira Morn.

Father Caldus.

And one other.

Then the Dragon Link slammed into him.

Not danger.

Urgency.

Drakonis.

A face.

Not Dren.

Not Mara.

The third name.

Keira Morn.

Ner sighed.

“Next.”

The world was making this efficient.

# Chapter Seventy-Three

Keira Morn attacked Drakonis because she thought Zee would not arrive in time.

With geography.

Dragonfire ahead.

No escape.

without wings.

Fast.

Blood on his teeth.

Teal-and-Gold fire leaking between them.

Anger.

Pride.

One image.

Keira.

Above.

High Witch.

Powerful.

Calm.

Zareth.

Ner.

Drakonis soldiers.

His people elsewhere.

Difference.

Around Zareth.

Dragon suppression.

Designed for true Dragon physiology.

Slits.

Good.

Trust.

Good.

Pressure point.

Elbow.

Unconscious.

Good.

Not full form.

Never.

Burned.

Healing started.

Pure Gold.

Precision.

Zareth stood.

“Oh.”

Smart.

Fear.

There.

Interesting.

Bloodsong humming faintly beneath his voice.

One man’s ideology.

Then Zareth.

Veyrath.

Mixed families at his fortress.

People born between categories.

Not total.

She knew something.

Strong.

Zee compelled.

Blood wards tightened.

Zee pushed.

Voice.

Predatory pressure.

Blood dominance.

Still resisted.

Powerful.

Good.

He stepped closer.

His fangs descended.

Fear.

Built a suppression cage around Zareth.

His fight.

His kingdom.

His choice.

Stared.

Final.

Good.

His judgment.

His kingdom.

Anger.

Satisfaction.

Rude.

Quick.

Warm.

Calm.

Thinking.

Dren before another experiment.

Each line different.

Each choice moving.

Bloodlines.

Entire categories of people.

Warning.

# Chapter Seventy-Four

## The Salt Cathedral

The western salt flats had no roads.

Only white.

Miles of cracked earth reflecting sunlight hard enough to hurt ordinary eyes.

Zee walked through it without squinting.

Ner beside him.

Rez had rejoined them at the border after Vesper’s aqueduct threat was contained.

Zareth arrived in human form.

That was still new enough that Rez stared.

Zareth noticed.

“If you keep looking at me like that, I am shifting back.”

Rez blinked.

“You talk more than I expected.”

Zareth’s expression went flat.

“I have always had opinions.”

Zee smiled.

“Unfortunately.”

Zareth looked toward him.

Through the Link:

**You missed this.**

Zee answered privately.

**A little.**

Warmth came back beneath the words.

Then smoke.

Drakonis.

Damage still under repair.

Responsibility waiting.

Zareth had come because Father Caldus threatened mixed bloodlines across kingdoms, including Veyrath and potentially Drakonis alliances.

Not because Zee summoned him.

Good.

The salt cathedral appeared near noon.

No towers.

No walls.

It had been carved downward.

A massive open pit cut into the flats, white stone descending in terraces toward a dark sanctuary beneath the earth.

Rez looked over the edge.

“I hate stairs.”

Ner glanced down.

“There are hundreds.”

“I hate them more now.”

Zareth smiled.

“You have legs.”

Rez stared.

“You had wings for most of your life.”

“Still do.”

“Exactly.”

Zee started down.

“Argue later.”

---

Nobody attacked them.

That was suspicious.

The first chamber contained no guards.

The second held candles.

The third held names.

Hundreds.

Painted across salt walls.

Zee stopped.

Wolf.

Witch.

Vampire.

Dragon-Witch.

Mixed blood.

Unknown blood.

Bloodsong.

Tribrid.

Ner went very still.

His name was there.

**NEREUS AZRION.**

Zareth found another.

**AURELIA VEYRATH.**

Dead.

Still listed.

Then:

**THERON VEYRATH.**

**SERAPHINE VEYRATH.**

Rez found his own.

Not because mixed.

Because proximity.

**REZ VESPER — ENABLER.**

He frowned.

“I am offended by how boring mine is.”

Ner looked toward Zee’s section.

His name occupied an entire column.

**ZEE DARKHEART.**

Below it:

**PRIMARY CONVERGENCE THREAT.**

**ADAPTIVE BLOOD.**

**UNSTABLE SPECIES BOUNDARY.**

**DIVINE-KILLING CAPACITY CONFIRMED.**

**CRIMSON DRAGON MUTATION.**

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Very dramatic.”

Zareth folded his arms.

“You are one to talk.”

Zee looked at him.

“You have become irritating in human form.”

“I had to compensate for twenty-one years of you translating me badly.”

Rez laughed.

Ner actually stopped reading to look between them.

Zee pointed.

“I never translated you badly.”

Through the Link, Zareth sent Zee an old childhood memory.

Zee telling someone Zareth had said hello.

What Zareth had actually felt was suspicion, hunger, and a desire to bite the roof.

Zee frowned.

“That was close enough.”

“Liar.”

Good.

The humor lasted four seconds.

Then Ner touched the wall.

Pure Golden Mana spread.

His expression changed.

“These names are recent.”

“How recent?” Rez asked.

“Some days.”

Zee looked down the corridor.

“Caldus is here.”

“No,” Ner said.

Silence.

He studied the structure again.

“These walls are receiving information.”

Rez’s hand moved to his sword.

“From where?”

“I don’t know.”

Zee listened.

No heartbeat beneath them.

No blood.

No obvious living presence.

Zareth’s Dragon senses sharpened.

Then he spoke aloud.

“There is something lower.”

Zee looked toward him.

“What?”

Zareth’s eyes narrowed.

“Not someone.”

Through the Link came more.

Heat without fire.

A pressure beneath the salt.

Something old, but not divine.

Not friendly.

Not awake.

Zee felt the sensory layer beneath Zareth’s words.

Deep vibration.

Mineral.

Bone?

No.

Something structural.

Ner stepped away from the wall.

“The cathedral is built on something.”

Rez sighed.

“Of course it is.”

---

They found Father Caldus in the lowest chamber.

Alone.

Old.

Human.

No supernatural blood.

No armor.

No guards.

He sat at a stone table surrounded by paper.

He looked up when they entered.

“King Darkheart.”

Zee stopped.

“Father Caldus.”

Caldus looked toward Ner.

Then Rez.

Then Zareth.

His gaze lingered.

“Crown Prince Drakonis. Human form suits diplomacy.”

Zareth’s voice went colder.

“You cut Dragon bloodlines into categories.”

Caldus smiled.

“I classify risk.”

“You classify people you intend to erase.”

“Yes.”

No denial.

Rez looked disgusted.

“That saves time.”

Caldus folded his hands.

“I wondered which of you would say it first.”

Zee walked closer.

“Where are the kill orders?”

“Already distributed.”

Ner’s Gold flared.

Rez moved.

Zareth’s eyes sharpened.

Zee did not.

Calm.

“Targets?”

Caldus smiled.

“All over.”

Zee heard the heartbeat.

Steady.

No bluff.

Bad.

“How many?”

“Forty-three bloodlines.”

“Active strikes?”

“Seven.”

Rez swore.

Zareth’s voice dropped into something closer to Dragon thunder even in human shape.

“Drakonis?”

“One.”

“Ner?”

“One.”

“Veyrath?”

“Two.”

Zee’s pupils became slits.

“And Darkheart?”

Caldus smiled.

“Not the House.”

“You.”

Silence.

Zee looked at him.

“Where?”

“You are already here.”

That was the trap.

Ner realized first.

“Zee.”

The salt beneath them lit.

Not Witchcraft.

Something else.

Caldus stood.

“I could never overpower you.”

“No.”

“So I built a place that does not need to.”

The floor split.

Not downward.

Inward.

White salt opened into a black mineral chamber far beneath the cathedral.

Zareth’s voice sharpened.

“Move!”

Too late.

The entire sanctuary dropped.

---

They fell into darkness.

Zareth shifted midair.

Human body exploded outward into true Dragon form.

Wings opened.

Massive.

He caught Rez with one foreclaw.

Ner with the other.

Zee did not need catching.

He hit the sloped wall, claws digging in, slid twenty feet, then pushed off.

Dragon durability absorbed the rest.

He landed hard.

Caldus landed on a suspended platform above.

Protected by mechanisms.

Zee looked up.

“You planned that.”

“Yes.”

“I respect preparation.”

Caldus stared.

“That is not the response I wanted.”

Zee smiled.

Then the chamber woke.

Something moved beneath the salt.

Not a creature.

A network.

Black crystal roots spread through the cavern.

Every supernatural nature reacted differently.

Ner’s Gold flickered.

Rez’s Blue-White Mana weakened.

Zareth’s Dragonfire dimmed.

Zee felt all four natures strain.

Not suppression.

Separation.

The chamber was trying to make each supernatural force exist alone.

Zee’s Witch nature pulled away from Vampire.

Wolf from Dragon.

Not physically.

Structurally.

Caldus looked down.

“This is what the world should have remained.”

Zee’s face went cold.

“Separate.”

“Yes.”

Ner gritted his teeth.

“You built a weapon out of a natural formation.”

Caldus smiled.

“Finally.”

Rez looked around.

“Can it be broken?”

Ner studied.

“Not quickly.”

Zareth spoke through the Link while also growling aloud.

**Three anchors. North wall. Under platform. Beneath us.**

Zee received more than words.

Heat.

Positions.

A weak pulse under the salt.

He answered instantly.

**Take the north. Rez gets the platform. Ner finds the lower anchor. I take Caldus.**

Zareth’s mental reply came with irritation.

**You always take the person.**

**He talks too much.**

A wave of Dragon amusement broke through the strain.

Then they moved.

The adult Link made them terrifying.

No shouted explanation.

No delay.

Zareth blasted the north wall.

Rez used the opening to climb toward the platform.

Ner drove Gold into the floor in hair-thin lines.

Zee ran straight up the salt column.

Caldus saw him.

Panic finally entered his heartbeat.

Good.

Zee reached the platform.

Caldus triggered another mechanism.

Iron spikes fired.

Zee barely turned his wrist.

Silent magic.

The spikes shifted around him.

One embedded beside Caldus’s head.

Zee continued walking.

Caldus backed up.

“You are destabilizing everything.”

“Yes.”

“You could collapse the chamber.”

“Yes.”

“And kill us all.”

Zee smiled faintly.

“You keep forgetting.”

Caldus’s face changed.

Right.

Zee could not die.

Caldus could.

“Stop.”

“No.”

Zee crossed the last distance.

Caldus raised a poison blade.

Nanda Parbat read the shoulder.

Zee caught his wrist before the blade cleared cloth.

Twist.

Break.

Caldus screamed.

Zee’s smile vanished.

“Where are the seven strikes?”

Caldus spat blood.

“Too late.”

Vampire compulsion hit.

“Where?”

Caldus resisted.

Ordinary Human.

Extraordinary discipline.

Zee pushed harder.

“Tell me.”

The man shook violently.

Then laughed.

“Even if I tell you, you cannot reach them all.”

Zee looked toward Zareth.

The Link opened.

Not words first.

Drakonis.

Distance.

Air routes.

Then speech.

**I can reach one.**

Rez shouted from below.

“Vesper can reach another if we send now!”

Ner looked up.

“Veyrath survivors are scattered. We can warn both.”

Zee returned to Caldus.

“You were saying?”

Fear.

Good.

“Locations.”

Compulsion broke him.

Seven places.

Fast.

Specific.

Rez memorized.

Ner sent Golden signal marks through prepared communication charms.

Zareth’s Link carried one thought before he shifted toward flight.

**I am taking Drakonis.**

Zee answered.

**Go.**

No ownership.

No request to stay.

Zareth launched upward through the broken chamber.

Caldus watched.

His plan collapsing faster than he could process.

Zee leaned close.

“You chose bloodlines before they acted.”

Caldus glared.

“They would have.”

“Some.”

“Yes.”

“Not all.”

“Eventually.”

There it was.

Possibility as guilt.

Victor again.

Zee was tired of it.

He killed Caldus quickly.

One hand.

Neck.

No feeding.

He did not want the blood.

Caldus dropped.

The last principal name was finished.

Then the floor cracked.

Ner shouted.

“Zee!”

The chamber began collapsing.

Permanent progress had arrived.

Now survival.

Good.

Zee jumped.

---

They escaped through the upper shaft as the salt cathedral imploded behind them.

Rez emerged coughing.

Ner covered in white dust.

Zee barely singed.

Zareth already gone toward Drakonis.

Through the Link:

**Still alive.**

Zee answered.

**Disappointing.**

Zareth’s laughter came through with mountain wind and urgency.

Then he was gone.

Rez looked toward the horizon.

“Seven attacks.”

Ner nodded.

“Now six.”

Zee looked at him.

“How?”

Ner smiled faintly.

“Bloodsong warning reached one Veyrath enclave before the strike landed.”

Good.

Rez drew breath.

“Vesper will handle ours.”

“Drakonis handles theirs.”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“And the others?”

Ner looked toward him.

“Darkheart has people.”

Zee understood.

Not everything required him personally.

King.

Network.

Influence.

He turned east.

“Then we move.”

The Covenant’s Five were finished.

But Caldus had already thrown seven knives into the world.

Now the question was not whether Zee could stop them all himself.

It was whether the world had finally learned something worse.

King Zee Darkheart was no longer one predator.

He had people who moved when he did.

And they were getting faster.

# Chapter Seventy-Five

## Seven Knives

The attacks landed within three hours.

None looked the same.

That was what made them dangerous.

Vesper’s was sabotage.

Drakonis faced a direct strike.

One Veyrath enclave received poisoned rain.

A mixed-blood settlement east of Darkheart was attacked by hired Wolves.

A coastal Bloodsong rumor-cell was targeted by Vampire killers who thought Ner had created more like himself.

Wrong.

There was only Ner.

Another strike hit a Demon-Witch refuge under neutral protection.

The last came for Zee.

That one waited until he returned to Darkheart.

Of course.

---

Rez’s message arrived first.

**Aqueduct secure. Four dead. Nine captured. Father furious. I am enjoying it.**

Zee smiled.

Ner read over his shoulder.

“He wrote that?”

“Yes.”

“That is concerning.”

“No.”

“Why?”

“Lucien furious is apparently entertaining.”

Ner looked unconvinced.

Then his own Bloodsong pulsed.

He stopped.

“Veyrath.”

Zee’s face changed.

“What?”

“Someone is bleeding.”

“Who?”

Ner closed his eyes.

His Bloodsong had learned distance imperfectly over the years.

Not names.

Not thoughts.

Resonance.

Blood he had encountered before was easier.

Theron.

Zee smelled Ner’s fear before he spoke.

“Theron.”

Zee’s hand closed.

Then the Link hit.

Zareth.

Full sentence.

**Drakonis is under control. Do not come here. Go to Theron.**

Beneath it Zee felt torn wing membrane, smoke, two broken talons, and Zareth lying about how fine he was.

Zee answered privately.

**You are bleeding.**

**I said under control, not comfortable.**

**Idiot.**

**Go.**

Zee went.

---

Theron had already killed three attackers when Zee arrived.

Seraphine killed the fourth.

Good.

No helpless family.

Theron leaned against a stone wall with poison spreading black beneath one Dragon scale patch.

Seraphine stood over a dead Witch.

“You are late.”

Zee crouched beside Theron.

“You are alive.”

“Barely.”

“Dramatic.”

Theron smiled weakly.

“Family trait.”

Ner arrived seconds later and dropped beside him.

Pure Gold formed.

Bloodsong followed.

The poison reacted badly.

Ner frowned.

“This was designed for Veyrath.”

Zee smelled it.

Dragonbane.

Witch suppression.

Blood clotting agent.

Specialized.

His body recognized pieces.

Not whole.

He opened his palm with one claw.

Seraphine immediately said:

“No.”

Zee looked at her.

“One drop.”

“You do not know what that does.”

“Neither do you.”

“That is why I said no.”

Theron coughed.

“I vote yes.”

Seraphine glared.

“You are poisoned.”

“Exactly. Motivated reasoning.”

Zee almost laughed.

Then seriousness returned.

He placed one drop of Crimson blood against the poison near Theron’s wound.

Ner isolated it with Gold.

The reaction was immediate.

The black spread stopped.

Not cured.

Stopped.

Zee’s accumulated resistance interfered with the poison’s structure.

Ner used Bloodsong to push the broken toxin away from Theron’s heart.

Seraphine added Witchcraft.

Three powers.

Not one solution.

Theron breathed easier.

Zee looked at Ner.

“Can you finish?”

“Yes.”

Good.

Zee stood.

One attacker remained alive.

Seraphine had kept him that way deliberately.

The man knelt against a pillar.

Human.

Terrified.

Zee approached.

The attacker whispered:

“Please.”

Zee crouched.

“Who gave you the poison?”

“Caldus.”

“Directly?”

“Yes.”

Truth.

“Anyone else involved?”

“No.”

Truth.

“Did you know who lived here?”

“Yes.”

“Did you know there were children?”

The man froze.

Seraphine’s face hardened.

Zee smelled the answer.

“Yes.”

He killed him.

Quick.

No speech.

No guilt.

Then turned back to Theron.

Different.

Gentler.

Both Zee.

Theron watched him.

“Aurelia would worry about you.”

Zee stopped.

Not because the name was forbidden.

Because Theron had earned the right to use it.

“I know.”

“She would also be glad I am alive.”

“Yes.”

“Then focus on that.”

Zee looked at him.

For one second, human pupils.

Then he nodded.

No moral reset.

Just family.

---

The mixed-blood settlement survived because Darkheart riders arrived before Zee.

That mattered.

His people were learning.

The coastal Vampire strike failed because Ner sent a Bloodsong warning through three connected blood samples before the killers reached shore.

That frightened him.

Not because the power was bad.

Because it was growing.

He told Zee later.

“I could feel them before they arrived.”

“How far?”

“Too far.”

“That is not a measurement.”

“I know.”

Zee smiled.

Ner did not.

Zee touched his face.

“What?”

Ner looked at him.

“If I can reach blood from that far away eventually…”

“Yes.”

“What stops me from touching everyone?”

Zee’s expression softened.

“You.”

Ner stared.

Not because Zee was calling him good.

Because the answer placed responsibility where it belonged.

Ner nodded.

“Fair.”

Then kissed him.

Brief.

Needed.

The moment ended when a Darkheart horn sounded.

Attack seven.

Home.

---

The killers came through the throne hall.

Four.

Not an army.

Professionals.

They knew Zee’s patrol schedule.

They knew the hidden stair.

They knew the old Victor-era passages.

One had been a Darkheart servant years ago.

Betrayal.

Different category.

Zee entered silently behind them.

The first assassin never knew.

Knife.

Down.

Second turned.

Vampire.

He saw Zee’s eyes.

Slits.

Tried compulsion.

Zee smiled.

“Really?”

The command broke against him.

Zee answered.

“Kneel.”

The Vampire resisted.

Strong.

Older than Zee.

Did not matter enough.

Vampire dominance pressed through voice and blood.

The attacker’s knees hit stone.

Third and fourth moved together.

Witch and Wolf.

Good coordination.

Zee barely lifted one hand.

The Witch’s spell veered left.

The Wolf adjusted.

Exactly what Zee expected.

Nanda Parbat.

He stepped into the new line.

One elbow.

One broken wrist.

Wolf claws caught his shoulder.

Crimson-black scales took most of it.

Zee grabbed the Wolf.

Headbutt.

Horn edge opened blood.

Then claws.

Wolf Zee without transforming.

Natural.

Complete.

He drove the attacker down.

The Witch tried another spell.

Zee closed his fist.

Her spell structure collapsed.

“Silence.”

Her mouth stopped.

Not compulsion.

Witchcraft.

Precise.

The kneeling Vampire struggled against Zee’s command.

Interesting.

Zee looked at him.

“Still.”

The command deepened.

No eye contact.

The Vampire froze completely.

The Wolf on the floor smelled terrified.

Zee liked that.

Then the former Darkheart servant—the first assassin he thought was down—moved.

Not dead.

Feigning.

Good technique.

Bad luck.

Zee heard the heartbeat change.

He turned before the hidden blade reached him.

Caught the hand.

The servant stared.

“You remember me.”

“Yes.”

That surprised him.

Zee remembered everyone who had worked near Aurelia.

This man had served wine at two dinners.

Opened doors.

Carried letters.

Then disappeared after Victor died.

“Why?”

The man’s face twisted.

“You destroyed the House.”

Zee looked around.

Darkheart banners.

Living guards.

People choosing loyalty instead of inherited fear.

“No.”

“You killed the King.”

“Yes.”

“My King.”

There.

Personal.

Not Caldus.

Not bloodline philosophy.

Grief.

Zee understood more than he wanted to.

The servant continued.

“You killed my brother when you took the throne.”

Zee searched memory.

Fight.

Victor loyalists.

One man attacked Ner after surrender was offered.

Zee killed him.

“Yes.”

“You remember.”

“Yes.”

The servant’s eyes filled.

“I hate you.”

Zee’s grip loosened slightly.

Not mercy yet.

Recognition.

“That is fair.”

The man froze.

Zee continued.

“You still came here to kill me.”

“Yes.”

“And them?”

The assassin glanced toward the hall.

Darkheart guards.

Servants.

Ner entering behind Zee.

His answer came too slowly.

Zee smelled it.

He had planned collateral.

There went the sympathy.

Zee broke the wrist.

The man screamed.

“Your grief is yours.”

Zee’s expression went cold.

“What you do with it is also yours.”

Then Zee killed him.

Personal.

Fast.

No feeding.

The remaining three surrendered after that.

Zee spared two.

The Vampire tried to break compulsion and reach a hidden blade.

Zee drained him.

Fully.

Because he wanted the blood.

No apology.

---

By midnight, all seven attacks had failed.

Not without losses.

Nine dead across four territories.

Twenty-three wounded.

Theron alive.

Zareth alive.

Lucien alive.

Veyrath survivors still standing.

Mixed-blood settlements damaged but not destroyed.

The world had thrown seven knives.

None reached the heart.

Zee sat on the Darkheart throne after the reports ended.

Rez appeared through a communication mirror from Vesper.

His hair was wet.

His coat burned.

He looked exhausted.

“Still alive?”

Zee smiled.

“Unfortunately.”

Rez nodded.

“Same.”

Zareth spoke privately through the Link from Drakonis.

**My wing is fine.**

Zee felt the pain immediately.

**Liar.**

**Minor lie.**

Then aloud, through a Drakonis mirror, Zareth said:

“Stop telling everyone I am injured.”

Rez stared at the mirror.

“You can hear him from there?”

Zee smiled.

“Yes.”

Zareth replied:

“And he can feel that I am considering throwing something at him.”

Ner laughed.

The room felt almost normal.

Almost.

Then Lord Merek entered.

“Majesty.”

Zee looked up.

“What?”

“One of Caldus’s strike teams surrendered before attacking.”

Silence.

Rez’s face changed in the mirror.

Ner looked toward Merek.

“Why?”

“They heard Caldus was dead.”

Zee leaned back.

“And?”

Merek hesitated.

“They said they believed if they carried out the order, you would hunt every surviving member personally.”

Zee’s face went still.

Fear.

Reputation.

Prevention.

No blood spilled because people feared what Zee would do afterward.

That was new.

And Zee liked it.

Perhaps too much.

Ner saw.

Did not say anything.

Zareth felt it through the Link.

His mental voice came quietly.

**You like that they were afraid.**

Zee answered honestly.

**Yes.**

**Good.**

Zee blinked.

**Good?**

Zareth sent heat, exhaustion, and one clear thought.

**They did not kill anyone. Fear did what an army could not. Use what works. Just know when you are using it.**

Zee smiled faintly.

Dragon morality.

Different.

Useful.

Rez’s voice came through the mirror.

“You are both having a private conversation, aren’t you?”

Zee looked at him.

“Yes.”

“That is rude.”

Zareth said aloud:

“We were discussing you.”

Rez narrowed his eyes.

“Liar.”

“Completely.”

Ner laughed again.

Zee looked around.

His people.

His lover.

His brother.

His bonded Dragon prince.

No Aurelia.

Never again.

Still, life.

Still war.

Still blood.

The Covenant’s Five were dead or neutralized.

Seven attacks had failed.

The world had learned something.

Not that Zee could stop everything.

He could not.

Not that his people were untouchable.

They were not.

Something more dangerous.

Attacking King Zee Darkheart no longer meant dealing only with Zee.

It meant Darkheart.

Vesper.

Bloodsong.

Drakonis.

Veyrath.

Wolves.

Witches.

Vampires.

People who had chosen him.

And now, for the first time, one group had decided not to attack because Zee’s reputation reached them before his claws did.

Zee rested one hand against the throne.

Crimson-and-gold eyes calm.

Human pupils.

For now.

He had spent his childhood hating fear.

At twenty-one, he was beginning to understand its most useful form.

Not panic.

Not cruelty.

Deterrence.

And King Zee Darkheart had every intention of learning how far it could reach.

# Chapter Seventy-Six

## The Attack That Never Happened

No alarm sounded.

No village burned.

No assassin entered Darkheart.

Nobody was poisoned.

That was why the report mattered.

Lord Merek placed one folded letter on Zee’s table.

“Intercepted at the southern border.”

Zee opened it.

Rez leaned over one shoulder.

Ner sat across from him.

Zareth occupied another chair in human form, boots on the table until Zee looked at them.

Zareth lowered them slowly.

“You became annoying the moment you got a throne.”

“You put your feet on my war table.”

“It survived.”

Zee ignored him and read.

A minor southern lord.

Lord Vaelor Tannis.

Seven hired killers.

Three Witch suppressors.

Two Dragonbane weapons.

One blood-tracking hound.

A planned strike against a Darkheart refuge housing mixed supernatural families.

The attack was scheduled for four nights from now.

Rez read the last line.

“He has not done anything yet.”

“No.”

Ner’s eyes stayed on Zee.

The room went quiet.

Everyone knew what came next.

Six months ago, Zee might have fortified the refuge.

Then waited.

Three months ago, he might have captured the killers on the road.

Now?

Zee folded the letter.

“I want confirmation.”

Rez nodded immediately.

Good.

Ner did too.

Zareth smiled.

“Then?”

Zee looked at him.

“If it is real, I kill the people organizing it.”

Rez exhaled.

“Not the hired blades?”

“If they have not moved yet, they get one chance to walk away.”

Ner studied him.

“And Tannis?”

Zee’s pupils narrowed into slits.

“No.”

The difference was small.

Also enormous.

He was no longer waiting for violence.

He was verifying intent.

Then eliminating it.

---

Confirmation took one day.

Darkheart scouts found the hired killers.

The weapons.

The payment.

The target maps.

The refuge layout.

The children’s sleeping quarters marked in red.

That ended the question.

Zee left at dusk.

No army.

Zareth came in human form.

Rez stayed behind to coordinate the refuge defenses anyway.

Ner came because one of the documents mentioned Bloodsong containment methods.

Zee did not tell him to stay.

He had learned.

Mostly.

---

Lord Tannis held dinner for fourteen guests.

Zee entered through the kitchen.

Not dramatically.

He simply walked through a side door after compelling the guard to forget he had seen him.

Ner followed.

Zareth took the front entrance.

That was deliberate.

The hall went silent when the Dragon Crown Prince entered in human form.

Teal-and-Gold Mana touched the air.

Tannis stood quickly.

“Prince Drakonis.”

Zareth smiled.

“Lord Tannis.”

“I was not informed—”

“That is because I did not inform you.”

While every guard watched Zareth, Zee crossed the upper gallery without making a sound.

Nanda Parbat.

Old habits.

Permanent.

Ner entered the lower archive and began looking for the contracts.

Three approaches.

Three jobs.

No need to crowd the same hallway.

Zee reached Tannis’s private study first.

Two guards outside.

One looked left.

Zee struck.

Pressure point.

Caught the body.

Second turned.

One hand covered his mouth.

“Sleep.”

The guard collapsed silently.

Zee entered.

The desk held the original contract.

Signed.

Sealed.

Target confirmed.

No uncertainty left.

He took the paper.

Then walked downstairs.

---

Tannis was still trying to impress Zareth.

Badly.

“Our Houses have always respected Drakonis—”

Zareth glanced toward the staircase.

“There he is.”

Tannis turned.

Saw Zee.

His face died.

Not literally.

Yet.

“King Darkheart.”

Zee descended.

Human pupils.

Calm.

That frightened Tannis more.

“How did you—”

Zee tossed the contract onto the dining table.

Tannis stopped talking.

Ner entered behind Zee holding a second ledger.

“Found the payments.”

Zee looked at Tannis.

“You planned to attack my refuge.”

Tannis glanced toward his guests.

Political calculation.

Witnesses.

Good.

“I planned nothing.”

Zee smelled fear.

Lie.

“Try again.”

Tannis’s jaw tightened.

Zee did not compel him.

Not yet.

The evidence already existed.

“You house dangerous bloodlines,” Tannis said.

There it was.

“Which?”

“Mixed ones.”

Ner’s face cooled.

Tannis continued.

“Unstable creatures.”

“Children?”

Tannis hesitated.

Wrong.

Zee’s pupils became slits.

“They are not children forever.”

Zareth’s expression changed.

Even Dragon morality had limits.

Zee walked closer.

“You marked their rooms.”

Tannis swallowed.

“They will become what their blood makes them.”

Zee smiled faintly.

“Interesting.”

Tannis’s eyes flicked toward his guards.

Too late.

Zareth spoke aloud.

“Don’t.”

One word.

Not magic.

Authority.

The guards froze anyway.

Zee stopped in front of Tannis.

“You know what my father believed?”

Tannis frowned.

“No.”

“Good.”

Zee leaned closer.

“It means you invented this stupidity independently.”

Ner almost smiled.

Tannis reached for a hidden blade.

Zee caught the wrist without looking.

Snap.

Tannis screamed.

The guests scattered backward.

Zee did not chase anyone.

They were witnesses.

Useful ones.

“You planned an attack.”

“Yes!”

Finally.

“You knew families were there.”

“Yes.”

“Children.”

“Yes.”

No remorse.

Enough.

Zee looked toward the guards.

“Leave.”

They hesitated.

Compulsion rolled outward.

“Leave.”

Every guard obeyed.

Some resisted for seconds.

Then failed.

Mass domination.

Voice.

Presence.

Blood.

No eye contact needed.

Tannis stared.

Zee returned his attention to him.

“You will not attack Darkheart.”

Tannis laughed weakly.

“You are going to kill me.”

“Yes.”

“Before I did anything.”

The room went very still.

There it was.

The line.

Zee looked at the marked contract.

Then at Tannis.

“You paid them.”

Tannis said nothing.

“You selected the targets.”

Silence.

“You bought Dragonbane.”

Silence.

“You marked where children sleep.”

Tannis’s breathing became uneven.

Zee smiled.

“You did plenty.”

Then he killed him.

Knife.

Heart.

Fast.

No feeding.

Not everything needed blood.

---

The seven hired killers received messages before midnight.

Zee sent them copies of the contract.

And one sentence.

**Walk away, or I come next.**

Six abandoned the job.

One did not.

The seventh decided the warning was a bluff.

He reached the refuge two nights later.

Zee was waiting.

Wolf form.

Near-black.

Crimson-and-gold eyes shining between trees.

The assassin stopped.

He had not expected the King personally.

That was the point.

Zee stalked forward.

No rush.

The man fired the Dragonbane bolt.

Wolf Zee dodged.

Circled.

The assassin tried blood-tracking powder.

Wrong prey.

Zee went downwind.

Disappeared.

The man spun.

“Darkheart!”

Nothing.

Then breathing behind him.

He turned.

Too late.

Wolf jaws caught his shoulder.

Dragged him down.

Zee shifted human while pinning him.

The assassin stared up at mature horns and slit pupils.

“You warned me.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“To give you a choice.”

The man swallowed.

“And now?”

Zee’s fangs descended.

“You chose.”

He fed.

Completely.

The refuge never saw a battle.

The children never woke.

No buildings burned.

No one screamed except the man who ignored the warning.

By morning, the story had already changed.

King Zee Darkheart had killed a lord for an attack that had not yet happened.

Some kingdoms called it tyranny.

Some called it necessary.

Some called it proof that Darkheart had become dangerous.

The families inside the refuge called it something else.

Nothing.

Because they slept through the night.

Zee liked that result most.

---

# Chapter Seventy-Seven

## Teeth Beneath the Lake

The next threat did not care about politics.

That was refreshing.

A fishing town north of Vesper lost twelve people in six days.

No bodies.

No blood.

No ransom.

No warning.

Just boats returning empty.

Lucien sent investigators.

Two vanished.

Rez went himself.

That was when Zee received the message.

Not a plea.

A report.

**Something is under Lake Edrin. It is not Vampire, Wolf, Witch, or Demon. Bring Ner if he wants to come. Leave the army.**

Zee smiled.

Ner looked over.

“What?”

“Rez found something weird.”

“That sentence has killed people before.”

Zareth, in human form beside the window, looked interested.

“Lake?”

“Yes.”

Zareth immediately stood.

Zee looked at him.

“Drakonis?”

“My mother has it.”

“You said that last time.”

“And she still does.”

Through the Link came an additional layer.

Drakonis calm.

No immediate threat.

A council later.

Zareth had chosen to come.

Fine.

They left before sunrise.

---

Lake Edrin looked peaceful.

That meant nothing anymore.

Rez stood on the pier wearing Vesper armor.

Twenty-one.

Tired.

Irritated.

Future King.

“You took your time.”

Zee stepped onto the dock.

“You said nothing about urgency.”

“Twelve people are missing.”

“You sent a report.”

“I assumed you could infer.”

Ner sighed.

“Still brothers.”

Zareth looked over the lake.

His Dragon senses sharpened.

“There is something alive beneath us.”

Rez stared.

“You can just say that now.”

Zareth looked at him.

“Yes.”

“I miss when Zee had to translate.”

“No, you don’t.”

“I really don’t.”

Zee crouched at the edge.

Wolf scent found wet wood.

Fear.

Fish.

Human.

Then nothing.

Vampire blood sense reached only so far through water.

No heartbeats below.

Ner touched the surface.

Pure Gold spread in thin rings.

His expression changed.

“Blood.”

Rez stepped closer.

“Where?”

“In the lake.”

Zee looked down.

No red.

Ner continued.

“Old.”

“Diluted.”

“Moving.”

Bloodsong hummed beneath his voice.

The water answered.

A faint vibration traveled toward the center of the lake.

Then stopped.

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Something collected it.”

Zareth looked east.

“I can see movement.”

“Where?”

“Deep.”

A full image crossed the Link.

Dark water.

A shape longer than a ship.

Many limbs.

No normal Dragon outline.

Zee smiled.

Rez stared.

“Why are you smiling?”

“Because nobody is trying to overthrow me.”

“That is your standard now?”

“Yes.”

---

They took one boat.

Zareth remained in human form because true Dragon size would disturb half the lake before they knew what they were hunting.

Rez rowed.

Complained.

Ner listened to the blood.

Zee watched the water.

Halfway out, the boat stopped.

Not slowed.

Stopped.

Rez looked down.

“We hit something.”

Zee shook his head.

“No.”

Something grabbed the underside.

The boat lifted.

Then shattered.

Water swallowed all four.

---

Zee shifted before hitting the bottom.

Wolf form.

Wrong environment.

He shifted back immediately.

Useful information.

Zareth changed next.

Not full true Dragon.

Too large for the confined depth.

Human form remained, Teal-and-Gold Mana exploding around him as he kicked upward.

Ner’s Gold formed a bubble around his head.

Rez created Blue-White pressure beneath his feet and pushed himself toward the surface.

Zee did neither.

He let himself sink.

Something moved below.

Good.

He wanted to see it.

The lake darkened.

Then a mouth opened.

Too wide.

Circular.

Rows of inward teeth.

Not one creature.

Several bodies fused around a central feeding cavity.

Zee barely moved before it struck.

Vampire speed worked badly underwater.

Still enough.

He twisted.

Teeth tore his side instead of taking him whole.

Blood flooded the lake.

The creature changed instantly.

Every limb turned toward Zee.

Predator.

Blood-driven.

Zee smiled underwater.

Of course.

He cut his own palm.

More blood.

Bait.

Then swam deeper.

The creature followed.

Above, Zareth’s mental voice hit through the Link.

**You are doing something stupid.**

Zee sent back location, depth, the shape, and amusement.

**I am testing it.**

The Link returned irritation layered with Zee’s own blood loss.

**It has thirty-seven mouths.**

**Thirty-eight. You missed the lower one.**

**I hate you.**

Warmth beneath the insult.

Then Zareth moved.

---

The creature lunged again.

Zee waited.

Wolf instinct could not track scent underwater properly.

But predatory reading remained.

The thing always tightened the left cluster of limbs before turning.

Assassin observation.

Pattern.

Zee dodged right.

Grabbed one fleshy appendage.

Crimson Demonic Dragon heat surged through his palm.

The creature convulsed.

Heat mattered.

Good.

Zee pulled.

Vampire strength against water resistance.

The creature twisted.

One mouth closed over Zee’s forearm.

Dark crimson-black scales spread.

Teeth penetrated between them.

Pain.

Blood.

Zee snarled.

Then Witchcraft.

One hand.

“Open.”

The mouth forced apart.

Zee tore free.

Above him, Gold flashed through the lake.

Ner.

Not attacking the creature.

Mapping blood.

His voice resonated underwater strangely.

“Three cores!”

Rez heard through the water badly.

Zareth heard Zee through the Link perfectly.

Zee received Ner’s hand signal.

Three feeding centers.

Not one heart.

That explained the fused body.

Zee sent the positions instantly through the Link.

Zareth answered with a complete tactical concept in less than a second.

One core each.

Fourth person controls escape.

Zee agreed.

---

Zareth shifted above the surface.

True Dragon.

Massive wings spread.

Then he plunged.

The lake exploded around him.

His size displaced enough water to send waves toward shore.

Rez shouted something rude from a floating wreck.

Zareth ignored him.

Teal-and-Gold Dragonfire could not burn normally underwater.

Dragon Mana could.

He drove it through one claw directly into the first core.

The creature screamed through thirty-eight mouths.

Ner hit the second.

Pure Gold boundary tightened around the blood circulation leading into it.

Then Bloodsong.

One sharp tone.

Every stolen human blood trace inside the creature resonated at once.

The second core spasmed.

Rez found the third through movement.

Blue-White Mana froze the water around it into one crushing block.

Not enough to kill.

Enough to hold.

Zee went in.

No giant spell.

No grand attack.

He reached the frozen section.

Claws extended.

Wolf aggression.

Vampire strength.

Dragon durability.

Assassin precision.

He tore through the exposed tissue and found the third core.

It pulsed.

Not a heart.

A blood sac filled with mixed blood from dozens of species.

Interesting.

Dangerous.

Zee’s fangs descended.

Ner felt his intent immediately.

“Zee!”

Zee looked up.

Ner shook his head violently.

Unknown creature.

Unknown blood.

Good argument.

Zee almost listened.

Then the creature opened another mouth around Rez.

Decision over.

Zee bit the core.

---

The blood was awful.

Salt.

Rot.

Predatory enzymes.

Human.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Fish.

Unknown.

Not one species.

A collector.

The creature had survived by storing blood from everything it ate.

Zee drank.

His Crimson biology reacted violently.

Rejected most of it immediately.

Good.

Then something useful remained.

Not power.

Adaptation.

His body recognized the creature’s method of functioning without a conventional heartbeat.

The old lesson from bloodless beings returned.

Foreign circulation patterns.

Multiple centers.

Distributed life.

Zee’s blood sense changed.

Expanded slightly.

No longer searching only for hearts or normal vascular flow.

Now it noticed concentrations.

Movement.

Where supernatural life gathered inside a body even when anatomy was wrong.

Permanent.

Small.

Dangerous.

Enough.

Zee stopped drinking before the mixture poisoned even him.

Then ripped the core free.

The creature convulsed.

Zareth destroyed the first.

Ner collapsed the second.

All thirty-eight mouths opened.

Then went still.

The thing sank.

Dead.

---

They found the missing people afterward.

Not all dead.

Five remained alive inside membrane sacs along the lake floor.

Stored.

Like food.

Rez cut the first free.

Ner stabilized two with Gold and Bloodsong.

Zareth returned to human form so his Dragon body would not crush the rescue site.

Zee carried the last survivor to shore.

A boy of maybe seventeen.

Cold.

Terrified.

Alive.

The fishing town gathered.

Nobody cheered at first.

They stared at Zee.

Wet black clothes.

Blood on his throat.

Horns.

Crimson-and-gold eyes.

One fisherman whispered:

“The Crimson Demonic Dragon.”

Zee sighed.

Rez laughed.

“It followed you north.”

“I hate people.”

Ner smiled.

“No, you don’t.”

Zee looked toward the rescued boy.

Then the families running forward.

“No.”

Human pupils returned.

“Not all of them.”

Zareth stood beside him, soaked and deeply offended.

“My clothes are ruined.”

Rez stared.

“You are a Dragon.”

“I liked these clothes.”

Ner started laughing.

Zee joined him.

Even Rez did.

For a moment there was no kingdom war.

No Covenant.

No prophecy.

No bloodline extermination.

Just four twenty-one-year-old men standing soaked beside a dead lake monster while five families got people back they thought were gone forever.

Then a Vesper rider arrived at full speed.

Of course.

Rez saw him and groaned.

“No.”

The rider dismounted.

“Prince Rez.”

“What?”

“A border fortress has been taken.”

Rez’s humor vanished.

“By whom?”

The rider swallowed.

“They say they belong to no kingdom.”

Zee’s expression sharpened.

Zareth looked toward him.

Through the Link:

**You were enjoying yourself.**

Zee answered privately.

**For almost a minute.**

Ner sighed.

“Where?”

The rider pointed south.

Rez already started walking.

“My problem.”

Zee followed.

Rez looked back.

“I said my problem.”

“Yes.”

“You do not have to come.”

“I know.”

Rez stopped.

Zee smiled faintly.

“That is why I am coming.”

Rez stared.

Then shook his head.

“Fine.”

Zareth shifted back into true Dragon form.

Ner climbed onto his own horse.

No one climbed onto Zareth.

Never.

The four moved south.

Behind them, the lake was safe.

Ahead, somebody had taken a Vesper fortress and claimed allegiance to no crown.

The world had finally offered them something new.

Zee’s pupils narrowed into slits.

Good.

He had been getting bored.

# Chapter Seventy-Six

## The People Zee Could Not Reach

Winter reached Darkheart three months after the Covenant fell.

Zee turned twenty-two beneath a sky full of snow.

He did not celebrate much.

Darkheart did.

That was different.

The old Witch kingdom had changed around him.

Vampires now lived beyond the eastern market.

Wolf families had taken homes near the northern forest.

Witches still filled the oldest districts, but they no longer stood alone.

Mixed-blood families crossed the gates without hiding what they were.

Refugees arrived every week.

Some had heard stories about the Crimson Tribrid.

Others knew only one thing.

Darkheart did not punish blood.

Darkheart punished what people chose to do with it.

That reputation kept growing.

So did the kingdom.

And so did the attacks.

---

The first horn sounded before sunrise.

Western border.

Raiders.

Zee was already moving when the second horn came.

South.

Poison attack against a refugee caravan.

Then a third.

North.

A Darkheart village under siege.

Three attacks.

At once.

Zee stopped in the war room.

For one second.

Only one.

Merek looked at him.

“Majesty?”

Zee stared at the map.

He could reach the western border fastest.

Ner was already near the southern road inspecting new Bloodsong wards.

The north had Captain Elara Voss and forty Darkheart defenders.

Not enough.

Rez was in Vesper.

Zareth in Drakonis.

Different kingdoms.

Different responsibilities.

Zee hated the answer before he gave it.

“Send reinforcements north.”

Merek nodded.

“South?”

“Ner has it.”

“And you?”

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“West.”

Then he was gone.

---

The western raiders were Vampires.

Thirty-two.

Old enough to believe numbers mattered.

They entered through frozen woods and slaughtered the first patrol before anyone sounded the alarm.

Zee found them by blood.

Not tracks.

Not sound.

Blood.

His Vampire nature opened the forest around him.

Three wounded Darkheart soldiers.

One dead.

Thirty-two foreign bloodlines.

Two carrying silver.

Four recently fed.

One poisoned.

Zee shifted into Wolf form.

Near-black fur disappeared through snow.

He hunted without magic.

One raider vanished.

Then another.

Then a third.

By the time they understood the King was inside the forest, seven were already down.

A Vampire shouted:

“Form on me!”

Zee circled behind him.

Shifted human.

One hand lifted.

“Still.”

Four froze.

The others resisted.

Zee moved before resistance became action.

Vampire speed.

Assassin precision.

A throat.

A knee.

A wrist.

One Wolf-like strike with clawed fingers beneath a rib.

Then blood.

He fed from the strongest Vampire.

Deliberately.

The enemy’s blood carried an anti-compulsion tincture.

Zee tasted it.

His Crimson biology separated it before it spread.

Not immunity.

Recognition.

Another adaptation becoming familiar.

The Vampire weakened.

Zee released him alive.

“Who sent you?”

The man spat blood.

“No one.”

Lie.

Zee smiled.

“Again.”

Compulsion hit through voice and blood dominance.

The Vampire’s eyes widened despite trying not to look at him.

“Who?”

“Lord Arven.”

Different lord.

Different motive.

Border land.

Good.

No grand conspiracy.

Zee broke his neck.

Then finished the battle.

Twenty-seven minutes.

Too long.

Because when Zee returned to the war room—

the northern messenger was already there.

Blood on his cloak.

Zee stopped.

No one spoke.

He knew.

“How many?”

Merek swallowed.

“Eleven.”

Zee’s face emptied.

“Defenders?”

“Seven.”

“Civilians?”

“Four.”

Snow melted beneath Zee’s boots.

Heat.

Crimson Demonic Dragon heat.

Controlled.

Barely.

“Captain Voss?”

“Alive.”

That helped.

Not enough.

Zee turned toward the northern map.

He had killed thirty-two enemies.

Protected the western border.

Saved dozens.

And eleven people died somewhere else because he could not stand in two places at once.

The truth was becoming impossible to ignore.

Zee could survive the world.

His people could not always do the same.

---

He reached the northern village after sunset.

The battle was over.

Darkheart had won.

That word felt useless beside bodies.

Captain Elara Voss sat against a broken wall while a healer wrapped her ribs.

Thirty-three.

Witch.

Born Darkheart.

Had served under Victor.

Chose to stay under Zee.

She tried standing when he approached.

“Don’t.”

She stopped.

“Majesty.”

Zee looked around.

“Tell me.”

Elara did.

The attackers were Wolves hired by a northern claimant who wanted Darkheart forest territory.

No connection to the western Vampires.

No connection to the southern poisoners.

They struck because Zee was elsewhere.

Darkheart held.

Barely.

Elara killed four herself.

Lost seven soldiers.

Then something in her voice changed.

“Kael is dying.”

Zee turned.

“Who?”

“One of mine.”

Elara forced herself up despite his order.

“This way.”

---

Kael Marrin was twenty-four.

A Witch.

Not famous.

Not noble.

Not important to history.

Not yet.

He had been born in the northern village.

His mother made winter medicines.

His younger sister worked in the mill.

He joined Darkheart’s guard at eighteen because raiders had taken his father years earlier.

He was sarcastic when nervous.

Terrible at cards.

Apparently owed half the barracks money.

And he had spent the morning holding a cellar door while six children hid behind it.

A Wolf had ripped through his side.

Another had bitten deep into his shoulder.

The healer had stopped most of the bleeding.

Could not stop the poison.

Not normal venom.

Something made to kill Witches by turning their own Mana against damaged organs.

Kael’s mother knelt beside him.

His sister held his hand.

Zee stood in the doorway.

He smelled death approaching.

Slowly.

Certainly.

The healer looked at Zee.

“We cannot pull the poison without tearing his magic apart.”

Zee stepped closer.

Kael opened one eye.

“Majesty.”

His voice was barely there.

Zee crouched.

“You saved six children.”

Kael smiled weakly.

“Seven.”

Elara looked over.

“Seven?”

“Boy under the grain table.”

Even dying, correcting the count.

Zee almost smiled.

Then Kael coughed blood.

His mother broke.

Zee looked at the blood.

Witch.

Only Witch.

Strong.

Young.

Dying.

And suddenly—

Ner.

Fifteen.

Blood everywhere.

Heart stopping.

Zee biting open his own wrist because he had nothing else.

*Take mine. Live.*

Back then, Zee knew nothing.

Now he knew one thing.

His blood could change survival.

He still did not know how.

That made the choice worse.

Kael’s mother looked at him.

“Can you help him?”

Zee did not lie.

“I don’t know.”

She gripped Kael’s hand harder.

“Will it hurt him?”

“Yes.”

Kael laughed once.

“Bit late for that.”

Zee looked directly at him.

“This has to be your choice.”

Kael’s eyes focused.

Good.

Person first.

Always.

“If I do this, you may change.”

“Into what?”

“I don’t know.”

“Will I live?”

“I don’t know.”

Kael looked toward his mother.

Then his sister.

Then Zee.

“Do it.”

No hesitation.

His mother whispered:

“Kael…”

He squeezed her hand.

“I don’t want to die.”

That was enough.

Zee opened his wrist.

Crimson-and-gold eyes narrowed.

His blood welled dark red.

Hot.

Alive.

He held it to Kael’s mouth.

“Drink.”

Kael did.

One swallow.

Then another.

His Witch Mana convulsed.

The healer stumbled backward.

Kael screamed.

Pure Witch energy erupted across the room.

Zee grabbed his shoulders.

“Stay with me.”

Kael’s eyes snapped open.

Then his heart stopped.

His mother screamed.

Zee froze.

No.

Not again.

One second.

Two.

Three.

Then—

heartbeat.

Hard.

Different.

Kael gasped.

His back arched.

The Wolf poison inside him began burning out.

Not disappearing.

Losing.

His Witch Mana stayed.

Zee felt it clearly.

Still Witch.

But something else entered beside it.

Predatory.

Cold.

Hungry.

Kael’s eyes opened.

Dark red flashed beneath them.

Fangs descended.

His mother stopped crying.

For a different reason.

Kael stared at Zee.

“What did you do to me?”

Zee looked at him.

Alive.

Changed.

No answer simple enough.

“I saved you.”

Kael breathed.

His Witch Mana flared again.

Then his new Vampire senses hit.

Every heartbeat in the room.

Every blood scent.

His face twisted.

“Hunger.”

Zee understood immediately.

He looked at the healer.

“Animal blood first.”

Kael grabbed Zee’s wrist before he could rise.

Strong.

Stronger than before.

“Majesty.”

Zee looked down.

Kael’s fear was real.

Not of Zee.

Of himself.

“What am I?”

Zee did not give him a race name.

Not yet.

He squeezed Kael’s hand once.

“Kael Marrin.”

The young guard stared.

Zee continued.

“We figure out the rest after you stop dying.”

Kael laughed.

Weak.

Still himself.

Good.

That mattered more than history.

---

By morning, Kael was walking.

Barely.

His Witchcraft remained.

His Vampire nature was undeniable.

Fangs.

Healing.

Strength.

Blood hunger.

Enhanced senses.

No collapse between the two.

No Witch nature burned out.

No Vampire corruption erasing magic.

Two supernatural natures living together.

Naturally.

Because of Zee’s blood.

Ner arrived from the southern road before noon.

He had stopped the poison attack there without Zee.

Twenty-three people saved.

Two attackers captured.

One killed by Ner personally.

He entered Kael’s room and stopped.

Gold flashed in his eyes.

Then dark-red.

Bloodsong hummed beneath his breathing.

He looked at Zee.

“You did it again.”

Zee stared at Kael.

“No.”

Ner frowned.

Zee continued.

“This time I chose to.”

Silence.

That changed everything.

Ner walked to Kael.

“May I?”

Kael looked suspicious.

“Do what?”

“Listen.”

“That is somehow worse.”

Ner smiled.

“I like him.”

Kael sighed.

“Everyone says that until cards.”

Ner placed two fingers near Kael’s wrist.

Bloodsong.

Pure Gold.

His expression sharpened.

“Witch.”

“Yes.”

“Vampire.”

Zee’s face remained still.

Ner looked toward him.

“Both stable.”

There it was.

Proof.

Not theory.

Not Ner’s complicated Siren inheritance.

Something cleaner.

Something reproducible?

Maybe.

Too early.

Zee looked at Kael’s mother sleeping in the chair beside him.

His sister curled beneath a blanket.

Kael alive between them.

That was why this existed.

Not armies.

Not experiments.

Not history.

One person refusing to die.

Zee stood.

Outside, eleven graves were being prepared.

He could not save them.

But Kael would not join them.

Something inside Zee settled.

A new belief.

Cold.

Simple.

If the world would not stop trying to kill his people—

then he would make his people harder to kill.

---

# Chapter Seventy-Seven

## What His Blood Had Made

Kael Marrin hated mornings now.

Not because of Vampire weakness to daylight.

There was none.

Not in him.

At least not yet.

He hated mornings because everyone wanted to examine him.

Healer.

Witch.

Ner.

Zee.

Elara.

His mother.

His sister.

Then Merek.

Then two Darkheart scholars who Kael threw out after one called him “the subject.”

Zee approved.

Strongly.

By the third day, Kael stood in the training courtyard with a sword.

Elara stared.

“You were dead four days ago.”

“Almost.”

“Put the sword down.”

“No.”

“You are still healing.”

Kael looked at the wound in his side.

Closed.

Not scarless.

But impossible compared to four days earlier.

“That seems debatable.”

Elara hit him.

Wooden practice blade to ribs.

Kael moved faster than expected.

Caught it.

Both froze.

Vampire speed.

Not Zee’s.

His own.

Kael stared at his hand.

Then released the blade.

“I hate that.”

Elara lowered hers.

“You will learn.”

“What if I don’t want to?”

Zee stood above the courtyard balcony.

He heard.

Did not interrupt.

That question belonged to Kael.

Elara answered:

“Then you decide what kind of life you want with what happened.”

Good.

Zee left before either noticed him.

He did not own Kael’s future.

Blood did not make ownership.

That law formed naturally.

Because the alternative disgusted him.

---

Darkheart noticed anyway.

People talked.

The northern village knew Kael should have died.

Soldiers had watched his heart stop.

Now he walked.

Cast Witch magic.

Healed too quickly.

Smelled blood through walls.

And had fangs.

Rumors moved before Zee could control them.

By the end of the week:

**King Zee brought a dead Witch back as a Vampire.**

Wrong.

**King Zee can turn any Witch into a creature with two bloodlines.**

Unproven.

**King Zee is building an immortal army.**

Completely false.

**Darkheart has a Witch that drinks blood.**

Unfortunately accurate.

Kael hated that one most.

---

Ner found Zee in Aurelia’s old solar.

The room had changed over the years.

Not erased.

Changed.

Zee kept her chair.

Her books.

One hairpin.

But the room now held kingdom maps too.

Reports.

Blood samples sealed behind wards.

Not trophies.

Research.

Careful.

Ner placed Kael’s latest notes on the desk.

“No instability.”

Zee leaned back.

“Yet.”

“Yet.”

“Magic?”

“Still Witch.”

“Hunger?”

“Manageable.”

“Compulsion?”

Ner smiled.

“He accidentally told his sister to stop yelling.”

Zee frowned.

“And?”

“She stopped.”

Silence.

Then Zee almost laughed.

“Accidentally?”

“He panicked.”

“That sounds familiar.”

Ner gave him a look.

Fair.

Zee read further.

Kael could cast.

Heal.

Feed.

Use Vampire strength.

His Witch nature did not weaken.

No new Siren blood.

No Bloodsong.

Just Witch and Vampire.

Two stable natures.

Ner sat opposite him.

“You know what this means.”

“Yes.”

“You can do this again.”

“Maybe.”

“Do you want to?”

Zee looked at him.

“No.”

Ner waited.

Zee continued.

“I want people to stop dying.”

Different.

Ner nodded.

“That is not the same thing.”

“No.”

Silence.

Then Ner asked:

“If another Kael happens?”

Zee looked toward the window.

Snow.

Darkheart rooftops.

People.

More than Victor ever allowed inside these walls.

“If they are dying.”

“And they choose?”

“Yes.”

Ner’s face softened slightly.

“Then?”

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“Then I give them the choice Kael had.”

Not creation program.

Not army.

Emergency.

Life.

For now.

---

Kael’s first real problem came that night.

Hunger.

Not ordinary.

Not manageable.

Three bags of animal blood were not enough.

His body rejected the fourth.

He became restless.

Aggressive.

Scared.

His Witch Mana reacted to the hunger and started breaking objects around him.

Kael locked himself inside the northern barracks before he hurt anyone.

Zee arrived to find six soldiers outside.

One held a silver chain.

Zee looked at him.

“Put that away.”

“He asked us to use it.”

“Put it away.”

The soldier obeyed.

Not compulsion.

King.

Zee entered alone.

Kael stood near the far wall.

Eyes dark.

Fangs visible.

Crimson Witch energy crawling around his fingers.

“Stay back.”

Zee closed the door.

“No.”

“I can hear everyone.”

“Yes.”

“I can smell them.”

“Yes.”

“I want—”

Kael stopped.

Ashamed.

Zee’s expression cooled.

“Say it.”

“I want blood.”

“Good.”

Kael stared.

“Good?”

“You know what it is.”

Zee stepped closer.

“Now control what you do with it.”

Kael’s breathing worsened.

“I don’t know how.”

“Then learn.”

Zee opened his wrist.

Kael recoiled.

“No.”

“You need supernatural blood.”

“I am not feeding from you.”

“Why?”

“You are the King.”

Zee stared.

“That is a terrible reason.”

Kael almost laughed despite himself.

Then hunger hit again.

He bent over.

Zee held out his wrist.

“One swallow.”

Kael hesitated.

Then fed.

One.

Only one.

He pulled away himself.

Good.

The effect was immediate.

His Witch Mana stabilized.

The hunger retreated.

Kael stared.

“Why did that work?”

Zee looked at the wound closing on his wrist.

“Because animal blood feeds the Vampire.”

“And yours?”

Zee’s expression sharpened.

“Apparently speaks to both.”

Witch.

Vampire.

His blood had created the bridge.

Interesting.

Dangerous.

Zee was beginning to understand.

Not enough to be comfortable.

Enough to continue.

---

The next attack came eleven days later.

Not on Zee.

Not Darkheart Castle.

A frontier refuge.

Forty miles east.

Zee was in council when the alarm arrived.

Sixty mercenaries.

Demon-backed.

Wards preventing communication.

Three Darkheart units trapped.

Zee stood immediately.

Then another messenger entered.

Northern forest.

Monster breach.

Children missing.

Two crises.

Again.

Merek looked toward him.

Zee looked at the maps.

Old instinct:

Go.

Personally.

Everywhere.

Impossible.

Kael entered the war room wearing guard armor.

Still pale.

Still adjusting.

But standing.

“Send me east.”

Zee looked over.

“No.”

Kael’s jaw tightened.

“Why?”

“You are eleven days old in this body.”

“I am twenty-four years old.”

Good correction.

Zee stared.

Kael continued.

“My unit is trapped there.”

“Elara commands them.”

“She trained me.”

“You are not ready.”

Kael stepped closer.

“Neither were the seven people we buried.”

Silence.

That landed.

Zee’s face hardened.

Kael did not back down.

“I am stronger now.”

“Unproven.”

“Then let me prove it.”

Zee hated the logic.

Not because Kael was wrong.

Because Zee finally saw the future inside it.

People would choose to become stronger if the alternative was watching everyone die.

Not soldiers made by Zee.

People choosing survival.

Merek interrupted.

“Majesty, we need a decision.”

Zee looked at the map.

East.

North.

Two places.

He could not take both.

Fine.

“Kael goes east.”

Kael nodded once.

“Elara commands.”

“Yes.”

“You follow her orders.”

Kael looked annoyed.

“Yes.”

“Ner goes with them.”

Ner stood.

“What about you?”

“North.”

Rez’s voice came through a communication mirror from Vesper.

“I can send ten riders east within the hour.”

Zee nodded.

“Do it.”

Zareth’s voice entered Zee’s mind through the Link from Drakonis.

**There is movement near your northern mountains. I can reach the forest faster than you.**

Zee stopped.

More beneath the sentence.

Wind.

High altitude.

No current Drakonis emergency.

Zareth was already flying.

**You are supposed to be in council.**

**So are you.**

Zee smiled faintly.

**Take the forest. I will go east.**

Zareth answered instantly.

**Done.**

There.

No one person everywhere.

Network.

Kingdom.

Family.

Choice.

Zee looked at Kael.

“Change of plan.”

Kael frowned.

“You are coming east?”

“Yes.”

“That defeats the point.”

Zee smiled.

“No.”

He looked toward Merek.

“Next time I may not.”

That silenced the room.

Because everyone understood there would be a next time.

---

The eastern refuge was already breaking when they arrived.

Demon-backed mercenaries had breached two walls.

Darkheart soldiers held the inner courtyard.

Elara fought with one arm burned nearly useless.

Kael saw her.

Something changed.

Vampire speed.

He disappeared.

Not Zee-fast.

Fast enough.

Kael hit the first mercenary before the man reached Elara.

Witch force threw another backward.

Then Kael bit the third.

Everyone froze.

Including Kael.

Blood entered his mouth.

Human.

He released immediately.

Horror.

Zee saw.

Not weakness.

First feeding in battle.

Different.

“Kael!”

Kael looked over.

Zee pointed toward Elara.

“Protect your commander.”

Simple.

No shame.

No lecture.

Kael moved.

Good.

Zee took the center.

Silent Witchcraft broke a Demon ward.

Wolf senses found the hidden caster.

Vampire speed crossed the courtyard.

Assassin knife ended him.

A Demon emerged behind Zee.

Crimson Demonic Dragon heat forced it solid when it tried slipping into shadow.

Zee caught its throat.

Fangs descended.

Demon blood.

Old enemy.

Familiar pressure.

He drank until it weakened.

Then killed it.

Around him, Darkheart fought.

Not perfectly.

Not safely.

But stronger than months earlier.

Kael moved among them like something the attackers had never seen.

Witch sigils in one hand.

Vampire strength in the other.

He took a blade through the stomach.

Elara screamed his name.

Kael looked down.

Then back up.

Healing already starting.

The mercenary who stabbed him froze.

Kael smiled.

Not like Zee.

His own smile.

Nervous.

A little disbelieving.

Then he punched the man unconscious.

Zee saw it.

History beginning.

Not as a title.

As one person refusing to fall where he should have.

The refuge survived.

Six Darkheart soldiers died.

Too many.

But without Kael—

it would have been more.

That mattered.

It also terrified Zee.

Because now he had proof of the thing he feared wanting.

His blood could make survival more likely.

---

Three weeks later, the first foreign letter arrived asking to purchase Kael’s blood.

Zee burned it.

The second asked whether Darkheart would “supply transformed soldiers.”

He burned that too.

The third came from a kingdom demanding Kael be surrendered for “containment.”

Zee sent that one back.

With one sentence.

**Come take him.**

No one did.

Not yet.

Kael read the copy later.

“You did not have to do that.”

Zee looked at him.

“Yes, I did.”

“I am not property.”

“I know.”

“Then why speak for me?”

Zee paused.

Good.

Kael had caught him.

Zee corrected immediately.

“You are right.”

Kael blinked.

“That was easier than expected.”

Zee frowned.

“Do not ruin it.”

Kael smiled.

Then looked toward the letter.

“If they come?”

Zee leaned back.

“You decide whether you stay.”

“And if I leave Darkheart?”

“You leave.”

Kael stared.

“No curse?”

“No.”

“No blood oath?”

“No.”

“No ownership because you made me?”

Zee’s face went cold.

“I saved you.”

“That is all.”

Kael nodded slowly.

Good.

Person first.

Always.

Outside the chamber, people had begun calling Kael something.

Not officially.

Not yet.

The Witch with Vampire blood.

The Blood Witch.

The Night Witch.

Most names were terrible.

History would eventually settle on something simpler.

Witch-Vampire.

One of the first original hybrid bloodlines Zee Darkheart would ever create.

But Zee did not care about history tonight.

He cared that Kael’s mother still had a son.

His sister still had a brother.

Elara still had a soldier.

And six children from the northern village still had the man who held the cellar door.

That was enough.

For now.

Then the northern report arrived.

Zareth had stopped the monster breach.

Three missing children recovered.

One dead.

Zee read the name twice.

A girl.

Eight years old.

Too late.

Again.

The victory soured instantly.

Kael watched him.

“You cannot save everyone.”

Zee’s eyes lifted.

Human pupils.

Calm.

Cold.

“No.”

He folded the report.

“But I can change the odds.”

There it was.

Not an army.

Not yet.

Not ambition.

A belief.

And somewhere beyond Darkheart, kingdoms had begun hearing that King Zee Darkheart had done something no ordinary ruler could do.

A dying Witch had survived.

Now he possessed fangs.

Vampire strength.

Vampire hunger.

And all of his Witchcraft.

The world had spent twenty-two years fearing what Zee Darkheart was.

Now it had something new to fear.

What his blood could make.
