# Chapter One Hundred Twenty

## The Prince Who Stayed in the Light

The morning after the kidnapping attempt, Darkheart expected Zee to disappear his son.

The rumor moved before breakfast.

Some thought Zayrlen would be moved beneath the castle.

Others believed Rez would take him somewhere beyond Darkheart.

A few assumed Zee would place so many concealment spells around the newborn Prince that nobody outside the family would ever see him again.

They were wrong.

At noon—

Zee carried Zayrlen into the central courtyard.

Publicly.

No disguise.

No veil.

No hidden carriage.

No illusion changing his face.

Zayrlen slept against his father's chest beneath a dark blanket embroidered in Crimson and Gold.

Ner walked beside them.

Still recovering.

Still armed.

Still capable of killing anyone stupid enough to mistake recovery for weakness.

Rez stood near the steps.

Zareth leaned against one column in Human form.

Elias, Kael, Tessa, Amara, and Rhyven were spread through the courtyard.

Not arranged like guards.

Family rarely needed arranging.

Darkheart gathered quietly.

Zee stopped in the center.

Zayrlen stirred.

His tiny heartbeat changed.

Then settled again when Zee adjusted his hold.

A councilor stepped forward carefully.

“Majesty.”

Zee looked at him.

“We assumed the Prince would remain within the inner keep.”

“He will not.”

Silence.

Another official asked:

“After yesterday?”

“Yes.”

Someone farther back whispered:

“They nearly took him.”

Zee heard.

Of course he did.

He looked toward the crowd.

“They nearly reached him.”

Different.

The courtyard quieted.

“My son will grow up knowing his kingdom.”

His Crimson Phoenix wings remained folded.

His voice did not need them.

“He will know its roads.”

Its people.

Its walls.

Its names.

“He will not spend his childhood inside a locked room because enemies decided his existence frightened them.”

Ner looked at him.

Something passed between them.

Agreement.

Not discussion.

Already decided.

Zee continued.

“If they come again—”

His pupils narrowed.

“Darkheart kills them again.”

No grand applause followed.

The statement was too simple.

Too believable.

Then an old Wolf woman stepped out of the crowd.

She held one of the badly carved wooden animals Darkheart children had been leaving outside the royal rooms.

Zee recognized it.

A Wolf.

Mostly.

One leg was shorter than the others.

The woman stopped several feet away.

“For the Prince.”

Zee looked at Ner.

Ner nodded.

The woman placed the toy on the stone.

Then walked away.

Another person came.

Then another.

Within minutes, the courtyard floor held gifts.

Nothing expensive.

Nothing royal.

Blankets.

Carvings.

Small charms.

A tiny practice wand that would not be useful for years.

A child's wooden shield painted Gold.

A Wolf tooth tied to Crimson cord.

Zee looked down at Zayrlen.

The baby opened his eyes.

Crimson-Gold.

Then sneezed.

A tiny spark burned a hole in the blanket.

Ner closed his eyes.

“Wonderful.”

Zee looked at the smoke.

“He is improving.”

“He damaged clothing.”

“Accurately.”

“He is a month old.”

“Still.”

Ner looked toward the crowd.

Darkheart was laughing.

Not at Zayrlen.

With him.

That was the point.

The Prince stayed in the light.

---

Darkheart changed around him anyway.

Not by hiding.

By becoming harder.

Rez rewrote inner access systems until even Zee complained about them.

“You added three checkpoints between my rooms and the west balcony.”

Rez did not look up from his papers.

“Yes.”

“I live here.”

“Yes.”

“I am King.”

“Unfortunate.”

Zee stared.

Rez continued writing.

“You wanted Darkheart harder to enter.”

“I meant for enemies.”

“You look suspicious.”

“I have wings.”

“Exactly.”

Zee considered killing him.

Did not.

Barely.

---

Elias changed the concealment wards.

Not by making them stronger.

By making them stranger.

The kidnappers had masked heartbeats.

Suppressed scent.

Hidden Witch signatures.

So Elias stopped designing detection around what intruders possessed.

He designed it around what was missing.

A hallway with no scent where scent should exist.

A heartbeat gap moving through populated space.

Magic behaving too quietly.

Fear existing without a visible source.

His Demon-Witch nature proved unexpectedly perfect for it.

Deep-blue Witch circles spread beneath Darkheart's inner floors.

Black demonic sigils lived inside them.

Not corrupted Witchcraft.

His Witchcraft.

His race.

His expression.

Zee watched Elias finish the nursery corridor.

“You made the ward unpleasant.”

Elias smiled.

“Thank you.”

“That was not praise.”

“I accepted it anyway.”

The ward activated.

For one second, Zee felt as though the hallway itself had noticed he had secrets.

He frowned.

“I dislike this.”

“Excellent.”

Ner walked through carrying Zayrlen.

Nothing happened.

Elias looked satisfied.

“It recognizes family patterns.”

Zee looked at him.

“Everyone?”

“Core family, approved guards, healers, household staff.”

“Rez?”

Elias smiled.

“Especially Rez.”

From somewhere beyond the corridor came:

“WHY DID THE FLOOR BITE ME?”

Elias looked delighted.

Zee almost smiled.

---

Zareth took the aerial defenses personally.

He remained in Darkheart for four days instead of returning immediately to Drakonis.

On the second day, Zee found him in true Dragon form above the keep.

Huge.

Teal-and-Gold scales catching the sunlight.

Original Dragon wings stretched over the towers.

Phoenix fire traced their edges.

Witch sigils rotated in the air around him.

Zareth was mapping every possible flight path toward the nursery.

Through the Link came:

**There are seventeen approaches.**

Zee looked upward.

**There were.**

Zareth sent an image.

Towers.

Crosswinds.

Roofs.

Blind angles.

Then several routes disappeared beneath Teal-and-Gold ward structures.

**Now there are four.**

**Make it two.**

A pause.

**You are unreasonable.**

**Yes.**

**Good.**

Zareth continued.

---

Ner changed too.

Not power.

Behavior.

Before Zayrlen, Ner had slept lightly because he was a Bloodsong.

After the kidnapping attempt—

he barely slept at all.

Zee noticed by the third night.

Ner sat beside the cradle.

Zayrlen slept.

Zee stood in the doorway.

“You need sleep.”

“So do you.”

“I do not.”

“You absolutely do.”

Zee entered.

Ner did not move.

“The ward is active.”

“I know.”

“Elias is outside.”

“I know.”

“Amara has Wolves in the lower hall.”

“I know.”

“Rhyven is on the eastern roof.”

“I know.”

“Rez has somehow turned the west staircase into a legal process.”

Ner almost smiled.

Still did not move.

Zee crouched beside him.

“They almost took him from me.”

There.

Not weakness.

Truth.

Zee looked at Zayrlen.

“From us.”

Ner stared at the cradle.

“I heard that restraint open.”

His voice stayed controlled.

“I saw his hand reach down.”

Zee's jaw tightened.

Ner looked toward him.

“I know you killed him.”

“Yes.”

“I wish I had.”

Zee understood.

No moral correction.

No reminder that the attacker was already dead.

He simply reached for Ner's hand.

Ner let him.

After a moment, Zee said:

“He stays public.”

“Yes.”

“We do not make him smaller because they frightened us.”

“No.”

“We make them more afraid to try again.”

Ner finally smiled.

“There you are.”

---

Zayrlen woke.

Both fathers turned immediately.

The baby blinked.

Then stared at them.

His pupils narrowed.

Slits.

Wolf.

Heat spread over the cradle.

Dragon.

Crimson-and-Gold magic moved faintly around his fists.

Witch.

Then all three disappeared when he realized both fathers were there.

He relaxed.

Ner stared.

“He was checking.”

Zee listened.

The heartbeat had changed the moment Zayrlen woke.

Searching.

Pack.

Then settled.

“He was.”

Ner picked him up.

Zayrlen buried his face against his chest.

Zee looked at the small child who had already learned enough instinct to recognize absence.

Something in him hardened.

Not toward Zayrlen.

Toward the world.

No one would teach his son fear before he learned language.

Not if Zee could help it.

---

The next attack did not come for Zayrlen.

It came for the people rebuilding the northern settlement destroyed by the Pale Court.

A message arrived near midnight.

Thirty-one workers trapped.

Unknown creatures in the foundations.

No enemy banners.

No political demand.

Just danger.

Zee listened.

Then looked toward the cradle.

Ner understood immediately.

“Go.”

Zee hesitated.

Only a second.

That second mattered.

Ner saw it.

“I am here.”

“Yes.”

“So are all the unreasonable people you call family.”

“Yes.”

“Then be King.”

Zee looked at Zayrlen.

The baby slept.

Then Zee opened his wings.

“Call me if his heartbeat changes.”

Ner stared.

“You are twenty miles away.”

“I can still get back.”

“You are insane.”

“Yes.”

Zee flew.

The Prince remained in Darkheart.

Not hidden.

Protected.

And the King returned to work.

---

The creatures beneath the northern settlement were not supernatural experiments.

That almost felt novel.

They were burrowing predators.

Ancient.

Six-legged.

Blind.

Drawn toward magical concentrations.

Rebuilding had disturbed a buried nest.

No mastermind.

No laboratory.

No kingdom.

Just the world being dangerous.

Zee landed beside Amara.

She pointed toward a collapsed foundation.

“Thirty-one below.”

“Alive?”

“Twenty-eight.”

Zee's expression tightened.

“Three?”

“Already dead.”

No one to kill for that.

No villain.

No revenge.

Only rescue.

Sometimes those were harder.

Zee entered the ground.

---

He used everything differently.

Not execution.

Precision.

Witchcraft held collapsing tunnels.

Vampire hearing separated human heartbeats from the creatures' strange internal pulses.

Wolf scent followed trapped workers.

Dragon strength moved stone.

Phoenix wings shielded survivors when sections collapsed.

Crimson fire provided heat without burning oxygen too quickly.

No new evolution.

No new race.

No dramatic transformation.

Just mastery.

The Crimson Sovereign at work inside a body carrying far more than Sovereign blood now.

Zee found the first twelve.

Then six.

Then five.

The final five were trapped beyond the nest.

The largest creature waited between.

It was nearly the size of a house.

Zee looked at it.

The creature screamed.

Zee's wings opened in the tunnel.

Barely.

“Move.”

It did not.

Fair.

He killed it.

Quickly.

Then continued.

Twenty-eight came home alive.

Three did not.

Darkheart rebuilt anyway.

---

Zee returned before dawn.

Ner was asleep.

Finally.

Zayrlen was awake.

Alone in the cradle.

Not unguarded.

Elias sat outside.

Amara's Wolves occupied the hall.

Zareth's aerial wards covered the roof.

Rez's ridiculous checkpoints still existed.

But inside the room—

Zayrlen was simply awake.

Zee approached.

Crimson-Gold eyes found him.

Tiny hands moved.

Reaching.

Zee picked him up.

The baby relaxed against his chest.

“Your father finally slept.”

Zayrlen made a small sound.

“Yes.”

Zee looked toward Ner.

Then down at his son.

“This is what we chose.”

Not safety.

Not peace.

Life.

Openly.

Danger included.

And Zee would not take that choice back.

---

# Chapter One Hundred Twenty-One

## The First Month of the Prince

By the end of Zayrlen's first month, Darkheart had learned three things.

The Prince hated being cold.

He liked Wolf howls.

And he had already destroyed four blankets.

The fifth died during breakfast.

Ner stared at the new hole.

Zee looked at Zayrlen.

The baby looked back.

A tiny wisp of Crimson-and-Gold heat rose from his mouth.

Ner pointed.

“That was Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“He burned another blanket.”

“Yes.”

“You are smiling.”

“No.”

“You absolutely are.”

Zee stopped smiling.

Poorly.

Ner sighed.

“We need fireproof fabric.”

Zee considered.

“I know a Dragon.”

“You know several.”

“I know one who owes me.”

Through the Link came instantly:

**I owe you nothing.**

Zee looked toward the ceiling.

**You are listening.**

**Unfortunately.**

Ner shook his head.

“Your family is exhausting.”

Zayrlen sneezed.

Another spark.

Ner closed his eyes.

“So is yours.”

---

The first month did not bring another kidnapping attempt.

It brought something almost stranger.

Diplomats.

Dozens of them.

Kings wanted to know what Zayrlen was.

Witch councils wanted bloodline records.

Wolf clans wanted to know whether his future true Wolf would count as a pack-born Alpha by ancestry.

Dragon courts wanted confirmation of Veyrath blood.

Vampires wanted to know why Zee's son carried no Vampire nature.

One extraordinarily stupid ambassador asked whether Zayrlen would be available for future marriage negotiation.

Zee stared at him.

Ner stared too.

The ambassador slowly realized both fathers were deciding which one would kill him.

Rez intervened.

For diplomatic reasons.

“He is one month old.”

The ambassador swallowed.

“I meant eventually.”

Zee's Crimson Phoenix wings opened.

Rez sighed.

“You should leave.”

The ambassador left.

Quickly.

Ner looked toward Rez.

“You saved his life.”

“I save many disappointing people.”

Zee frowned.

“I was only going to scare him.”

Rez stared.

“No.”

Fair.

---

The important diplomatic meeting came from Drakonis.

Not because Zareth demanded it.

Because his court did.

Three elder Dragons arrived in Human form.

They carried no threats.

No weapons.

That was respectful.

They requested formal recognition of Zayrlen's Veyrath descent.

Zee's expression cooled.

“Why?”

The eldest Dragon answered:

“Because a naturally born child carrying Dragon blood outside an active Dragon House has not occurred in recorded generations.”

“He is Darkheart.”

“Yes.”

“Then recognize that.”

The Dragon inclined his head.

“We do.”

Good answer.

Ner held Zayrlen.

The elder looked toward him.

“May I sense the bloodline?”

Zee said:

“No.”

Ner said:

“Yes.”

They looked at each other.

Ner raised an eyebrow.

“He asked.”

Zee frowned.

“He is staring.”

“He is a Dragon.”

“That is not an excuse.”

Zareth stood nearby.

“It often is.”

Zee ignored him.

Ner looked toward the elder.

“No touching.”

The Dragon nodded.

Teal light gathered around his eyes.

Not Zareth's exact Teal-and-Gold Mana.

His own.

He sensed.

Then went completely still.

The other Dragons noticed.

“What?”

The elder looked at Zee.

“Veyrath.”

Zee said nothing.

“Strong.”

Still nothing.

“Stronger than expected.”

Zee's pupils narrowed slightly.

“Meaning?”

The Dragon hesitated.

Then wisely chose precision.

“The line did not weaken passing through you.”

That mattered.

Aurelia's blood had not survived inside Zee as some hidden remnant.

It remained real.

Complete enough to pass naturally into his son.

Zayrlen shifted against Ner.

Heat moved through the room.

The elder Dragon took one instinctive step backward.

Zareth smiled.

“You felt that.”

The elder looked toward the child.

“Something looked back.”

Silence.

Zee's expression changed.

Not alarm.

Attention.

“What?”

The Dragon slowly answered:

“Not conscious.”

Good.

“Not awake.”

Good.

“But large.”

Zee remembered the kidnapping attempt.

That enormous Dragon presence flashing behind the cradle.

Something far too vast for the tiny body currently chewing on Ner's sleeve.

Ner looked down.

Zayrlen continued chewing.

The absurdity did not lessen the truth.

Something enormous existed inside him.

Waiting.

---

The Dragons left without titles.

Without claims.

Without trying to make Zayrlen Drakonis.

Zareth made certain of that.

“He is Darkheart.”

The eldest Dragon had nodded.

“Of course.”

Zareth's expression remained hard.

“And Veyrath through Zee.”

“Yes.”

“Not Drakonis.”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

Zee looked at him afterward.

“You threatened them politely.”

“I am Crown Prince.”

“Barely.”

Zareth smiled.

“You sound jealous.”

Zee's wings opened.

Zareth left before the argument became structural damage.

---

That evening, Elias found Zee in the nursery.

Zayrlen was asleep.

Ner had gone to bathe.

Elias leaned against the door.

“You look strange.”

Zee looked toward him.

“I always look like this.”

“No.”

Elias approached.

“You look peaceful.”

Zee stared.

Elias smiled.

“I know. Horrifying.”

“Leave.”

“No.”

He sat in the chair opposite.

For a few minutes, neither spoke.

Then Elias looked at Zayrlen.

“He has your eyes.”

“Yes.”

“And Ner's attitude.”

“He cannot speak.”

“Still obvious.”

Zee almost smiled.

Elias's expression became quieter.

“You know I remember when you said you would never have this.”

Zee looked at him.

Years earlier.

Before the crown.

Before hybrids.

Before the God.

Before Phoenix blood.

Before Aidan.

Before Ner had ever told Zee he wanted his child.

Elias had known him long enough to remember versions of Zee most people never met.

“You said the world would turn anything you loved into leverage.”

Zee looked down at Zayrlen.

“It tries.”

“Yes.”

“And?”

Elias waited.

Zee touched one small hand.

Zayrlen closed around his finger without waking.

“It has not convinced me to stop.”

Elias smiled.

“Good.”

That was all.

Old friends did not always need speeches.

---

The next serious problem arrived from Vesper.

Rez received the message first.

Then came to Zee.

His face told Zee enough.

“Vesper?”

“Yes.”

“What?”

Rez handed him a sealed report.

Three villages near Vesper's northern edge had gone silent.

Not destroyed.

Not kidnapped.

People remained.

But something had taken their magic.

Witches could not cast.

Vampires could not accelerate healing.

Wolves could not shift.

Every supernatural nature had been suppressed simultaneously.

Zee read the report twice.

“Permanent?”

“We do not know.”

“Dead?”

“Not yet.”

Ner entered carrying Zayrlen.

Rez looked toward the baby.

Then back at Zee.

“I need to go.”

“Obviously.”

“I want you there.”

That made Zee look up.

Rez rarely asked.

He usually informed.

“Why?”

“Because one survivor said the thing that touched them was looking for new blood.”

The room changed.

Ner heard it.

“So this is connected to the Age of New Blood.”

Rez shook his head.

“Maybe.”

Good.

No assumptions.

Zee handed the report back.

“When?”

“Now.”

Zee looked at Ner.

Ner looked at Zayrlen.

Then at Zee.

“Go.”

Again.

Zee hated how much trust required leaving.

But he understood it now.

Ner smiled faintly.

“I am not going anywhere.”

Zee looked toward the nursery wards.

Elias's detection.

Amara's rotations.

Kael's guards.

Rhyven's patrol.

Zareth could reach them through the sky.

Tessa was nearby.

Ner himself could kill most things foolish enough to enter the room.

Zee touched Zayrlen's cheek.

The baby's eyes opened.

Crimson-Gold.

Recognition.

Zee whispered:

“I will be back.”

Zayrlen grabbed his finger.

Then let go.

Zee stood.

Phoenix wings opened.

Rez watched him.

“Ready?”

Zee's pupils narrowed.

“Yes.”

---

They reached Vesper before sunset.

What waited there was not an army.

Not a laboratory.

Not a kingdom.

The first village looked normal.

People stood outside homes.

Witches held dead spell circles in their palms.

A Vampire had cut his hand and watched the wound remain open.

A Wolf stood beneath the moon—

unable to shift.

Rez's Blue-White Mana flared.

It still worked.

Zee's abilities remained.

Whatever had happened was selective.

One elderly Witch approached them.

“It came from the forest.”

“What?”

“We never saw it.”

Zee crouched beside the dead magic burned into the soil.

His Witch nature touched it.

Nothing.

His Vampire senses found no blood.

Wolf found no scent.

Dragon found no heat.

Phoenix found no life-resonance.

Interesting.

Rez looked at him.

“You have that face.”

“What face?”

“The one you make when something is finally difficult.”

Zee smiled faintly.

Then looked toward the forest.

The King's Hunt had nothing to claim yet.

No confirmed prey.

No scent.

No blood.

No heartbeat.

No magic signature.

For the first time in a long while—

Zee Darkheart looked into a forest and could not immediately identify what was looking back.

Something moved between the trees.

Not visible.

Felt.

The nearest Witches collapsed.

Rez's Blue-White Mana flickered.

Zee's Crimson fire dimmed for one second.

Only one.

Then returned.

His expression changed.

Whatever lived in the northern Vesper woods could suppress supernatural bloodlines.

And it had just tried him.

Zee smiled.

Darkly.

“Well.”

Rez looked toward him.

“What?”

Zee's Crimson-Gold eyes sharpened.

“It knows I am here.”

The forest answered.

Every tree bent toward them at once.

And somewhere far away in Darkheart—

Zayrlen Keal Darkheart suddenly opened his Crimson-Gold eyes.

# Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Two

## The Forest That Silenced Blood

The trees bent toward Zee and Rez.

Not from wind.

There was none.

Every trunk leaned.

Every branch angled inward.

Leaves turned their undersides toward the road.

The entire forest behaved like one thing had noticed them.

Rez's Blue-White Mana flickered again.

Then stabilized.

Zee's Crimson Phoenix fire dimmed across one wing.

Only slightly.

Enough to matter.

The old Witch beside them stumbled.

Her magic disappeared completely.

Zee caught her before she hit the ground.

“Back.”

Rez moved first.

Blue-White Witchcraft formed a barrier around the surviving villagers.

The barrier held.

Barely.

The forest pushed.

Not physically.

Supernaturally.

Every bloodline inside the village reacted.

Vampires weakened.

Wolves shook.

Witches lost casting entirely.

Zee listened.

The silence was wrong.

No natural supernatural rhythm.

No blood signature.

No heartbeat.

Nothing to hunt.

That irritated him.

Then a voice came from the forest.

Not spoken.

Heard.

**Too many.**

Rez's eyes narrowed.

“You heard that?”

“Yes.”

**Too many bloodlines in one body.**

Zee's expression changed.

The forest was speaking to him.

Specifically.

He stepped beyond Rez's barrier.

Rez grabbed his shoulder.

“Do not.”

Zee looked back.

“You asked me here.”

“I did not ask you to walk into the thing that removes supernatural nature.”

“Fair.”

Rez released him.

Zee continued anyway.

Rez closed his eyes.

“Of course.”

---

The first step into the forest weakened Zee's Witchcraft.

The second dulled Vampire hearing.

The third muted Wolf scent.

His Dragon heat cooled.

Phoenix flame retreated beneath his skin.

Crimson Sovereign synchronization remained.

But there was less to synchronize.

That was new.

Zee stopped.

Then smiled.

Not because this was easy.

Because it was not.

The voice returned.

**Wrong.**

Zee looked between the trees.

“What?”

**You should collapse.**

“That sounds disappointing for you.”

The forest tightened.

Pressure struck.

Zee's knees nearly bent.

Nearly.

His body reacted differently than the villagers.

Not immunity.

Adaptation.

His blood had survived suppression before.

Witch-suppression poison.

Dragonbane.

Dark Divinity wounds.

Phoenix fire.

Divine blood.

Silver.

Compulsion.

Restraints.

His biology knew how to resist being told what it was allowed to be.

The forest suppressed.

Zee's body pushed back.

Not enough to break it.

Enough to remain standing.

Rez watched from the road.

“That is very annoying.”

Zee glanced toward him.

“What?”

“You are proving difficult to suppress through spite.”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

---

Something moved behind Zee.

He turned.

Too late.

A pale limb struck him across the back.

His Phoenix wings failed to open.

He hit a tree hard enough to crack it.

The creature stepped into view.

Tall.

Thin.

Gray skin stretched across a body almost Human.

No eyes.

No mouth.

No obvious organs.

Its chest was hollow.

Literally.

A cavity opened between the ribs.

Inside—

nothing.

No heart.

No blood.

No flame.

No Mana.

No scent.

Rez looked at it.

“That explains the tracking problem.”

The creature attacked again.

Zee blocked with one arm.

Without Dragon strength fully available, the impact hurt more than expected.

Bone cracked.

Zee smiled.

The creature tilted its head.

Then Zee punched it.

Human strength compared to usual.

Still enough to stagger it.

His broken arm began healing.

Slowly.

Vampire regeneration fighting suppression.

Phoenix vitality barely answering.

The creature reached for his throat.

Zee caught its wrist.

Its skin was cold.

Not dead.

Empty.

That was different.

He looked toward the hollow chest.

Then understood.

“It is not taking powers.”

Rez heard him.

“What?”

“It is creating absence.”

The creature slammed Zee into another tree.

He hit the ground.

Rez moved.

Blue-White Mana erupted.

The forest suppressed half the spell.

Half remained.

Enough.

A blade of Blue-White force cut across the creature's back.

It turned toward Rez.

Good.

Zee stood.

His Witchcraft flickered.

One word.

“Hold.”

Nothing.

Then—

a fraction of effect.

The creature slowed.

Not enough.

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“Again.”

His magic answered harder.

“Hold.”

The creature stopped for one heartbeat.

Rez understood.

He attacked.

Blue-White chains wrapped its legs.

Zee crossed the distance.

Claws barely formed.

Enough.

He drove one through the hollow chest.

Nothing there.

No heart.

No core.

No immediate kill.

The creature grabbed him.

Then Zayrlen screamed across the bond of blood.

Not literally across miles.

Not a Link.

Something more primitive.

Pack.

Family.

Zee froze.

---

Darkheart.

Ner sat upright in the nursery.

Zayrlen was crying.

Not normal crying.

Crimson-and-Gold Witch pressure pushed against the cradle.

Tiny claws extended.

Heat rolled through the room.

Elias entered first.

“What happened?”

“I do not know.”

Ner picked Zayrlen up.

The baby did not calm.

His heartbeat hammered.

Wolf distress.

Dragon heat.

Witch pressure.

All three reacting to something not inside the room.

Ner immediately understood one thing.

“Zee.”

Elias's expression changed.

“Can Zayrlen sense him?”

“Not like a Link.”

“No.”

Ner held Zayrlen closer.

Bloodsong opened.

Not controlling the child.

Listening.

The baby's blood resonance was pulling toward something distant.

A familiar rhythm.

Father.

Ner's face hardened.

“Something is happening to him.”

Zareth arrived through the balcony in Human form before anyone called.

His face was already wrong.

“The Link is fading.”

Silence.

Ner looked at him.

“What does that mean?”

“I can still feel Zee.”

Zareth's Teal-and-Gold Mana flickered.

“But less.”

Rez's location.

Vesper.

Everyone understood.

Ner handed Zayrlen to Elias.

Elias blinked.

“What are you doing?”

“Going.”

“No.”

Ner looked at him.

Elias continued quickly.

“I mean—absolutely not alone.”

Amara entered behind him.

“Already coming.”

Kael appeared from the hall.

“So am I.”

Rhyven arrived next.

Tessa last.

Zayrlen screamed again.

Zareth's expression became lethal.

“Move.”

---

Back in Vesper, Zee felt the forest push deeper.

Witchcraft dimmed again.

Wolf instinct went quiet.

Vampire senses collapsed to almost Human range.

Dragon blood cooled.

Phoenix fire disappeared entirely.

For the first time in years—

Zee felt small.

Not powerless.

But reduced.

The hollow creature noticed.

Its fingers closed around Zee's throat.

Rez attacked from behind.

The creature released Zee and struck him instead.

Rez's Vampire speed failed halfway through the dodge.

The blow caught his ribs.

He flew.

Zee heard the crack.

Something inside him changed.

Not power.

Decision.

He could not overpower the forest as himself.

So he stopped trying.

Zee looked at the creature.

Human heartbeat absent.

No blood.

No scent.

No Mana.

No supernatural core.

But it still occupied space.

Still moved air.

Still had weight.

Still bent branches.

Assassin training answered.

Not bloodline.

Skill.

Zee watched the shoulders.

Hip rotation.

Foot placement.

Balance.

The creature lunged.

Zee stepped aside.

Human speed.

Perfect timing.

He caught the elbow.

Turned.

Used momentum.

The creature hit the ground.

Zee drove his knee into the shoulder joint.

Bone snapped.

The creature reacted.

Good.

Physical anatomy.

Different.

But present.

Zee smiled.

“There you are.”

---

Rez rose slowly.

“You look happy.”

“I found something it cannot suppress.”

“What?”

Zee broke the creature's second arm.

“Practice.”

Rez smiled.

“Finally useful.”

The creature twisted violently.

Its leg struck Zee's chest.

He went backward.

Then rolled.

Stood.

No supernatural flourish.

No flight.

No spells.

Just Nanda Parbat.

Angles.

Breath.

Joint destruction.

Momentum.

Pressure.

Zee stopped fighting like a supernatural King.

He fought like the assassin he had trained to become.

The creature adapted.

So did he.

It reached.

He broke fingers.

It kicked.

He took the leg.

Twisted the knee.

It tried using the hollow chest to release suppression directly.

Zee jammed a broken branch through the cavity.

The creature froze.

Rez stared.

“That worked?”

Zee did too.

Then smiled.

“Apparently.”

Blue-White Mana returned slightly around Rez.

The forest shuddered.

The creature had been part of the suppression network.

Not the source.

But an anchor.

Zee drove the branch deeper.

The hollow body cracked from inside.

Then collapsed into gray ash.

The forest screamed.

Every tree bent away.

Zee's powers returned at once.

Not fully.

Enough.

Phoenix fire ignited.

Crimson wings erupted.

Vampire hearing flooded back.

Wolf scent returned.

Witchcraft sharpened.

Dragon heat roared beneath his scales.

The Crimson Sovereign snapped into complete alignment.

Rez looked at him.

“There he is.”

Zee's eyes became Crimson-Gold.

“No.”

He looked deeper into the forest.

“Now I am angry.”

---

The surviving villagers behind Rez's barrier began recovering.

Slowly.

A Wolf shifted accidentally.

A Vampire's wound started closing.

Witches felt Mana return in weak pulses.

The suppression had not permanently stripped them.

Good.

Zee looked toward the ashes.

Then farther into the trees.

“How many anchors?”

Rez closed his eyes.

His Blue-White Mana spread carefully.

“More than one.”

Zee's Wolf scent found nothing.

Blood Mark had nothing.

The King's Hunt had no biological prey.

So he used the one thing the forest could not erase.

Pattern.

The trees bent toward active anchors.

Not randomly.

Directionally.

Zee studied them.

Then pointed northeast.

“There.”

Rez frowned.

“How?”

“They lean.”

Rez looked.

Then smiled.

“Very annoying.”

“Yes.”

They moved.

---

The second anchor died faster.

The third fought harder.

By the fourth, the forest understood Zee had learned.

So it changed.

Suppression no longer attacked all his bloodlines equally.

It targeted Witch first.

Then Phoenix.

Then Wolf.

Trying different order.

Zee noticed.

“So you learn.”

The voice answered.

**Yes.**

“Good.”

Rez looked at him.

“Why is that good?”

Zee smiled.

“Because now I know it is choosing.”

Choice meant responsibility.

Responsibility meant prey.

---

They found the center before midnight.

Not a creature.

A tree.

Ancient.

Larger than any living tree in Vesper.

Its roots spread beneath all three affected villages.

Its trunk was pale.

No leaves.

No bark.

The surface looked like bone.

Hundreds of hollow creatures were embedded inside it.

Sleeping.

Or waiting.

At the base stood one person.

Human.

Or looked Human.

An old woman in gray robes.

She watched Zee approach.

“You killed four children.”

Rez's expression changed.

Zee did not.

“The hollow ones?”

“They are extensions.”

“Yours?”

“Yes.”

“Then you attacked Vesper.”

“I corrected imbalance.”

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“What imbalance?”

“You.”

There it was.

The woman looked at him.

“Creation has accelerated.”

Phoenix–Wolf.

Phoenix–Dragon–Witch.

Demon–Witch.

Natural Tribrid Prince.

New bloodlines.

Old boundaries collapsing.

The woman continued.

“You create where nature did not.”

Zee's expression remained flat.

“Nature created me.”

“And the world broke around your birth.”

“Sounds like a world problem.”

Rez almost laughed.

The woman did not.

“You multiplied the error.”

“No.”

Zee's wings opened.

“I multiplied survivors.”

The tree behind her pulsed.

Suppression slammed outward.

Rez dropped to one knee.

Zee's wings extinguished.

Again.

The woman smiled.

“You cannot kill what has no bloodline to consume.”

Zee stared.

Then drew a knife.

Plain steel.

The woman's smile disappeared.

Zee stepped forward.

“I have killed people without magic before.”

---

# Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Three

## The Thing That Could Not Silence Choice

The old woman raised one hand.

The forest swallowed sound.

Not Absolute Silence.

Something different.

A dead zone.

No spell words.

No Dragon roar.

No Wolf howl.

No Bloodsong.

Nothing supernatural carried.

Zee continued walking.

The knife remained in his hand.

Plain.

Human.

Sharp.

The woman stared.

Then the first hollow creature tore itself from the tree.

Zee killed it without magic.

The second followed.

Then the third.

Rez forced himself upright.

His Blue-White Mana was almost completely gone.

He drew his sword.

Zee glanced at him.

Rez understood.

No powers.

Fine.

They had both lived before some of these abilities existed.

They had both survived worse.

The hollow creatures attacked.

---

Rez fought like a Prince who had spent too much of his life around monsters.

Efficient.

No wasted movement.

Steel through joints.

Knees broken.

Throats cut even when no blood came.

Zee fought differently.

Faster.

More surgical.

Not supernatural speed.

Skill.

One creature reached for him.

He ducked.

Knife through elbow.

Turn.

Blade beneath jaw.

Twist.

Another came from behind.

He used the dying body as leverage.

Kicked backward.

Broke a knee.

Then crushed the skull against the pale roots.

The woman watched.

“You should be helpless.”

Zee could not hear the words.

But he read her lips.

He smiled.

Then mouthed back:

**I was born helpless once.**

She did not understand.

Good.

---

The tree opened.

Not physically at first.

The suppression deepened.

Zee felt Vampire vanish.

Then Witch.

Wolf.

Dragon.

Phoenix.

Everything supernatural collapsed.

Even Crimson Sovereign became inaccessible because there was nothing active to synchronize.

For one impossible moment—

Zee Darkheart stood as only flesh.

No healing.

No claws.

No fire.

No supernatural strength.

No immortality expressing through regeneration.

Nothing.

The old woman approached.

She drew a blade.

Then stabbed him through the heart.

Rez saw it.

His face changed.

Zee looked down.

Blood spread across his shirt.

Red.

Ordinary-looking.

The woman whispered:

“You see?”

Zee looked at her.

Then grabbed the blade.

His hand shook.

His heart kept beating.

Weakly.

But beating.

Her eyes widened.

Immortality remained.

Not as an active bloodline.

As fact.

Death had already ended once.

The forest could suppress expression.

Not rewrite history.

Zee smiled through blood.

Then headbutted her.

Hard.

She staggered.

Rez laughed despite himself.

The sound still did not carry.

---

Zee ripped the blade free.

Bad idea for anyone else.

Not ideal for him either.

His heart continued beating.

Slow.

Painful.

He used the same knife to cut her throat.

She blocked.

Good.

Finally.

The woman was trained.

Not enough.

Zee attacked again.

She parried.

He shifted angle.

She anticipated.

He changed rhythm.

She smiled.

He kicked dirt into her eyes.

Then stabbed her thigh.

The smile vanished.

No dignity.

No ceremony.

Survival.

The pale tree convulsed.

The suppression flickered.

One heartbeat of Wolf returned.

Enough.

Zee smelled her blood.

Blood Mark locked.

Then suppression hit again.

Gone.

But the identity remained in memory.

Interesting.

Zee grinned.

The woman backed away.

“You marked me.”

He could hear again.

Only barely.

“Yes.”

“That should be impossible.”

“So am I.”

---

The tree released every hollow creature at once.

Hundreds.

Rez looked toward Zee.

“This feels excessive.”

“Yes.”

“Plan?”

Zee looked at the pale trunk.

“Kill the tree.”

“How?”

Zee looked at the knife in his hand.

Then at the enormous tree.

Rez stared.

“That is a terrible plan.”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

They ran.

---

The hollow creatures overwhelmed them before twenty yards.

Rez went down first.

Three bodies dragged him beneath the mass.

Zee turned.

Choice.

Tree or brother.

No hesitation.

Brother.

He changed direction.

Jumped onto the pile.

Knife through one skull.

Heel into another spine.

Hands tearing.

Flesh breaking.

Without powers, every hit mattered more.

Every wound stayed open.

Zee bled.

A lot.

He did not stop.

One hollow creature bit into his shoulder.

He drove fingers through the soft tissue beneath its ribs.

Ripped.

Another broke two of his fingers.

He used the broken hand anyway.

Rez emerged coughing.

“You should have gone for the tree.”

“No.”

“That was stupid.”

“Yes.”

They stood back-to-back.

The forest pressed harder.

Then the sky above them turned Teal and Gold.

The suppression field reacted.

Zareth arrived.

True Dragon form.

Huge.

Wings spread across the moon.

He hit the suppression boundary and nearly fell from the sky.

His Phoenix fire extinguished.

Witch sigils vanished.

Dragon strength weakened.

But the Link—

did not disappear.

It dimmed.

Not gone.

**Zee.**

**Do not enter.**

**Too late.**

Zareth hit the ground in Human form before impact killed his flight.

He rolled.

Stood.

No Dragon power.

No Phoenix.

No Witch.

Just Zareth.

He drew a sword.

Rez looked at him.

“You carry that?”

“I am royalty.”

“That did not answer the question.”

“No.”

Good enough.

---

Then came Elias.

His Demon–Witch magic failed at the boundary.

He kept walking.

Kael followed.

Vampire side gone.

Witch diminished to nothing.

Still Kael.

Amara crossed next.

Wolf gone.

Still dangerous.

Rhyven entered and his Phoenix-Wolf nature shut down almost completely.

He staggered.

Then stood.

Tessa came last.

No healer glow.

No magic.

Still holding medical knives.

Rez stared.

“You all came.”

Elias looked offended.

“Obviously.”

Zee's expression changed.

Family.

Not because of power.

Not because of bloodlines.

Because they chose to enter the place where all those things could be taken away.

For him.

That mattered more than any new race.

---

Far away in Darkheart, Ner held Zayrlen.

The baby had stopped crying.

Not because Zee was safe.

Because something else had stabilized.

The pack signal around him changed.

Ner felt it.

Not fear now.

Recognition.

Many.

Family moving toward father.

Zayrlen's tiny claws retracted.

His heartbeat slowed.

Ner looked toward the window.

“Your family found him.”

Zayrlen blinked.

Crimson-Gold eyes.

Ner kissed his forehead.

“Of course they did.”

---

Inside the suppression forest, power meant nothing.

So the fight became honest.

Kael fought with a sword.

Amara with knives.

Elias used a broken spear.

Rhyven used his hands.

Tessa dragged wounded people out of the pile and treated them without magic.

Zareth fought beside Zee.

Rez held the left flank.

No one transformed.

No one cast.

No regeneration saved mistakes.

Blood hit the roots.

Real blood.

Family blood.

The pale tree drank none of it.

It was built around absence.

That was its weakness.

It understood supernatural structure.

Not ordinary life.

Not loyalty.

Not training.

Not refusal.

Zee saw that.

Then the solution became obvious.

“Roots.”

Rez heard him.

“What?”

“The tree is suppressing through the roots.”

Zareth looked down.

“They run beneath us.”

“Yes.”

“How do we kill all of them without magic?”

Zee looked at the dry forest.

Then smiled.

Rhyven noticed.

“No.”

Zee looked at him.

“You still carry flint?”

Rhyven stared.

“My Phoenix side is gone.”

“I asked about flint.”

Rhyven reached into his coat.

Pulled out two stones.

Zee smiled wider.

Elias understood.

“Ordinary fire.”

“Yes.”

The old woman finally looked afraid.

Good.

---

They set the forest on fire.

Not Crimson Phoenix flame.

Not Dragonfire.

Fire.

Wood.

Oil from abandoned supply packs.

Dry leaves.

Cloth.

Flint.

Human fire.

The pale tree had spent centuries suppressing supernatural forces.

It had never prepared to be burned like timber.

The first flames touched the roots.

The tree screamed.

Suppression weakened.

One percent.

Enough.

Zee's Vampire healing flickered.

His heart wound began closing.

The woman stared.

“No.”

More roots burned.

Wolf returned.

Then Witch.

Then Dragon heat.

Then Phoenix.

Crimson Sovereign synchronization snapped back piece by piece.

Zee opened his eyes.

Crimson-Gold.

The woman backed away.

“No.”

His Phoenix wings erupted behind him.

Huge.

Crimson.

Black-edged.

Burning.

Zareth's Dragon nature exploded back next.

He shifted.

True Dragon form filled the clearing.

Teal-and-Gold scales.

Phoenix fire.

Witch sigils.

Elias's blue-black Demon-Witch Mana returned.

Rhyven dropped into true Wolf form as Crimson fire burst through his claws.

Amara shifted beside him.

Kael vanished in Vampire speed.

Rez's Blue-White Mana flooded the forest.

The pale tree had made one mistake.

It taught them exactly what they were without power.

Then gave the power back.

---

The old woman ran.

Blood Mark found her immediately.

The King's Hunt now had identity.

Wolf scent caught her fear.

Vampire hearing found the heartbeat.

Witchcraft read the escape ward.

Phoenix wings made distance meaningless.

Dragon force broke the trees between.

Zee landed in front of her.

She stopped.

“You do not understand.”

“No.”

“We exist to prevent bloodline collapse.”

“You attacked villages.”

“To preserve balance.”

“You suppressed children.”

“To preserve the world.”

Zee's expression became flat.

“That sounds like your choice.”

She understood.

Too late.

“Wait.”

Zee did not.

She died.

No surrender.

No second chance.

She had knowingly attacked Vesper citizens and stripped supernatural natures from entire villages.

Confirmed.

Enough.

---

The pale tree came next.

Zareth attacked from above.

Dragonfire hit the upper trunk.

Phoenix renewal twisted strangely through it, making the fire sustain itself.

Elias used Demon-Witch sigils to bind the roots in place.

Rez's Blue-White Mana prevented the suppression pulse from rebuilding.

Rhyven burned the lower roots.

Amara hunted the hollow creatures escaping the trunk.

Kael destroyed each exposed anchor.

Tessa stayed with the wounded.

Zee flew straight into the center.

Phoenix wings shielding.

Dragon force driving him through pale wood.

Witch sight finding the internal structure.

There.

A knot.

Not a heart.

Not blood.

A vacancy.

An intentional absence around which the entire network had been built.

Zee stared.

Then used Spell Sever.

“Sever.”

The tree resisted.

Ancient.

Exactly the kind of magic Spell Sever could not casually destroy.

Zee pushed harder.

The knot cracked.

Not enough.

He added Witch precision.

Dragon force.

Phoenix flame.

Crimson Sovereign fully mastered beneath all of it.

Not one giant attack.

Synchronization.

Each nature doing its part.

Wolf instinct told him where resistance shifted.

Vampire senses caught the tiniest returning pulses around the roots.

Witchcraft cut seams.

Dragon strength held the opening.

Phoenix flame prevented regrowth.

“Sever.”

The knot broke.

The tree died.

---

Every affected village felt it.

Witches collapsed as their magic came rushing back.

Vampires healed.

Wolves shifted.

Children with supernatural blood started crying from the sudden return of sensation.

Rez stood in the burning clearing.

Blue-White Mana strong again.

He looked toward Zee.

“Permanent?”

Zee listened.

“No.”

Good.

No stolen bloodlines.

No ruined generations.

The forest had suppressed.

Not erased.

Zee looked toward the dead pale tree.

The Age of New Blood had produced another enemy.

Not one that wanted to steal his power.

Not one that wanted to imitate him.

One that wanted to stop supernatural change entirely.

It had failed.

And it was dead.

Arc over.

---

They returned to Darkheart the following evening.

Ner waited in the courtyard with Zayrlen.

The moment Zee landed, the baby's heartbeat changed.

Zee heard it from across the stone.

His wings folded.

He walked forward.

Not King.

Father.

Again.

Ner handed Zayrlen to him.

No words.

Zee took his son.

The baby settled immediately.

One tiny hand closed around Zee's collar.

Zee touched his head.

“I am fine.”

Ner looked at the still-healing wound beneath Zee's shirt.

“You were stabbed through the heart.”

Rez answered from behind him.

“He was being dramatic.”

Zee looked back.

“You were there.”

“Yes.”

“You were also injured.”

“Less dramatically.”

Ner sighed.

Zayrlen opened his eyes.

Crimson-Gold.

Slit for one heartbeat.

Then round.

A tiny patch of Crimson-and-Gold scales appeared across his shoulder.

Zee watched them fade.

Not fear.

Not distress.

Recognition.

His Dragon blood had reacted to Zee's return.

The baby's Wolf instincts had found pack.

His Witch pressure settled.

Zee smiled.

The world could suppress power.

Hide blood.

Build cages.

Silence magic.

Erase scent.

Mask heartbeats.

Create absence.

None of that changed the one thing Zee had learned beneath the pale tree.

Power was not what made Darkheart dangerous.

Choice was.

And surrounded by the people who had crossed into a forest stripped of every supernatural advantage simply because Zee was inside—

Zayrlen Keal Darkheart had been born into one of the most dangerous things in the world.

A family that came when called.

# Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Four

## The Blood That Chose Its Own Shape

Zayrlen developed a habit of waking before sunrise.

Not crying.

Watching.

Zee discovered this on the third morning after returning from Vesper.

He entered the nursery quietly.

Zayrlen was already awake.

Crimson-Gold eyes followed him across the room.

No sound.

No movement except one tiny hand opening and closing against the blanket.

Zee stopped beside the cradle.

“You are supposed to be asleep.”

Zayrlen stared.

Zee stared back.

The baby blinked.

Then a tiny patch of Crimson-and-Gold scales appeared along his temple.

Gone.

Zee smiled.

“Terrible argument.”

Ner’s voice came from the doorway.

“You are debating a newborn again.”

Zee looked over.

“He started it.”

“He cannot speak.”

“That has not stopped him.”

Ner entered.

Recovery had gone well.

Tessa had finally stopped threatening to physically lock him in bed.

Mostly.

Zayrlen saw Ner.

His heartbeat changed.

Wolf recognition.

Then he looked back at Zee.

Same response.

Both fathers.

Pack.

Ner noticed.

“He does that every morning now.”

“Yes.”

“He checks for us.”

Zee’s expression changed slightly.

Ner saw that too.

“Do not make it sad.”

“I was not.”

“You were.”

Zee looked down at Zayrlen.

Then reached into the cradle.

The baby immediately caught his finger.

No fear.

No hesitation.

Public child.

Known child.

Protected child.

Loved without concealment.

Zee exhaled.

“Fine.”

Ner smiled.

“Progress.”

---

Darkheart’s defenses had become aggressive enough to annoy its own citizens.

That meant Rez considered them successful.

A merchant arrived at the eastern gate and spent twenty minutes arguing with a ward that refused to believe his mule was not enchanted.

It was not.

The mule simply hated everyone.

Elias inspected the ward.

Then the mule.

“The ward is correct.”

The merchant stared.

“What?”

Elias nodded toward the animal.

“There is definitely evil here.”

The mule kicked him.

Elias looked offended.

Rez laughed from the gatehouse.

“Excellent detection.”

Elias raised one hand.

Deep-blue Mana formed.

Black demonic sigils appeared.

The mule backed away immediately.

Rez pointed.

“You are threatening livestock.”

“It started first.”

Darkheart had returned to something resembling normal.

That never lasted.

---

The first indication came from Rhyven.

He was patrolling the western forest when his Phoenix-Wolf nature reacted to something underground.

Not danger.

Heat.

He stopped.

His claws ignited.

Then extinguished.

Amara noticed.

“What?”

Rhyven crouched.

Placed one hand against the soil.

“Something is warm.”

“Burrow?”

“No.”

“Magic?”

“Maybe.”

Amara shifted partially.

Wolf senses opened.

She smelled nothing unusual.

Rhyven's Phoenix side felt it instead.

Heat moving beneath the earth in deliberate lines.

Not lava.

Not fire.

Something traveling.

He stood.

“It is going toward Darkheart.”

Amara’s expression changed.

“Call Zee.”

---

By the time Zee arrived, the heat had crossed half a mile.

Phoenix blood recognized it immediately.

Not Phoenix.

Something adjacent.

Artificial heat.

Contained.

Moving through stone.

Zee's Witch sight opened.

There.

A narrow line beneath the soil.

Runes.

Not attacking.

Transporting something.

Kael arrived next.

Then Elias.

Zareth landed in Human form.

Rez was still in Vesper.

Ner remained at the keep with Zayrlen.

For now.

Zee crouched.

“Someone built another route beneath us.”

Amara frowned.

“Not another tunnel.”

“No.”

Elias studied the runes.

“A spellway.”

Zee looked toward him.

“Old?”

“Yes.”

“How old?”

“Older than Darkheart’s current borders.”

Good.

Not another enemy who had built beneath them yesterday without detection.

This had existed before Zee expanded.

Kingdom progression had simply reached it.

Zareth touched the soil.

His Witch senses reacted.

Then his Dragon side.

“Something living traveled through here.”

Zee’s eyes narrowed.

“What?”

Zareth shook his head.

“Not sure.”

Rhyven's Phoenix heat surged again.

Then a roar came from beneath the ground.

Not loud.

Deep.

Everyone stopped.

Zareth’s eyes widened.

“Dragon.”

Zee looked at him.

“Drakonis?”

“No.”

“Veyrath?”

Zareth listened.

“No.”

Another Dragon bloodline.

Ancient.

Independent.

Good.

The world remained larger than their family.

---

They opened the spellway.

Carefully this time.

Mostly because Elias threatened to leave if Zee simply punched through another ancient magical structure.

The entrance appeared beneath three layers of stone.

A circular shaft lined with red-metal runes.

Warm air rose from below.

Then came the smell.

Dragon.

Blood.

And something else.

Wolf.

Zee froze.

Amara noticed.

“You smell it too.”

“Yes.”

Not one body.

Two.

One Dragon.

One Wolf.

Both injured.

Badly.

Zee descended first.

Phoenix wings carried him through the shaft.

Zareth followed by magic.

Rhyven and Amara climbed.

Elias created steps for the others.

The chamber beneath had been sealed for centuries.

Broken chains lined one wall.

Old blood covered another.

At the center—

a Dragon lay in Human form.

Female.

Dark copper skin.

Black hair.

Burned red scales across both arms.

One horn broken.

Beside her—

a Wolf man.

Barely conscious.

His body covered in old scar tissue.

They were not attacking.

They were trying to survive.

Zee listened.

Two heartbeats.

Weak.

The Dragon opened one eye.

Saw Zee’s horns.

Saw Zareth.

Then smelled Crimson Phoenix blood.

Her face changed.

“Not them.”

Zee crouched.

“Who?”

She tried moving.

Failed.

“The collectors.”

Zee's expression hardened.

Again?

Then the Wolf man spoke weakly.

“Not blood.”

Different.

Good.

Zee looked toward him.

“What do they collect?”

The Wolf swallowed.

“Bonds.”

Silence.

Zareth’s expression changed.

Dragon Link.

Zee immediately looked at him.

The Dragon woman saw it.

Then laughed once despite the pain.

“You have one.”

Zareth went very still.

Zee’s pupils narrowed.

“You know what this is?”

She looked between them.

“Yes.”

“What is it called?”

“A soul-link.”

Zee's expression did not change.

Zareth's did.

Because that sounded too close to something neither wanted casually named by strangers.

The Dragon continued.

“Rare. Natural. Cannot be manufactured correctly.”

Good.

“People have been trying.”

Worse.

---

They brought both survivors above.

Tessa arrived from Darkheart personally.

Ner came too.

With Zayrlen.

Zee saw him and immediately frowned.

Ner stared.

“Do not.”

“There are injured strangers with unknown bloodlines.”

“Yes.”

“And you brought our son.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because Tessa needed my Bloodsong to stabilize one of them.”

Zee looked at the Wolf.

His heartbeat was collapsing.

Ner was right.

Annoying.

Again.

He handed Zayrlen to Elias.

Elias blinked.

“Why me?”

“Because your hands are clean.”

“That is disturbingly rare.”

Zee ignored him.

Ner knelt beside the Wolf.

Pure Gold Mana opened.

Bloodsong reached into the damaged rhythm.

The heartbeat steadied.

Barely.

Tessa worked.

The Dragon woman watched Zayrlen.

Her eyes widened.

“What is that child?”

Every member of Zee’s family turned toward her at once.

She noticed.

Good.

Ner answered first.

“Our son.”

The Dragon woman looked at Zee.

Then Zayrlen.

Her senses reacted.

Dragon.

Witch.

Wolf.

Natural.

Her face went still.

“They will come for him.”

Zee's expression flattened.

“Who?”

“The Bond Collectors.”

“That is a terrible name.”

Elias muttered:

“Agreed.”

The Dragon woman ignored them.

“They do not take bloodlines.”

“What do they take?”

“Relationships.”

Ner’s expression changed.

The woman looked at Zee and Zareth.

“They find rare supernatural bonds. Dragon Links. Pack-binding. Witch soul-pacts. Bloodsong resonance. Sire connections.”

Rez was absent.

But Zee immediately thought of him.

Aidan.

Uncle Rez.

Memory.

No.

Not relevant.

Not exposed.

He pushed it aside.

The Dragon woman continued.

“They cut the bond out of one person and force it into another.”

Zareth’s face became murderous.

Zee’s wings opened.

Crimson fire moved.

That was enough explanation.

---

The collectors arrived before sunset.

Fast.

Too fast.

Meaning they had been tracking the survivors.

Not Darkheart.

Good.

Independent event.

No conspiracy swallowing everything.

Five black riders crossed the western boundary.

No banner.

No masks.

No attempt at diplomacy.

Each carried a long hooked weapon made from silver-black bone.

Zareth saw them.

His Link with Zee flared instinctively.

The lead rider smiled.

“There.”

Bad.

He could perceive it.

Zee stepped forward.

“Leave.”

The rider looked at him.

“Zee Darkheart.”

“Yes.”

“We only want what belongs to us.”

Zee looked toward the survivors.

“They do not.”

“The Dragon carries a severed bond.”

Zareth's expression sharpened.

“Severed from whom?”

The woman behind them answered.

“My brother.”

Silence.

The collector smiled.

“He died.”

Her face broke for half a second.

Then hardened.

“And you kept the link.”

“Part of it.”

Zee understood immediately.

The spellway.

The heat.

The suffering.

They had been trying to take an inherited echo of a dead Dragon Link.

Not blood.

Not race.

A relationship made supernatural.

Disgusting in a new direction.

The collector pointed toward Zareth.

“But yours is better.”

That was the last useful sentence he ever spoke.

Zee killed him.

Immediately.

The other four attacked.

---

One hook struck toward Zareth.

Zee caught it with a Phoenix wing.

The weapon bit through three feathers.

Then something tried pulling.

Not flesh.

Link.

Zee felt the tug inside his skull.

His eyes changed.

Zareth felt it too.

Rage struck through the Link.

**They touched it.**

Zee's answer came colder.

**I know.**

The hook tried extracting the connection.

The Dragon Link stretched.

Not broke.

Zee grabbed the weapon.

Crimson Phoenix flame burned along it.

The collector holding the other end screamed.

Zee pulled him forward.

Dragon strength.

Vampire speed.

Wolf aggression.

Witch precision.

One movement.

He tore the man’s arm off.

Then killed him.

Zareth shifted.

True Dragon form erupted.

Teal-and-Gold scales.

Phoenix fire.

Witch sigils.

He hit another collector hard enough to bury him in the ground.

No humor.

No mercy.

They had tried to touch the Link that had existed since birth.

Wrong family.

---

Ner protected the survivors.

And Zayrlen.

Pure Gold Mana formed a dome.

Bloodsong destabilized one rider who crossed too close.

The collector stumbled.

Rhyven hit him in true Wolf form.

Crimson fire followed claws.

The man survived the first impact.

Elias ended the second.

Deep-blue Witchcraft formed around black Demon sigils.

“Down.”

The collector slammed into stone.

Kael moved with Vampire speed.

Ended him.

The last rider turned toward Ner.

Saw Zayrlen in Elias's arms.

His expression changed.

Opportunity.

He moved.

Zee saw it.

So did everyone else.

The man never got within twenty feet.

Amara hit first.

Wolf speed.

Rhyven hit second.

Phoenix-Wolf fire.

Elias's Demon-Witch restraint locked the legs.

Kael broke one arm.

Ner's Bloodsong stopped the heart.

The body collapsed.

Zee had not touched him.

Good.

He did not need to.

That was the point.

Zayrlen was surrounded by monsters.

Plural.

---

The Dragon woman stared at Ner.

“You killed him.”

Ner looked at the body.

“He was moving toward my son.”

Fair.

Tessa continued healing the Wolf man without looking up.

“Can everyone stop fighting near my patients?”

Zareth returned to Human form.

“You chose the battlefield badly.”

“They came here.”

“Still.”

Tessa glared.

Zareth stopped speaking.

Even Dragons learned eventually.

---

The collectors were dead.

Arc over.

No surviving master.

No secret larger order.

The two survivors gave names.

Not exposition.

People.

The Dragon woman was **Selyra Kaen**.

The Wolf was **Torren Vale**.

Brother and sister by choice, not blood.

They had spent twelve years surviving together after Selyra's actual Dragon brother died.

The collectors wanted the remaining echo of her original sibling Link.

Torren had helped her escape.

That was why he had almost died.

Zee looked at him.

“Why?”

Torren frowned.

“Why what?”

“You are Wolf.”

“Yes.”

“She is Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“No blood relation.”

“No.”

“You nearly died anyway.”

Torren looked offended.

“She is family.”

Zee smiled faintly.

Correct answer.

---

Selyra recovered enough to leave three days later.

She refused Darkheart sanctuary.

That pleased Zee.

Not because he wanted her gone.

Because independence mattered.

She would return to her own people in the western volcanic territories.

Before leaving, she looked toward Zayrlen.

The baby was awake in Ner’s arms.

“Your son’s Dragon nature is unusual.”

Zee stared.

“Everyone keeps saying that.”

“It is not a warning.”

“Good.”

Selyra looked at Zareth.

Then Zee.

“The thing behind him is not a Link.”

“We know.”

“It is blood memory.”

Zee’s expression changed.

“Meaning?”

“Dragon inheritance can carry ancestral instinct without carrying ancestral consciousness.”

Good.

No ghosts.

No Aurelia resurrection.

No hidden memory spirit.

Just blood.

Selyra continued.

“He may express more of Veyrath than you expect.”

Zee looked toward Zayrlen.

Crimson-Gold eyes.

Tiny scales.

Heat.

Something enormous waiting.

“Good.”

Selyra almost smiled.

Then left.

---

That night, Zayrlen developed another problem.

He refused sleep.

For three hours.

Ner blamed Zee.

Zee blamed genetics.

Ner stared.

“Whose?”

Zee paused.

“Yours.”

Ner threw a pillow.

Zayrlen laughed.

Not a real laugh yet.

Closer to a breathy sound.

But both fathers froze.

Again.

The baby did it a second time.

Ner’s face changed completely.

Zee stared.

“Was that—”

“Yes.”

Zayrlen made the sound again.

A tiny Crimson-and-Gold spark escaped his hand.

Ner smiled.

Zee smiled too.

Outside, kingdoms hunted new blood.

Collectors hunted bonds.

Ancient forests suppressed supernatural life.

Darkheart kept expanding.

The world remained dangerous.

Inside the nursery—

their son had almost learned how to laugh.

For tonight, that mattered more.

---

# Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Five

## The First Time the Prince Left Darkheart

Zayrlen left Darkheart for the first time at two months old.

Zee hated the idea.

Which was exactly why Ner decided they were doing it.

“He cannot spend his entire infancy inside one kingdom.”

“He is two months old.”

“Yes.”

“He does not know what a kingdom is.”

“Then this will be educational.”

“He cannot hold his own head up for long.”

“Zee.”

“No.”

Ner stared.

Zee corrected immediately.

“I would prefer not.”

“Better.”

“Still no.”

Ner smiled.

“You do understand you are not winning.”

“Yes.”

That was the problem.

---

The destination was Vesper.

Safe.

Close.

Family.

Rez had been demanding a visit since the birth.

Demanding was generous.

Threatening was more accurate.

His last message had read:

**If you do not bring my nephew soon, I am coming to collect him myself.**

Zee had replied:

**Try.**

Rez responded:

**I raised you better than this.**

Completely false.

Still irritating.

So they went.

Ner carried Zayrlen.

Zee flew above part of the route.

Then landed because Ner accused him of scouting every bush.

He was.

Amara led a Wolf escort.

Kael rode near the rear.

Elias came because he claimed Vesper owed him replacement books.

Rhyven came because Rez had apparently promised him food.

Zareth joined midway through the route without invitation.

Naturally.

Zee looked at him.

“Why are you here?”

“I am traveling.”

“To Vesper.”

“Yes.”

“At the exact same time.”

“Yes.”

“To see Zayrlen.”

Zareth looked offended.

“That is speculative.”

Through the Link came:

**Obviously.**

Zee ignored him.

---

The road remained quiet.

No attack.

No hidden threat.

No kidnapping.

That itself felt suspicious.

Zee checked the tree line every few minutes.

Ner noticed.

“You are doing it again.”

“What?”

“Expecting the world to ruin something.”

Zee looked toward him.

Ner adjusted Zayrlen against his chest.

“He is allowed to have a boring trip.”

Zee looked at their son.

Zayrlen slept through the entire conversation.

“Boring feels irresponsible.”

Ner smiled.

“That might be the most Zee sentence you have ever said.”

---

Vesper saw them coming.

Mostly because Zee's enormous Crimson Phoenix wings were difficult to miss.

The gates opened.

Blue-White banners moved in the wind.

Rez stood in the courtyard before their horses fully stopped.

He did not greet Zee.

Did not greet Ner.

He walked directly toward Zayrlen.

“Give him to me.”

Ner laughed.

Zee frowned.

“You could say hello.”

Rez looked at him.

“Hello.”

Then at Ner.

“Hello.”

Then back at Zayrlen.

“Give him to me.”

Ner handed him over.

Zee stared.

“That was fast.”

“You have had him for two months.”

“He is my son.”

Rez smiled.

“And my nephew.”

The word settled warmly.

No hidden meaning spoken aloud.

No dangerous truth.

Just Zayrlen.

Rez held him carefully.

Zayrlen opened his eyes.

Crimson-Gold.

Then grabbed Rez's coat.

Rez smiled.

“There he is.”

Zee's expression shifted.

Something old moved quietly in his chest.

Rez had done this before.

With another son.

Another child who knew him as Uncle Rez.

No one else remembered why that mattered.

Rez did.

He looked at Zee for half a heartbeat.

That was enough.

Then he turned his attention fully to Zayrlen.

No comparison.

No stolen moment.

Good.

---

Vesper welcomed the Prince without ceremony.

That had been Zee's condition.

Lucien was gone from the story’s active center now, but Vesper still carried the culture he had built.

Blue-White flame lit the central courtyard.

Children gathered.

Witches whispered.

Some stared at Zee's wings.

More stared at Zayrlen.

One child asked loudly:

“Is he dangerous?”

Zee answered:

“Yes.”

Ner answered:

“He is a baby.”

Both at once.

The child looked confused.

Rez smiled.

“Both answers are correct.”

Zayrlen sneezed.

A tiny Crimson-and-Gold spark hit Rez's shoulder.

The child laughed.

“Dangerous.”

Zee looked smug.

Ner gave up.

---

The important moment happened in the old Vesper gardens.

Rez carried Zayrlen beneath trees Zee remembered from childhood.

Zee and Ner walked behind him.

Zareth had disappeared somewhere with Elias and Kael.

Probably causing expensive damage.

Amara and Rhyven were arguing near the wall.

For once, nothing was on fire.

Rez stopped beside a fountain.

Zayrlen stared at the water.

Zee stopped too.

Water.

Aidan.

Great Vesper River.

Maternal inheritance.

A boy saying:

**It knows me.**

The memory hit sharply.

Rez felt Zee go still.

Ner noticed only the change in posture.

“What?”

Zee looked at the fountain.

“Nothing.”

Ner studied him.

Different from years ago.

He knew when not to push.

Rez turned slightly.

Zayrlen reached toward the water.

Nothing happened.

Good.

No Ocean.

No Abyss.

No Siren inheritance.

Different son.

Different blood.

The fountain remained ordinary.

Rez looked at Zee.

Zee nodded once.

The moment passed.

---

Then Zayrlen growled.

Tiny.

Ridiculous.

Unmistakable.

Everyone froze.

Ner looked at him.

“Was that a growl?”

Rez smiled.

“Yes.”

Zee stepped closer.

Zayrlen stared at a statue beside the fountain.

A carved Wolf.

His pupils narrowed.

Slit.

Tiny claws appeared.

Then came the pack response.

Not distress.

Recognition.

The Vesper garden carried old Wolf scent from visiting allies.

Zayrlen reacted.

His true Wolf nature remained far from awakening.

But instinct was becoming more expressive.

Rez held him closer.

The growl stopped.

Zee looked at him.

“Do that again.”

Ner stared.

“He is not a performance.”

“I want to hear it.”

“He is two months old.”

“Still.”

Rez laughed.

Zayrlen immediately growled again.

Everyone stopped.

Rez looked smug.

Zee looked betrayed.

Ner laughed.

“Apparently he likes Uncle Rez.”

Zee folded his arms.

“Temporary.”

---

That evening, Vesper held dinner.

Nothing political.

Just family.

Rez sat with Zayrlen asleep against his chest for almost the entire meal.

Zee kept watching him.

Finally Elias noticed.

“You are jealous.”

“No.”

“You are.”

“No.”

Kael looked toward Rez.

“He has been holding the baby for an hour.”

“One hour and twelve minutes,” Zee said.

Silence.

Elias smiled.

“You counted.”

“No.”

Everyone laughed.

Zee regretted bringing any of them.

Zareth looked toward the sleeping Prince.

“He should visit Drakonis next.”

Zee answered immediately.

“No.”

Ner answered:

“Eventually.”

Zareth smiled.

Zee looked betrayed.

Again.

---

The attack came after dinner.

Not for Zayrlen.

Not for Zee.

Not for Vesper.

A meteor struck the western fields.

Actual meteor.

The impact shook the kingdom.

Every ward screamed.

Rez stood instantly.

Zayrlen woke and started crying.

Zee was beside him before the second tremor.

Ner took Zayrlen.

Rez's Blue-White Mana filled the hall.

“What was that?”

Zareth's Dragon senses reached farther.

His expression changed.

“Not stone.”

Zee looked toward him.

“What?”

Zareth turned toward the west.

“Alive.”

Silence.

Beyond the windows, something enormous moved inside the crater.

Not Demon.

Not Dragon.

Not Phoenix.

Not anything Zee recognized.

Good.

The world was still capable of surprising him without tying every threat to his bloodline.

Rez handed control of the inner keep to Vesper guards.

Zee looked at Ner.

Ner looked toward the crying baby.

Then at him.

“Go.”

Zee nodded.

No hesitation this time.

Progress.

He left his son with Ner in Vesper.

Protected.

Known.

Loved.

Then Zee, Rez, Zareth, Elias, Kael, Amara, and Rhyven went to find out what had fallen from the sky.

---

The crater was enormous.

The thing inside it was larger.

Black shell.

Six limbs.

Translucent sections showing blue light inside.

No recognizable blood.

No familiar Mana.

No scent Zee could classify.

Zareth stared.

“This is not from here.”

Rez looked toward the sky.

“Meaning?”

Zareth looked at Zee.

“Not this world.”

Silence.

Zee's expression sharpened.

Beyond the stars.

The possibility had always existed.

Now something had landed in Vesper.

The creature rose.

Its shell unfolded.

Blue light spread across the field.

Zee's Phoenix wings opened.

Crimson flame answered.

The creature looked directly at him.

Then spoke in a language none of them knew.

Except Elias.

His new Demon-Witch sigils reacted.

Not translation.

Pattern recognition.

He stared.

“What?”

Elias looked toward Zee.

“I think it asked what you are.”

Zee smiled.

Crimson-Gold eyes brightened.

“Tell it I am busy.”

Rez looked at him.

“You cannot be serious.”

The creature charged.

Zee launched.

“Apparently it understood.”

And for the first time in the Age of New Blood—

the danger coming toward Darkheart had not come from another kingdom.

It had come from beyond the world.
