# Chapter One Hundred Thirty

## The Monster Who Remembers Losing

Zee lasted three days in the medical chamber.

Tessa considered that a miracle.

Zee considered it imprisonment.

On the fourth morning, she entered carrying fresh bandages and found the bed empty.

She stopped.

Looked at the open window.

Then at the Crimson feather lying on the floor beneath it.

Her face went completely still.

“Of course.”

---

Zee was on the eastern roof.

Not flying.

That part mattered.

His damaged Phoenix wing remained folded tightly against his back beneath a support binding.

New feathers had begun growing between the torn ones.

Slowly.

Unevenly.

His cracked horn had sealed along the deepest fracture, though a dark line still marked the damage.

His left eye opened fully now.

Mostly.

The bruising had faded from black to deep purple.

His ribs remained wrapped.

Three still hurt every time he breathed too deeply.

Dragon scales had begun regrowing across the injuries along his side.

New ones came in darker at first before settling back into their normal Crimson-black pattern.

His Vampire hearing had stabilized.

Wolf scent nearly had.

Witchcraft—

that he had tested first.

Naturally.

A small stone hovered above his palm.

Perfectly still.

“Turn.”

It rotated.

“Stop.”

It stopped instantly.

Precision restored.

Mostly.

His Phoenix fire was another problem.

Crimson flame moved across his fingertips.

Normal.

Then deeper.

Scarlet.

For half a heartbeat—

black-crimson appeared inside it.

Zee stared.

The fire returned to ordinary Crimson.

He closed his hand.

Nothing.

Again.

Crimson flame.

Nothing strange.

He hated that.

Not fear.

Lack of control.

Different.

Tessa's voice came from behind him.

“You climbed stairs.”

Zee did not turn.

“Yes.”

“You are supposed to be in bed.”

“No.”

“That was not a question.”

“Then why did you phrase it like one?”

Tessa approached.

Looked at the wing.

Then the ribs.

Then the still-healing eye.

“You are not flying.”

“I know.”

“You were considering it.”

“I consider many terrible ideas.”

“At least one of you is self-aware.”

Zee looked at her.

“I needed air.”

“You have windows.”

“I needed outside air.”

“That is not medically distinct.”

“It is to me.”

Tessa stared.

Then sighed.

“You are impossible.”

Zee looked toward the horizon.

“No.”

His expression changed.

“Just less predictable than yesterday.”

Tessa noticed.

Said nothing.

---

That was the real injury.

Not ribs.

Not wing.

Not horn.

Knowledge.

Somebody had studied Zee Darkheart and reduced him into answers.

Witch?

Suppress casting.

Vampire?

Poison blood and distort senses.

Wolf?

Attack hearing and scent.

Dragon?

Dragonbane.

Phoenix?

Ash restraints and heat suppression.

Adaptation?

Rotate tactics.

Crimson Sovereign?

Never allow enough control for unified power to dominate the field.

It had worked.

That mattered.

Zee replayed the battle without comforting himself.

No excuses.

No secret flaw in their victory.

He had killed many.

They still won.

Power had not failed him.

Control had.

That distinction had been sitting inside his mind since the courtyard.

Now it began changing shape.

---

Rez found him later in the lower training yard.

Not training.

Observing.

Three guards sparred at once.

Zee watched their feet.

Nothing supernatural.

Just patterns.

Rez leaned against the gate.

“Tessa knows you are here?”

“Yes.”

“Does she approve?”

“No.”

“Good.”

Zee looked toward him.

Rez smiled faintly.

Then watched the guards.

“What are you looking for?”

“Repetition.”

“In them?”

“In everyone.”

Rez's smile disappeared.

Now he understood.

Zee pointed toward the first guard.

“He always steps left before committing.”

The second.

“He watches the weapon instead of the shoulders.”

The third.

“He waits for one opponent to become occupied before attacking.”

Rez nodded.

“And?”

Zee looked at him.

“The people who jumped me did none of that for long enough to punish.”

Rez folded his arms.

“They rotated behavior.”

“Yes.”

“They turned unpredictability into structure.”

“Yes.”

“And now you want to do the same.”

Zee's eyes sharpened.

“No.”

Rez waited.

“I want to stop giving people structure to study.”

That was darker.

Better.

---

Zee stepped into the yard.

The guards immediately stopped.

One looked nervous.

“Majesty.”

“Continue.”

They hesitated.

Zee removed the support brace from his good arm.

Rez frowned.

“What are you doing?”

“Watching.”

“You were already watching.”

“Closer.”

The guards resumed.

Zee entered the edge of the sparring circle.

One guard backed away immediately.

Zee noticed.

“Why?”

The man swallowed.

“You are injured.”

“Correct.”

“I do not want to accidentally—”

Zee punched him in the throat.

Not hard enough to damage permanently.

Hard enough to drop him.

The other two froze.

Zee looked down.

“You noticed weakness and changed your behavior because of it.”

The guard coughed.

“Yes.”

“Good.”

Zee turned toward the others.

“Again.”

Rez watched quietly.

This was not training.

Not really.

Zee was studying instinct.

His own.

Theirs.

How people changed when they thought he was vulnerable.

How quickly attention moved.

How fear altered choices.

How respect made enemies predictable in ways hostility sometimes did not.

Useful.

Very useful.

---

Ner noticed the shift that evening.

Zee sat in the nursery holding Zayrlen.

The baby slept against his chest.

No armor.

No blood.

No battlefield.

One damaged wing remained carefully folded so the new feathers would not brush the cradle.

Ner sat across from him.

“You are thinking loudly.”

Zee looked up.

“I am not thinking about anything.”

“Terrible lie.”

Zayrlen moved in his sleep.

One tiny hand closed around Zee's shirt.

Zee automatically adjusted him.

Ner watched.

“You are changing how you fight.”

“Yes.”

“Because they beat you.”

“Yes.”

No shame now.

Fact.

Ner leaned back.

“What changes?”

Zee looked down at Zayrlen.

Then answered.

“I stop assuming the first dangerous person is the most important.”

Ner waited.

“I stop using the same opening simply because it worked before.”

More.

“I stop answering every threat immediately.”

Ner's eyes narrowed slightly.

That one mattered.

Zee continued.

“Sometimes I let someone think their attack worked.”

“Feigned weakness.”

“Yes.”

“False retreat.”

“Yes.”

“Letting someone lie.”

“Yes.”

“Not compelling immediately.”

“Yes.”

Ner smiled faintly.

“You are becoming unpleasant.”

“I already was.”

“More unpleasant.”

“Good.”

No lecture.

No attempt to soften him.

Ner understood exactly why.

Then he asked the question Zee had been asking himself.

“What if Zayrlen is there?”

Zee's expression changed.

That one had no easy answer.

“If he is present, winning is secondary.”

Ner nodded.

“Good.”

“Control the child first.”

“Obviously.”

“Remove family from battlefield.”

“Yes.”

“Then kill.”

Ner smiled.

“There you are.”

Zee looked at him.

“What?”

“You learned something without becoming afraid.”

Zee looked down at their son.

Fear had never been the lesson.

Preparation was.

---

Elias brought the first real clue before midnight.

Not theory.

Evidence.

He placed six objects across Zee's table.

A Dragonbane spear fragment.

A Phoenix restraint hook.

A sonic Wolf disruptor.

An anti-Witch cuff.

A Vampire suppression vial.

A segmented tactical chain.

Rez stood beside him.

Zareth had returned from Drakonis.

Kael leaned against the wall.

Amara and Rhyven remained near the doorway.

Ner sat with Zayrlen asleep nearby.

Elias pointed toward the Dragonbane metal.

“This alloy comes from the eastern volcanic foundries.”

Zareth frowned.

“Drakonis?”

“No.”

“Good.”

“An older weapons region south of your borders.”

Then the anti-Witch cuff.

“The runes are western.”

Rez recognized them.

“Mercenary Witch-killers.”

“Yes.”

Then the sonic device.

Amara's expression changed.

“That tuning pattern is northern Wolf-hunter design.”

Elias nodded.

Kael picked up the suppression vial.

“And this?”

“Vampire hunting compounds from the coastal principalities.”

Silence.

Zee looked across all six.

Different regions.

Different traditions.

Different enemies.

No common culture.

Rez reached the same conclusion first.

“They were assembled.”

Elias nodded.

“Not one natural faction.”

Zareth's eyes hardened.

“Someone selected specialists.”

Rhyven looked toward the Phoenix hook.

“Specifically for Zee.”

“Yes.”

Ner looked at the table.

“Meaning somebody built the attack like a weapon.”

Exactly.

Zee stared.

That sentence settled something.

Not random enemies cooperating in fear.

A constructed team.

Someone had gone shopping for weaknesses.

Different cultures.

Different expertise.

One battlefield.

One target.

Zee.

---

Kael placed a small metal token beside the evidence.

“Found under one of the bodies.”

Zee looked.

A trade stamp.

Not royal.

Not military.

Three crossed lines inside a broken circle.

Rez recognized it.

“Black-market logistics.”

“Where?”

“Graymarket.”

Zee frowned.

“That is a city?”

“Unfortunately.”

Rez picked up the token.

“Neutral trading settlement on the western border routes. Mercenaries. weaponsmiths. couriers. smugglers. People who need things without wanting to know why.”

Elias looked at the stamp.

“This mark is used by brokers who assemble cross-regional contracts.”

Zee's eye sharpened.

“Recruiters.”

“Yes.”

Not identity.

Not mastermind.

But a direction.

Progress.

Real.

---

Then Zee's damaged wing caught fire.

Everyone turned.

Crimson flame spread across the regenerating feathers.

Normal.

Then the newest feather—

changed.

It grew black-crimson from the base.

Scarlet light running through the shaft.

Zee froze.

The feather extended another inch.

Then the strange color disappeared.

Crimson returned.

The fire went out.

Silence.

Tessa, who had been summoned specifically because everyone expected something like this eventually, stepped closer.

“Do not move.”

Zee stared.

“I was not moving.”

“Good. Continue.”

She touched the regrown feather.

No pain.

Then Zee's pulse changed.

One beat.

Deeper.

Hotter.

Something ancient moved beneath his ribs.

Then vanished.

Zee inhaled sharply.

Ner stood.

“What?”

“Heat.”

“Dragon?”

“No.”

“Phoenix?”

Zee looked at the wing.

“Not mine.”

Elias frowned.

“It is yours.”

Zee looked at him.

“You know what I mean.”

“I do.”

Elias opened his Witch senses.

Zareth did the same.

Teal-and-Gold Mana hovered near Zee's shoulder without touching.

Rez watched both.

Finally Elias said:

“The deeper signature is still there.”

“Inherited?” Ner asked.

“Yes.”

Zareth's eyes narrowed.

“And old.”

“How old?”

Zareth shook his head.

“Cannot tell.”

Elias looked toward Zee.

“But it is waking.”

Zee's expression flattened.

“I did not invite it.”

Ner almost smiled.

“Your blood has never cared about invitations.”

Fair.

No answer.

No name.

No source.

Only another fact.

Something old existed beneath Zee's known biology.

Inherited.

Awakening.

Slowly.

He hated mysteries inside his own body.

The world seemed determined to give him more.

---

Far away, Victor's hand caught fire.

Black-crimson.

Scarlet beneath.

He stopped walking.

The road beneath him crossed a small trade village two kingdoms closer to Darkheart than the sanctuary he had abandoned.

The flame appeared without command.

Stayed for one heartbeat.

Then vanished.

Victor stared.

Again.

His son.

Somewhere distant—

the same blood had moved.

He knew it now.

Not enough to speak.

Enough to recognize.

A merchant nearby noticed the fire and backed away.

Victor closed his hand.

“Nothing.”

The merchant decided not to argue.

Smart.

Victor continued walking.

---

Later, Zee returned to the nursery.

No council.

No evidence.

No revenge plan.

Zayrlen was awake.

Ner had fallen asleep in the chair.

Zee lifted his son quietly.

The baby's Crimson-Gold eyes found him immediately.

Then relaxed.

Zee sat.

For several minutes, nothing moved except Zayrlen's tiny fingers.

Monster outside.

Father here.

Both true.

Zee looked toward the dark window.

The people who beat him had learned the King.

The Sovereign.

The Phoenix.

The Dragon.

The Witch.

The Vampire.

The Wolf.

They had mapped his habits and built answers.

Fine.

Zee smiled faintly.

Cold.

“They studied the King.”

Zayrlen stared.

Zee's good wing shifted.

“Good.”

His eyes sharpened.

“Next time they get someone harder to study.”

The baby yawned.

Zee looked down.

“Exactly.”

---

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-One

## The First Trail

Tessa told Zee not to leave Darkheart.

Zee listened carefully.

Then left Darkheart.

Ner watched him fasten a coat over still-healing ribs.

“You know she is going to kill you.”

“She can try.”

“She has access to your organs.”

Zee paused.

“Fair.”

His damaged wing had improved enough to open halfway.

Not enough for sustained flight.

The cracked horn remained visible.

His left eye looked normal unless someone stared too long.

The newest Dragon scales along his ribs were still tender.

He could fight.

He should not.

That distinction had never interested him.

Rez entered.

“Ready?”

“Yes.”

Ner looked at both.

“Bring him back in approximately the same number of pieces.”

Rez nodded.

“No promises.”

Zee looked toward the cradle.

Zayrlen was awake.

Watching.

He crossed the room.

Touched two fingers to his son's hand.

Zayrlen grabbed them.

Then released.

Zee smiled.

“I will be back.”

No hiding.

No disappearing into revenge.

He left as father.

Then became something else on the road.

---

Graymarket was not pretty enough to deserve the word city.

Stone walls.

Narrow streets.

Black awnings.

Metal workshops.

Mercenary taverns.

Couriers moving constantly.

No flags.

No throne.

No one asking too many questions.

Exactly the kind of place where a person could buy six specialists from six cultures and never learn their real names.

Zee entered through the western gate on foot.

No Phoenix wings displayed.

The damaged one remained bound beneath his coat.

He wore no royal colors.

No crown.

No Darkheart insignia.

Rez walked beside him.

Blue-White Mana suppressed deliberately.

Elias followed several steps behind.

Not appearing connected.

Kael and Amara had entered through another gate.

Rhyven remained outside the city, tracking outbound movement.

No Zareth.

Too recognizable.

That was intentional.

The first change.

Do not arrive as the obvious weapon.

---

The trade mark from the ambush token belonged to a broker called Hask Renn.

They learned that within an hour.

Not through torture.

Through pretending not to care.

Zee sat in a tavern with one hand wrapped around a cup he never drank.

Rez played irritated noble.

Very convincing.

Elias looked bored.

Also convincing.

A weapons courier at the next table whispered too loudly about Hask's contracts.

Zee heard.

Did nothing.

The courier glanced toward him.

Recognized the damaged horn.

Then the eye.

Then the way Zee favored one side slightly.

Recognition arrived.

Fear after.

Zee saw it.

Pretended not to.

The courier stood.

Left.

Rez waited.

“He recognized you.”

“Yes.”

“You are letting him go.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

Zee looked toward the door.

“Because he thinks I did not notice.”

Rez smiled.

There.

New Zee.

---

The courier left Graymarket through the north gate.

Rhyven caught his scent.

Did not follow closely.

Amara picked it up farther east.

Then Kael.

Rotating trackers.

No obvious pursuit.

Zee and Rez remained inside the tavern another twenty minutes.

Long enough for anyone watching to believe the King had missed the trail.

Then Zee stood.

Elias followed.

No rush.

No wings.

No spectacle.

---

The courier reached an abandoned military waystation two miles outside Graymarket.

Old walls.

Collapsed stable.

One intact tower.

Two people waited inside.

Hask Renn was one.

The second was a weapons supplier Zee did not know.

Rhyven watched from the forest.

Amara from the opposite side.

Kael behind the tower.

Zee approached openly.

Rez frowned.

“I thought we were being unpredictable.”

“We are.”

“You are walking through the front gate.”

“Yes.”

“That is very predictable.”

“Wait.”

Rez did.

---

Hask saw Zee.

Immediately panicked.

He was older.

Human.

Maybe Witch ancestry somewhere distant.

No active magic.

His eyes went to Zee's damaged side.

Then the bound wing beneath the coat.

Then the cracked horn.

Confidence returned.

Slightly.

Good.

Zee deliberately limped once.

Rez noticed.

Almost smiled.

Hask straightened.

“King Darkheart.”

Zee looked around.

“You know me.”

“Everyone does.”

Zee stopped ten feet away.

“I am looking for someone.”

Hask's heart sped up.

Vampire hearing caught it.

Zee ignored the obvious lie before it arrived.

“I sell information.”

“No.”

Hask blinked.

“I did not ask.”

Silence.

Zee looked toward the courier.

The man tried edging toward the rear door.

Zee saw.

Did nothing.

Hask noticed too.

Now he thought Zee was weak.

Slow.

Injured.

Good.

“I heard you had a bad week,” Hask said.

Rez's Blue-White Mana twitched.

Zee did not react.

“Did you?”

Hask smiled.

“Stories travel.”

“What story?”

“That someone finally put the great Zee Darkheart on the ground.”

Silence.

Zee looked down at his own hand.

Then laughed quietly.

Hask relaxed further.

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Two

## The Father Who Watches

Victor saw Zee holding Zayrlen before Zee ever knew he was there.

Darkheart had changed so much that Victor almost did not recognize it.

The old kingdom had been narrower.

Quieter.

More obedient.

This place breathed differently.

Witches crossed the courtyard beside Wolves.

Vampires stood watch beside Humans.

Children ran between soldiers without fear.

Phoenix feathers occasionally passed overhead when Zee moved between towers.

Darkheart had become something Victor never built.

Something he would once have called unstable.

Something alive.

Victor remained beyond the inner grounds beneath concealment older than most of the wards surrounding the keep.

His evolved Witchcraft bent attention away from him.

Black-crimson flame remained buried beneath his skin.

The Abyssal Titan Phoenix Sovereign inside him stayed quiet.

Mostly.

He had not come to attack.

Not yet.

He had come to see.

Then Zee entered the western courtyard carrying his son.

Victor stopped breathing.

---

Zee still looked injured.

The ambush had not vanished from him.

One Phoenix wing remained uneven where feathers continued regenerating.

A dark fracture line still marked one horn.

The bruising around his left eye had almost faded but not completely.

New Dragon scales were still filling in along his ribs beneath the open edge of his coat.

He moved normally.

Almost.

Victor noticed the difference.

A father notices things even after failing to deserve the word.

Zee carried Zayrlen against his chest.

One hand supported the baby's head automatically.

The other held beneath him.

No servant.

No nurse.

No guard.

Zee.

Zayrlen moved.

Zee adjusted instantly.

Tiny change.

Barely visible.

Victor saw it.

Then the baby grabbed Zee's finger.

Zee stopped walking.

Looked down.

“Sir.”

Zayrlen tightened his grip.

Ner walked beside him and laughed.

“He is not listening.”

“He is disrespecting the King.”

“He cannot sit upright.”

“That is unrelated.”

Zayrlen released Zee's finger.

Then reached higher.

His tiny hand found Zee's horn.

Victor's eyes widened.

Zee froze.

The baby grabbed it.

Hard.

Ner started laughing immediately.

Zee stared at his son.

“Absolutely not.”

Zayrlen pulled.

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“Sir.”

Ner laughed harder.

“He likes it.”

“It is attached to my skull.”

“He does not care.”

Zayrlen pulled again.

Zee sighed.

Then adjusted his grip so the baby's neck remained supported.

He did not move the hand away.

Did not frighten him.

Did not snap.

Did not even raise his voice.

He simply stood there while his two-month-old son held one of the most threatening parts of his body like a toy.

Victor felt something inside his chest twist.

Years ago, he had looked at impossible eyes.

Tiny fangs.

Blood rain.

A child that frightened the world by existing.

And he had chosen murder.

Zee looked at an impossible child and let him pull on his horn.

The difference hurt worse than Victor expected.

---

Ner leaned closer.

“He is getting sleepy.”

“I know.”

“You heard it?”

“His breathing changed.”

Victor's expression tightened.

Zee had noticed before Ner finished speaking.

The baby's heartbeat.

Breathing.

Tiny movement.

Everything.

Zee lowered his voice.

“Sleep.”

No Witch command.

Just father.

Zayrlen stared at him.

Then yawned.

Zee smiled.

Small.

Barely there.

Victor almost hated him for that smile.

Not because it was weakness.

Because Zee had something Victor had thrown away.

---

Victor left the observation point before Zee could look toward him.

Not because Zee had sensed him.

Because Victor needed distance.

He walked deeper into the old forest beyond Darkheart's western edge.

Pride fought guilt.

Guilt fought habit.

Habit won first.

He needed certainty.

That was what Victor told himself.

He needed to know whether what he had seen was real.

Whether Zee's gentleness survived pressure.

Whether the monster disappeared when the child became inconvenient.

Whether fear changed him.

Victor had spent years building excuses around his own failure.

The prophecy.

The blood rain.

The world's reaction.

Zee's immortality.

The impossible combination inside a newborn body.

All true.

None enough.

Still, Victor clung to one final lie.

Perhaps anyone would have broken under enough fear.

Perhaps Zee simply had not been tested correctly.

Victor looked back toward Darkheart.

Then black-crimson flame rose over his fingers.

Scarlet beneath.

He closed his hand.

One test.

Deeply wrong.

He knew that.

He did it anyway.

Because Victor Darkheart was still Victor Darkheart.

---

The first fire appeared in the eastern watchtower.

No spark.

No caster.

No projectile.

One second the tower stood cold.

The next—

black-crimson flame erupted across the upper stone.

Scarlet depth burned inside it like blood trapped beneath darkness.

The fire moved against the wind.

Darkheart alarms rang instantly.

Then three more fires appeared.

Southern wall.

Old council roof.

Western barracks.

No conventional trajectory.

No visible attacker.

Witch sigils burned inside the flames.

Ancient.

Unfamiliar.

Every nearby ward reacted differently.

Some cracked.

Some dimmed.

One completely reversed itself and tried sealing the fire inside.

The fire ate the ward.

Zee looked up from the courtyard.

Zayrlen still in his arms.

His expression changed instantly.

Father vanished behind King.

Not completely.

Never completely.

“Ner.”

Ner was already moving.

He took Zayrlen.

Pure Gold Mana rose around them.

Rez appeared from the lower passage.

“What?”

“Unknown fire. Multiple positions.”

Elias arrived seconds later.

Deep-blue Mana spread through the courtyard.

Black sigils appeared.

His face changed.

“That is not Phoenix ash behavior.”

Zareth's presence struck Zee through the Dragon Soul Link from elsewhere in Darkheart.

**I feel it.**

Zee looked toward the western tower.

**Do you recognize it?**

**No.**

Good.

Bad.

Both.

---

“Rez,” Zee said.

“Evacuating affected sections.”

“Keep civilians away from fire.”

“Already.”

“Elias.”

“Studying.”

“Ner.”

“I have Zayrlen.”

Zee's eyes sharpened.

That was all he needed.

He launched.

His damaged Phoenix wing opened.

Pain.

Then something strange happened.

The wing caught black-crimson fire.

Not Victor's flame.

Zee's.

Scarlet blood-fire spread through the damaged feathers.

The torn sections regenerated faster.

Not instantly.

Far faster than they had the day before.

Zee stopped midair.

His heartbeat changed.

One deep strike.

Then another.

He felt it beneath his ribs.

Ancient heat.

Different from Dragon.

Different from acquired Crimson Phoenix.

His cracked horn burned.

The fracture line sealed another inch.

New feathers emerged along the injured wing.

Not Crimson.

Black-crimson.

Scarlet veins glowing through them.

Zee stared.

“What the hell?”

Then another tower ignited.

No time.

He moved.

---

Zee hit the first fire with Crimson Phoenix flame.

His normal fire should have collided.

Instead—

the two flames recognized each other.

Not identical.

Related.

The black-crimson fire curved toward him.

Zee's own Phoenix blood surged.

Scarlet spread across his wings.

His eyes flared violently Crimson-Gold.

The heat doubled.

Then tripled.

Stone beneath him cracked.

Elias shouted from below:

“Zee!”

“I know.”

“No, you do not.”

Fair.

Zee forced the fire outward.

Too much.

A wave of scarlet-black Phoenix flame exploded across the roof.

It burned through the strange attack.

Then kept going.

Zee had to slam both hands together.

“Stop.”

Witchcraft caught his own fire.

Barely.

The flames shuddered.

Then folded inward.

Zee landed hard.

His expression was furious.

Not because of the attack.

Because his own power had failed to obey cleanly.

---

Victor watched from beyond the outer wall.

He had expected reaction.

He had expected recognition.

He had not expected this.

His own Abyssal Titan Phoenix Sovereign fire had touched Zee's presence—

and Zee's blood had answered like dry forest meeting lightning.

Black-crimson feathers.

Scarlet flame.

Accelerated regeneration.

Phoenix pressure thick enough that Victor felt it through concealment.

His son's biology was not simply awakening the inheritance.

It was changing it.

Victor's eyes narrowed.

“No.”

Not rejection.

Disbelief.

The ancient bloodline inside Victor had always felt vast.

Old.

Complete.

Zee's version did not feel complete.

It felt hungry.

Transformative.

His acquired Crimson Phoenix blood was fusing with the inheritance instead of yielding to it.

Victor understood one thing immediately.

This was becoming something the original bloodline had never been.

---

Zee extinguished the third fire.

Then the fourth.

No civilians dead.

Several wounded by collapsing wards.

Darkheart intact.

Then Victor moved the attack.

Closer.

A black-crimson sigil appeared above the royal residence.

Zee saw it.

His entire body changed.

The sigil turned.

A spear of scarlet-black flame formed beneath it.

Pointed directly toward the nursery level.

Zee did not calculate.

Did not assign defense.

Did not think about walls.

“Ner.”

Bloodsong answered from inside.

**Here.**

Zee moved.

---

He entered through the balcony.

Ner already had Zayrlen.

Pure Gold barriers layered around them.

The baby had started fussing.

Not combat.

Not power.

Just instinct responding to the pressure.

Tiny Crimson-Gold scales flickered across his shoulder.

Zee stepped between the balcony and his family.

“Behind me.”

Ner did not argue.

He moved one step back.

Not because he was helpless.

Because Zee was physically between the attack and the child.

That was the correct position.

Zee opened both Phoenix wings.

One still healing.

Not anymore.

The strange paternal heat surged.

Black-crimson feathers tore through the remaining damaged sections.

Scarlet fire spilled between them.

His wing regenerated almost completely in seconds.

Zee gasped.

The cracked horn sealed.

Blood from a reopened wound along his ribs ignited before reaching the floor.

Scarlet.

His Dragon scales glowed from beneath.

His heartbeat thundered.

Deeper.

Older.

The air around him changed.

Then something enormous appeared behind him.

A Phoenix.

Not physical.

Not complete.

A silhouette made from black-crimson blood-flame.

Predatory.

Colossal.

Head lowered.

Wings wider than the room could contain.

Crimson-Gold eyes burning inside the shape.

Victor saw it from outside.

And went completely still.

That was not his Phoenix.

---

The attack descended.

Zee raised Witchcraft first.

“Hold.”

The scarlet-black spear slowed.

Crimson Sovereign followed.

Witch precision.

Vampire reaction.

Wolf protection instinct.

All three unified.

Dragon force grounded his body.

His existing Crimson Phoenix fire rose.

The inherited fire erupted through it.

Zee's wings wrapped backward around Ner and Zayrlen.

His own body stood in front.

No hesitation.

The spear hit.

The balcony exploded.

Stone shattered.

Wards broke.

Flame swallowed Zee.

Ner tightened Gold around Zayrlen.

Zee took the rest.

The impact forced him backward one step.

Then another.

His feet dug trenches into the floor.

His skin burned.

Regenerated.

Burned again.

Black-crimson feathers grew through the damage as fast as the attack tore them.

His voice changed.

A Phoenix cry lived beneath the sound when he shouted:

“NO.”

The strange fire bent.

Not mastered.

Not controlled elegantly.

Overpowered by instinct.

Father before power.

Zee drove everything outward.

The incoming attack broke around him.

Never touched Ner.

Never touched Zayrlen.

Victor diverted the final force before impact could become lethal.

Zee never knew.

To Zee—

he had simply stopped it.

With his body.

---

Then the attack vanished.

All of it.

No final strike.

No visible caster.

No signature remaining long enough to follow.

Zee stood in the ruined nursery balcony breathing hard.

Scarlet-black fire still crawled over his wings.

Some feathers had turned almost entirely black-crimson.

His eyes remained unnaturally bright.

The giant Phoenix silhouette flickered behind him.

Then disappeared.

Ner stepped forward.

“Zee.”

“I am fine.”

Ner stared at the burned remains of Zee's coat.

“Not doing this again.”

Fair.

Zayrlen cried.

That sound cut through everything.

Zee turned immediately.

Ner handed him over.

The baby settled against Zee's chest within seconds.

Heartbeat.

Recognition.

Father.

Zee's expression softened despite the fire still moving across his feathers.

He rocked him carefully.

“Nothing touched you.”

Zayrlen made a tiny sound.

Zee looked down.

“I know.”

Ner looked around at the destroyed balcony.

Then back at Zee.

“You are on fire.”

“Yes.”

“Different fire.”

“Yes.”

“Can you put it out?”

Zee tried.

Nothing happened.

He frowned.

Ner almost laughed.

Did not.

Not yet.

---

Far beyond the courtyard, Victor watched one last time.

Zee's wings still carried black-crimson feathers.

Scarlet fire curled around them without burning the child.

Zayrlen slept against his chest.

Zee adjusted the baby's head automatically.

Gentle.

Exact.

Victor closed his eyes.

That was the answer.

Threaten the kingdom—

Zee became King.

Threaten his son—

Zee became something else.

Worse.

Better.

Everything Victor had not been.

He turned away.

Then stopped.

Because Zee looked suddenly toward the western forest.

Not directly at Victor.

Close enough.

Zee's Wolf instincts stirred.

Vampire senses sharpened.

Witch Mana resonated.

Phoenix fire rose without permission.

His blood reacted.

Known.

Impossible.

Known.

Zee frowned.

He stared into the dark.

“What are you?”

Victor left before Zee could find out.

Without visible Phoenix fire.

Wolf scent.

Vampire hearing.

Witch perception.

King's Hunt.

No obvious pursuit.

Quiet.

Patient.

Wrong direction.

Black-crimson fire barely visible beneath one palm.

East.

Then—

closer.

Nothing.

False.

False.

False.

Changed.

Enemy.

Kin.

Enemy.

Kin.

---

Barely.

Made noise.

Let his damaged coat scrape bark.

Waited.

Nothing.

Old Witchcraft.

Darkheart Witchcraft.

Not identical.

Related.

Vampire speed.

No clear view.

Older.

Scarred.

Victor's black-crimson flame.

Zee's Crimson fire.

---

Transformation pressure.

Larger.

Broader.

Predatory.

Every remaining injury from Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Eight burned away beneath violent regeneration.

Dragon scales glowed from underneath.

Scarlet fire poured from between them.

Massive talons made from blood-flame formed over Zee's hands.

His spine arched.

Bones shifted.

Not enough to break.

Enough to change intention.

Something inside his body was trying to become something else.

Bigger.

Winged.

Ancient.

A colossal Phoenix outline erupted around him.

Black-crimson.

Scarlet.

Crimson-Gold eyes.

A hooked predatory face.

Fangs suggested inside the shape where a normal Phoenix should not have them.

Witch lightning cracked around its body.

Zee's mouth opened.

A Phoenix cry came out beneath his voice.

Victor stared.

Stunned.

His own flame bent toward Zee.

Not submission.

Recognition.

Kinship.

Then alteration.

Victor understood.

The bloodline inside Zee had stopped simply awakening.

It was fusing.

His son's acquired Crimson Phoenix blood was rewriting the inheritance into something new.

Something Victor had never possessed.

Something no old name fully covered.

The beginning of a Crimson Abyssal Phoenix.

---

Zee's body tried shifting farther.

Shoulders changed.

Wing joints widened.

Scarlet fire flooded his throat.

His fingers curled beneath phantom talons.

The Phoenix silhouette closed around him.

Too much.

Too fast.

No mastery.

Zee forced his knees straight.

“No.”

His voice layered with another cry.

The fire surged.

Victor watched.

Zee clenched both fists.

Witch discipline.

Crimson Sovereign control.

Wolf grounding.

Vampire focus.

Dragon endurance.

Father.

Home.

Zayrlen.

That was the anchor.

Not fear.

Purpose.

Zee forced the change backward.

Bone settled.

Hands remained hands.

Wings remained physical Phoenix wings instead of something larger.

The enormous silhouette flickered.

Then stayed behind him without swallowing him.

Zee breathed hard.

Scarlet-black fire poured from his mouth once.

Then stopped.

His eyes remained blazing.

He looked toward Victor's concealed position.

“What are you?”

Victor did not answer.

Zee stepped forward.

Victor stepped back.

Then Zee smiled.

Cold.

“You are afraid.”

Victor hated that he was right.

---

Zee changed direction.

Not toward Victor.

Past him.

Victor realized too late.

Zee had noticed the escape route.

He cut it off.

The post-defeat lesson.

Do not chase where the enemy wants.

Take away where they intend to go.

Victor turned.

Zee was already there.

Wings spread.

Scarlet-black fire behind him.

“You attacked my home.”

Silence.

“You aimed at my son's room.”

Victor's face remained hidden beneath distortion.

Zee's voice dropped.

“I am going to kill you.”

Victor believed him.

Completely.

That was when he made the final test.

And hated himself for needing it.

---

Victor raised one hand.

Not toward Zee.

Toward Darkheart.

A Witch sigil formed high above the trees.

Far away on the horizon—

scarlet-black flame erupted.

An illusion.

A resonance.

Perfectly shaped to mimic the royal defenses breaking.

Then came another signal.

A distorted magical pulse patterned after the nursery wards.

Impact.

Collapse.

Distress.

Zee's head snapped toward Darkheart.

Victor watched him.

Here.

Enemy almost caught.

One step from the answer.

Revenge within reach.

Home apparently burning.

Zayrlen possibly inside.

Zee did not hesitate.

Not even one heartbeat.

He abandoned Victor.

Phoenix wings exploded open.

Scarlet-black fire ripped through the forest.

Zee launched toward Darkheart.

Gone.

Victor stood alone.

The test ended.

Complete.

---

He chose the boy.

Victor closed his eyes.

Every time.

There was no excuse left.

No prophecy.

No impossible biology.

No fear of what the child might become.

Zee had just stood close enough to finally seize the person who attacked his home—

and left him alive the instant his son appeared threatened.

Victor remembered his own newborn.

Zee.

Small.

Impossible.

Terrifying.

Victor had chosen himself.

His crown.

His fear.

His control.

Zee chose the child.

Victor's jaw tightened.

The shame did not redeem him.

It only removed one more lie.

He was still proud.

Still angry.

Still afraid of what would happen when Zee finally learned who he was.

Because Victor had crossed Zee's law now.

He had attacked Darkheart.

Worse—

he had made Zee believe Zayrlen was in danger.

Victor understood exactly what that meant.

If he revealed himself tonight, Zee would probably attack before listening.

And Victor could not honestly call that unreasonable.

Not anymore.

---

Zee hit Darkheart like falling scarlet fire.

He landed in the royal courtyard.

Stone cracked.

Black-crimson feathers flared.

Scarlet blood-flame poured from his wings.

“NER.”

Ner appeared at the upper passage with Zayrlen in his arms.

Alive.

Safe.

Completely unharmed.

Zee stopped.

The illusion broke inside his mind.

False.

Manipulated.

His face became terrifying.

Ner saw it.

“What happened?”

Zee crossed the courtyard.

“The attacker lied.”

Ner immediately understood.

“About Zayrlen.”

“Yes.”

Pure Gold Mana flared.

Not at Zee.

At the idea.

“I hate this person.”

“Yes.”

Good.

---

Zee reached for Zayrlen.

Ner handed him over.

The baby recognized him instantly.

Heartbeat changed.

Relaxed.

Tiny hand caught against one black-crimson feather now lying over Zee's shoulder.

The scarlet fire moved around Zayrlen's fingers.

Did not burn.

Zee froze.

Everyone nearby noticed.

Ner stared.

Zayrlen pulled the feather closer.

Then made a tiny happy sound.

Zee looked down at him.

“You are supposed to be impressed.”

Zayrlen chewed on his own fist.

Ner laughed.

“He is two months old.”

“Still rude.”

Zayrlen grabbed the feather again.

Scarlet fire curled around his hand like silk.

No Phoenix inheritance in the child.

No awakening.

No transfer.

Only Zee's power recognizing family and refusing harm.

Zee stared.

Then his entire expression softened.

Daddy Zee won.

Completely.

Ner smiled.

“There he is.”

“Do not.”

“You melted.”

“No.”

“You absolutely did.”

Zayrlen made the happy sound again.

Zee looked down.

“Traitor.”

---

Rez returned from the false eastern search shortly afterward.

One look at Zee's transformed wings stopped him.

Black-crimson feathers.

Scarlet blood-fire moving persistently between them.

No longer a flicker.

No longer one strange feather.

A permanent change during active power.

Elias arrived and stared.

Zareth landed behind him.

The Dragon Soul Link slammed into Zee's newest sensations.

His face changed.

“You nearly transformed.”

“Yes.”

“Into what?”

“I do not know.”

Elias stepped closer.

“The inherited signature?”

“Wide awake.”

“Mastered?”

Zee laughed once.

“No.”

Good.

That answer mattered.

Tessa arrived.

Looked at Zee.

Her eyes narrowed.

“You are healed.”

“Yes.”

“I dislike that.”

“Why?”

“Because I did not do it.”

Fair.

She examined the wing.

No damage.

Horn fully restored.

Scales complete.

Eye clear.

Regeneration had changed dramatically.

Not ordinary Crimson Phoenix anymore.

Something deeper had taken over repair.

Elias looked toward the scarlet fire.

“It is fusing.”

Zee's expression hardened.

“With what?”

“We still do not know.”

Zareth looked at the wings.

“But it is yours now.”

Zee glanced toward Zayrlen.

The baby still had one fist wrapped around a feather.

“Yes.”

That much was obvious.

---

Far outside Darkheart, Victor watched from one final ridge.

Too far for Zee to detect.

Darkheart glowed below.

Victor saw movement.

Small.

The silhouette of Zee holding Zayrlen near the window.

Black-crimson scarlet fire moving around him.

The baby completely unafraid.

Victor's chest tightened.

He had his answer.

All the way.

That was how far Zee would go.

Not to control the child.

Not to kill what frightened him.

Not to make him smaller.

To protect him.

Everything outward.

All violence pointed away from the boy.

Victor closed his eyes.

“He chose the boy.”

Quiet.

No pride.

Not yet.

Too much guilt for that.

He turned from the ridge.

Not retreat forever.

Delay.

Because now he knew exactly what Zee had become.

And exactly what Zee would do if Victor revealed that the attacker who had threatened Darkheart and made him believe Zayrlen was in danger—

was his dead father.

Victor walked away before sunrise.

Black-crimson fire burned once across his hand.

Scarlet beneath.

The old bloodline.

The original inheritance.

Still his.

But inside Zee—

it was becoming something else.

Something larger.

Something the ancient Abyssal Titan Phoenix Sovereign bloodline had never produced.

---

Inside Darkheart, Zee sat beside the nursery window.

Zayrlen slept against him.

Ner nearby.

Scarlet-black Phoenix fire moved quietly through Zee's feathers.

Persistent now.

Controlled enough not to spread.

Not mastered enough to disappear when he wanted.

His body felt different.

Hotter.

Deeper.

Like something colossal had folded itself beneath his skin and was waiting for space.

He still did not know its name.

Did not know its source.

Did not know his father lived.

Did not know Victor had been watching.

He knew only three things.

The power was inherited.

It was fusing with his Crimson Phoenix blood.

And something inside him had almost become a Phoenix instead of merely carrying one.

Zayrlen shifted.

Tiny fingers caught another feather.

Zee looked down.

The fire moved around the baby's hand.

Gentle.

Ner smiled.

Zee stared at his son.

Monster to the world.

Father here.

Outside, one enemy had already taught Zee he could lose.

Somewhere else, Merek Voss remained alive and moving through Ravelin Cross.

And somewhere beyond Zee's knowledge, a father who had once chosen fear was walking away from the son who had just proven he would choose his own child every time.

The Crimson Abyssal Phoenix had not awakened completely.

But now—

it was no longer sleeping.

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Four

## The Father Who Came Back

Zee found him at dusk.

Not by sight.

By blood.

The trail had been impossible all day.

No stable scent.

No heartbeat pattern he could trust.

No ordinary Witch signature.

No Phoenix trail that behaved like Pyrathis.

Every method gave him the same infuriating answer.

Known.

Kin.

Wrong.

Zee stopped at the edge of an abandoned stone field beyond Darkheart’s western roads.

The old ruins had once belonged to a minor Witch garrison.

Now half the walls were gone.

Trees grew through the barracks.

Wind moved through broken arches.

Nothing else.

Zee stood quietly.

No visible fire.

No open wings.

No announcement.

He had learned.

“If you are here,” he said, “you have ten seconds before I stop being polite.”

Nothing.

Zee smiled faintly.

“Good.”

Then the first black-crimson blade of Witchfire struck from behind.

---

Zee moved before impact.

Barely.

The attack cut through his coat and burned across the scales beneath.

Scarlet fire followed the wound.

Not his.

The familiarity hit immediately.

His own Phoenix blood surged in answer.

Victor remained hidden behind distortion.

No face.

No name.

Only the same impossible magical presence.

Zee turned.

“Found you.”

A second strike came from above.

Then a third from the left.

Different angles.

Old Darkheart Witchcraft.

Zee knew the architecture even though the exact spells had evolved beyond anything used in Victor’s reign.

That made no sense.

He answered with Witch precision.

“Sever.”

The nearest sigil split.

Victor countered.

“Close.”

The broken spell folded back together.

Zee’s expression changed.

That word.

That rhythm.

Old.

Familiar in a place memory did not want to touch.

Victor attacked again.

Zee opened his Phoenix wings.

Black-crimson feathers now mixed through the Crimson.

Scarlet blood-fire erupted.

Victor’s own flame met it.

The collision shook the ruins.

Zee slid backward.

Victor did too.

For one breath, neither moved.

Then Zee looked toward the concealed figure.

“Who taught you Darkheart Witchcraft?”

No answer.

Wrong choice.

Zee disappeared in Vampire speed.

---

Victor anticipated the direct attack.

Zee did not finish it.

He vanished halfway.

Wolf instinct changed angle.

Nanda Parbat changed rhythm.

Victor turned toward where Zee should have been.

Zee came from below.

Dragon strength drove one shoulder into Victor’s ribs.

They crashed through a wall.

Victor rolled.

Zee followed.

Claws came out.

Victor caught his wrist.

Black-crimson Phoenix flame exploded between their hands.

Both recoiled.

The blood resonance became unbearable.

Zee stared at his own palm.

Then at Victor’s concealed one.

Related.

Not metaphorically.

Biologically.

His Vampire senses screamed ancestry.

His Witch Mana pulled toward the stranger.

His Phoenix fire kept answering before Zee commanded it.

Even his Wolf hesitated.

Enemy.

Kin.

Enemy.

Kin.

Zee hated the contradiction.

He attacked harder.

---

Victor’s concealment survived the first three collisions.

Not the fourth.

Zee stopped trying to break the entire spell.

He watched.

Waited.

Let Victor cast.

Then struck one point.

“Sever.”

The distortion cracked across the chest.

Victor immediately reinforced it.

Too late.

Zee saw a jawline.

Older.

Familiar.

Impossible.

He froze.

Victor saw the recognition begin.

Zee’s face changed.

“No.”

Victor stepped back.

Zee did not move.

The concealment failed completely.

Victor Darkheart stood inside the ruins.

Alive.

Older.

Scarred.

Black-crimson fire moving around one hand.

Scarlet beneath.

Zee stared.

For once, nothing came out.

No threat.

No sarcasm.

No violence.

Just shock.

Victor looked exactly wrong.

Alive when he should not be.

Breathing when Zee knew he had stopped.

Standing when Zee had already buried that chapter of his life.

Zee’s voice came quietly.

“I killed you.”

Victor said nothing.

Zee took one step closer.

His Crimson-Gold eyes did not leave Victor’s face.

“I killed you.”

“I know.”

That voice.

Real.

Not illusion.

Not mimicry.

Not resurrection spell wearing a corpse.

Victor.

Zee’s expression emptied.

“How?”

Victor’s black-crimson flame moved once.

Then died down.

“Death woke something in me.”

Zee stared at the fire.

Then at Victor.

Phoenix.

The realization came piece by piece.

Victor died.

Then returned.

Phoenix bloodline.

Dormant.

Inherited.

The deeper fire inside Zee.

His own awakening.

Everything turned at once.

Zee’s face changed.

“You.”

Victor did not answer fast enough.

Zee looked toward the black-crimson fire.

Then remembered Darkheart burning.

The royal residence.

The nursery.

The false strike toward Zayrlen.

His voice dropped.

“You attacked my home.”

Victor inhaled.

“Yes.”

“You aimed at my son.”

“No.”

Zee’s eyes became slits.

“You made me believe you did.”

Victor held his ground.

“Yes.”

Silence.

Worse than shouting.

---

Victor spoke first.

“It was a test.”

Zee stared at him.

Victor continued because he had already crossed too many lines to stop halfway.

“I watched you with the boy.”

Zee’s entire body went still.

Victor saw that and immediately knew he had chosen the worst possible wording.

“You watched my son.”

“Yes.”

“You watched us.”

“Yes.”

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Five

## The Man Who Refused to Stay Dead

Scarlet beneath.

Reconstruction.

Blood returned from ash.

Again.

Again.

Again.

Not almost.

Real death.

Then resurrection.

Again.

No hole.

Nothing.

Massive black-crimson body.

Scarlet blood-fire.

Crimson-Gold eyes.

Fangs.

Witch lightning.

One coherent supernatural organism.

Abysscin.

Something new.

Uncomfortably correct.

First Natural Tribrid.

Black-crimson flame answered.

His.

Ancient.

Unchanged.

The Crimson Black Abyss Phoenix.

Unique.

Impossible.

Of course.

Not dignity.

His pride hurt more.

Leave.

Very far.

Possibly forever.

Not today.

Appropriate.

Proud.

Intrusive.

Complicated.

Alive.

Again.

his father had officially become a problem death could no longer solve.

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Six

## The Third Time He Walked In

Victor returned through the front gate.

That was somehow worse.

No concealment.

No hidden fire.

No distant Witch sigils.

No attack.

He simply walked toward Darkheart like a man arriving somewhere he had already been invited.

The guards disagreed.

Spears lowered immediately.

Wards activated.

Wolf sentries growled.

Witch circles opened across the stone.

Victor stopped before the outer arch and looked around at the weapons pointed toward him.

Black-crimson fire moved once across his fingers.

Scarlet beneath.

Every nearby ward screamed.

One guard shouted:

“Identify yourself.”

Victor looked toward the keep.

“Victor Darkheart.”

Silence.

Then everything became more dangerous.

---

Zareth felt him first.

Teal-and-Gold Mana erupted around him before anyone finished delivering the message.

Victor.

Alive.

Again.

The Dragon Soul Link snapped toward Zee instantly.

Not panic.

Warning.

Rage.

Rez heard the name and stopped halfway through a conversation.

Ner looked up from Zayrlen.

Pure Gold Mana filled the nursery.

Elias cursed.

Kael reached for a blade.

Amara's Wolf came forward in her eyes.

Rhyven's Phoenix-Wolf fire rose around his claws.

Tessa said:

“Absolutely not.”

Then Zee walked into the courtyard.

Victor was waiting beneath the gate.

Alive.

Again.

Zee stopped.

For several seconds he said nothing.

Not shock this time.

No confusion.

He understood exactly what he was looking at.

His father.

The man he had killed.

Twice.

Standing upright for a third appearance like death had become an inconvenience.

Zee stared.

Victor waited.

Zee finally spoke.

“I just killed you.”

“Yes.”

The answer was immediate.

That made it worse.

Zee took another step.

“Completely.”

“Yes.”

“I put my foot through your heart.”

“I remember.”

“I watched you stop breathing.”

“Yes.”

“I checked.”

“I know.”

Zee stared at him.

Then looked toward the sky as though asking the universe for patience it had no intention of giving.

When he looked back down:

“Why are you here?”

Victor's expression remained composed.

“I came back.”

“That was not the question.”

“I wanted to see you.”

Zee's face went blank.

Ner arrived behind him.

“That may be the worst possible answer.”

Victor looked toward Ner.

Ner's expression made the boundary obvious.

Do not.

Victor wisely looked back at Zee.

Zee took one more step.

Then punched him.

---

The courtyard exploded into movement.

Victor hit the stone.

Rolled.

Black-crimson Phoenix fire erupted around him.

Zee was already there.

No full Crimson Black Abyss Phoenix transformation.

No need.

Vampire speed.

Dragon force.

Crimson Sovereign.

One fist struck Victor across the mouth.

Victor blocked the second.

Witchcraft cracked between them.

“Hold.”

“Break.”

The commands collided.

Scarlet-black fire surged.

Zee drove a knee into Victor's ribs.

Victor answered with a Phoenix blast that forced Zee backward.

Zareth moved.

Zee snapped:

“No.”

Zareth stopped.

Barely.

This was theirs.

For now.

Victor rose.

Blood at his mouth.

“You can kill me again.”

Zee advanced.

“I intend to.”

Victor wiped the blood away.

“And then I will wake up again.”

Zee stopped.

Only for a second.

Then hit him again.

Victor slammed into the wall.

“That did not sound convincing.”

Zee followed.

“You have died twice.”

“Yes.”

“By me.”

“Yes.”

“And you keep coming back.”

“Yes.”

Zee grabbed him by the throat.

Victor did not struggle.

Much.

“You are beginning to understand.”

Zee's grip tightened.

Victor's eyes darkened.

“If you crush my throat, I will die.”

“Good.”

“And then I will resurrect.”

Zee stared at him.

Victor continued:

“And come back.”

Ner folded his arms.

“This is deeply irritating.”

Rez arrived beside him.

“For once, I agree with Victor on something.”

Zee looked toward Rez.

Rez lifted both hands.

“Only the factual part.”

Zee looked back at Victor.

His fingers remained around his throat.

One twist.

That would do it.

Maybe.

Again.

Then what?

Another corpse.

Another resurrection.

Another return.

Another argument.

Another murder.

Victor's face was already beginning to look annoyingly patient.

Zee released him so suddenly Victor almost fell.

Everyone noticed.

That mattered.

The first time.

Zee had deliberately chosen not to kill him.

Not mercy.

Not forgiveness.

Efficiency.

Victor rubbed his throat.

“That was almost mature.”

Zee's eyes sharpened.

“Do not ruin it.”

Fair.

---

Zee stepped back.

His voice changed.

King now.

Not son.

“You are alive because killing you has become inconvenient.”

Victor nodded once.

“Understood.”

“No.”

Zee moved closer.

“You do not understand yet.”

Scarlet-black fire rose along Zee's wings.

Not transformation.

Warning.

“You do not approach Zayrlen.”

Victor's face changed slightly.

Zee caught it.

“Without permission from me or Ner.”

Ner spoke immediately:

“Preferably never.”

Victor glanced toward him.

Ner did not blink.

Zee continued.

“You do not test me.”

Victor nodded.

“You do not test Darkheart.”

Another nod.

“You do not test my family.”

“Yes.”

“You do not create false attacks.”

“Yes.”

“You do not use my son in any plan, lesson, demonstration, question, experiment, threat, or fucking metaphor.”

That one landed.

Victor's expression hardened with something close to shame.

“Yes.”

Zee stepped closer until only inches separated them.

“If you threaten my people again, I will kill you even if I have to do it every week for the next century.”

Victor looked at him.

“I believe you.”

“Good.”

Silence.

Then Victor said:

“I did not come to threaten anyone.”

Zee's face remained cold.

“Then do not.”

---

A guard near the gate looked between them.

“Majesty?”

Zee turned.

The poor man immediately regretted speaking.

“What?”

“Is he…”

The guard looked at Victor.

Then back at Zee.

“Allowed inside?”

Zee stared at Victor.

Victor waited.

Ner waited.

Rez looked suspiciously entertained.

Zareth was not entertained at all.

Zee exhaled through his nose.

“Yes.”

Victor started forward.

Zee pointed at him.

“Do not make me regret that before dinner.”

Victor stopped.

Then continued more slowly.

Darkheart watched its former King walk into the territory of the son he had once tried to erase.

Alive.

Again.

And Zee watched him like reality itself had personally decided to become annoying.

Victor crossed the gate.

No crown.

No authority.

No welcome.

Just survival.

That was enough to make the truth unavoidable.

Victor was back.

---

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Seven

## The Only Parent Left

Victor hated what Zee had done to Darkheart.

Then he hated that he did not entirely hate it.

The first thing he noticed was noise.

People spoke freely.

Too freely.

Witches argued with guards.

Vampires laughed near the fountain.

Two Wolves were openly criticizing a road decision while a Darkheart official wrote down complaints instead of threatening them.

A hybrid child ran past Victor without bowing.

Victor turned.

The child did not even notice him.

He looked toward Zee.

Zee noticed.

“What?”

“Your people have no discipline.”

“They are not yours.”

Victor's jaw tightened.

Zee kept walking.

That answer explained more than Victor wanted.

---

They crossed the main courtyard.

Kael stood with Amara near a supply table.

Tessa was arguing with a soldier about healing protocol.

Rhyven sat on a wall sharpening a blade.

Elias passed with three different ledgers.

No one bowed when Zee approached.

Not immediately.

Some nodded.

One guard called:

“King.”

Zee responded:

“What?”

The guard lifted a broken gate hinge.

“This is your fault.”

Zee looked at it.

“How?”

“You broke it last week.”

“I broke several things last week.”

Victor stared.

The guard stared back at Zee.

“Exactly.”

Zee sighed.

“Send it to the smiths.”

“Already did.”

“Then why are you telling me?”

“So you know.”

Zee looked toward Victor.

“See?”

Victor did not.

Not yet.

The guard walked away.

Alive.

Unpunished.

Victor watched him go.

“Your subjects speak to you like that.”

“My people.”

Victor looked at him.

Zee did not correct himself.

That was the point.

---

Later, Victor watched Rez argue with Zee over trade routes.

Actually argue.

No lowered voice.

No careful phrasing.

No fear.

“You are wrong,” Rez said.

Zee looked at him.

“About?”

“The western route.”

“No.”

“Yes.”

“No.”

Rez unfolded a map.

“Look.”

“I have.”

“Then look better.”

Victor waited for the room to become dangerous.

It did not.

Zee leaned over the map.

Zareth entered halfway through and immediately disagreed with both of them.

Elias joined and somehow made the argument worse.

Ner passed through carrying Zayrlen and said:

“All of you sound stupid.”

No one died.

Victor found that deeply unsettling.

Zee looked toward him.

“You are staring.”

“I am observing.”

“You did enough of that recently.”

Victor looked away.

Fair.

---

The first real conversation happened that evening.

No council.

No guards.

No battle.

Just Zee and Victor on a balcony overlooking the lower city.

Victor stood at one end.

Zee at the other.

Distance chosen deliberately.

The silence lasted long enough to become hostile.

Victor spoke first.

“You still tap your thumb when you are angry.”

Zee looked down at his hand.

He was.

He stopped immediately.

Victor almost smiled.

Zee noticed.

“Do not.”

“You did it as a child.”

“I was a child.”

“You would do it whenever Aurelia told you no.”

Zee's face changed.

Barely.

Victor continued before he could stop himself.

“You would sit beneath the eastern staircase afterward and refuse to speak to anyone.”

Zee looked toward him.

“How old?”

“Four.”

The answer came too quickly to be invented.

Zee's expression tightened.

Nobody alive remembered that.

Not like this.

Aurelia would have.

Aurelia was gone.

That thought arrived without invitation.

Zee hated it.

Victor saw something shift and made the mistake of stepping closer.

Zee's eyes snapped toward him.

“Stay there.”

Victor stopped.

“I was only—”

“I know.”

Silence.

Victor remained where he was.

Good.

---

Zee looked back over the city.

“You do not get to come back and act like my father.”

Victor's jaw tightened.

“I am your father.”

“Biologically.”

“Yes.”

“Historically.”

Victor looked at him.

Zee continued.

“Those are not the same as being one.”

That landed harder.

Victor did not argue.

Unexpected.

Zee glanced over.

“You agree?”

“I know what I did.”

“That is not the same as understanding it.”

“No.”

Victor looked toward Darkheart.

“I am beginning to.”

Zee laughed once.

“Convenient timing.”

Victor's old pride surfaced.

“I died.”

“You murdered me first.”

“I know.”

“You tried to control everything you feared.”

“I know.”

“You made my mother spend years protecting me from you.”

Victor's expression hardened.

Not anger at Zee.

Pain.

“Aurelia chose you.”

“She was supposed to.”

“She chose you over me.”

Zee looked at him.

“She chose the child you tried to kill.”

Silence.

Victor had no answer.

Good.

---

Then he said something smaller.

“You hated milk.”

Zee blinked.

“What?”

“As a child.”

Victor looked almost irritated by the memory.

“You would drink anything else. Water. fruit juice. broth. But if Aurelia handed you milk, you would stare at the cup like it had insulted your bloodline.”

Zee stared.

“That is not true.”

“It is.”

“I do not remember that.”

“I do.”

That was the problem.

Victor remembered.

Before King.

Before gods.

Before hybrids.

Before Dragon awakening.

Before Crimson Sovereign.

Before the First Natural Abysscin.

Before Zee had become anything the world knew.

Victor remembered a four-year-old hiding under stairs because Aurelia said no.

Zee looked away.

He hated how much that mattered.

---

Ner found them eventually.

He did not interrupt immediately.

He looked at Victor.

Then Zee.

Then said:

“Zayrlen is awake.”

Zee turned instantly.

That ended the conversation.

Victor followed.

Not close.

He had learned at least one thing.

---

The nursery became dangerous the second Victor entered the doorway.

Ner stood beside the cradle.

Zee moved in front of him automatically.

Not dramatic.

Habit.

Victor stopped several feet inside.

Zayrlen lay awake.

Two months old.

Crimson-Gold eyes open.

Tiny hands moving.

No Phoenix power.

No impossible manifestation.

Just baby.

Victor looked at him.

Really looked.

No test.

No spell.

No plan.

The child's Dragon-Witch-Wolf nature sat quietly beneath the surface.

Impossible blood.

Yet Zee had never feared him.

Victor understood the difference again.

Deeper now.

Zayrlen turned his head.

Saw Victor.

Stared.

Victor stared back.

Something about familiar blood perhaps.

Nothing more.

Zee watched every breath.

Victor took one step.

“No.”

Victor stopped.

“I moved one foot.”

Zee pointed.

“Move it back.”

Victor looked toward Ner.

Ner said:

“You heard him.”

Victor moved back.

Zayrlen blinked.

Victor stared at the baby again.

A minute later he adjusted his stance slightly.

Zee looked over.

“Victor.”

“I am standing.”

“Stand farther away.”

Rez, leaning against the wall near the doorway, turned his face to hide a smile.

Victor noticed.

“I see why you like him.”

Rez answered:

“I have known him longer than you have lately.”

That one hurt.

Victor said nothing.

---

Zayrlen made a small sound.

Victor's attention snapped back.

Not fear.

Interest.

Then another sound.

Tiny.

Almost a coo.

Victor's expression changed.

He stepped forward without thinking.

Zee's voice sharpened.

“No.”

Victor stopped immediately this time.

No argument.

That mattered.

He looked at Zee.

Then Ner.

Then the child.

The distance between him and Zayrlen suddenly felt much larger than the room.

He had earned every inch.

Victor understood that.

Zee trusted Rez near the baby.

Zareth.

Elias.

Kael.

Tessa.

Amara.

Rhyven.

All of them.

Victor—

his own father—

stood at the edge of the room like an armed stranger.

Because he was.

Blood did not erase history.

Victor looked down.

For once, no defense came.

---

Zee lifted Zayrlen.

The baby settled immediately.

Victor watched how automatic it was.

Support head.

Check breathing.

Adjust against chest.

Listen.

Zee did not even know he was doing half of it.

Zayrlen grabbed his shirt.

Victor said quietly:

“He trusts you.”

Zee looked over.

“He should.”

Victor nodded.

“Yes.”

Simple.

Painful.

True.

---

Later, when Zayrlen slept, Victor found himself still in Darkheart.

That surprised him.

It surprised Zee more.

Zee passed him in the hall.

Stopped.

“Why are you still here?”

Victor looked at him.

“You said I could remain.”

“I said killing you was currently useless.”

“Which resulted in me remaining.”

Zee stared.

Victor waited.

Zee finally said:

“You are exhausting.”

Victor almost smiled.

“Also hereditary.”

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“Do not start.”

Victor did smile this time.

Zee walked away.

No murder attempt.

Progress.

Tiny.

Probably temporary.

Still real.

---

That night, Victor stood alone in a guest chamber he had not been offered so much as assigned under supervision.

He looked out over Darkheart.

The kingdom was louder than his.

Messier.

Freer.

More dangerous in some ways.

More loyal in others.

People loved Zee.

Not because he had trained them to fear displeasing him.

Because they chose him.

Victor understood that reluctantly.

Zee had become a different King.

A different father.

A different creature entirely.

The First Natural Abysscin.

And somehow still the same impossible child who once hid under a staircase after Aurelia told him no.

That contradiction sat painfully inside Victor.

---

Across the keep, Zee sat with Zayrlen asleep against his chest.

Ner beside him.

No Victor.

Good.

Zee looked toward the window.

Somewhere in the same building, his father was alive.

Again.

Aurelia was not.

That truth arrived quietly.

He did not say it.

Did not want it.

Could not remove it.

Victor was the only parent left who remembered Zee before everything.

That did not forgive murder.

Did not restore trust.

Did not make him safe.

It simply existed.

Zee looked down at Zayrlen.

Tiny hand curled against his chest.

Then he muttered:

“This family is getting ridiculous.”

Ner smiled.

“You made most of it.”

“Not him.”

“Unfortunately.”

Zee looked toward the hallway where Victor had disappeared.

For one second, irritation almost became something else.

He killed the thought before it formed.

Not tonight.

The new reality was already difficult enough.

Victor Darkheart was alive.

Still unwelcome.

Still dangerous.

Still unforgiven.

Still his father.

And for the first time in decades—

Zee had one parent left.

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Eight

## The First Form

Time finally moved.

Not in one clean jump.

Not in birthdays lined neatly across a page.

It moved in smaller things.

Zayrlen learning how to sit without falling sideways.

Then learning how to stand.

Then discovering that standing was not nearly as interesting as running.

Too early.

Too fast.

Usually directly toward something breakable.

---

His first steps happened in the southern hall.

Ner stood three feet away.

Zee stood four.

Zayrlen looked between them.

Tiny.

Unsteady.

Determined.

Ner held out both hands.

“Come here.”

Zayrlen took one step.

Wobbled.

Stopped.

Zee smiled.

“Good.”

Zayrlen looked toward him instead.

Ner immediately frowned.

“No.”

Zee looked innocent.

“I did nothing.”

“You exist.”

“That sounds personal.”

Zayrlen took another step.

Then another.

Straight toward Zee.

Ner stared.

“He was supposed to come to me.”

Zee crouched.

“He made a choice.”

“He is barely walking.”

“Still counts.”

Zayrlen stumbled the last step.

Zee caught him instantly.

Lifted him.

Zayrlen laughed.

That was the end of walking practice.

At least according to Zee.

Ner folded his arms.

“You are supposed to put him back down.”

“He walked.”

“Yes.”

“That sounds exhausting.”

“He needs practice.”

Zee looked at Zayrlen.

Zayrlen grabbed one of his horns.

Zee sighed.

“No.”

The child pulled.

Ner smiled.

“Looks like he disagrees.”

---

By the time Zayrlen learned to speak in full little sentences, Darkheart had accepted one important fact.

The Prince had opinions.

Many.

Most of them inconvenient.

He liked climbing.

He liked sitting on Zee's shoulders.

He liked following Rhyven around because Rhyven could become a Wolf.

He liked Zareth because Zareth was huge when transformed.

He liked Rez because Rez let him touch almost anything in Vesper that was not actively on fire.

He liked Elias because Elias answered questions seriously.

He liked Kael because Kael cheated at games.

He liked Amara because she did not.

He liked Tessa until she brought medicine.

Then he considered her an enemy of the state.

Victor—

was complicated.

Zayrlen had grown up knowing him as the older man who appeared often enough to become familiar but not trusted enough to ever be left alone with him.

Victor never complained about that in front of the child.

Mostly.

Zee still watched.

Always.

Years had not erased what Victor did.

They had only made murder less practical.

---

Zayrlen's Witch Mana appeared naturally.

Not during a lesson.

During breakfast.

He wanted fruit.

The bowl was across the table.

Ner said:

“Ask.”

Zayrlen reached.

Nothing happened.

He frowned harder.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana sparked around his fingers.

The bowl launched across the table.

Zee caught it before it hit Victor in the face.

Silence.

Zayrlen stared.

Victor looked toward Zee.

Zee looked at the bowl.

Then at his son.

“Did you do that?”

Zayrlen smiled.

“Yes.”

Ner closed his eyes.

“That is not encouragement.”

Zee set the bowl down.

“I asked a question.”

“You sounded proud.”

“I am allowed to be proud.”

“He almost hit Victor.”

Victor said:

“I have survived worse.”

Zee looked at him.

“Unfortunately.”

Victor sighed.

Zayrlen laughed.

---

The magic became more frequent after that.

Crimson-and-Gold Witch Mana.

His own.

Not Ner’s exact Pure Gold.

Not Zee’s Crimson Witch expression.

Distinct.

Sometimes it lifted toys.

Sometimes it shut doors.

Sometimes it cracked glasses when his temper got ahead of him.

Once it turned every candle in the nursery Crimson-and-Gold because Zayrlen wanted “pretty fire.”

Zee stared at the room.

Ner stared at Zayrlen.

Zayrlen looked delighted.

Victor, standing at the doorway, said:

“He gets that from you.”

Zee turned.

“Leave.”

“I meant the flair.”

“Leave farther.”

---

Wolf instincts came differently.

Quietly at first.

Zayrlen could hear footsteps before ordinary children should.

He recognized family by scent.

He sometimes growled when annoyed.

Not consciously.

The first time he did it at Victor, Zee nearly smiled himself sick.

Victor noticed.

“You are enjoying this.”

“No.”

“You are.”

Zayrlen growled again.

Zee picked him up.

“My baby has excellent instincts.”

Victor stared.

Ner laughed from across the room.

---

Dragon traits appeared in flashes.

Heat when upset.

Temporary scales along his shoulders.

A strange weight behind his presence.

Strength wildly disproportionate to his size.

Once, at maybe four years old, Zayrlen pulled a heavy training chest across the floor because it was “in the way.”

Kael watched.

Then looked at Zee.

“He should not be able to do that.”

Zee looked at the chest.

Then at Zayrlen.

“Apparently he disagrees.”

The Crimson Demonic Dragon inside Zee sometimes reacted to his son.

Not alarm.

Recognition.

Blood.

Something old.

Something growing.

Zareth noticed too.

But never pushed.

Never called it awakening.

Never predicted when anything would happen.

It simply existed.

Waiting.

---

Zayrlen remained a child.

That mattered more than the power.

He scraped his knee running through the western courtyard and came directly to Zee like he had been mortally wounded.

Zee abandoned a council discussion instantly.

Rez watched him go.

Victor looked confused.

“It is a scraped knee.”

Zee turned while lifting Zayrlen.

“Correct.”

“He is not dying.”

“I know.”

“You left a council.”

“My son is bleeding.”

“One drop.”

Zee looked down.

There were technically three.

Victor gave up.

Ner arrived with a cloth.

“He is fine.”

Zee was already inspecting the knee.

“I know.”

Zayrlen sniffed.

“It hurts.”

Zee's entire face softened.

“I know, baby.”

Victor looked away.

That word still did something uncomfortable to him.

Years later, it still would.

---

The first transformation happened in the rain.

Zayrlen was still young.

Old enough to run fast.

Young enough that he still slept better if one of his fathers stayed until he drifted off.

He had been playing in the lower gardens with Rhyven.

Not training.

Playing.

Rhyven had shifted into his Phoenix-Wolf form because Zayrlen begged.

The child chased him between the hedges.

Laughing.

Wet.

Mud on his clothes.

Zee watched from beneath a stone arch with Ner beside him.

Victor remained farther back.

Exactly where he had learned to remain.

Rhyven darted left.

Zayrlen followed.

Then slipped.

Not badly.

But the sudden movement triggered something.

Wolf instinct.

Adrenaline.

Excitement.

Frustration.

All at once.

Zayrlen hit the wet ground.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana burst outward.

Rhyven stopped.

Zee straightened.

Ner whispered:

“Zee.”

“I see it.”

The child pushed himself up.

Then froze.

His heartbeat changed.

Wolf pressure rolled across the garden.

Zayrlen looked at his hands.

“Dad?”

Fur appeared first.

Crimson.

Deep.

Then Gold streaked through it.

His body shifted rapidly.

Bones moving.

Spine changing.

Hands becoming paws.

Clothing tearing loose beneath the transformation.

Zayrlen cried out.

Zee moved one step forward.

Then stopped.

Not because he was afraid.

Because forcing contact during an uncontrolled first transformation could make panic worse.

Ner grabbed his arm.

“Let him finish.”

Zee looked like he hated that sentence.

Still—

he stayed.

For three seconds.

Then the transformation completed.

---

A Wolf stood in the rain.

Four-legged.

Crimson and Gold.

Not black.

No horns.

No wings.

No Dragon tail.

No scales.

No Phoenix fire.

Wolf.

True.

Beautiful.

The coat was deep Crimson with Gold running through it in natural streaks along the shoulders, chest, flanks, and legs.

Crimson-Gold eyes stared out from a face still unmistakably Zayrlen.

Young.

Powerful.

Confused.

He looked down at his paws.

Then immediately fell over.

Rhyven made a noise suspiciously close to laughter.

Zee looked at him.

Rhyven stopped.

Zayrlen tried standing.

Managed.

Took three steps.

Then every new Wolf sense hit him at once.

Rain.

Mud.

Grass.

Heartbeats.

Blood.

Magic.

People.

Castle stone.

Rhyven.

Ner.

Victor.

Guards.

Everything.

His ears flattened.

He backed up.

Whined.

Zee's expression changed instantly.

“That is enough.”

He stepped into the rain.

Ner did not stop him.

---

Zayrlen saw him.

Or smelled him.

Probably both.

The Wolf froze.

Zee crouched.

No King.

No Abysscin.

No monster.

Just father.

“Hey.”

Zayrlen whined again.

“You are okay.”

The Wolf took one uncertain step.

Then another.

Then suddenly ran.

Straight at Zee.

Fast.

Far too fast for his size.

Zee caught him anyway.

The young Wolf crashed into his chest.

Zee landed on one knee in the mud.

Zayrlen shoved his head under Zee's chin.

Zee wrapped both arms around the Wolf.

“There you are.”

The Wolf trembled.

Ner came closer.

Not touching yet.

“Can he change back?”

Zee looked at the Wolf.

“No idea.”

Victor almost said something.

Zee looked over.

Victor wisely did not.

---

Zayrlen tried.

Nothing.

He made a frustrated sound.

Tried harder.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana sparked.

Nothing changed.

Zee immediately realized the mistake.

“Stop.”

The Wolf looked at him.

“Do not force it.”

Zayrlen whined.

“I know.”

Zee stroked the fur between his ears.

“You do not have to fix anything right now.”

The Wolf settled slightly.

“Just breathe.”

Ner crouched beside them.

“You are still you.”

Zayrlen looked toward him.

Ner smiled.

“Very fluffy you.”

The Wolf sneezed.

Rhyven lost the battle and laughed.

Zayrlen turned and barked at him.

Zee smiled.

“Good.”

Ner stared.

“Do not encourage him.”

“He defended himself.”

“He barked.”

“Still.”

---

They stayed in the garden.

No ritual.

No command.

No forced shift.

Eventually Zayrlen stopped panicking.

He sniffed Zee.

Then Ner.

Then walked in a small circle around them.

Then discovered his tail.

That became a problem.

He spun after it.

Missed.

Tried again.

Zee watched with absolute seriousness.

Victor stared at him.

“You are smiling.”

“No.”

“You are.”

Zee ignored him.

Zayrlen caught his tail.

Fell over.

Ner laughed.

Zee picked him up again.

The Wolf was too large to carry comfortably.

Zee did it anyway.

“Do not start.”

Ner raised both hands.

“I said nothing.”

“You were going to.”

“Yes.”

---

By sunset, Zayrlen's body finally relaxed.

The Wolf form released.

Crimson-and-Gold fur folded away.

Bones shifted back.

A small Human child ended up curled against Zee's chest, exhausted and naked beneath the remains of a cloak.

Zee wrapped him immediately.

Checked his hands.

Arms.

Face.

Breathing.

Heartbeat.

Eyes.

Ner watched.

“He is fine.”

“I know.”

“Then why are you checking him like he fell from a tower?”

“He transformed into a Wolf.”

“Yes.”

“My baby transformed into a Wolf.”

Zayrlen opened one tired eye.

“Dad.”

Zee looked down instantly.

“What?”

“Did I do good?”

That finished him.

Zee's expression softened completely.

“Yes.”

No hesitation.

“You did perfect.”

Ner smiled.

Victor looked away again.

Rhyven grinned.

Zayrlen smiled weakly.

Then fell asleep against Zee.

Zee carried him all the way back to the keep.

Of course he did.

His son had found his first true form.

Crimson and Gold.

Four-legged.

Wolf.

And Zee Darkheart—

First Natural Abysscin.

First Natural Tribrid.

King.

Monster.

Was unbearably proud of his baby.

# Chapter One Hundred Thirty-Nine

## The Boy Behind the Power

The Wolf became easier.

Not easy.

Never immediately.

But easier.

Years moved.

Zayrlen learned how to recognize the first pressure behind his ribs.

How hearing changed before the shift.

How scent sharpened.

How his heartbeat settled into the Wolf rhythm.
