Learned how to let the transformation happen instead of fighting it.

Sometimes.

Other times he still ended up halfway through a hallway because he got angry and suddenly had four paws.

Once, during an argument with Victor, he transformed by accident.

Victor stared at the Crimson-and-Gold Wolf.

The Wolf growled.

Victor looked toward Zee.

“Is this your doing?”

Zee looked innocent.

“I am sitting down.”

Zayrlen barked.

Victor sighed.

“Wonderful.”

---

By the time Zayrlen was old enough to understand what the world thought of his father, Darkheart had become normal to him.

That was the strange part.

People whispered outside the kingdom.

The First Natural Abysscin.

The First Natural Tribrid.

Crimson Sovereign.

Crimson Demonic Dragon.

The King who killed Gods.

The man who destroyed Pyrathis.

The monster who created races.

The Blood Hunter.

Zayrlen heard the titles.

He understood some.

Others sounded ridiculous.

Because the terrifying creature kingdoms warned their children about was the same man who still inspected every bruise Zayrlen came home with.

---

One afternoon, Zayrlen returned from the training yard with a split lip.

He was older now.

Not little.

Still a child.

Old enough to be embarrassed.

Zee saw the blood.

Stopped mid-conversation with Rez.

“What happened?”

Zayrlen kept walking.

“Nothing.”

Zee appeared in front of him.

Vampire speed.

Zayrlen sighed.

“Dad.”

“Who?”

“Nobody.”

“Your lip disagrees.”

“I was sparring.”

“With?”

“Amara.”

Zee looked toward the courtyard.

Amara raised one hand from fifty feet away.

“He started it.”

Zayrlen looked offended.

“You said I could try.”

“I did.”

“You hit me.”

“That is what sparring is.”

Zee looked back at his son.

“Open.”

“No.”

“Zayrlen.”

“I am fine.”

Zee narrowed his eyes.

Zayrlen narrowed his back.

Rez watched with interest.

Then Zayrlen opened his mouth.

Zee checked the injury.

Small.

Already healing.

He nodded.

“Fine.”

Zayrlen wiped his mouth.

“You know I heal.”

“I know.”

“You still check.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

Zee stared like the answer was obvious.

“Because you are mine.”

Zayrlen rolled his eyes.

But smiled while walking away.

Rez looked toward Zee.

“Teddy bear.”

Zee turned.

“Leave.”

---

Zayrlen's Witch Mana grew with him.

Crimson-and-Gold.

Bright.

Dense.

Temperamental when he was younger.

More disciplined as he matured.

He did not cast like Zee.

That became clear early.

Zee favored precise one-word laws.

Zayrlen liked shaping.

He built.

Barriers.

Threads.

Spears.

Moving structures of Crimson-and-Gold Mana that changed shape during use.

His magic felt physical.

Almost architectural.

Ner recognized the precision underneath it.

Zee recognized the instinct to turn magic into something useful immediately.

But the expression belonged to Zayrlen alone.

Once Elias watched him form three floating Mana rings around a training target.

The rings tightened from different angles.

Elias nodded.

“Interesting.”

Zayrlen smiled.

Zee said:

“Do not compliment him too much.”

Zayrlen turned.

“You compliment me all the time.”

“That is different.”

“How?”

“I am your father.”

“That did not answer the question.”

Victor, sitting nearby, said:

“He does that.”

Zee looked toward him.

Victor smiled faintly.

Years had changed some things.

Not everything.

---

Victor had stayed.

Annoyingly.

Repeatedly.

He disappeared for weeks sometimes.

Returned without invitation.

Argued with Zee.

Argued with Ner.

Lost arguments to Rez.

Was threatened by Zareth often enough that it became routine.

But he stayed.

That mattered.

Not enough to erase anything.

Enough that Zayrlen grew up knowing him.

At first:

Victor.

Then occasionally:

Grandfather.

Never forced.

The first time Zayrlen said it, Victor went completely still.

Zee noticed.

Said nothing.

Ner noticed too.

Also said nothing.

Victor recovered badly.

“Do not call me that if you are about to ask for something.”

Zayrlen smiled.

“I was.”

Victor sighed.

“What?”

Zee looked over immediately.

“No.”

Victor frowned.

“He has not even asked.”

“I know.”

Zayrlen laughed.

---

Zayrlen's personality sharpened with age.

He was less brooding than Zee.

More openly expressive.

More willing to laugh.

More curious.

He liked maps.

Not royal borders.

Terrain.

Rivers.

Mountain passes.

Old roads.

He liked understanding how places connected.

He hated sitting through court ceremony.

Loved field reports.

Liked sparring with Amara.

Liked tracking with Rhyven.

Loved arguing magical structure with Elias.

Kael taught him how to cheat at cards.

Ner found out.

Kael denied everything.

Rez made it worse by teaching Zayrlen how to cheat better.

Zee discovered all of them.

No one was sorry.

---

His temper came hot.

Fast.

Not like Zee's coldest rage.

Zayrlen's anger arrived visibly.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana sparking.

Wolf eyes flashing.

Heat rising through the room.

Sometimes scales appeared along his neck or forearms.

He hated being lied to.

Hated seeing people bullied.

Hated being treated like a Prince before being treated like a person.

Once a visiting noble bowed too deeply and called him:

“Future weapon of Darkheart.”

Zayrlen stared.

“I am a person.”

The noble laughed awkwardly.

Zee heard.

The entire room changed temperature.

The noble stopped laughing.

Zayrlen looked toward his father.

“Dad.”

Zee's expression said murder.

Zayrlen shook his head.

“No.”

Zee waited.

Then looked back at the noble.

“Apologize.”

The man did.

Immediately.

Zayrlen accepted.

Zee did not forget.

---

His fears were quieter.

Zayrlen did not fear battle.

He feared losing control.

The first Wolf transformation had left something behind.

Not trauma.

Respect.

He knew his body contained things that could become larger than his intentions.

As he grew stronger, that mattered more.

Sometimes Dragon pressure escaped without warning.

Rooms felt smaller around him.

Candles bent.

Stone warmed.

People noticed.

Zayrlen noticed them noticing.

He did not like that.

One night he asked Zee:

“Did people look at you like that?”

Zee knew exactly what he meant.

“Yes.”

“When you were little?”

“Yes.”

“Did you hate it?”

Zee looked toward him.

“Yes.”

Zayrlen sat beside him on the balcony wall.

Older now.

Legs hanging over the edge.

“Does it stop?”

“No.”

Zayrlen frowned.

Zee continued.

“You stop needing it to.”

That answer sat with him.

---

The Dragon remained the unanswered part.

Scales.

Heat.

Strength.

Pressure.

Durability.

Instinct.

All present.

No form.

No shift.

No wings.

No Dragon body.

Zareth sometimes watched him when the pressure rose.

Never pushed.

One afternoon, Zayrlen caught him.

“What?”

Zareth smiled.

“Nothing.”

“You are staring.”

“I learned from Victor.”

Victor, across the courtyard, looked offended.

Zayrlen frowned.

“Is something wrong with me?”

Zareth's expression changed immediately.

“No.”

“Then what?”

Zareth crouched.

“You have Dragon blood.”

“I know.”

“It is getting louder.”

Zayrlen looked toward Zee.

Zee had felt it too.

His Crimson Demonic Dragon nature responded differently now whenever Zayrlen entered a room angry or excited.

Recognition.

Pressure.

Something approaching.

But Zee gave no prediction.

No schedule.

No promise.

“When?” Zayrlen asked.

Zee answered:

“I do not know.”

“Will it hurt?”

Zee paused.

“I do not know.”

Zayrlen studied him.

“You hate saying that.”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

Zee stared.

Zayrlen smiled and ran.

Ner laughed from nearby.

“He is yours.”

“He is also yours.”

“Unfortunately.”

---

Zayrlen's Wolf form changed as he grew.

Larger.

Faster.

Still Crimson and Gold.

Still unmistakably Wolf.

No Dragon anatomy.

No Phoenix traits.

He became skilled enough to shift during movement.

Not perfect.

Sometimes one paw hit the floor wrong.

Sometimes he overestimated how large he was.

Once he shifted indoors and destroyed a table.

Victor looked at the pieces.

“Your father did worse.”

Zayrlen looked toward Zee.

“How much worse?”

Zee pointed at Victor.

“Do not encourage him.”

Victor smiled.

---

Ner trained Zayrlen differently.

Not combat first.

Control.

Breathing.

Mana flow.

Listening.

Knowing when anger belonged to him and when instinct was amplifying it.

Zayrlen inherited none of Ner's exact Bloodsong.

None of his Pure Gold Mana.

But Ner understood what it meant to contain multiple supernatural natures without letting one erase the person.

That lesson mattered.

“You are not your Wolf,” Ner told him.

Zayrlen nodded.

“You are not your Witchcraft.”

Another nod.

“You are not your Dragon.”

Zayrlen looked down.

Ner tapped his chest.

“They are you.”

Zayrlen looked back up.

That distinction stayed.

Years later, it would save him.

---

Darkheart changed around him too.

Children became friends.

Friends became young fighters, scholars, healers, scouts.

Zayrlen learned which guards would let him sneak through kitchens.

Which Witches hated paperwork.

Which Wolves cheated at races.

Which Vampires pretended not to smile.

He knew Darkheart not as a kingdom he might inherit.

As home.

That mattered more.

---

One evening, Zee returned from a border mission covered in blood that was not his.

Zayrlen met him in the hall.

Older now.

Old enough to know what the blood meant.

He looked at Zee.

“Bad?”

Zee removed one glove.

“Handled.”

Zayrlen nodded.

Then looked at the blood again.

“You kill a lot of people.”

“Yes.”

No lie.

“Are they always bad?”

Zee paused.

Important question.

“Not everyone I have killed deserved it.”

Zayrlen looked surprised.

Zee continued.

“I learned that too late.”

The old Rell scar sat beneath that answer.

Zayrlen listened.

“Now?”

“Now I make sure.”

Zayrlen nodded slowly.

Then asked:

“Would you kill someone for me?”

Zee looked at him.

“Immediately.”

Zayrlen stared.

“That was too fast.”

Ner, entering behind them, laughed.

Zee ignored him.

“You asked.”

“I meant if they hurt me.”

“Yes.”

“What if I started it?”

Zee stopped.

Different question.

“If you started it, then we find out why.”

“And if I was wrong?”

“You answer for being wrong.”

Zayrlen smiled faintly.

“There.”

“What?”

“That sounded like Dad.”

Zee frowned.

“What did the first answer sound like?”

“Monster.”

Zee considered.

“Also Dad.”

Zayrlen laughed.

---

Later that same year, Zayrlen stood alone in the upper courtyard at sunset.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana moved around his hands.

Wolf senses open.

Small Dragon scales along one shoulder.

Nothing dramatic.

Yet.

Zee watched from the arch.

The Crimson Demonic Dragon inside him stirred.

Harder than before.

Zee's eyes narrowed.

Zayrlen turned.

“What?”

“Nothing.”

“You are doing the Zareth thing.”

“I am not.”

“You are staring.”

Zee walked over.

Placed one hand on Zayrlen's shoulder.

The scales were warm.

Too warm.

Not dangerous.

Different.

Something deep inside the boy pressed back against Zee's Dragon nature.

Ancient blood recognizing itself.

Zayrlen frowned.

“Dad?”

Zee removed his hand.

“It is getting stronger.”

“The Dragon?”

“Yes.”

Zayrlen looked toward the castle.

Then back at Zee.

“Do you know when?”

“No.”

“Still hate saying it?”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

Zee grabbed the back of his shirt before he could run.

Zayrlen laughed.

“Dad!”

“You are disrespectful.”

“You raised me.”

“That is not a defense.”

“It is a strong one.”

Zee pulled him close anyway.

Zayrlen complained.

Did not actually try very hard to escape.

Older.

Stronger.

More independent.

Still his son.

Still the same child Zee once carried out of a rain-soaked garden wrapped in a cloak after becoming a Wolf for the first time.

The Dragon remained beneath the surface.

Growing.

Waiting.

And somewhere ahead—

without ritual, warning, or permission—

it would finally decide it had waited long enough.

# Chapter One Hundred Forty

## The Pressure Across the Castle

Years moved again.

Not gently.

Not evenly.

Zayrlen grew.

The little Crimson-and-Gold Wolf that once chased its own tail in the rain became larger.

Sharper.

Faster.

His Human form changed with him.

Childhood softened into adolescence.

His face lengthened.

His shoulders broadened.

His Witch Mana strengthened.

His Wolf control became reliable enough that he could transform without falling over afterward.

Most of the time.

Darkheart stopped seeing a child running through its halls.

It started seeing a young Prince.

Zee did not.

Not entirely.

To Zee, the boy who stood nearly eye-to-eye with him on some days was still somehow the same baby who once grabbed his horn with both hands.

Zayrlen hated when Zee said that.

Zee said it anyway.

---

By his teenage years, Zayrlen had become dangerous.

Not theoretically.

Actually.

His Crimson-and-Gold Mana could crack reinforced Witch wards.

His Wolf form could outrun most ordinary supernatural trackers.

His strength had grown far beyond what anyone expected from his age.

Dragon scales appeared more often now.

Not just during anger.

Sometimes during combat.

Sometimes during stress.

Sometimes for no obvious reason at all.

His body temperature ran hotter.

His presence became heavier.

Some days the Crimson Demonic Dragon inside Zee responded to Zayrlen from rooms away.

Zareth noticed it too.

Never forced it.

Never scheduled anything.

Never tried to make the Dragon emerge.

It would come when it came.

Nobody knew when.

That answer still irritated Zayrlen.

---

He was in his room when it happened.

Alone.

No training.

No battle.

No ritual.

No argument.

Nothing dramatic.

At first.

Zayrlen sat at the edge of his bed reading a field report he had stolen from Rez.

Not technically stolen.

Borrowed without asking.

Which Rez would later insist was theft.

Zayrlen disagreed.

He turned one page.

Then stopped.

Something moved beneath his skin.

He looked down.

A Crimson-and-Gold scale appeared along the back of his hand.

Then another.

Zayrlen frowned.

“Not now.”

The scales spread anyway.

He stood.

Heat filled the room.

Too fast.

His Wolf senses sharpened violently.

His Witch Mana flickered.

The candles blew out.

Then relit Crimson-and-Gold.

Zayrlen looked toward the mirror.

His eyes had changed.

Crimson-Gold.

Brighter.

Slit.

Dragon.

His heartbeat accelerated.

“Dad?”

Quiet.

No one answered.

He had not called loudly.

Not yet.

He looked down as another line of scales crossed his forearm.

The room creaked.

Then something inside him pushed outward.

Hard.

Zayrlen gasped.

---

Across the castle, Zee was arguing with Victor.

Naturally.

Victor had somehow decided that Darkheart’s western defense towers were aesthetically offensive.

Zee had informed him that nobody cared.

Victor had informed Zee that architecture mattered.

Zee had informed Victor that he had been dead for years and had missed his opportunity to file complaints.

Rez was laughing.

Ner was pretending not to.

Then Zee felt it.

Small.

A pressure.

Deep inside Darkheart.

He stopped speaking.

Victor noticed.

“What?”

Zee looked toward the opposite side of the castle.

Nothing obvious.

Darkheart held too many powerful creatures for every pressure shift to mean danger.

Witches.

Vampires.

Wolves.

Hybrids.

Dragons visiting.

Rhyven.

Elias.

Ner.

Zareth, when present.

Zee pushed the sensation aside.

“Nothing.”

Victor stared.

“You stopped insulting me.”

“Do not get used to it.”

Rez smiled.

Then the pressure grew.

Fast.

The glass in the council chamber trembled.

Everyone stopped.

Ner looked up.

Pure Gold Mana reacted.

Victor's expression changed.

“That is not nothing.”

Zee was already standing.

The pressure doubled.

Then tripled.

A ward somewhere deep in the castle activated.

Another answered.

Windows shook.

Stone groaned.

Supernatural heartbeats throughout Darkheart accelerated.

Zee's Vampire hearing sharpened.

Wolf instincts surged.

Witch Mana rose automatically.

Then the Crimson Demonic Dragon inside him reacted so violently that black-crimson scales flashed across his throat.

Zee froze.

Not fear.

Recognition.

Blood.

His blood.

His son's blood.

His head snapped toward the far side of the keep.

“Zayrlen.”

Then Zee disappeared.

---

Vampire speed tore through the castle.

No announcement.

No guard escort.

No strategy.

Nothing else mattered.

Zee crossed two corridors.

One stairwell.

A balcony.

Another hall.

Every step closer made the pressure worse.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana leaked beneath doors.

Stone cracked.

Wards bent inward toward one room.

Zayrlen's room.

Zee hit the door.

It exploded off its hinges.

Then he stopped.

For one second.

Because his son was changing.

---

Zayrlen stood in the center of the room.

Barely.

Crimson-and-Gold scales covered one arm completely.

Half his chest.

His neck.

Part of his face.

Claws had emerged.

Not Wolf claws.

Dragon.

Larger.

Curved.

His back arched.

Bones shifted beneath the skin.

His breathing came too fast.

Crimson-and-Gold Witch Mana flooded the room without direction.

The Wolf inside him reacted badly.

Instinct fighting instinct.

One true form already known.

Another trying to emerge.

Zayrlen looked at Zee.

And for perhaps the first time in years—

he looked young.

Scared.

“Dad.”

Zee crossed the room.

The Dragon pressure hit him hard enough to slow even him.

Furniture shattered behind Zayrlen.

A window cracked.

Gold light flashed beneath Crimson scales.

Zayrlen grabbed his own arm.

“I can't stop it.”

Zee reached him.

“Look at me.”

“I am trying.”

“No.”

Zee caught his face carefully between both hands.

Dragon heat burned against Zee's palms.

Did not matter.

“Look at me.”

Zayrlen's Crimson-Gold eyes found his.

“I can't stop it.”

Zee heard the panic.

Not Prince.

Not fighter.

Son.

That changed everything.

Zee lowered his voice.

“Then stop trying.”

Zayrlen stared.

“What?”

The room shook again.

His shoulder shifted violently.

He cried out.

Zee stayed close.

“Stop fighting it.”

“It hurts.”

“I know.”

“You do not know.”

That hit.

Because Zayrlen was right.

Zee had Dragon blood.

Real.

Biological.

Awakened.

Evolved into the Crimson Demonic Dragon.

But Zee had never become a true Dragon.

Never had a full Dragon body.

Never experienced this.

He could not say:

Do what I do.

He had nothing to demonstrate.

So he did the only thing left.

He stayed.

---

Zayrlen's back bowed again.

More scales erupted.

The room filled with a low Dragon growl that did not come from his throat alone.

Zee held him steady.

“Listen to me.”

“I am.”

“No. You are listening to the pain.”

Zayrlen clenched his jaw.

“The Dragon is not attacking you.”

Another shift.

Zayrlen nearly dropped.

Zee caught him.

“It feels like it.”

“I know.”

“You said you didn't.”

“I do not know the transformation.”

Zee's voice remained steady.

“But I know you.”

Zayrlen looked at him.

That landed.

Zee continued.

“You learned this with the Wolf.”

Zayrlen's breathing hitched.

“When you fought the Wolf, you panicked.”

“I was a kid.”

“You are still my kid.”

“Dad.”

“Not the point.”

Despite everything, Zayrlen almost laughed.

Good.

Zee saw it.

Held on.

“The Dragon is not something trying to take you.”

Zayrlen's claws dug into the floor.

“It is you.”

Silence.

The pressure surged.

Zee moved closer.

“So stop trying to beat yourself.”

Zayrlen stared.

Fear.

Pain.

Understanding beginning.

“What if I cannot come back?”

“You will.”

“You do not know that.”

“No.”

Zee did not lie.

“Then how—”

“Because if you cannot, I will stay until you can.”

That silenced him.

Zee's hands remained against his face.

“However long it takes.”

Zayrlen's eyes burned.

Zee spoke softly.

“Let go.”

---

Zayrlen closed his eyes.

Stopped resisting.

The change became violent.

But different.

Not war anymore.

Release.

Crimson-and-Gold light erupted through the room.

Zee stepped back only because Zayrlen's body needed space.

His spine lengthened.

Human shoulders broadened into Dragon structure.

Arms extended.

Hands became massive forelimbs.

Claws tore through stone.

Wings burst outward.

Real Dragon wings.

Crimson membrane threaded with Gold.

No Phoenix flame.

No Phoenix feathers.

The walls cracked.

The ceiling groaned.

Zee raised one hand.

“Hold.”

Witchcraft reinforced the room long enough.

Not to stop Zayrlen.

To give him room to become himself.

His neck lengthened.

Jaw shifted.

Teeth became Dragon fangs.

A tail formed behind him.

True Dragon anatomy.

Nothing borrowed from Zareth.

Nothing demonic.

Nothing Phoenix.

Crimson-and-Gold scales spread across an enormous body.

The transformation kept growing.

And growing.

And growing.

Zee stared.

Then smiled.

Pride hit harder than fear ever could.

---

A true Dragon filled what remained of Zayrlen's chamber.

Young.

Enormous.

Majestic.

Crimson and Gold.

The scales carried deep Crimson across the body with brilliant Gold along the chest, face, wing ridges, and limbs.

Crimson-Gold eyes opened.

Massive wings struggled for space.

His tail knocked over what remained of a table.

Zayrlen looked down at himself.

Then immediately panicked again.

A Dragon sound shook the entire room.

Zee stepped closer.

“Hey.”

The Dragon froze.

Zee looked up at his son.

Huge.

Powerful enough to terrify kingdoms someday.

Still his baby.

“You did it.”

Zayrlen lowered his head.

Carefully.

Zee put one hand against the Dragon's snout.

Heat.

Blood recognition.

Family.

The Crimson Demonic Dragon inside Zee responded so strongly his own eyes flashed.

No jealousy.

No sadness.

Nothing but pride.

“My baby is a Dragon.”

Zayrlen made a sound that was probably intended as:

Dad.

It came out as a thunderous rumble.

Zee smiled.

“Yeah.”

The Dragon nudged him.

Too hard.

Zee slid three feet.

He stared.

Zayrlen froze.

Zee looked offended.

“Control yourself.”

The Dragon made another low sound.

Zee narrowed his eyes.

“You are laughing.”

Zayrlen absolutely was.

---

Nobody else entered.

Not yet.

They felt it.

Everyone in Darkheart did.

Zareth, miles away in Drakonis, felt Zee's emotional explosion through the Dragon Soul Link but did not see the transformation itself.

Victor stood in the damaged council chamber staring toward the far tower.

Rez looked at Ner.

Ner already knew.

“That is him.”

Rez nodded.

“No one goes.”

Victor looked toward them.

“Why?”

Ner answered:

“Because Zee is already there.”

That was enough.

The first moment belonged to father and son.

---

Zayrlen remained in Dragon form for almost an hour.

At first he could barely move without breaking something.

Then he learned how to fold his wings.

Mostly.

How to shift his weight.

How not to destroy the floor.

Eventually the pressure began easing.

Zee stayed beside him the entire time.

No lesson plan.

No lecture.

Just presence.

When Zayrlen finally tried changing back, Zee said:

“Do not force it.”

The Dragon looked at him.

“You know what happened last time.”

Zayrlen huffed hot air directly into Zee's face.

Zee stared.

“Disrespectful in every form.”

Then the Dragon body began to fold.

Crimson-and-Gold light pulled inward.

Wings vanished.

Tail shortened.

Scales receded.

Bones returned.

And suddenly a teenage Zayrlen collapsed forward.

Zee caught him before he touched the ground.

Immediately.

Of course.

---

“Dad, I am fine.”

“No.”

“I am.”

Zee grabbed his face.

Checked his eyes.

“Dad.”

His breathing.

Heartbeat.

Hands.

Arms.

Shoulders.

Zayrlen groaned.

“I just became a Dragon and you are checking me like I fell down stairs.”

“You became a Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“My point.”

“That does not make sense.”

Zee touched his forehead.

Zayrlen pushed his hand away.

“Stop.”

“No.”

“I am not five.”

“Unrelated.”

Zayrlen stared.

Then smiled despite himself.

Zee pulled him into a hug.

Teenager.

Dragon.

Prince.

Did not matter.

Zayrlen hugged him back.

For a few seconds, neither said anything.

Then Zee whispered:

“You did good.”

Zayrlen closed his eyes.

“Yeah?”

“Yes.”

That mattered more than everything else.

---

# Chapter One Hundred Forty-One

## The Dragon in His Blood

The castle found out twenty minutes later.

Mostly because Zayrlen's room no longer had a wall.

That made secrecy difficult.

Rez arrived first.

Stopped outside.

Looked at the destruction.

Then at Zee.

Then at Zayrlen.

“What happened?”

Zayrlen answered:

“I became a Dragon.”

Rez looked at the missing wall.

“I gathered that.”

Ner arrived next.

He saw Zayrlen.

Ignored the room.

Crossed directly to his son.

“You okay?”

“Yes.”

Ner hugged him.

Zayrlen accepted that one with less complaining.

Then Ner pulled back.

“Did it hurt?”

“A lot.”

Zee's expression changed.

Ner noticed.

“Did you know what to do?”

Zee answered before Zayrlen could.

“No.”

Zayrlen looked toward him.

“But he stayed.”

Ner softened.

“That sounds like him.”

Zee looked away.

Uncomfortable.

Good.

---

Victor arrived.

Stopped at the doorway.

Looked at the broken room.

Then at Zayrlen.

Then at Zee.

“You let him destroy an entire chamber.”

Zee stared.

“He transformed into a Dragon.”

“Yes.”

“First time.”

“Yes.”

“What did you want me to do? Ask him to be smaller?”

Victor opened his mouth.

Closed it.

Fair.

Zayrlen smiled.

Victor noticed.

“You find this amusing.”

“Yes.”

Victor looked toward Zee.

“He definitely gets that from you.”

Zee folded his arms.

“Careful.”

---

Zareth arrived later.

He did not pretend to be calm.

The moment he saw Zayrlen, his Teal-and-Gold Dragon Mana reacted.

He stopped.

Then smiled.

Wide.

“You did it.”

Zayrlen nodded.

“Apparently.”

Zareth looked toward Zee.

“You saw?”

“Yes.”

“First?”

“Yes.”

Only.

Zareth understood immediately.

No jealousy.

No offense.

Good.

“That was yours.”

Zee nodded.

Zayrlen looked between them.

“You are being weird.”

Zareth laughed.

Then crouched slightly.

“Show me.”

Zayrlen's expression changed.

“No.”

Zareth blinked.

“What?”

“I cannot just do it again.”

“Why not?”

“Because I do not know how.”

Good.

Reality.

Awakening was not mastery.

Zareth's expression softened.

“Then do not.”

No pressure.

No scheduled transformation.

No ritual.

The Dragon would become controllable with time.

---

That time came gradually.

Not instantly.

The next shift happened three weeks later.

By accident again.

Zayrlen sneezed.

Nobody ever let him forget that.

He was standing in the eastern training yard with Amara when Dragon pressure surged.

He tried stopping it.

Remembered Zee's words.

Did not fight.

Shifted halfway.

Then lost it.

Human again.

Amara stared.

Zayrlen stared back.

“If you tell anyone—”

Rhyven was already laughing from across the yard.

Too late.

---

The third transformation worked.

Mostly.

He chose it.

No panic.

No tearing through a bedroom.

The true Crimson-and-Gold Dragon emerged in an open field beyond the castle.

This time everyone saw.

Zee stood with Ner.

Zareth beside them.

Rez.

Victor.

Elias.

Kael.

Tessa.

Amara.

Rhyven.

Family.

The Dragon opened his wings.

Enormous.

Young.

Crimson and Gold burning beneath sunlight.

Darkheart soldiers along the wall stopped what they were doing.

Some stared.

Some cheered.

Zee said nothing.

Ner looked toward him.

“You are doing the face.”

“What face?”

“The proud one.”

“I have no proud face.”

Victor said:

“You absolutely do.”

Zee looked at him.

Victor smiled.

“Do not kill me. We already established how pointless that is.”

Zee sighed.

Progress.

Unfortunately.

---

Zayrlen landed badly.

Very badly.

The ground shook.

One wing hit dirt.

His tail took out a training post.

Silence.

Then Rez started laughing.

Zayrlen shifted back immediately.

His face burned.

“Not a word.”

Rez could barely breathe.

Zee looked toward him.

“Enough.”

Rez pointed.

“He destroyed the post with his ass.”

Zayrlen looked horrified.

Ner lost the fight and laughed too.

Zee tried not to.

Failed.

Zayrlen stared at his father.

“You too?”

Zee covered his mouth.

“No.”

“You are literally laughing.”

“No.”

“I hate this family.”

Victor nodded.

“Finally something we agree on.”

Zayrlen pointed at him.

“You are part of the problem.”

Victor looked almost pleased.

That was new.

---

The Dragon changed how Zayrlen understood himself.

Not because it replaced the Wolf.

It did not.

The Wolf remained his first true form.

Crimson and Gold.

Fast.

Grounded.

Predatory.

Instinctive.

The Dragon was different.

Massive.

Aerial.

Powerful.

Harder to hide.

Harder to control.

Where the Wolf sharpened the world, the Dragon expanded it.

He could feel distance differently in the air.

Could sense heat beneath stone.

Could hear the pressure of wind around his wings.

Could feel his own body as something built to dominate space.

That frightened him at first.

Then fascinated him.

---

His Witchcraft began adapting around both true forms.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana threaded through Wolf movement.

Not transforming the Wolf into anything else.

Simply his Witch nature working while Wolf.

In Dragon form, Witch structures became enormous.

Barriers large enough to shield buildings.

Mana rings orbiting wings.

Crimson-and-Gold spears forming in the air around him.

Still unstable.

Still young.

Still learning.

But distinctly Zayrlen.

Not Zee.

Not Zareth.

Him.

---

Zee noticed that first.

During one field exercise, Zayrlen shifted into Wolf form instead of Dragon.

Amara tried forcing him toward open terrain.

Zayrlen refused.

He used Wolf speed to disappear between trees.

Then Crimson-and-Gold Witch rings formed around Amara from three different directions.

She broke two.

The third trapped her ankle.

Zayrlen hit from behind.

Human again before impact.

Shoulder into ribs.

Amara rolled.

Recovered.

Smiled.

“Good.”

Zee watched from the ridge.

Rez stood beside him.

“He fights like neither of you.”

“Yes.”

“That bothers you?”

“No.”

Immediate.

Rez looked over.

Zee's expression held something almost fierce.

Pride.

“He should not fight like me.”

That mattered.

Zayrlen needed his own identity.

Zee understood that now.

---

The first real argument about battle came not long after.

Zayrlen stood in Zee's council chamber.

Older.

Stronger.

Still teenage.

“I am ready.”

Zee looked up from a map.

“No.”

Zayrlen's jaw tightened.

Ner, nearby, immediately knew where this was going.

“For what?” Zee asked.

“Field deployment.”

“No.”

“You did not even think.”

“I did.”

“For half a second.”

“That was enough.”

Zayrlen's Dragon heat rose.

“Dad.”

“No.”

“I fight better than half the outer guard.”

“Probably.”

“I can shift.”

“Yes.”

“I can use Witchcraft in both forms.”

“Yes.”

“I have done live exercises.”

“Yes.”

“Then what exactly am I waiting for?”

Zee looked at him.

That was harder.

Because the answer could not be:

Until I stop seeing you as my baby.

That would never happen.

So Zee said:

“Until I trust your judgment more than your power.”

Zayrlen went quiet.

Ner looked toward Zee.

Good answer.

Zee continued.

“You are strong enough.”

Zayrlen listened.

“You are fast enough.”

Another beat.

“You are dangerous enough.”

Zayrlen's eyes sharpened.

“But battle is not proving what you can survive.”

Zee leaned back.

“It is knowing when not to chase.”

Chapter One Hundred Twenty-Eight lived underneath that sentence.

“When to retreat.”

Another.

“When the most dangerous target is bait.”

Another.

“When someone is using you to move the rest of the battlefield.”

Zayrlen looked at his father differently now.

Zee continued.

“If you come with me, I cannot spend the entire fight deciding for you.”

There.

The real standard.

“I need to know that if I turn my back, you will make your own correct choice.”

Zayrlen's anger cooled.

Not gone.

Understood.

“Okay.”

Zee blinked.

That had been easier than expected.

Then Zayrlen said:

“So how do I prove it?”

There he was.

Zee smiled faintly.

“By living long enough to annoy me.”

“I already do that.”

“Excellent progress.”

---

Human form.

Legs hanging over the edge.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana moving lazily around one hand.

Zee sat beside him.

No King.

No lesson.

Zayrlen looked over.

“You still think I am a baby.”

“Yes.”

Zayrlen sighed.

“I am serious.”

“So am I.”

“I can become a Dragon.”

“You are still my baby.”

“I can become a Wolf.”

“Still.”

“I can break castle wards.”

“Still.”

“I am almost as tall as you.”

Zee looked at him.

“Dangerous argument.”

Zayrlen laughed.

Then went quiet.

“Will you ever let me fight with you?”

Zee looked out over Darkheart.

Eventually.

He knew that now.

Zayrlen was not asking to play at violence.

He was growing into someone capable of carrying it.

That terrified some part of Zee.

Not because of what Zayrlen was.

Because Zee knew exactly what battle cost.

He looked at his son.

“Yes.”

Zayrlen turned.

“Really?”

“When you earn it.”

“I will.”

“I know.”

That answer surprised Zayrlen.

Zee looked away before the emotion showed too clearly.

Too late.

Zayrlen smiled.

“Proud face.”

Zee groaned.

“Victor needs to die again.”

Zayrlen laughed.

“No, he was right.”

“That makes it worse.”

---

Below them, Darkheart lived.

Victor argued with Rez somewhere.

Ner was probably looking for both of them.

Zareth had returned to Drakonis.

Rhyven trained near the southern wall.

Elias still worked too late.

Kael cheated at cards.

Amara pretended not to notice.

Tessa threatened everyone equally.

The world kept moving.

The Devouring Choir remained somewhere beyond the stars.

Merek Voss remained unresolved somewhere beyond Darkheart's borders.

Victor remained irritatingly alive.

And Zayrlen Keal Darkheart had become something new without ceasing to be himself.

Witch.

Wolf.

Dragon.

Crimson and Gold.

Still learning.

Still growing.

Not ready for war yet.

But close enough that Zee could finally see the day coming.

And when that day arrived—

Zee would have to learn the hardest thing Teddy Bear Dad had faced yet.

Not how to protect his son from every battle.

How to trust him inside one.

# Chapter One Hundred Forty-Two

## Father and Son

The attack came before sunrise.

Not prophecy.

Not destiny.

Not the Devouring Choir.

Not Merek Voss.

Just people making a stupid decision.

A mercenary force crossed into the southern protection route under cover of fog and hit a Darkheart settlement hard enough to kill before anyone understood what was happening.

Three watch posts burned.

Two supply houses collapsed.

Seven people were already dead by the time the first message reached the castle.

More were trapped inside the settlement.

And the mercenaries had made one thing very clear.

They knew exactly whose protection they were violating.

They did it anyway.

Zee read the report once.

Then stood.

No council vote.

No negotiation.

No second warning.

“They touched my people.”

That was enough.

---

Zayrlen heard about it before Zee reached the lower armory.

He appeared at the doorway already dressed for field movement.

Not ceremonial clothes.

Not Prince.

Fighter.

Zee looked at him.

Really looked.

Teenage now.

Crimson-Gold eyes steady.

No excitement.

No grin.

No desperation to prove something.

Just ready.

Zayrlen asked:

“Can I come?”

The old answer almost came automatically.

No.

It reached Zee’s throat.

Stopped.

Chapter One Hundred Forty-One returned.

Power is not the issue.

Judgment is.

Zee stared at his son.

Ner arrived behind him.

He understood immediately what the silence meant.

Zayrlen waited.

Did not push.

Good.

Zee finally said:

“You are not coming to impress me.”

“I know.”

“You are not chasing kills.”

“I know.”

“You do not use the Dragon just because it is bigger.”

Zayrlen nodded.

“You do not pursue anyone off the field unless the battlefield allows it.”

Another nod.

“You protect civilians before pride.”

“Yes.”

“If I tell you to leave?”

“I leave.”

“If I do not tell you anything?”

Zayrlen paused.

That was the real question.

Then:

“I make the right call.”

Zee held his gaze.

“Show me.”

That was all.

Zayrlen’s expression changed.

Not joy.

Something deeper.

Ner walked to him.

Placed one hand against the side of his face.

“You come back.”

Zayrlen smiled faintly.

“That sounds like an order.”

“It is.”

Then Ner looked toward Zee.

“You too.”

Zee kissed his forehead.

“Always.”

Ner did not believe that answer completely.

He let them go anyway.

Because this mattered.

For both of them.

---

They entered the southern valley with smoke already covering half the settlement.

The mercenaries had chosen their ground well.

Low stone buildings.

Narrow paths.

A river on one side.

Dense woodland on the other.

Civilians trapped between.

Darkheart fighters held the center.

Barely.

The enemy had numbers.

Witch artillery.

Wolf trackers.

Vampire skirmishers.

Heavy enchanted armor.

Not a new species.

Not a grand order.

Just paid killers with enough experience to be dangerous.

And enough arrogance to attack Darkheart civilians.

Zee landed first.

No full Crimson Black Abyss Phoenix form.

He did not need it.

Black-crimson wings spread behind him.

Scarlet blood-fire moved across the feathers.

The battlefield changed the second people recognized him.

Fear moved through the mercenary line.

Then Zayrlen landed beside him.

Human form.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana already shaping into three rotating rings behind his shoulders.

Young.

Still proving himself.

The enemy commander saw him.

Smiled.

Mistake.

---

Zee looked toward his son once.

No speech.

No final warning.

Just:

“Stay alive.”

Zayrlen looked back.

“You too.”

Then they moved.

---

Zee hit the center.

Of course he did.

Crimson Sovereign synchronized instantly.

Vampire speed tore through the first rank.

Wolf instinct identified weak points.

Witch precision broke active enchantments.

Dragon force shattered armor.

Scarlet Phoenix fire moved through the gaps.

Not wild.

Controlled.

Terrifying.

Zayrlen did not follow.

That was the first good choice.

Instead, he went left.

Two mercenaries were moving toward a collapsed supply house where civilians had taken cover.

Crimson-and-Gold threads snapped from Zayrlen’s hands.

One wrapped a sword arm.

Another hooked an ankle.

A third anchored into stone.

He pulled.

Both attackers hit the ground.

A Mana spear formed above him.

Dropped.

One mercenary stopped moving.

The second tried crawling.

Zayrlen shifted.

Wolf.

Crimson and Gold exploded across the dirt.

Four-legged.

Fast.

He closed the distance before the man reached his blade.

Teeth.

Throat.

Done.

Then the Wolf turned away.

No wasted attack.

No mauling after the threat ended.

He immediately moved toward the civilians.

Good.

---

Zee saw it from the corner of his eye.

Kept fighting.

No praise.

Not yet.

Zayrlen shifted back to Human long enough to build a barrier over the trapped doorway.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana locked into an angled lattice.

A Witch blast struck.

The barrier held.

Barely.

Zayrlen grunted.

Blood ran from one nostril.

He adjusted the structure instead of simply pouring more power into it.

Changed the angle.

Redirected the next blast into the ground.

Better.

---

A heavy mercenary charged him.

Dragonbane weapon.

Not for Zayrlen specifically.

Still dangerous.

Zayrlen saw the weapon.

Did not become Dragon.

Too narrow.

Too many civilians.

Instead he dropped low.

Wolf form again.

The blade passed over him.

He came around the attacker’s side.

Shifted Human mid-motion.

Mana ring locked around the man's knee.

Zayrlen twisted.

The knee went the wrong direction.

The mercenary screamed.

Zayrlen struck the throat.

Done.

No flourish.

Good.

---

Zee's battlefield moved differently.

Brutal.

Efficient.

He tore through the center until the mercenary commander realized the obvious.

He could not beat Zee directly.

So he changed the game.

He ran.

Not randomly.

West.

Toward the forest.

Fast enough to look frightened.

Slow enough to be chased.

Zayrlen saw him.

The commander looked back.

Made eye contact.

Then deliberately raised a blood-covered blade.

Taunting.

Zayrlen’s temper flashed.

The man had been giving orders when the civilians died.

Zayrlen knew that.

Wanted him.

Badly.

The commander disappeared into the trees.

Zayrlen took one step.

Stopped.

Something was wrong.

---

Wolf scent caught it first.

Too many bodies where there should have been none.

Not civilians.

Mercenaries.

Hidden.

Downwind.

Waiting.

Then Dragon perception caught the shape of heat beneath the earth.

Runes.

Buried.

Large.

Witch Mana followed.

Threads of hostile magic ran from the treeline back toward the settlement.

Not escape route.

Trigger line.

The commander wanted pursuit.

He wanted someone powerful to chase.

Then the hidden explosives would cut the southern defenders away from the civilians.

Zayrlen looked toward the forest.

The commander was still visible between the trees.

Easy target.

Satisfying target.

Wrong target.

Zayrlen turned away.

No one warned him.

No one ordered him.

He made the choice.

---

The real threat moved at the same time.

Three concealed mercenaries rose from beneath illusion near the wounded.

One carried a detonation trigger.

Another carried a Witch blade.

The third had a crossbow pointed directly toward the Darkheart healers.

Zayrlen moved first.

Crimson-and-Gold barriers snapped into existence around the wounded.

The crossbow fired.

Bolts struck Mana.

Stopped.

Zayrlen shifted Dragon.

Not because it was biggest.

Because he needed the space.

The true Crimson-and-Gold Dragon exploded upward.

Wings filled the smoke.

One beat.

He landed between the hidden attackers and the healers.

Massive body.

Territorial force.

The first mercenary froze.

Zayrlen’s claw came down.

Crushed him.

The second ran.

The Dragon's tail swept low.

Not elegant.

Effective.

Bones broke.

The third raised the trigger.

Zayrlen saw it.

Witchcraft formed while Dragon.

Three Crimson-and-Gold rings appeared around the man's arm.

Elbow.

Wrist.

Hand.

They snapped shut in sequence.

The trigger fell.

Zayrlen caught it in one talon before it touched the ground.

Then looked toward the forest.

The hidden runes never detonated.

The trap failed.

Because he did not take the bait.

---

Zee saw all of it.

The commander fleeing.

Zayrlen almost following.

The pause.

The turn.

The hidden attackers.

The barrier.

The Dragon.

The trigger.

For one second, father and son looked at each other across the battlefield.

Zayrlen still in Dragon form.

Blood on one side of his jaw.

Crimson-and-Gold Mana burning around his wings.

Zee gave him nothing.

No smile.

No praise.

Just one look.

Recognition.

Then Zee did something he had never done before in a real battle.

He turned his back.

Completely.

Danger still active.

Enemies still moving.

Zayrlen understood.

His chest tightened.

Not fear.

Trust.

Zee had just told him without words:

I trust you with this side.

Zayrlen did not waste it.

---

The battle became uglier after that.

Better.

Father and son stopped feeling separate.

Not because they fought the same.

Because their styles locked together.

Zee destroyed pressure points.

Zayrlen controlled the space around them.

Zee broke through armored ranks.

Zayrlen built moving Mana corridors that prevented retreat toward civilians.

Zee used absolute precision.

Zayrlen reshaped the battlefield.

When mercenaries tried flanking Zee from the ridge, Zayrlen took Dragon form and owned the air.

Crimson-and-Gold wings beat once.

The downdraft threw two archers from position.

Mana spears formed around him.

Not one.

Six.

They dropped in staggered timing.

Three struck weapons.

Two struck legs.

One killed.

Zayrlen landed.

Shifted Human.

Then Wolf.

Chased the one Zee deliberately let run.

Not bait this time.

Real runner.

Wolf scent confirmed he was alone.

Zayrlen caught him before the river.

The man turned.

Raised both hands.

“Wait—”

Zayrlen smelled blood.

Civilians.

Fresh.

Confirmed.

His eyes hardened.

The Wolf attacked.

No mercy.

---

Zee was worse.

The mercenary commander finally reappeared when the trap failed.

Tried escaping through the north.

Zee met him there.

The man stopped.

Realized.

Too late.

“You could have surrendered before the first civilian died,” Zee said.

The commander lifted his sword.

Zee looked almost bored.

“No.”

One word.

The sword shattered.

The commander backed up.

“You are doing this in front of your son.”

Zee's expression changed.

Not shame.

Not hesitation.

“So?”

The man glanced toward Zayrlen.

“He should see what you are.”

Zee looked toward his son.

Zayrlen had returned to Human form.

Blood on his clothes.

Watching.

Zee looked back at the commander.

“He knows.”

Then Zee killed him.

Fast.

No ceremony.

No apology.

Zayrlen watched the body fall.

Nothing inside him broke.

Dad.

King.

Monster to enemies.

Protector to his people.

All true.

He had always known.

Now he had seen it beside him.

Different from hearing stories.

Different from training.

Real.

He understood the weight better now.

That mattered.

---

The remaining mercenaries broke.

Some tried running.

Darkheart fighters hunted down the ones confirmed to have participated in the attack.

No mercy for the people who burned homes and slaughtered civilians.

Those who had been forced into service and dropped weapons before harming anyone were separated.

Zayrlen noticed that too.

Distinction.

Not softness.

Judgment.

The same standard his father demanded from him.

The fight ended shortly after.

Smoke remained.

Blood remained.

The settlement remained standing.

Barely.

But alive.

---

Combat Zee disappeared immediately.

Zayrlen did not even get a full breath.

Zee was already in front of him.

“Where are you hurt?”

Zayrlen blinked.

“I’m not.”

Zee grabbed his face.

“That was not the question.”

“Dad.”

“Zayrlen.”

Zee turned his head left.

Then right.

Checked the blood near his jaw.

“Not mine.”

Zee ignored that.

Hands moved to shoulders.

Arms.

Ribs.

Zayrlen groaned.

“I literally just turned into a Dragon and crushed a man.”

“Yes.”

“You watched me.”

“Yes.”

“I am fine.”

Zee pressed two fingers against his side.

Zayrlen flinched.

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“There.”

“That is nothing.”

“You flinched.”

“He hit me.”

“With what?”

“A hammer.”

Zee's face changed.

“Where is he?”

“Dead.”

“Good.”

Zayrlen stared.

Then laughed despite himself.

“You are ridiculous.”

Zee checked his breathing.

Heartbeat.

Then his hands.

Zayrlen looked toward the Darkheart soldiers.

Several were pretending not to watch.

“Dad.”

“What?”

“People are looking.”

Zee looked around.

“So?”

Zayrlen covered his face.

“Teddy bear.”

Zee froze.

Slowly turned toward him.

“Who taught you that?”

Zayrlen smiled.

“Rez.”

“Of course.”

---

Ner arrived with the second support group after the main fighting ended.

He saw Zee inspecting Zayrlen.

Smiled immediately.

Zayrlen looked betrayed.

“Do not encourage him.”

Ner walked over.

“Let me see.”

Zayrlen stared.

“No.”

Both fathers looked at him.

He sighed.

“Fine.”

Ner checked the bruised side.

Zee looked smug.

Zayrlen pointed.

“This is why I did not want two fathers.”

Ner laughed.

“You say that now.”

Zee looked at him.

“He did good.”

Ner's face softened.

That sentence meant more than the bruise.

Zayrlen heard it too.

He went quiet.

---

Later, after the wounded were stabilized and the dead accounted for, Zayrlen found Zee near the ruined watch post.

The sun had started rising.

Smoke turned gold at the edges.

Zee stood alone.

Zayrlen walked beside him.

For a moment, neither spoke.

Then Zayrlen asked:

“Did I prove it?”

Zee turned toward him.

No joke.

No delay.

“Yes.”

Zayrlen's expression changed.

Zee continued.

“You saw the commander.”

“Yes.”

“You wanted him.”

“Yes.”

“You knew he was bait.”

“Yes.”

“And you left him.”

“Yes.”

Zee nodded toward the wounded behind them.

“Because they mattered more.”

Zayrlen looked back.

Then at Zee.

“Yes.”

“That is what I needed.”

Zayrlen swallowed.

Zee's voice stayed steady.

“I turned my back on you.”

“I know.”

“You noticed.”

“Yes.”

“Good.”

Zee stepped closer.

“You earned that.”

Zayrlen looked down for half a second.

Then back up.

“So I can come next time?”

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“Appropriate missions.”

Zayrlen smiled.

“That is not a no.”

“It is not a yes to everything.”

“Still progress.”

“Yes.”

Clean.

Earned.

---

They walked back through the settlement together.

Not King and little Prince.

Not father carrying a child.

Two fighters.

Different.

Complementary.

Zayrlen stopped to help lift debris from a trapped house.

Zee waited.

Did not rush him.

That mattered too.

Years ago, Zayrlen had grabbed Zee's horns with tiny hands.

Run crying with a scraped knee.

Turned into a little Crimson-and-Gold Wolf in the rain and panicked because he did not know how to become himself again.

Years later, he had stood in his room terrified while a Dragon tore its way out of him.

Dad—I can't stop it.

Then stop trying.

Now that same son had stood in a real battlefield and made the right choice when no one was there to make it for him.

Zee watched him.

Pride settled deep.

Not loud.

Not performative.

Permanent.

---

Zayrlen finished helping the civilians.

Then walked back.

Zee reached up.

Wiped a streak of dried blood from his son's cheek with his thumb.

Zayrlen sighed.

“Again?”

“Yes.”

“I fought beside you.”

“Yes.”

“I saved half the wounded line.”

“Yes.”

“I stopped the trap.”

“Yes.”

“I killed mercenaries.”

“Yes.”

“And you are cleaning my face.”

“Yes.”

Zayrlen stared.

Zee stared back.

Finally Zayrlen smiled.

“You are never stopping, are you?”

“No.”

Immediate.

Zayrlen laughed.

Then leaned into Zee's shoulder for one second.

Only one.

Teenage pride had limits.

Zee wrapped an arm around him anyway.

Of course.

The warrior had earned his place.

The son had earned his father's trust.

And Zee Darkheart had finally learned something harder than killing gods, creating races, surviving death, or becoming the First Natural Abysscin.

How to turn his back in battle—

and trust his son to hold the line.

Zayrlen had grown.

Zee had let him.

But when they finally started home, Zee still looked at the young fighter beside him and saw every version at once.

The baby.

The little Wolf.

The frightened boy becoming a Dragon.

The teenager asking if he had done good.

His son.

His baby.

Always.

And now—

someone Zee Darkheart trusted beside him in war.

# Chapter One Hundred Forty-Two

## Father and Son

The alarm reached Darkheart before sunrise.

Not bells.

Blood.

A wounded Wolf rider collapsed through the eastern gate with half his armor missing and another man's blood dried across his throat.

Zee smelled it before the guards finished carrying him inside.

He entered the lower hall already knowing someone had crossed the line.

Tessa knelt beside the rider.

Ner stood nearby.

Rez had a map open across the nearest table.

Zayrlen arrived seconds later.

Older now.

Teenage.

Tall enough that the difference between boy and young man had become impossible to ignore.

Still Zee's son.

Always.

The rider tried to sit up.

Tessa pushed him back down.

“Do that again and I will personally knock you unconscious.”

He obeyed.

Zee looked at him.

“What happened?”

The Wolf swallowed.

“Ridge settlement east of Vaelor Pass.”

Darkheart protected territory.

Families.

Supply roads.

People who had sworn to Zee because Zee had promised something simple in return.

Safety.

The rider continued.

“Raiders came before dawn. Mixed group. Mercenaries. Wolves. Vampires. Witches.”

“How many?”

“Forty, maybe fifty.”

Rez looked at the map.

“Too organized for ordinary bandits.”

The rider nodded.

“They knew the patrol rotation.”

Zee's expression cooled.

“Dead?”

“Three guards.”

Silence.

“Civilians?”

“Two wounded when I left. They were trying to drag people out of the houses.”

That was enough.

Zee turned.

“Rez.”

“Already sending reinforcements.”

“Ner.”

“I'll keep Darkheart sealed until you return.”

Zee nodded.

Then he looked toward the door.

Zayrlen stood there.

Waiting.

Neither spoke for several seconds.

The conversation from the rooftop lived between them.

Will you ever let me fight with you?

Yes.

When you earn it.

Zayrlen stepped forward.

“I am coming.”

Ner looked at Zee.

Not Zayrlen.

This decision belonged to both fathers.

Zee studied his son.

Really studied him.

Not the Dragon.

Not the Wolf.

Not the Mana.

Him.

Then:

“Why?”

Zayrlen frowned.

“Because they're attacking our people.”

“Not enough.”

Zayrlen understood immediately.

He thought.

Then answered:

“Because you need fighters who can move between the ridge and the forest quickly. The road is narrow. Dragon form gives me air control, Wolf form gives me ground pursuit, and Witchcraft lets me hold routes without destroying the settlement.”

Zee's expression did not change.

“Better.”

Zayrlen held his gaze.

“And because I asked you to trust my judgment.”

There.

Zee nodded once.

“Get your gear.”

Ner exhaled quietly.

Zayrlen did not move.

“That's a yes?”

Zee stared.

“Do not make me change it.”

Zayrlen disappeared.

Rez smiled.

“That was almost sweet.”

Zee looked at him.

“No.”

---

Ner caught Zayrlen before he reached the armory.

Not to stop him.

To look at him.

Zayrlen slowed.

Ner adjusted the strap across his shoulder.

The same way he had once adjusted blankets around a baby.

Years changed scale.

Not instinct.

“You listen to your father.”

Zayrlen nodded.

“But?”

Ner touched his chest.

“You also listen to yourself.”

Zayrlen's expression softened.

“I know.”

“You are not there to impress him.”

“I know.”

“You are not there to prove you are the strongest.”

“I know.”

“And you come home.”

Zayrlen smiled faintly.

“That one sounded less like advice.”

“It was not.”

Zee appeared at the end of the hall.

“Ready.”

Ner looked toward him.

Then back to Zayrlen.

“Go.”

Zayrlen did.

---

They rode only partway.

The ridge became too broken for horses.

Zee dismounted first.

Zayrlen followed.

Kael came with a strike group behind them.

Amara took the southern tree line.

Rhyven ranged ahead through the woods.

No grand army.

No ceremony.

A response.

Fast.

Direct.

The smell of smoke reached them before the settlement came into view.

Zayrlen's Wolf senses opened.

Blood.

Fear.

Metal.

Pitch.

Magic.

Too much movement.

He looked toward Zee.

“Three groups.”

Zee glanced at him.

Zayrlen continued.

“One near the houses. One behind the grain store. One higher on the ridge.”

“How sure?”

“Very.”

“Good.”

Zee drew no weapon.

He rarely needed one.

Zayrlen's Crimson-and-Gold Mana formed around his hands.

Zee looked at him once.

“Remember why you are here.”

Zayrlen nodded.

“Judgment.”

“Good.”

Then Zee vanished.

The battle began.

---

The first mercenary died before he understood Zee had arrived.

Vampire speed.

One hand through the chest.

Zee dropped the body and kept moving.

Two Witches turned.

“Hold.”

Both froze mid-cast.

Zee broke one neck.

The second tried screaming.

“Silence.”

Nothing came out.

Crimson Sovereign rolled through him with perfect control.

Wolf awareness.

Vampire speed.

Witch precision.

The Crimson Demonic Dragon burned beneath his skin.

Enemies felt him before they saw him.

Some ran.

Wrong.

Zayrlen entered differently.

He lifted both hands.

Crimson-and-Gold rings formed across the road.

Not one.

Seven.

Moving.

Rotating.

They snapped into position around the settlement entrances.

A Vampire tried crossing one.

The ring collapsed inward.

Crushed his momentum.

Threw him into a wall.

Zayrlen shifted left.

Mana threads spread between buildings like luminous wire.

Not traps for civilians.

Paths.

Channels.

Enemy movement redirected.

Friendly movement opened.

He was shaping the battlefield.

Not copying Zee.

Not trying.

A mercenary Wolf lunged at him.

Zayrlen dropped low.

Human one second.

Crimson-and-Gold Wolf the next.

Four-legged.

Fast.

He slipped beneath the strike.

Teeth caught the attacker's forearm.

Twisted.

Released.

Kept moving.

No waste.

No flourish.

The Wolf disappeared behind a wagon.

A Human Zayrlen came out the other side with a Crimson-and-Gold spear already formed.

It struck a Witch through the shoulder and pinned her to the ground.

Zee saw it.

Did not comment.

Kept killing.

---

The attackers had prepared for resistance.

Not for them.

A group on the ridge released enchanted bolts downward.

Zayrlen looked up.

Dragon senses sharpened.

Air pressure.

Heat.

Trajectory.

He raised both arms.

A broad Crimson-and-Gold barrier unfolded over three houses.

Bolts struck.

The shield bent.

Held.

One bolt punched through the edge and sliced his upper arm.

Blood ran.

Zayrlen hissed.

Did not stop.

Zee smelled it immediately.

His head turned.

Only once.

Zayrlen saw the look.

“I'm fine!”

Zee's eyes narrowed.

Then another attacker came at him.

Zee killed the man instead of answering.

Good.

He was not babysitting.

Not during the battle.

---

The commander appeared ten minutes in.

At least Zayrlen assumed he was the commander.

Black armor.

Red sash.

Two curved blades.

Protected by four fighters.

He had been directing movement from the ridge.

Now the line had collapsed.

He turned.

Ran.

Directly toward the eastern cut.

Zayrlen saw him.

Everything inside the Wolf surged.

Target.

Responsible.

Fleeing.

Perfect.

He started after him.

One step.

Two.

Then stopped.

Something was wrong.

Not emotion.

Pattern.

The commander smelled afraid.

But not enough.

His stride was too even.

Too deliberate.

He kept looking forward.

Never back.

Someone actually fleeing Zee Darkheart checked behind them.

Always.

Zayrlen's ears sharpened.

He listened.

The eastern cut should have held panicked movement.

Instead—

quiet.

Too quiet.

Then Dragon perception caught heat behind stone.

Six bodies.

Hidden.

Waiting.

And Witch Mana.

Buried beneath the path.

A constructed spell.

Triggered by weight.

Zayrlen's own kind of battlefield magic.

Only cruder.

The commander wanted pursuit.

He wanted someone fast.

Someone angry.

Someone important.

Zayrlen almost smiled.

Bait.

---

He did not follow.

The commander's scent changed.

Confusion.

Then irritation.

Good.

Zayrlen turned away.

That was when he saw the real threat.

Three attackers had slipped around the grain store.

Not toward Zee.

Toward the wounded.

Darkheart guards had moved injured civilians behind a stone wall.

The hidden team had waited for the battlefield to split.

One carried a Witch charge.

Enough force to collapse the entire structure.

Zayrlen moved.

No warning.

No shout.

No order from Zee.

He became Wolf.

Crimson-and-Gold tore across the ground.

One hidden attacker turned too late.

Zayrlen hit him at full speed.

Bones broke.

He shifted Human during the roll.

Mana threads snapped from both hands.

One wrapped the Witch charge.

Another wrapped the attacker's wrist.

A third anchored to the stone wall.

The charge ignited.

Zayrlen's eyes widened.

Not enough time to disarm.

So he changed the geometry.

Five Crimson-and-Gold rings formed around the device.

One inside another.

Each rotated opposite the last.

The explosion hit.

The rings folded inward.

Compressed the blast.

Directed it up.

Fire punched into the sky instead of through the wounded civilians.

The force still threw Zayrlen backward.

He hit the ground hard.

Ribs screamed.

One ear rang.

He rolled.

Got up.

The remaining two attackers charged.

Zayrlen did not shift Dragon.

Too large.

Too close to civilians.

Wrong tool.

Wolf again.

Fast.

Low.

First attacker lost a knee.

Human.

Mana spear through the second man's thigh.

He dropped.

Zayrlen kicked the weapon away.

Then smelled another presence behind him.

He spun.

Too late.

A blade cut across his ribs.

Deep enough to bleed.

Not deep enough to stop him.

He caught the attacker's wrist.

Headbutted him.

Then Crimson-and-Gold threads wrapped the man's throat and arms.

He pulled.

The attacker slammed face-first into stone.

Done.

---

Across the battlefield, Zee saw everything.

The fleeing commander.

The eastern cut.

Zayrlen stopping.

Turning.

Choosing.

The explosion redirected into the sky.

The wounded civilians still alive.

The hidden attackers down.

Zee understood immediately.

His son had seen the bait.

Rejected it.

Found the real threat.

No order.

No warning.

No help.

Something inside Zee changed.

Not relief.

Not exactly.

Trust.

The thing he had refused to give cheaply.

The thing Zayrlen had wanted more than permission.

Zee met his son's eyes across the smoke.

No smile.

No praise.

Just recognition.

Zayrlen understood.

Then Zee deliberately turned his back on him.

There were still enemies alive.

Still danger.

And Zee turned away.

Not carelessness.

Trust.

My son has this side.

Zayrlen felt it hit harder than any compliment could have.

He straightened.

Then went back to work.

---

The commander realized the bait had failed.

He ran harder.

Zee appeared in front of him.

The man stopped so suddenly his boots dragged through mud.

Zee looked at him.

“You were leaving.”

The commander raised both blades.

Zee smiled slightly.

“That was rude.”

They fought for less than twenty seconds.

The commander was good.

Very good.

Silver edges.

Anti-Vampire coating.

Witch resistance charms.

Wolf irritant oil.

Someone who had prepared for monsters.

Not enough.

Zee let one blade glance off Dragon scales.

Caught the wrist.

Broke it.

The second blade came up.

“Down.”

The man's knees hit earth.

Zee's hand closed around his throat.

The commander spat blood.

“You protect animals and mixed-blood filth.”

There it was.

Reason.

Verified.

Zee's expression emptied.

“They are mine.”

Then he crushed the man's throat.

No speech.

No mercy.

Done.

---

The remaining attackers broke.

Some tried the forest.

That belonged to Zayrlen.

Zee did not even look.

He trusted him now.

The young Prince shifted into his Crimson-and-Gold Wolf form and disappeared between the trees.

Ground pursuit.

Scent.

Speed.

Three fleeing mercenaries split.

Zayrlen tracked the one carrying blood from a wounded Darkheart guard.

Priority.

The others were moving away from civilians.

He chose the dangerous one.

Correct.

The mercenary doubled back suddenly.

Zayrlen anticipated it.

Shifted Human beneath the swing.

Mana ring closed around the man's weapon hand.

Another around the ankle.

Pulled opposite directions.

The attacker hit the ground.

Zayrlen stood over him.

The man reached for a hidden knife.

Zayrlen smelled the movement before he saw it.

Crimson-and-Gold spear.

Straight through the chest.

Then silence.

---

Above the ridge, two enemy Witches escaped onto a rock shelf.

Zayrlen looked up.

Different problem.

Wolf would take too long.

He shifted.

Dragon.

Crimson-and-Gold power erupted through the trees.

Wings opened.

Massive.

True.

No Phoenix.

No demonic corruption.

His Dragon form launched upward.

The surviving attackers looked back.

Regretted everything.

Zayrlen circled once.

Not to show off.

To see.

Wind.

Terrain.

Friendly positions.

Then Crimson-and-Gold Witch rings formed around his wings.

He drove downward.

One barrier blocked the enemy's escape path.

Three Mana spears forced them apart.

A wingbeat knocked one off balance.

The second fired a spell.

Zayrlen took it across the shoulder.

Scales cracked.

Pain.

He roared.

Did not lose himself.

He slammed one claw into the shelf.

Stone fractured.

Not beneath the civilians.

Not beneath allies.

Only under the attackers.

They fell into the lower clearing.

Zee was waiting.

One landed at his feet.

Zee looked down.

Then up at the Dragon.

Zayrlen understood.

Your problem now.

Zee killed the man.

The second tried crawling.

Kael ended that one.

---

Then father and son finally moved together.

Not planned.

Natural.

Zee tore through the center.

Zayrlen controlled the edges.

Crimson one-word laws cut openings.

Crimson-and-Gold structures turned those openings into cages.

“Break.”

An enemy barrier shattered.

Zayrlen's rings flowed through the gap before the fragments hit ground.

Three mercenaries trapped.

Zee entered.

Finished them.

A Witch launched a chained curse toward Zee's blind side.

Zayrlen saw it from above.

Mana thread caught the spell.

Pulled its path two feet wide.

That was enough.

Zee turned.

“Silence.”

The Witch's follow-up died in her throat.

Zayrlen landed behind her in Human form.

One spear.

Done.

Another group rushed from the road.

Zee stepped toward them.

Zayrlen shifted Wolf and came around the flank.

They never coordinated verbally.

Did not need to.

Zee forced the center.

Zayrlen broke the edges.

One monster.

One young hunter.

Different.

Complementary.

Terrifying.

For a brief moment the enemy understood exactly what Darkheart had become.

Not one impossible King.

A bloodline capable of standing beside him.

---

The final attacker dropped his weapon.

Too late.

He had spent the morning dragging Darkheart civilians from homes.

Zee knew.

Zayrlen knew.

The man looked at the teenager first.

Maybe hoping youth meant softness.

“Please.”

Zayrlen looked toward Zee.

Not for permission.

For understanding.

Zee said nothing.

Zayrlen looked back at the man.

“You had people tied inside that house.”

The attacker swallowed.

“Yes.”

“You set it on fire.”

Silence.

Zayrlen's expression hardened.

The man backed up.

Zee moved.

One hand.

One strike.

The attacker dropped.

Dead.

Zayrlen watched.

No flinch.

No horror.

He knew his father.

Dad at home.

King here.

Monster to the people who harmed theirs.

Protector to everyone behind him.

The contradiction had stopped being a contradiction years ago.

---

The battlefield went quiet.

Smoke.

Blood.

Broken stone.

Wounded people alive because Zayrlen had chosen correctly.

Zee scanned the area once.

Threats gone.

Then battle-Zee vanished.

Completely.

He turned.

Found Zayrlen.

Walked straight toward him.

Zayrlen saw the expression and immediately knew what was coming.

“Oh, no.”

Zee reached him.

“Where are you hurt?”

“I am not.”

Zee grabbed his chin.

“That was not the question.”

“Dad.”

“Zayrlen.”

“I am fine.”

“You are bleeding.”

“It is barely—”

Zee lifted his shirt.

Zayrlen slapped his hand down.

“Can you not do this in front of everyone?”

“No.”

Kael turned away to hide a smile.

Amara did not bother.

Zee inspected the cut across Zayrlen's ribs.

Then the upper arm.

Then the cracked scale line along the shoulder from Dragon form.

Zayrlen groaned.

“I fought an entire battle.”

“Yes.”

“I became a Dragon.”

“I noticed.”

“I stopped an explosive.”

“I noticed.”

“I killed people.”

“I noticed.”

“And now you're checking my ribs.”

“Yes.”

Zayrlen stared.

Zee stared back.

Teddy Bear Dad had returned with absolute authority.

---

Ner arrived with the second reinforcement group before Zee finished checking him.

He dismounted.

Saw Zayrlen standing.

Alive.

Bloody.

Then looked at Zee.

“Well?”

Zee said:

“He is hurt.”

Zayrlen said:

“I am fine.”

Ner walked over.

Looked at the rib wound.

Then at Zayrlen.

“You are hurt.”

Zayrlen looked betrayed.

“Not you too.”

Ner touched his face once.

Just once.

Then stepped back.

“Did he do well?”

Zee looked toward his son.

The question changed the air.

Zayrlen went quiet.

No jokes now.

No irritation.

No pride.

Just waiting.

The same look, somehow, as a child curled against Zee after his first Wolf transformation.

Did I do good?

Years disappeared for one second.

Zayrlen finally asked:

“Did I prove it?”

Zee did not tease him.

Did not make him wait.

“Yes.”

Clean.

Certain.

Zayrlen's face changed.

Zee continued.

“You saw the commander.”

“I did.”

“You wanted him.”

“Yes.”

“You knew he was bait.”

“Yes.”

“And you left him.”

Zayrlen nodded.

“There were people behind the grain store.”

“I know.”

“I thought if I chased him—”

“You made the right call.”

Zayrlen went still.

Zee stepped closer.

“You protected the battlefield instead of feeding your ego.”

A pause.

“You made the decision without me.”

Another.

“And when I turned my back—”

Zayrlen smiled faintly.

“I knew.”

Zee nodded.

“I know.”

That was the answer.

The blanket refusal ended there.

Not every mission.

Not every war.

Not every danger.

But no longer:

You are not ready.

Zayrlen had earned his place.

---

Later, as Darkheart soldiers secured the road, Zee and Zayrlen stood on the ridge together.

Zayrlen looked down at the settlement.

Smoke still rose.

People were alive.

That mattered more now.

He understood why Zee had spoken so much about judgment.

Power had been the easiest part.

The harder thing had been knowing where not to use it.

Zee stood beside him.

Zayrlen glanced over.

“So I can come next time?”

Zee looked at him.

“Appropriate missions.”

Zayrlen sighed.

“There it is.”

“I am still your father.”

“I know.”

“And King.”

“I know.”

“And if I say no—”

“I know.”

Zee narrowed his eyes.

Zayrlen smiled.

“But sometimes you'll say yes.”

Zee looked back over the valley.

“Yes.”

That was enough.

---

Zayrlen leaned against the stone railing.

Older.

Stronger.

Two true forms.

His own Witchcraft.

His own instincts.

His own judgment.

Zee looked at him.

And saw everything at once.

The baby gripping his horn.

The toddler running toward him instead of Ner.

The little boy with a scraped knee.

The Crimson-and-Gold Wolf lost in the rain.

The frightened teenager saying:

Dad—I can't stop it.

The enormous Dragon lowering its head so Zee could touch its snout.

And now—

the fighter who had stood beside him.

Not behind him.

Not protected from the world.

Beside him.

Zee had spent most of his life becoming impossible to kill.

Learning how to destroy threats.

Learning how to protect what belonged to him.

This had required something harder.

Letting go enough to trust.

Zayrlen looked over.

“What?”

Zee shook his head.

“Nothing.”

“You are staring.”

“I can stare at my son.”

“You do it weird.”

“Disrespectful.”

Zayrlen laughed.

Zee reached over.

Pulled him closer by the back of the neck.

Zayrlen immediately protested.

“Dad.”

“What?”

“I just fought beside you.”

“Yes.”

“I am covered in enemy blood.”

“Yes.”

“I became a Dragon over a battlefield.”

“Yes.”

“You cannot keep doing this.”

Zee looked at him.

“Watch me.”

Zayrlen groaned.

Ner laughed behind them.

And Zee smiled.

The warrior had earned his trust.

The son had earned his place.

But the child—

the one Zee had carried, protected, spoiled, taught, feared for, and loved from his first breath—

never disappeared.

That was the final truth.

Zayrlen Keal Darkheart had become strong enough and wise enough to stand beside his father in battle.

And Zee Darkheart had finally become strong enough as a father to let him.

The monster trusted his son.

The son proved that trust deserved to exist.

And when they went home—

Zee was still going to make Tessa check his ribs.
