# Chapter One Hundred Forty-Three

## The Scent

Zee was doing absolutely nothing important.

That mattered.

No hunt.

No council crisis.

No enemy at the gates.

No ancient bloodline waking inside him.

No son accidentally becoming something enormous.

For once, Darkheart was simply alive around him.

Zee sat in the western courtyard with one boot resting against the edge of a stone bench while Rez complained about trade paperwork.

Again.

Ner had disappeared into the keep after deciding both of them were useless.

Zayrlen was somewhere on the training grounds.

Victor was thankfully nowhere nearby.

Zee had a cup in one hand.

Rez had three reports.

“You did not read these.”

“I looked at them.”

“That is not reading.”

“I saw words.”

Rez stared.

Zee drank.

“Good enough.”

Rez opened his mouth.

Then Zee stopped.

Completely.

The cup never reached his mouth.

His eyes changed.

Crimson-Gold sharpening.

Rez saw it immediately.

“What?”

Zee did not answer.

Across Darkheart Kingdom—

far beyond the courtyard—

a man had cut his hand.

Barely.

A merchant stall.

A sharp metal edge.

One careless movement.

Skin opened.

One drop of blood fell.

That was all.

One drop.

And Zee smelled it.

---

The reaction came from somewhere older than thought.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Predatory memory.

Blood recognition.

His body identified the signature before his mind finished reaching for the name.

Metal.

Suppression compounds.

Sweat.

Old leather.

Fear.

Something remembered from documents.

From blood traces.

From evidence gathered after the night they put him on the ground.

The courtyard disappeared.

Not literally.

Memory did it.

Chains around a Phoenix wing.

White-light anti-Witch strikes.

Dragonbane driven under scales.

Wolf irritants burning through his senses.

Anti-Vampire stakes.

Sonic pressure.

Heat-drinking armor.

Rotating attackers.

Fresh bodies replacing tired ones.

Counter after counter after counter.

No single part of him failing.

Everything simply being demanded at once.

His own blood in his mouth.

Stone against his face.

The humiliation of realizing—

they had him.

Then the contract.

BREAK THE TARGET.

WITHDRAW ON CONFIRMATION.

Hask Renn.

Graymarket.

The ledger.

One name.

MEREK VOSS.

Zee lowered the cup.

“Merek.”

Rez went still.

The reports dropped onto the bench.

“Where?”

Zee was already standing.

“Inside my kingdom.”

That sentence changed Rez's expression completely.

---

Merek Voss had entered Darkheart under a false name.

Not because he planned to attack.

Not because he believed Zee had forgotten him.

Because he believed anonymity still mattered.

Years had passed.

Kingdoms changed.

Bloodlines evolved.

Wars happened.

People disappeared.

Merek had built a life around surviving the consequences of other people's violence.

He did not expect one old assembly contract to still have teeth.

Especially not here.

Especially not now.

His hand slipped while examining a metal fastening at a supply market in the lower eastern district.

A small cut opened across his palm.

“Damn.”

The merchant offered cloth.

Merek took it.

Wrapped his hand.

Kept moving.

Three streets later—

he felt it.

Nothing visible.

Nothing audible.

Instinct.

A professional survivor's awareness that somewhere behind him the world had changed.

Merek slowed.

Then forced himself to keep walking.

No sudden movement.

No panic.

He turned casually into a crowded lane.

Children.

Traders.

Witches.

Two Wolves carrying grain.

A Vampire couple arguing over fabric.

Good.

Crowds complicated pursuit.

He changed direction.

Then again.

Removed his outer coat.

Left it hanging behind a carriage.

Used scented oil on his wrists.

Walked through a butcher's market.

Then a spice row.

Then a forge district.

He did everything correctly.

For anyone else.

---

Zee left the courtyard without rushing.

At first.

Rez followed.

“You have the scent?”

“Yes.”

“How certain?”

Zee looked at him.

Rez stopped asking stupid questions.

“Right.”

They crossed one corridor.

Zee's wings remained hidden.

No Witchcraft.

No Wolf transformation.

No Vampire burst.

Nothing.

Not yet.

Rez noticed.

“You are walking.”

“I know.”

“That is concerning.”

Zee glanced at him.

“He is already mine.”

There was no arrogance in it.

Just fact.

Merek had spilled blood inside Darkheart.

That mistake had ended the chase before it began.

---

Zayrlen caught them near the lower gate.

He had training wraps around both hands.

Sweat darkened his shirt.

“Where are you going?”

Zee kept walking.

Zayrlen matched pace.

“Dad.”

“Merek Voss.”

Zayrlen stopped.

He knew the name.

Everyone close to Zee did.

Not because Zee repeated the old defeat constantly.

Because some wounds became family knowledge.

Zayrlen's expression changed.

“The ambush.”

“Yes.”

“I'm coming.”

“No.”

Immediate.

Zayrlen's jaw tightened.

“Dad—”

“This is not your debt.”

“I can help.”

“I know.”

That stopped him.

Zee looked at his son.

“This one is mine.”

Zayrlen studied his face.

Then nodded once.

No argument.

Good.

“Bring him back alive?”

Zee's smile held no warmth.

“For a while.”

Then he kept moving.

---

Merek reached the outer carriage road.

Too exposed.

He turned toward the south bridge.

Wrong.

Stopped.

Three Darkheart guards had closed the crossing.

Not looking for him.

Not yet.

Normal inspection.

Merek turned before they noticed.

Walked fast.

Not running.

Then he heard footsteps behind him.

One set.

Unhurried.

He did not look back.

That was the second mistake.

Because the voice reached him anyway.

“You always walk this fast?”

Merek stopped.

Every nerve in his body went cold.

He knew the voice.

Not personally.

From reports.

Testimony.

Survivor descriptions.

He turned.

Zee Darkheart stood twenty feet away.

Human form.

No visible claws.

No Witch Mana.

No Wolf eyes.

No Dragon scales.

No Crimson Sovereign pressure.

Nothing Merek expected.

That terrified him more.

---

“Merek Voss.”

Merek's face remained blank.

“Wrong man.”

Zee looked toward the wrapped hand.

“No.”

Merek glanced down.

Understood.

Blood.

One cut.

One stupid cut.

Years of survival ended by one drop.

He ran.

Zee let him.

---

Merek crossed the bridge.

Turned hard into a narrow stone lane.

Shoved through pedestrians.

Vaulted a cart.

Cut left.

Then right.

He knew Darkheart's lower districts from old maps.

Not current ones.

A wall had been added where an alley should have been.

Merek swore.

Turned back.

Zee stood at the entrance.

Still walking.

Merek pulled a silver-black cylinder from inside his coat.

Old habit.

Old equipment.

He activated it.

A suppression pulse spread through the lane.

Designed to disrupt Witch channels.

Merek watched Zee.

Nothing happened.

Zee continued walking.

Merek's expression changed.

He pulled another device.

Sonic.

Wolf-targeted frequency.

Activated.

Zee tilted his head.

Then kept coming.

Merek backed away.

“Wait.”

Zee's eyes stayed on him.

Merek reached for the third tool.

Anti-Vampire flare.

He threw it.

The flare burst white-red.

Zee walked through it.

No Vampire speed.

No fangs.

No attempt to counter it.

Nothing.

Merek finally understood something was wrong.

Very wrong.

“You changed.”

Zee stopped five feet away.

Black-crimson fire appeared around one hand.

Deep scarlet beneath it.

Merek had never seen that flame before.

Not in any report.

Not in any preparation packet.

Not in any description from the people who had studied Zee Darkheart for months.

Zee looked at him.

“You studied what I was.”

Then Phoenix pressure filled the lane.

Merek stopped breathing properly.

---

No spell.

No command word.

No Witch law.

Just heat.

Black-crimson flame crawled across the stone walls without consuming them.

Scarlet pulsed beneath.

Zee's eyes remained Crimson-Gold.

Human.

Mostly.

Then enormous Phoenix wings unfolded behind him.

Black-crimson feathers.

Scarlet fire moving through them like blood through veins.

Merek stumbled backward.

“What is that?”

Zee smiled.

“The part you missed.”

Merek turned.

One wing moved.

Not even fully.

Phoenix force hit him like a carriage.

He flew through a wooden door.

Inside.

Stone floor.

Broken furniture.

Merek coughed blood.

Zee stepped through the wreckage.

No hurry.

The old target had become the hunter.

---

Merek tried one final device.

Dragonbane wire.

He snapped it outward.

Zee caught it.

Bare hand.

No Dragon scales.

No Witch shield.

Black-crimson Phoenix fire moved over his fingers.

The wire glowed.

Melted.

Dropped.

Merek stared.

“That should have—”

“I know.”

Zee kicked him.

Not Dragon strength.

Phoenix force.

Enough.

Merek crossed the room and struck a support beam.

Something cracked.

Probably rib.

Maybe two.

Zee walked closer.

“You built people around my weaknesses.”

“I assembled them.”

Zee stopped.

Merek immediately realized that distinction mattered.

Not morally.

Practically.

Information.

“Yes.”

There it was.

Zee crouched.

“Say that again.”

Merek swallowed.

“I assembled the team.”

Zee's expression cooled.

Now the hunt changed.

---

Merek tried bargaining immediately.

Professional instinct.

“I did not order the contract.”

“I know.”

“I did not choose the objective.”

“Good.”

“I did not personally strike you.”

Zee looked at him.

Merek corrected quickly.

“I mean—I wasn't on the field.”

“Better.”

“I connected specialists. Equipment. Logistics.”

“Names.”

Merek hesitated.

Black-crimson Phoenix fire spread across Zee's hand.

Not touching him.

Yet.

Merek stared.

“Wait.”

Zee's voice remained calm.

“Names.”

“I need assurances.”

Zee smiled.

Merek's face fell.

Wrong request.

“No?”

“No.”

“Then why would I talk?”

Zee leaned closer.

“Because dying is not the only thing I can make painful.”

Merek believed him.

---

He stopped in the doorway.

Looked at the melted Dragonbane wire.

The broken sonic cylinder.

The inactive Witch suppression device.

Then at Zee.

“You didn't use any of the old sides.”

“No.”

Rez understood immediately.

The attackers had prepared for Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Dragon.

They had even prepared for combinations.

But none of them had ever known the Crimson Black Abyss Phoenix existed.

None of them had known Zee would become the First Natural Abysscin.

Rez looked at Merek.

“That is unfortunate for you.”

Merek laughed weakly.

“You have no idea.”

Rez's expression said otherwise.

---

Zee dragged a chair upright.

Sat.

Merek remained on the floor.

Appropriate.

“Start.”

Merek looked toward Rez.

Then Zee.

“Some names won't mean anything anymore.”

“Try me.”

Merek exhaled.

“The assembly came through multiple channels.”

“I know.”

“Hask Renn handled some of the equipment movement.”

“Dead.”

Merek's eyes flickered.

Of course.

Zee continued.

“You are next if this becomes boring.”

“Fine.”

He started talking.

The first name:

**SELK VARREN.**

A Witch-suppression architect.

Not merely a supplier.

Selk helped design the rotating suppression sequence used during the ambush.

He studied known descriptions of Zee's casting behavior and built timing windows around them.

Merek had recruited him personally.

Zee remembered white-light disruption biting through his Witch side.

Name one.

---

The second:

**BRANNIC DOR.**

Former Wolf hunter.

Specialized in scent disruption, irritants, pursuit denial, and anti-pack tactics.

He selected the compound used to overload Zee's Wolf senses.

Also trained three direct participants.

Name two.

---

The third:

**LORD VAEREN THOSS.**

A minor coastal noble with deep access to anti-Vampire weapon markets.

Provided silvered restraint mechanisms, blood-loss inhibitors, and two of the specialized stakes.

Financed part of the equipment acquisition.

Not entire operation.

Part.

Name three.

---

The fourth:

**KALDREK VANE.**

Dragonbane smith.

Eastern volcanic territories.

Built the barbed internal healing disruptor and heat-resistant restraint fittings.

Had personally modified equipment after receiving descriptions of Zee's Dragon durability.

Name four.

---

The fifth:

**SERA QUILL.**

Tactician.

Not frontline.

Not supplier.

She studied battle reports.

Every known pattern.

Every response.

Every documented adaptation.

She designed the attacker rotation itself.

Fresh fighters.

Changing tools.

No stable rhythm.

Never letting Zee adapt to one problem before replacing it with another.

Rez's face changed at that one.

Zee remembered.

That had mattered.

A lot.

Name five.

---

Then Merek hesitated.

Zee saw it.

“Next.”

Merek looked at him.

“This one was there.”

The room went quieter.

“Name.”

“Jorren Vale.”

Merek swallowed.

“Strike leader.”

Zee's eyes sharpened.

“He was the one coordinating field timing.”

Images returned.

A voice through blood and noise.

Rotate.

Change pattern.

Do not let him settle.

Fresh team.

Now.

Merek continued.

“Jorren gave the withdrawal call when confirmation came through.”

Confirmation.

Break the target.

Withdraw.

Zee remembered someone saying:

You are not untouchable.

His jaw tightened.

Name six.

Direct participant.

Meaningful.

Personal.

---

Rez spoke.

“Who gave confirmation?”

Merek looked at him.

“I don't know.”

Zee studied him.

Not lying.

Interesting.

Merek continued before the silence became dangerous.

“The order did not come directly to me.”

“Through who?”

“A sealed broker.”

“Name.”

“I never got a true one.”

Zee's expression cooled.

Merek rushed onward.

“The payments were layered through three channels. One was Thoss. One came through Graymarket. One came from an account tied to a neutral holding house in Caldrin territory.”

Rez frowned.

“That can be traced.”

“Maybe.”

“Who delivered the original terms?”

Merek swallowed.

“A masked intermediary.”

Zee said nothing.

Merek knew that was not enough.

“But I can give you the seal.”

That mattered.

“What seal?”

Merek described it.

Not a known faction symbol.

Not a prophecy mark.

Not anything from Victor.

Not the Devouring Choir.

A contract seal.

Black wax.

Three vertical cuts crossed by a single horizontal line.

No name.

No kingdom.

No identity.

Just one more piece.

The original commissioner remained out there.

Good.

Zee had not wanted Merek to be the ending.

He wanted the door.

---

“Anyone else?”

Merek nodded.

“Two more who mattered.”

Zee waited.

“**Neris Pell.** Information broker. She compiled your travel habits, known combat encounters, public ability sightings, prior enemies, and injury recoveries.”

Studied him.

Name seven.

“And **Drovak Senn.** Logistics controller. Built the extraction plan. Safe routes. replacement weapons. Retreat timing. Wounded recovery.”

Name eight.

Rez looked toward Zee.

Eight meaningful contributors.

Not random.

Not inflated.

Each tied directly to the night Zee lost.

Merek had finally become useful.

Zee leaned back.

“Who is still alive?”

Merek hesitated.

Then answered.

“Last I knew?”

Zee nodded.

“Selk. Brannic. Thoss. Kaldrek. Sera. Jorren. Neris. Drovak.”

All eight.

Zee smiled.

Merek looked sick.

---

“You're going after all of them.”

Not a question.

Zee looked toward him.

“Yes.”

Merek shook his head.

“You don't understand. Some of them have spent years preparing for you.”

That amused Zee.

“Good.”

“They know your Witch side.”

Zee's black-crimson flame appeared again.

“They know your Vampire side.”

Scarlet burned beneath it.

“They studied your Wolf.”

Phoenix wings opened slowly behind him.

“They built for your Dragon.”

Heat rolled through the room.

Merek stopped talking.

Zee's voice remained calm.

“They studied the monster they put on the ground.”

The flames deepened.

Black-crimson.

Scarlet below.

Alive.

Controlled.

“They never met this one.”

Merek stared.

For the first time, he understood the full irony.

Their victory had mattered.

They had succeeded.

They had broken Zee Darkheart.

And that night had helped stir the buried paternal Phoenix inheritance that eventually fused, rewrote, and became something none of them could have planned for.

They had beaten the version of Zee they understood.

Now the version born afterward had their names.

---

Rez looked at Merek.

“Does he know where they are?”

Zee's eyes stayed on Merek.

“He will.”

Merek swallowed.

“I can help.”

Zee smiled faintly.

“You already are.”

The smile vanished.

“And when I am done needing you, we will discuss your part.”

Merek's face lost what little color remained.

He had assembled the team.

He had connected specialists.

He had helped make the night possible.

He was not innocent.

Just useful.

Temporarily.

---

Zee stood.

Rez looked at the list he had written.

Eight names.

Eight roles.

One unresolved commissioner.

One unidentified intermediary.

A contract seal.

A supply architecture.

A field leader.

A tactician.

Specialists.

Financiers.

Information.

Logistics.

The revenge list had begun.

Not because Zee lost control.

Because he finally had enough control to collect an old debt properly.

Zee looked at Merek one last time.

Years ago, Merek Voss had helped assemble the people who studied Zee Darkheart like a problem.

Measured him.

Countered him.

Overwhelmed him.

Put him on the ground.

Now Merek sat bleeding on that same King's floor while black-crimson Phoenix fire moved quietly around Zee's hand.

He had thought entering Darkheart under a false name would hide him.

Instead—

one drop of blood had opened the door.

Zee turned toward Rez.

“Find Selk Varren.”

Rez looked at the names.

“First?”

Zee's Crimson-Gold eyes burned.

“First.”

Merek closed his eyes.

He finally understood.

He had not been the conclusion.

He had been the doorway.

And Zee Darkheart had just walked through.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Never lose the irony at the center of this sequence.

The Chapter 128 attack WORKED.

Do not cheapen that defeat.

Do not rewrite it as if Zee secretly could have won.

He lost.

They overwhelmed him.

Their planning succeeded.

That loss mattered.

But the consequences continued after they left.

That night helped stir Zee's dormant inherited Abyssal Titan Phoenix Sovereign bloodline.

Zee later evolved further.

He became the First Natural Abysscin.

His true Phoenix form became the Crimson Black Abyss Phoenix.

Years passed.

He learned.

He changed his tactics.

He became harder to predict.

Now the people who successfully defeated Zee once are facing the consequences of having taught him exactly where he was vulnerable.

They defeated an older Zee.

That victory does NOT guarantee they understand the current one.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE UNKNOWN COMMISSIONER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Do NOT reveal the commissioner too early.

Merek remains the intermediary who assembled the operation.

The original order still came through another layer.

The known contract wording remains:

BREAK THE TARGET.
WITHDRAW ON CONFIRMATION.

The unresolved question remains:

Why did the commissioner want Zee BROKEN rather than killed?

Allow the answer to develop gradually.

Do not decide the final motive prematurely unless the story naturally reaches it.

Do NOT connect the commissioner to:

• Victor.
• The Devouring Choir.
• A hidden single mastermind behind every problem in Zee's life.

The Chapter 128 operation remains its own thread.

The world contains many enemies.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE CONTRACT SEAL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Retain the contract seal introduced through Merek:

Black wax.

Three vertical cuts crossed by one horizontal line.

At first, it is only evidence.

Do NOT immediately make it a gigantic ancient faction symbol.

It may eventually lead somewhere.

For now, let it remain unsettling because nobody close to Zee recognizes it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
MEREK VOSS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Merek remains alive only while useful.

Do NOT suddenly make him a trusted ally.

Do NOT make Zee forgive him.

Do NOT make him innocent.

He knowingly helped assemble the operation.

He is responsible.

He simply was not the final commissioner.

Zee may keep returning to him for:

• Locations.
• Old aliases.
• Payment routes.
• Safehouses.
• Contact methods.
• Connections between the eight.
• Confirmation of information exposed by later targets.

Merek understands that every useful answer extends his usefulness.

He also understands usefulness is not forgiveness.

His eventual fate remains open until the story reaches it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE BLACK ABYSSCIN PHOENIX
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Do NOT invent a brand-new Phoenix ability for every target.

Zee has had YEARS to practice.

This sequence should show mastery, not another endless evolution ladder.

Let established Phoenix abilities become more sophisticated through use.

Examples:

Black-crimson fire used with precision rather than simply larger flames.

Phoenix pressure used psychologically.

Wings used offensively, defensively, and for movement.

Regeneration demonstrated casually against attacks that would once have changed a fight.

Heat shaped without destroying everything around Zee.

Partial transformations used deliberately.

Full Phoenix transformation reserved for moments that deserve its scale.

Zee does NOT need to become the giant Crimson Black Abyss Phoenix every chapter.

Sometimes Human Zee with black-crimson fire should be more frightening.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ZEE'S ENJOYMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Zee is allowed to enjoy this.

Do not sanitize him.

He has become darker over his life.

He enjoys hunting people he believes deserve what is coming.

He may smile when old counters fail.

He may deliberately let someone believe they have an opening.

He may enjoy watching somebody realize the research they trusted is obsolete.

But Zee is NOT mindlessly torturing random innocents.

The people being hunted are meaningfully connected to the attack against him.

Keep that distinction clear.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PACING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the lick back moving.

Do NOT spend five chapters looking for each person.

Tracking should generally be fast.

The LENGTH of this storyline comes from:

• Eight different people.
• Different reactions.
• Different confrontations.
• Consequences spreading between targets.
• Information revealed gradually.
• The unknown commissioner.
• Relationships between members of the original operation.
• Zee's emotional differences depending on each person's involvement.
• The world realizing Zee has started collecting.

The story is longer because the debt is LARGE.

Not because Zee suddenly becomes bad at finding people.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CORE FEELING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Chapter 128 belonged to them.

They chose the battlefield.

They chose the timing.

They chose the counters.

They chose when to rotate.

They chose when to leave.

They put Zee Darkheart on the ground.

That jump was theirs.

Now—

the lick back belongs to Zee.

# Chapter One Hundred Forty-Four

## Selk Varren

Selk Varren had spent years preparing to survive Zee Darkheart.

That was why his house had no windows.

Why the outer walls contained silver.

Why Wolfbane grew beneath the southern foundation.

Why every corridor could flood with scent-destroying smoke.

Why Dragonbane had been hammered into the support beams.

Why suppression stones sat beneath every floor.

Why six separate escape routes existed beneath the estate.

Selk had prepared for Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Dragon.

He had updated those preparations every year.

And when the message arrived that Merek Voss had disappeared inside Darkheart—

Selk did not panic.

He smiled.

“So.”

The older man folded the message.

“He finally came.”

Selk Varren was Human.

Entirely.

No supernatural blood.

No hidden ancestry.

No magic.

And that had never stopped him from becoming one of the most respected suppression architects money could buy.

He understood supernatural power because he had spent his life studying how it behaved.

Magic had patterns.

Predators had instincts.

Strength created habits.

Speed created confidence.

Immortality created arrogance.

Everything could be studied.

Everything could be interrupted.

Including Zee Darkheart.

Selk knew because once—

he had helped prove it.

---

Three days after Merek disappeared, Selk stood inside his underground command chamber.

Maps covered one wall.

Weapons another.

And across the largest table—

years of research.

ZEE DARKHEART.

Old sketches.

Witness accounts.

Battle reports.

Known Witch responses.

Vampire movement patterns.

Wolf pursuit behavior.

Dragon durability.

Later reports regarding the Crimson Sovereign.

Rumors about Phoenix wings had been added.

But rumors were not data.

Selk did not trust rumors.

One of his guards entered.

“Southern perimeter is clear.”

“Eastern?”

“Clear.”

“Air?”

“Nothing.”

Selk nodded.

“Then he is not here.”

A voice behind him answered.

“Yes, I am.”

Selk froze.

Every guard turned.

Zee sat on the edge of the research table.

One leg crossed over the other.

He was holding one of Selk's files.

Reading it.

Selk stared.

Zee flipped a page.

“You spelled my mother's name wrong.”

Nobody moved.

Zee looked up.

“Aurelia.”

He tapped the page.

“One L.”

Selk's hand moved beneath the table.

Zee smiled.

“Go ahead.”

Selk pressed the trigger.

The entire room activated.

---

Suppression hit first.

A brutal field exploded through the chamber.

Witch Mana interference.

Spell disruption.

Casting destabilization.

Zee felt it pass through him.

Did nothing.

Selk watched carefully.

Second layer.

Silver mechanisms opened inside the walls.

Anti-Vampire frequencies filled the chamber.

Nothing.

Third.

Wolf irritants flooded the vents.

Nothing.

Fourth.

Dragonbane bolts fired from hidden compartments.

Zee moved.

Black-crimson wings erupted behind him.

One sweep.

The bolts shattered against Phoenix force.

Selk's smile disappeared.

Zee remained sitting.

“Finished?”

Selk stared at the wings.

Black-crimson.

Scarlet burning through the feathers.

Not Dragon.

Not anything in his files.

He immediately changed tactics.

“Containment seven.”

The floor opened.

Metal restraints launched upward.

Designed for Zee's known strength.

Zee let them catch him.

Wrists.

Ankles.

Torso.

Wings.

The restraints locked.

Selk breathed.

There.

Zee looked down.

Selk approached slowly.

“You've changed.”

“Yes.”

“But not enough.”

Zee looked amused.

Selk stopped ten feet away.

“I studied you before people understood what you were.”

“You studied reports.”

“I predicted you.”

“You did.”

Selk smiled again.

“You always answer confinement with force.”

Zee said nothing.

“You test the restraint. Then Witchcraft. If magic fails, Vampire speed. If movement fails, Dragon strength. If—”

Black-crimson fire appeared beneath Zee's skin.

Selk stopped.

The restraints began glowing.

Not melting.

Glowing.

Then Zee's Phoenix wings folded inward.

Heat intensified.

The restraints turned white.

Selk backed away.

Zee had not pulled once.

Had not tested their strength.

Had not used Witchcraft.

Had not used Vampire speed.

Had not used Wolf instinct.

Had not used Dragon force.

The metal liquefied.

Zee stood.

Selk whispered, “Phoenix.”

“Closer.”

“What are you?”

Zee stepped through the molten restraints.

“The First Natural Abysscin.”

Selk's face tightened.

That word existed nowhere in his research.

Zee smiled.

“There's your problem.”

---

Selk ran.

Not blindly.

He hit a wall mechanism.

The chamber split into six corridors.

Doors slammed between them.

False routes opened.

Gas released.

Pressure traps activated.

Zee stayed where he was.

He did not chase.

Selk moved through the western route.

Changed to northern.

Dropped two levels.

Entered the secondary tunnel.

His guards scattered deliberately.

Different directions.

Different scents.

Different footfalls.

Everything designed to complicate Zee's Wolf tracking.

Except Zee was not using his Wolf.

He stood in the command chamber.

Closed his eyes.

And allowed Phoenix heat to expand.

Not fire.

Heat.

Controlled.

Through stone.

Through metal.

Through the architecture.

One corridor carried colder outside air.

An escape tunnel.

Zee opened his eyes.

His wings spread.

One violent beat—

and he was gone.

---

Selk reached the surface.

Night air struck his face.

A carriage waited.

Two horses.

Three armed guards.

He climbed aboard.

“Move.”

The carriage launched forward.

Selk looked behind them.

Nothing.

Good.

He exhaled.

Then the horses screamed.

Black-crimson fire landed across the road.

Not touching them.

A wall.

Perfectly controlled.

The driver pulled hard.

The carriage turned.

Phoenix pressure slammed into its side.

Wood exploded.

Selk rolled across the ground.

He came up with a silver weapon already in his hand.

Zee landed.

Human form.

Phoenix wings behind him.

Selk fired.

The projectile entered Zee's shoulder.

Deep.

Selk smiled.

Zee looked down.

Blood ran.

Then stopped.

The wound closed around the projectile.

Black-crimson heat pushed the metal back out.

It dropped onto the road.

Selk's smile vanished.

Zee looked at his healed shoulder.

Then at Selk.

“That one would've been annoying years ago.”

Selk backed away.

“This isn't possible.”

“It clearly is.”

“You cannot simply become something nobody prepared for.”

Zee laughed softly.

“You helped.”

Selk's face changed.

Zee approached.

“That night.”

Selk understood.

“No.”

“Yes.”

“We defeated you.”

“Yes.”

The answer came without hesitation.

Selk stared.

Zee did not rewrite it.

Did not diminish it.

Did not pretend otherwise.

“You did.”

Selk's pride returned.

Just slightly.

“It was perfect.”

Zee's smile disappeared.

Selk continued.

“Do you know what that operation was?”

“Yes.”

“One of the greatest tactical accomplishments of my life.”

Silence.

Selk's eyes brightened with old professional pride.

“You had answers for everything. So we stopped giving you one problem at a time.”

Zee remembered stone against his face.

Selk remembered timing charts.

That difference sat between them.

“You were extraordinary,” Selk said. “Which made solving you extraordinary.”

Zee's wings opened wider.

“You went home proud.”

“Yes.”

“I went home different.”

Selk finally heard the danger.

---

He raised both hands.

“I was not the commissioner.”

“I know.”

“I never met them.”

“I know.”

“I built suppression timing.”

“I know.”

“I didn't choose the contract.”

Zee stopped.

“You chose to help.”

Selk's jaw tightened.

“It was work.”

There it was.

Zee stared at him.

Selk did not apologize.

Perhaps that was the only respectable thing about him.

“It wasn't personal.”

Black-crimson fire crawled over Zee's fingers.

“For you.”

Selk swallowed.

Zee stepped closer.

“For you, I was timing.”

Another step.

“Patterns.”

Another.

“A problem.”

Selk stood his ground.

“For me, you were one of the people who helped put my face against stone.”

The fire darkened.

Scarlet burned beneath.

“So now it is personal.”

---

Selk attacked first.

Not with suppression.

A blade.

Human.

Simple.

Fast.

Zee moved his wing.

The blade struck black-crimson feathers.

Snapped.

Selk drove a second weapon toward Zee's throat.

Zee caught his wrist.

No Vampire speed.

Phoenix movement.

Selk twisted.

Kicked.

Zee released him.

Selk rolled backward.

Three guards attacked from opposite sides.

Zee's wings moved.

Phoenix force threw two into the dirt.

The third stopped.

Zee looked at him.

The man hesitated.

He had not been part of Chapter 128.

Just hired protection.

“Leave.”

The guard looked toward Selk.

Then ran.

Selk watched him go.

“You're letting him live?”

“He didn't jump me.”

That answer terrified Selk more than indiscriminate killing would have.

Zee knew exactly why he was here.

---

Selk activated his final defense.

A ring beneath the road ignited.

Dragon-resistant alloy rose around Zee.

Witch suppression layered over it.

Silver spikes locked inward.

Wolf irritants sprayed.

Selk backed away.

Four different counters.

Together.

Just like before.

For one second—

Zee disappeared inside.

Selk smiled.

Then black-crimson fire leaked through every seam.

His smile faded.

Scarlet followed.

The structure began shaking.

Selk stared.

“No.”

The entire containment system erupted outward.

Zee stepped through the fire.

Untouched.

His wings stretched behind him.

Selk finally understood.

Not that Zee had become impossible to hurt.

Not that his old work had been foolish.

Something worse.

His work had been good.

His conclusions had been good.

His preparation had been excellent.

For the wrong man.

“You knew,” Selk whispered.

Zee tilted his head.

“You let me activate everything.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

Zee smiled.

“I wanted you to know it wouldn't matter.”

Selk stared at him.

Then laughed once.

Bitterly.

“You really did learn from us.”

Zee's smile widened.

“That part was free.”

---

Selk's fear settled.

Not disappeared.

Settled.

He knew he was dead.

Professionals behaved differently once uncertainty ended.

He lowered his hands.

“Then ask.”

Zee's expression changed.

“Ask what?”

“The question you came with.”

“I came to kill you.”

“You always have another question.”

Zee studied him.

Selk smiled faintly.

“I studied you, remember?”

Zee almost laughed.

Almost.

“Fine.”

He stepped closer.

“Who kept the research?”

Selk's eyes flickered.

That was enough.

Zee noticed.

“Who?”

Selk looked away.

“Sera.”

Sera Quill.

The tactician.

One of the eight.

“She kept copies?”

“Copies?”

Selk laughed.

“She kept everything.”

Zee's expression hardened.

“Why?”

“Because she never believed the job was finished.”

That mattered.

Selk continued.

“After the operation, most of us moved on. Sera didn't.”

“How long?”

“Years.”

“Monitoring me?”

“You.”

Selk paused.

“Darkheart.”

Zee went still.

“Explain.”

“She continued collecting reports. Battles. New abilities. Changes in your behavior. Your kingdom. People close to you.”

The air became hotter.

Selk saw it.

“She wasn't commissioned to continue. Not as far as I know.”

“Then why?”

“Because you became the only target she never understood completely.”

Selk's mouth twisted.

“She hates incomplete work.”

Zee's eyes burned Crimson-Gold.

“Where is she?”

“I don't know.”

Zee's wings shifted.

“I genuinely don't.”

Selk continued quickly.

“But she contacted Jorren six months ago.”

Zee stopped.

Jorren Vale.

Strike leader.

The man who had been there.

“Why?”

“I don't know.”

“Did Jorren answer?”

“Yes.”

“How do you know?”

“Because Sera asked me for updated suppression designs two weeks later.”

There.

The board changed.

Sera and Jorren were still connected.

And someone had continued studying Zee long after Chapter 128.

Selk smiled weakly.

“Useful?”

“Yes.”

“Enough to live?”

“No.”

Selk nodded.

“Thought so.”

---

Zee raised one hand.

Black-crimson fire formed.

Selk looked at it.

Then at him.

“One thing.”

Zee waited.

“We did beat you.”

“Yes.”

“Don't pretend we didn't.”

Zee's face remained calm.

“I never have.”

Selk nodded.

For some reason, that seemed to matter to him.

Zee stepped closer.

“You won that night.”

Scarlet ignited beneath the black flame.

Selk held his gaze.

Zee's voice dropped.

“This one is mine.”

The fire moved.

Selk Varren died without screaming for long.

Zee made certain of that.

---

By dawn, Selk's estate still stood.

Most of it.

His guards lived if they had been smart enough not to force Zee's hand.

His research did not.

Black-crimson fire consumed every page involving Darkheart.

Every timing chart.

Every suppression model.

Every study of Zee's family.

Every copied weakness.

Except one bundle.

Sera Quill's correspondence.

Zee took that.

Then he left.

Behind him, one sentence began moving through the supernatural world.

Selk Varren was dead.

And Zee Darkheart had come personally.

---

# Chapter One Hundred Forty-Five

## The Reaction

The first version said Selk Varren had burned alive inside his own fortress.

The second said Zee Darkheart had become immune to suppression.

The third said an enormous black Phoenix had destroyed half the estate.

That one was wrong.

Zee had never fully transformed.

The fourth said Selk had vanished.

The fifth said the King of Darkheart was killing everyone connected to an old contract.

That one was close enough.

By the second day—

the remaining seven had heard something.

And each reacted differently.

---

Brannic Dor heard while eating breakfast.

He was older now.

Gray threaded through his beard.

The former Wolf hunter sat outside a mountain lodge while two younger hunters argued over tracks.

A messenger whispered into his ear.

Brannic stopped chewing.

“Selk?”

“Yes.”

“Confirmed?”

“Yes.”

Brannic looked toward the mountains.

“How?”

“Black fire.”

Brannic frowned.

“Witch?”

“No.”

“Dragon?”

“No.”

“Then what?”

The messenger hesitated.

“Wings.”

Brannic slowly placed his fork down.

He remembered Zee Darkheart's Wolf senses screaming beneath compounds Brannic had personally chosen.

Remembered reading the field report afterward.

Remembered satisfaction.

Not joy.

Professional satisfaction.

The compound had worked.

Brannic stood.

“Burn the old stores.”

The messenger blinked.

“All of them?”

“All.”

“What about the Wolfbane?”

“Especially that.”

Brannic looked toward the distant road.

“If he's coming as something else, I don't want to die holding the wrong weapon.”

---

Lord Vaeren Thoss laughed.

Actually laughed.

“Selk got careless.”

His guests did not join him.

The coastal noble poured another glass of blood-wine.

A Vampire.

Old.

Wealthy.

Comfortable.

His estate overlooked the sea.

“Zee Darkheart has been terrifying people for decades.”

One guest shifted.

“Selk's defenses were extensive.”

“Selk trusted machines.”

Thoss drank.

“I trust money.”

Another guest looked toward the armed guards surrounding the room.

Dozens.

Thoss smiled.

“Kings bleed.”

His eyes reddened.

“We proved that once.”

Then he raised his glass.

“To Selk.”

Nobody joined the toast.

---

Kaldrek Vane did not laugh.

He closed his forge.

Immediately.

The Wolf smith pulled the iron shutters himself.

His apprentices stared.

“Master?”

“Go home.”

“But the commission—”

“Go.”

They obeyed.

Kaldrek waited until the forge was empty.

Then he walked beneath the main furnace.

Opened a hidden compartment.

Inside rested an old Dragonbane barb.

Not the one used on Zee.

A prototype.

Kaldrek picked it up.

Stared.

Years ago, he had been proud of this design.

Proud that his craftsmanship could penetrate something people called unbreakable.

Now?

He threw it into the furnace.

The metal glowed.

Kaldrek watched it burn.

Then whispered—

“He finally came.”

---

Neris Pell destroyed records.

Not all.

Only specific ones.

The information broker moved through her archive with ruthless efficiency.

Zee's travel patterns.

Old maps.

Darkheart access routes.

Public sightings.

Family connections.

Battle observations.

She burned them.

Her assistant stared.

“You said information is never destroyed.”

“I lied.”

“Where are we going?”

Neris stopped.

“We?”

The assistant's face changed.

Neris handed him a bag of coin.

“You never worked for me.”

“What?”

“You have never heard the name Zee Darkheart.”

“Neris—”

“Go.”

He went.

Neris waited until the door shut.

Then removed a single sealed envelope from beneath the floor.

Black wax.

Old.

Three vertical cuts.

One horizontal line.

She stared at it.

Did not open it.

She had never opened it.

She had only delivered information where she was paid to deliver it.

“It wasn't personal,” she whispered.

Then she looked at the smoke rising from her burning records.

For the first time in years—

she wondered whether Zee would care.

---

Drovak Senn packed.

Efficiently.

Three shirts.

Coin.

Weapons.

Documents.

No sentimental objects.

The Human logistics controller had survived wars because he understood one rule better than most:

Know when the road is closing.

Selk dead meant the road was closing.

He opened a map.

North?

Too obvious.

East?

Darkheart influence.

West?

Ports.

South?

Neutral kingdoms.

He chose none.

Instead, he took out the extraction map from Chapter 128.

Old.

Folded.

Bloodstained.

Drovak studied it.

Then smiled grimly.

“If I were you…”

His finger moved across the map.

Not toward escape.

Toward someone else.

Jorren.

---

Sera Quill did not run.

She opened a book.

The Dragon woman sat alone inside a stone chamber lit by one hanging flame.

Before her rested thirteen years of observations.

Zee Darkheart.

Changes.

Adaptations.

Kingdom expansion.

Known battles.

Behavioral evolution.

New tactics.

His shift after Chapter 128 had fascinated her most.

False openings.

Misdirection.

Delayed responses.

Changing priorities.

He had become less predictable.

She had noticed before most.

Selk's death report lay beside her.

BLACK-CRIMSON FIRE.

PHOENIX WINGS.

UNKNOWN EXPRESSION.

NO OBSERVED WITCH COMBAT.

NO OBSERVED VAMPIRE COMBAT.

NO OBSERVED WOLF COMBAT.

NO OBSERVED DRAGON COMBAT.

Sera stared at the words.

Then opened a fresh page.

At the top she wrote:

**ABYSSCIN?**

She had heard the term.

Rumors from Darkheart.

Very little reliable information.

Below it:

**UNKNOWN PHOENIX EXPRESSION.**

Then:

**DO NOT ASSUME OLD COUNTERS APPLY.**

Sera leaned back.

For the first time in years—

she smiled.

Not because Selk was dead.

Because the problem had changed.

“Show me,” she whispered.

---

Jorren Vale received the news at night.

He read the message once.

Then again.

No visible reaction.

He was sharpening a blade.

He continued.

A younger mercenary waited.

“Should we move?”

“No.”

“Fortify?”

“No.”

“Contact Quill?”

Jorren stopped sharpening.

The room became quiet.

He remembered Zee Darkheart differently from the others.

Not from charts.

Not from supply lists.

Not from secondhand reports.

He remembered Zee breathing hard.

Bleeding.

Trying to rise.

He remembered calling rotations.

Remembered watching each team force another answer.

Remembered Zee adapting anyway.

Again.

Again.

Again.

Until adaptation could no longer keep pace.

He remembered the moment the King finally went down.

He remembered standing near him.

Close enough to see the hatred in Crimson-Gold eyes.

Close enough to know Zee was memorizing faces.

Jorren had given the order.

“Confirmation.”

Then—

“Withdraw.”

He had walked away.

Years passed.

Now Selk was dead.

Jorren placed the blade on the table.

“Send nothing to Sera.”

The mercenary hesitated.

“She contacted you.”

“I know.”

“What do we do?”

Jorren looked toward the dark window.

“Wait.”

“For what?”

Jorren's face went still.

“For him.”

---

Back in Darkheart—

Merek Voss had learned to hate footsteps.

Every set made him look toward the door.

Guards brought food.

Water.

Nothing else.

Zee had not tortured him constantly.

That was somehow worse.

Merek understood the arrangement.

Useful.

Alive.

Useless—

uncertain.

The door opened.

Merek looked up.

Zee entered.

No blood on him.

No visible wounds.

No armor.

Merek swallowed.

“Selk?”

“Dead.”

Merek closed his eyes.

Not grief.

Calculation.

One down.

Seven.

Zee placed correspondence on the table.

Merek looked.

Recognized the handwriting.

“Sera.”

“She kept studying me.”

Merek's face changed.

“What?”

“For years.”

“That wasn't part of the contract.”

“I know.”

Merek leaned forward.

“Let me see.”

Zee didn't move.

Merek remembered who controlled this room.

“Please.”

Zee slid one page across.

Merek read.

His brow furrowed.

Then deepened.

“This is recent.”

“Yes.”

“She's still working with Jorren.”

“Apparently.”

Merek looked up.

“That is bad.”

Zee smiled.

“For them.”

---

Rez waited outside.

Ner beside him.

Zayrlen leaned against the wall farther down the corridor.

Older now.

Powerful enough to have fought beside his father.

Wise enough not to pretend every war belonged to him.

Zee emerged.

Rez looked at the correspondence.

“Selk?”

“Finished.”

“Anything useful?”

“Sera never stopped watching.”

Rez's expression hardened.

“Darkheart?”

“Yes.”

Ner immediately lost whatever casualness remained in his posture.

“How much?”

“Enough.”

“Zayrlen?”

Zee looked toward his son.

“Reports. Public information. Nothing suggesting she got close.”

Zayrlen pushed away from the wall.

“She studied me?”

“Possibly.”

His Crimson-and-Gold eyes sharpened.

“I'm coming when you find her.”

“No.”

Zayrlen's jaw tightened.

Then he caught himself.

This was not Chapter 142.

Not his test.

Not his debt.

“Fine.”

Zee looked almost suspicious.

“That easy?”

“No.”

“Good.”

Zayrlen folded his arms.

“I said fine. I didn't say I liked it.”

Ner smiled faintly.

“That is unfortunately your child.”

Zee looked offended.

“He gets that from you.”

“He gets the attitude from you.”

“I don't have an attitude.”

Rez laughed.

Zee looked at him.

Rez immediately stopped.

Mostly.

---

Elias examined a scorched fragment Zee had brought back from Selk's containment system.

Not because Zee needed a healer.

Because Elias liked understanding what Zee's body was doing.

“The heat never spread beyond what you intended?”

“No.”

“Even underground?”

“No.”

Elias looked impressed.

Years ago, Zee's Phoenix power had been enormous.

Now it was disciplined.

Not simply hotter.

Better.

“You could have destroyed the estate.”

“Yes.”

“But you didn't.”

“There were people there who had nothing to do with it.”

Elias nodded.

That distinction mattered.

Zee's darkness had never required stupidity.

“Any trouble from the suppression?”

“No.”

“Dragonbane?”

“Didn't use Dragon.”

“Wolf irritants?”

“Didn't use Wolf.”

“Silver?”

“Didn't use Vampire.”

Elias smiled.

“And Witch suppression?”

Zee looked at him.

Elias laughed.

“Right.”

Zee leaned against the table.

“They built a cage for someone who didn't show up.”

“That someone still exists.”

“I know.”

Elias understood.

Zee had not lost Witch.

Vampire.

Wolf.

Dragon.

Crimson Sovereign.

Crimson Demonic Dragon.

All remained.

He had simply decided these eight did not deserve to see them.

They had studied those answers.

They were getting another one.

---

Victor entered without knocking.

Zee looked toward him.

“No.”

Victor stopped.

“I haven't said anything.”

“I know.”

“I was going to ask how it went.”

“Now you don't have to.”

Victor stared.

“You become more pleasant with age.”

“You keep resurrecting. We all suffer.”

Victor's mouth twitched.

Zayrlen laughed from the doorway.

Zee looked toward his son.

“Don't encourage him.”

Victor looked at Zayrlen.

“I like him.”

“You are still on probation.”

“It has been years.”

“And?”

Victor sighed.

Ner walked past.

“Your son is right.”

Victor looked at him.

“I was not speaking to you.”

Ner stopped.

Victor reconsidered.

“Good evening, Ner.”

“Better.”

Zee almost smiled.

Almost.

Then Rez entered with a message.

The humor disappeared.

---

“Movement.”

Zee straightened.

“Who?”

“Three of them.”

Rez laid reports across the table.

“Neris Pell has begun destroying archives.”

Zee nodded.

“Expected.”

“Drovak Senn vanished from his known residence.”

“Running?”

“Maybe.”

Rez touched another report.

“Brannic Dor dismissed most of his people and burned several stores.”

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“Smart.”

“And Thoss?”

“Still hosting parties.”

Zee looked disappointed.

“That might be the dumbest one.”

Rez continued.

“Kaldrek closed his forge.”

“Sera?”

“Nothing.”

“Jorren?”

Rez paused.

“Nothing.”

Zee looked at him.

That interested him more.

Seven people.

Seven reactions.

Fear.

Pride.

Preparation.

Flight.

Silence.

And somewhere between them—

someone still possessed the original research.

Someone had continued studying him.

Someone had contacted the man who once stood over Zee while he bled.

The game had changed.

Good.

---

Far from Darkheart, Sera Quill turned another page.

She had already revised three old conclusions.

Zee no longer responded to being studied the way he once had.

He deliberately fed false information.

Changed patterns.

Used expectation as a weapon.

Chapter 128 had taught him.

Sera knew because she had helped write the lesson.

She stared at Selk's final report.

Black fire.

Scarlet beneath.

Wings.

No old powers observed.

Then she wrote one final line.

**He is choosing what we see.**

Her pen stopped.

That realization disturbed her more than the fire.

Because if Zee was choosing what they saw—

then the hunt had already become tactical.

Sera closed the book.

Across another country, Brannic watched his old compounds burn.

Thoss raised another glass.

Kaldrek stood alone in a dark forge.

Neris held a sealed envelope.

Drovak disappeared down an unmarked road.

Jorren sat beside the blade he had sharpened.

And inside Darkheart—

Zee stood before seven names.

Selk Varren had been crossed out.

Not ceremonially.

One line.

Done.

Zee's finger moved down the list.

Brannic Dor.

Vaeren Thoss.

Kaldrek Vane.

Sera Quill.

Jorren Vale.

Neris Pell.

Drovak Senn.

Seven.

He remembered what Selk had said.

*We did beat you.*

Zee had answered truthfully.

They had.

That victory belonged to them.

He would never steal it.

Never rewrite it.

Never pretend he had secretly been stronger.

They chose the battlefield.

They chose the timing.

They studied his habits.

They rotated the counters.

They put him down.

Chapter 128 belonged to them.

Zee's black-crimson Phoenix wings slowly opened.

Scarlet burned through every feather.

The First Natural Abysscin looked at the remaining names.

Their night was over.

This one belonged to him.

# Chapter One Hundred Forty-Six

## Brannic Dor

Brannic Dor knew Selk Varren was dead.

He had received the message before sunrise.

No explanation.

No detailed report.

Only three words written across a strip of black paper.

**SELK Varren. DEAD.**

Brannic had burned the message immediately.

Then he doubled the guards.

Tripled the perimeter.

Opened every old weapons case he had kept hidden since the operation.

For years, he had told himself that if Zee Darkheart ever came looking for him, he would be ready.

He had believed that because preparation had once worked.

Chapter 128 had proven it.

They had studied Zee.

They had understood his Wolf instincts.

They had learned how he tracked.

How he moved.

How he reacted when cornered.

They had built compounds that disrupted his senses.

They had learned which scents confused him.

Which irritants weakened his concentration.

Which traps forced his Wolf nature into predictable movement.

Brannic had been proud of that work.

Until Selk died.

Now he stood inside an underground fortress surrounded by steel doors, scent burners, false tunnels, hidden hunters, and enough anti-Wolf compounds to poison an entire battlefield.

He looked at the weapons arranged before him.

Silvered hooks.

Wolfbane capsules.

Scent-nullifying powder.

Blood masking agents.

Chemical irritants.

Pressure traps.

Decoy trails.

Everything had a purpose.

Everything had been designed for one creature.

One man.

One Wolf.

Brannic slowly tightened the straps around his forearms.

“Let him come.”

A guard swallowed.

“Lord Dor…”

“What?”

“The reports say Selk wasn't killed with Witchcraft.”

Brannic looked at him.

“What was used?”

The guard hesitated.

“Black fire.”

Brannic's expression hardened.

“Fire doesn't change the fundamentals.”

The guard said nothing.

Brannic turned back toward the weapons.

“No.”

He picked up a Wolfbane blade.

“It just means Varren made a mistake.”

Far above them…

Zee walked alone.

No army followed him.

No guards.

No family.

No throne.

He had left Darkheart without announcing where he was going.

He did not need to.

Brannic's scent had already been given to him.

Merek had provided the location.

Selk had provided the next piece.

And Zee had spent enough years hunting monsters to know that fear left traces.

Brannic's fortress was buried beneath an abandoned hunting estate several miles beyond the eastern territories.

Zee reached the entrance just after nightfall.

He stopped.

The old man had prepared well.

Zee could smell the compounds before he even entered.

Wolfbane.

Chemical irritants.

Old blood.

Dozens of different animals.

Human sweat.

Leather.

Steel.

The entire underground structure had been turned into a maze designed to confuse one particular predator.

Zee smiled faintly.

Not because it was funny.

Because it was familiar.

They had really kept studying him.

He pushed open the first door.

A cloud of scentless powder exploded across the corridor.

Zee walked through it.

Nothing happened.

A second trap triggered beneath his feet.

Iron spikes shot upward.

Black-crimson flame appeared around Zee's boots.

The spikes melted before reaching him.

He continued walking.

Behind a wall, someone whispered.

“He didn't react.”

Another voice answered.

“Wait.”

A third trap activated.

The corridor filled with a chemical mist designed to interfere with supernatural scent recognition.

Zee stopped.

For half a second, the old version of him might have adjusted.

Tracked differently.

Changed forms.

Searched for another sensory anchor.

Instead…

Two black-crimson wings unfolded from his back.

The air changed.

The mist burned away.

Not exploded.

Not scattered.

Burned.

Every molecule of it seemed to disappear beneath the controlled heat radiating from the Phoenix manifestation.

The guards watching through the hidden passages stared.

One whispered:

“What is that?”

Zee looked directly toward the wall.

The guard froze.

Zee smiled.

“You built all this for a Wolf.”

The wall exploded inward.

Black-crimson fire rolled through the chamber.

The guards scattered.

Zee stepped through the flames.

He was still human.

Mostly.

Dark Phoenix wings stretched behind him.

Scarlet light burned underneath the black-crimson fire crawling across his shoulders.

His eyes had changed.

Not into the eyes they remembered.

Something deeper.

Older.

Wrong for every calculation they had made.

Brannic watched from the next chamber.

His face went pale.

“You…”

Zee walked toward him.

“You studied me.”

Brannic raised his weapon.

“You were a Witch.”

Zee kept walking.

“A Vampire.”

Another step.

“A Wolf.”

Another.

“A Dragon.”

Zee tilted his head.

“Among other things.”

Brannic fired.

Three Wolfbane bolts.

Zee didn't dodge.

The first struck his chest.

The second struck his shoulder.

The third struck beneath his ribs.

Brannic smiled.

Then the smile disappeared.

The bolts dissolved.

Not broke.

Not fell out.

They simply burned away.

The wounds closed beneath them.

Brannic stared.

Zee pulled the last bolt from his side.

The metal glowed.

Then vanished inside black-crimson flame.

Brannic backed away.

“No.”

Zee's wings spread.

“You prepared for everything you knew.”

Fire gathered between his fingers.

“You just never knew me.”

Brannic ran.

Zee let him.

That was the mistake.

The underground fortress suddenly became a hunting ground.

Brannic knew every passage.

Every door.

Every hidden tunnel.

He triggered traps behind him.

Steel jaws snapped shut.

Scent bombs detonated.

Wolfbane clouds filled corridors.

Hidden hunters fired from walls.

Zee moved through all of it.

Black Phoenix fire burned away the compounds.

His wings carried him over the traps.

His pressure alone forced hidden attackers out of their positions.

One hunter fired a crossbow.

Zee caught the bolt.

Black flame crawled over his fingers.

He looked at the man.

“You weren't on Merek's list.”

The hunter dropped his weapon.

“I was hired by Brannic.”

Zee stared at him.

“Leave.”

The man didn't need to be told twice.

Zee continued.

Brannic reached the deepest chamber.

He slammed his hand against a stone panel.

The floor opened.

A massive pit appeared beneath Zee.

Iron chains shot upward from every direction.

Brannic pulled a lever.

The chains wrapped around Zee's wings.

For the first time…

Zee stopped.

Brannic breathed heavily.

“Yes.”

He smiled.

“I knew it.”

The chains tightened.

“They may not understand what you are now…”

He pulled another lever.

“…but I know how to restrain movement.”

Zee looked at the chains.

Then at Brannic.

“You really don't.”

Black-crimson fire erupted.

The chains turned white.

Then melted.

Brannic's smile vanished.

Zee stepped forward.

The floor beneath him cracked.

Brannic reached for another weapon.

Zee crossed the distance before he could draw it.

One hand caught Brannic by the throat.

The other remained at his side.

No transformation.

No explosion.

No dramatic display.

Just overwhelming Phoenix pressure.

Brannic's feet left the floor.

“You're going to answer some questions.”

Brannic struggled.

“You think I'll help you?”

“I don't need help.”

Zee's grip tightened.

“I need information.”

Brannic coughed.

“About what?”

“The others.”

Brannic went still.

Zee's expression remained calm.

“Selk gave me something.”

“He's dead.”

“I know.”

“And you think he told you everything?”

“No.”

Zee's wings folded slowly behind him.

“That's why you're still breathing.”

Brannic stared at him.

“You're killing everyone?”

“Everyone who mattered.”

Brannic swallowed.

“You're insane.”

“No.”

Zee's voice became quieter.

“I'm organized.”

Brannic looked away.

Zee waited.

Eventually, Brannic spoke.

“Vaeren Thoss.”

Zee's eyes narrowed.

“What about him?”

“He paid more than Merek.”

“For what?”

“Logistics. Information. Protection.”

Zee said nothing.

Brannic continued.

“Thoss had access to Vampire networks. He helped arrange movement through territories we couldn't enter openly.”

“Next.”

“Kaldrek Vane supplied the weapons.”

“What weapons?”

“Dragon-resistant equipment. Specialized restraints. Armor.”

Zee's expression changed slightly.

“Next.”

“Sera Quill.”

“What did she do?”

“Intelligence.”

Brannic looked at Zee.

“She maintained files on you.”

“How much?”

“Enough.”

Zee's fingers tightened.

Brannic immediately continued.

“Jorren Vale led the strike.”

Silence.

That name landed differently.

Zee remembered the voice.

The commands.

The rotations.

The moment they had decided he was weakened enough.

**Break the target.**

**Withdraw on confirmation.**

Zee stared at Brannic.

“Where is Jorren?”

Brannic shook his head.

“I don't know.”

“Lie again.”

“I swear.”

Zee released him slightly.

Brannic coughed.

“Jorren disappeared after the operation.”

“Why?”

“I don't know.”

“Who does?”

Brannic hesitated.

“Neris Pell.”

Zee remembered the name.

“Next.”

“Drovak Senn handled movement. Safehouses. Routes. Transportation.”

Brannic's breathing became weaker.

“And Kaldrek?”

“You already asked.”

“No.”

Zee's eyes hardened.

“I asked what he supplied.”

Brannic understood.

“You want to know where he is.”

“Yes.”

“He moved north.”

“How long ago?”

“Three months.”

Zee released him.

Brannic dropped to his knees.

For one brief second, he believed he might live.

Then he looked up.

“You got your answers.”

Zee stared down at him.

“You helped put me on that floor.”

Brannic said nothing.

“You helped build the traps.”

Nothing.

“You helped study how to break me.”

Brannic's face tightened.

“It was a contract.”

Zee smiled without warmth.

“I know.”

Brannic stared at him.

“It wasn't personal.”

“I know that too.”

Black-crimson fire appeared around Zee's hand.

“That doesn't make it disappear.”

Brannic's eyes widened.

Zee stepped closer.

“You went home after.”

Brannic said nothing.

“You ate.”

The fire grew.

“You slept.”

Brannic's breathing shook.

“You forgot.”

Zee's eyes burned.

“I didn't.”

The Phoenix fire consumed Brannic.

There was no scream lasting long enough to echo.

Only black-crimson flame.

Then silence.

Zee stood alone in the chamber.

The fire disappeared.

His wounds were already gone.

His wings folded.

For several seconds, he simply looked at the place where Brannic had been.

Then he turned.

He walked out.

---

By midnight, the remaining six had begun receiving messages.

Not official ones.

Not organized ones.

Rumors.

Whispers.

Broken communications.

One message contained only:

**BRANNIC IS GONE.**

Another:

**SELK WAS NOT THE FIRST.**

Someone else received a much shorter warning.

**THE PHOENIX.**

At a fortified estate in the north, Vaeren Thoss stopped pouring wine.

At another location, Kaldrek Vane closed an old weapons ledger.

Sera Quill burned three folders.

Neris Pell stared at a message for nearly a minute before deleting it.

Drovak Senn immediately began changing routes.

And somewhere far from all of them…

Jorren Vale received the news.

He read it once.

Then again.

His face did not show fear.

Not yet.

He simply whispered:

“Two.”

The number hung in the darkness.

Selk.

Brannic.

Two down.

Six remaining.

Jorren slowly opened an old chest.

Inside was a weapon he had not touched in years.

The weapon he had carried the night Zee Darkheart was broken.

His fingers rested against the handle.

For the first time in years…

Jorren wondered whether the man they had defeated back then still existed.

Outside the window, something black crossed the moon.

Jorren looked up.

Nothing was there.

But he knew.

Zee had begun counting.

And this time…

there would be no withdrawal order.
